These downstream of gene ASOs (DG-ASOs) induce RNase H1-dependent cleavage, impairing mRNA 3’ end processing, directing the unprocessed mRNAs for exosome-dependent degradation and creating early entry points in the nascent RNA for the XRN2 exonuclease termination factor. Altogether, we show that termination windows are genuine ASO targets which can be exploited to suppress gene expression. Importantly, we also reveal an underappreciated source of off-target effects which may arise from ASOs binding downstream of genes. Our findings indicate the necessity to expand ASO design and off-target assessment guidelines to include termination window sequences, thereby improving therapeutic efficacy and safety.

title: Non-sewered sanitation systems reshape microplastics into chemically complex and reactive contaminants
abstract: Non-sewered sanitation systems (NSSSs) are gaining global attention as decentralized solutions, yet the transformation of microplastics (MPs) within these systems remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate MP characteristics in the influent and effluent of two NSSSs using laser direct infrared spectroscopy, Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Both systems substantially reduce MP abundance (retention: 53.7–77.1%) but also alter MP characteristics. MPs exhibit fragmentation, reduced particle size, increased morphological irregularity, and surface oxidation, evidenced by decreased spectral matching scores and emerging oxygen-containing functional groups. FT-ICR MS reveals molecular-level oxidation enrichment, and over 260 candidate plastic additives are identified. LC-MS/MS confirms elevated phthalate ester concentrations, including DBP and DEHP. Statistical analyses link MP fragmentation, oxidation, and additive release as coupled processes. These findings suggest that NSSSs reshape MPs into more chemically reactive forms, highlighting the need to evaluate transformation-associated risks beyond retention efficiency.

title: High-throughput spatial proteomics from cellular to subcellular scales via a hanging droplet workflow
abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples are central for clinical research and spatial proteomics (SP), yet liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) remains challenging due to protein extraction losses, evaporation during decrosslinking, and inefficient sample preparation. Current methods often involve complex protocols or specialized equipment, limiting scalability, throughput, and proteome depth. We present a streamlined micro-FFPE proteomics protocol for laser-capture microdissection (LMD) that enables high-throughput processing in a 96-well format, completing the workflow from tissue lysis to LC-MS-ready tryptic peptides on Evotips in just 2-hours. By integrating whole-slide imaging, LMD, and narrow-window data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (nDIA-MS), our approach optimizes lysis, decrosslinking, and digestion within nano-wells leveraging the hanging droplet concept. This design minimizes surface adsorption, enhances sample processing efficiency, reduces preparation time by ~30% compared with reference methods, and enables parallel handling of up to 192 samples with standard equipment. This enables the quantification of >5,500 protein groups (PGs) from 50,000 µm² regions (~250 cells), with robust performance down to 1000 µm2 (~5 cells) with ~2,500 PGs identified. Application to breast cancer (BC) tissue resolves BC subtypes and microenvironments via biomarkers (TP53, HER2, PR). Even from ~60 µm² regions of single nuclei identify ~1,800 protein groups, enabling microscale spatial proteomics approaching near-organelle resolution.

title: Precious metal free tunable manganese oxides for sustainable anion exchange membrane fuel cells
abstract: Eliminating platinum group metals from cathode catalysts in low-temperature polymer electrolyte fuel cells is highly important for addressing the sustainability challenge fuel cell systems face. Here, we propose modifying the electronic structure of Li-intercalated layered Mn-oxide as a cathode catalyst to overcome the activity/stability tradeoff in anion exchange membrane fuel cells. To achieve this goal, we deploy a precious metal free catalyst design strategy involving atomically dispersed p -block metal Sn doped in Li 2 MnO 3 , in addition to d -block metals, which has been poorly explored in the research thus far. Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy and rapid freeze-quench 119 Sn Mössbauer methodology are employed to visualize the catalytic dynamics, revealing that part of Mn 4+ ions are converted into Mn 3+ ions, whereas Sn 4+ ions remain unchanged during the oxygen reduction reaction. Under H 2 /O 2 conditions, anion exchange membrane fuel cells employing Li 2 Mn 0.9 Sn 0.1 O 3 cathodes achieve peak power densities above 1.0 W cm -2 geo and 3.96 W mg -1 Pt . This work demonstrates the beneficial modulation of the electronic structure through p -block metal substitution in earth-abundant Mn-enriched oxide materials.

title: Multi-model collaborative early warning for battery systems with integrated fiber optic sensors
abstract: The safety assessment of battery systems is constrained by sparse temperature measurements and monolithic diagnostic frameworks in conventional battery management systems (BMS). To address this, we propose a multi-model collaborative thermal-runaway early-warning framework using distributed temperature sensing. An integrated sensing scheme increases temperature sensing points within the battery pack from 32 to 540 with minimal wiring complexity and is validated in real-world vehicle operation. We establish a functional relationship between temperature Shannon entropy (SE) and average temperature variation to derive a dynamic warning boundary incorporating error tolerance. Integrating this boundary with thresholds for temperature, temperature change rate, and SE change rate enables collaborative early warning. Compared with conventional BMS warning benchmarks, the framework provides maximum warning lead times of 706 s in laboratory modules and 554 s in real-world vehicle operation. These findings demonstrate the potential of distributed sensing and collaborative diagnostics for proactive thermal-runaway risk identification.

title: Human-specific morphoregulatory signatures in basal radial glia characterise neocortex evolution
abstract: As the seat of our cognition, the human neocortex is an object of immense fascination. Human neocortex expansion during evolution has been attributed to an increase in the proliferative capacity of neural progenitor cells during development, particularly basal radial glia. Despite their evolutionary relevance, the genomic changes driving human basal radial glia biology remain uncharacterised. We use comparative chromatin and transcriptional profiling of neural progenitor cells isolated from gorilla, chimpanzee and human cerebral organoids to identify cis-regulatory elements that have gained activity in humans. Focusing specifically on basal radial glia, we discover that morphoregulatory enhancer activity and gene expression signatures distinguish human basal radial glia from other great apes. Functional analysis of the morphoregulatory genes FAM107A and CNGA3 in human organoids reveals that these genes contribute to the morphological complexity of human basal radial glia. Taken together, our inter-species comparison of basal radial glia suggests that human-specific morphoregulatory signatures characterise neocortex evolution.

title: De novo design of miniprotein inhibitors of bacterial adhesins
abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections necessitates the discovery of novel antimicrobial strategies. Here, we show that protein design provides a generalizable means of generating new antimicrobials by neutralizing the function of bacterial adhesins, which are virulence factors critical in host-pathogen interactions. We de novo designed high-affinity miniprotein binders to FimH and Abp chaperone usher pili adhesins from uropathogenic Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii , respectively, which are implicated in mediating both uncomplicated and catheter-associated urinary tract infections (UTI) responsible for significant morbidity worldwide. The designed antagonists have high specificity and stability, disrupt bacterial recognition of host receptors, block biofilm formation, and are effective in treating and preventing murine models of uncomplicated and catheter-associated UTIs in vivo.

title: A co-evolved peptide-GPCR system senses host entry to drive fungal infection
abstract: A successful infection requires pathogens to recognize the specific host environment in order to reprogram their physiology accordingly. One major way in which eukaryotic cells sense their surroundings is via G-Protein Coupled Receptors (GPCRs), which share a seven-transmembrane architecture and G-protein-mediated downstream signaling. While mammalian GPCRs are well-characterized and represent important drug targets, their fungal counterparts remain poorly understood. Here we uncover a GPCR-based mechanism that allows the corn pathogen Ustilago maydis to sense whether it has entered plant tissue. During infection, the fungus secretes the protein Pit2, which is cleaved by host apoplastic cysteine proteases, releasing a peptide ligand ‘hidden’ within the protein core. This ligand activates the fungal GPCR Gpe1, thus promoting fungal proliferation after initial host penetration. We elucidate the crystal structure of Pit2 and model the complex formed by Gpe1 and the Pit2-derived peptide. Structure-guided mutational analysis supports that disrupting this interaction reduces fungal virulence. The Gpe1/Pit2 system is conserved in related fungal species, with co-evolutionary signatures apparently preserving receptor-ligand specificity. Furthermore, this system shows mechanistic similarities to mammalian receptors, suggesting an evolutionary link between fungal and mammalian GPCRs.

title: A cryptic binding pocket regulates the metal-dependent activity of Cas9
abstract: Cas9 is a metal-dependent nuclease used for genome editing across diverse cells and organisms exhibiting distinct ionic environments, yet how metal ions regulate its catalytic function, and consequently its editing efficiency remains unclear. Here, molecular simulations, Markov state models, and mixed quantum–classical approaches reveal that divalent metals promote activation of the catalytic HNH domain through formation of a divalent metal-binding pocket (DBP) at the HNH–RuvC interface. This cryptic pocket emerges dynamically during HNH activation and is supported by NMR measurements revealing metal-dependent structural perturbations within the HNH–L2 region. Mutations targeting the DBP disrupt HNH activation and impair the coupled catalytic activity of both nucleases, identifying the pocket as a key regulator of Cas9’s metal-dependent activity. Together with quantum–classical simulations revealing distinct catalytic behaviours among divalent metals, these findings uncover an ion-dependent regulatory mechanism in Cas9 with insights for genome editing across diverse biological environments.

title: Lipid-organized tetramerization of PLPP1 defines the molecular basis of spatial lipid phosphate signaling
abstract: Bioactive lipid phosphates, such as lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) and sphingosine-1-phosphate, are potent membrane-embedded signals that regulate fundamental processes in development, immunity, and cancer. The termination of these signals is mediated by phospholipid phosphatases (PLPPs), yet the molecular principles governing their function at the membrane interface have remained poorly understood. Here we report high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy structures of human PLPP1 in apo (1.87 Å) and product-bound (2.21 Å) states. The structures reveal a highly ordered, C4-symmetric homotetramer with ordered lipid densities—including densities assigned to phosphatidylcholine, phosphatidic acid, and phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate—at inter-subunit interfaces. Structure-guided mutagenesis shows that residues surrounding these interfacial lipid densities affect enzymatic activity, whereas oligomerization analysis indicates that activity loss does not simply correlate with tetramer disruption. The product-bound structure defines the catalytic pocket and a membrane-facing tunnel that suggests a possible route for LPA access, while electrophysiological recordings detected no PLPP1-associated ion conductance under the conditions tested. Together, these findings provide a structural framework for PLPP1 tetramer assembly, lipid phosphate hydrolysis, and product recognition.

title: Author Correction: Cell cycle and p53 gate the direct conversion of human fibroblasts to dopaminergic neurons
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, the image shown in Fig. 4n incorrectly presented a shifted view of the image shown in Fig. 4m. Due to the age of the article, the figure cannot be updated directly. The corrected Fig. 4n is available as Supplementary Information alongside this amendment. This notice serves to correct the article.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Spinons, solitons and random-singlet-like behaviours in the spin-chain compound copper benzoate
abstract: The S = 1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain is a paradigmatic quantum system hosting exotic excitations. Using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) on copper benzoate, we characterise three distinct types of excitations by tuning the magnetic field at ultra-low temperatures. At 0.2 T, a nearly constant spin-lattice relaxation rate (1/ T 1 ) and a divergence-like spin-spin relaxation rate (1/ T 2G ) upon cooling provide experimental evidence for spinon excitations. Below 0.4 K, an additional relaxation channel, characterised by 1/ T 1 ∝ T with spectral weight growing as \(-\ln (T/{T}_{0})\) and a divergence of the NMR Knight shift ( K n ), reveals random-singlet-like behaviours. Above 1 T, a field-induced spin gap Δ ∝ H 2/3 signifies the onset of soliton excitations. This work offers NMR identification of spinons, solitons, and the low-energy behaviours of a random-singlet-like state in copper benzoate, and establishes this material as a unique platform for studying the interplay of quantum integrability and disorder.

title: Topological diversity and scintillating dynamics of dipolar surface twists in a van der Waals magnet
abstract: Realizing diverse configurations and dynamics of skyrmionic solitons offers additional topological and dynamical degrees of freedom for energy-efficient, topology-based spintronic devices. Extending these solitons into three dimensions further amplifies their potential, enabling the selective exploitation of surface- or bulk-topological characteristics, a regime that remains largely unexplored. Here, we report high-density dipolar-interaction-stabilized surface twists atop bulk stripe domains under zero magnetic field, through a systematic investigation of three-dimensional domain architectures in the room-temperature van der Waals ferromagnet Fe 3 GaTe 2 . Unlike conventional skyrmions with integer topological charges, these surface twists carry fractional charges and assemble into diverse composite configurations under field swapping, including aggregates of up to 13 surface twists and ring-like structures. Current-driven experiments uncover two distinct dynamic modes: scintillation, marked by the nucleation, annihilation, and helicity switching of surface twists, and ordered motion of bulk skyrmion strings. These behaviors arise from the interplay between spin-transfer torque and local pinning, establishing surface twists as tunable surface-localized topological states whose dynamics are decoupled from their bulk counterparts, thereby enabling versatile hybrid spintronic functionalities.

title: Freezing-induced solid-liquid microphase separation for self-assembly of functional nucleic acid nanoparticles
abstract: In nature, nuclear DNA complexed with histone form highly condensed chromatin via loop extrusion and microphase separation, yielding physically constrained solid-like structures. Inspired by this natural compaction, here we demonstrate that freezing-induced crystallization pressure and freeze-concentration effects trigger solid-liquid microphase separation for efficient DNA compression. Freezing compress various nucleic acids (single stranded DNA, molecular beacons, siRNA, plasmid DNA) into high-density states that self-assemble into nanoparticles (DNA-NPs, MB-NPs, siBcl-2-NPs, siPLK1-NPs, pEGFP-NPs). Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that ice crystal growth increases solute concentration, enhancing DNA intermolecular interactions to form supramolecular chains. Stress at advancing ice-liquid interfaces further orders and compacts these supramolecular chains into nanoparticles. In breast cancer cells, MB-NPs detect miRNA-21; siBcl-2-NPs downregulate Bcl-2 protein; siPLK1-NPs exhibited antitumor effects; and pEGFP-NPs mediate green fluorescent protein (GFP) expression. This freeze-induced self-assembly strategy replaces chemical synthesis with physical constraints, establishing a versatile platform for facile production of nucleic acid nanoparticles.

title: CROSS: A cross-species chromosome substitution platform for dissecting chromosome architecture and activity
abstract: The functional integrity of a mammalian chromosome depends on its long-term co-evolution with species-specific nuclear environment. How chromosomes co-adapt with their native environment to define 3D architecture and transcription remains unclear, largely due to a lack of experimental models that dissect this co-evolution. Here, we report cross-species chromosome substitution (CROSS), a method enabling stable, scarless replacement of host chromosomes with divergent orthologs. We integrate microcell-mediated chromosome transfer with CRISPR/Cas9 to import the intact 152-Mb rat X chromosome into male mouse embryonic stem cells, and subsequently replace the mouse X chromosome, maintaining its stability and integrity. Rat-specific LINE1 and RatSatRep2 repeats recruit mouse SETDB1 inefficiently, causing local H3K9me3 loss. This triggers 3D remodeling, characterized by de novo topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries that aberrantly activate adjacent genes, including Rhox5 , impairing differentiation. We provide a platform for dissecting sequence and epigenome cooperation in chromosome regulation, and evaluating fidelity of large-scale heterologous DNA.

title: FtmOx1-catalyzed diverse C(sp3)-H oxyfunctionalization enables versatile late-stage diversification of phenethylamines and tetrahydroisoquinolines
abstract: The enzymatic late-stage functionalization of C(sp 3 )-H bonds has emerged as a transformative strategy in medicinal chemistry. Verruculogen synthase (FtmOx1) is known to catalyze the endoperoxidation of its native substrate, fumitremorgin B. Here, we demonstrate the catalytic versatility of FtmOx1 by showing its ability to mediate diverse C(sp 3 )-H transformations on non-native substrates—phenethylamine and tetrahydroisoquinoline derivatives ( 1 ) —including β-hydroxylation, β-ketone formation, dealkylation, and α,β-desaturation. A total of 48 structurally diverse substrates prove suitable for this method, substantially expanding the biocatalytic repertoire of FtmOx1. Mechanistic studies, combined with crystallographic and mutagenesis analyses, reveal the distinct molecular basis for this diverse C(sp 3 )-H oxyfunctionalization compared to native pathway. Notably, the relative flexibility of the phenethyl and benzyl chains of 1 , assisted by specific substitutions that allow the two chains to swing, enables high β-selectivity for hydroxylation and prevents secondary oxidation. This C(sp 3 )-H activation platform efficiently generates structurally diverse oxyfunctionalized derivatives, including 1,2-amino alcohols ( 2 ), 1,2-amino ketones ( 3 ), and enamines ( 4 ), accelerating lead discovery for modulators of the human relaxin family peptide receptor 4 (RXFP4). Collectively, our work establishes FtmOx1 as a powerful biocatalytic tool, expanding the frontiers of C–H functionalization in drug discovery.

title: Genotype-phenotype single-cell transcriptomics for massive parallel assessment of genetic variants
abstract: Predicting the pathogenic effect of rare genetic variants is significantly hampered by the limited cohort of diagnosed patients and the difficulty in functionally evaluating the effect of existing and novel variants. To address this issue, we leveraged a protein Multiplexed Assay of Variants Effect (MAVE) to functionally assess the effect of ~ 2200 missense variants of the TP63 gene, some of which cause autosomal dominant developmental disorders. The activity of each variant was measured using an optimized fibroblast-to-keratinocyte conversion protocol, and a subset of mutants was validated through multiple orthogonal biochemical and genomics functional assays to assess consistency and robustness. To systematically expand MAVEs beyond predefined assay, we here introduce SCRAMseq ( S ingle C ell R NAseq A ssociated with M AVEs by seq uencing). This generalizable platform leverages full-length scRNAseq for high-throughput, single-cell genotype-to-phenotype mapping. We validate SCRAMseq across different experimental and genetic contexts to demonstrate its reproducibility and accuracy. SCRAMseq provides a robust and versatile workflow poised to accelerate the discovery and dissection of gene variant effects on any potential disease-driving pathway, thereby significantly broadening MAVEs applicability to virtually any possible disease-driving gene.

title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
abstract: In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe 2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1 ∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits.

title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
abstract: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo 12 , which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo 12 -based PE-skin ( 1 ) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device ( 1A ) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1 -based facial-computer interface ( 1B ) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals and advanced human-computer interaction.

title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
abstract: Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) drive aggressive diffuse midline gliomas by blocking differentiation of radial glial progenitor cells committed to oligodendrogenesis. We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1 , co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy.

title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
abstract: The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi —the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear.

title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
abstract: Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

title: Quantum-sensing-based super-resolution live cell microenvironment imaging
abstract: Direct monitoring the multifaceted intracellular microenvironment is fundamental for deciphering localized cellular behavior and function. However, performing nanoscale spatiotemporal sensing of the dynamic physiochemical environment within a live cell has remained challenging, mainly limited by the lack of robust, biocompatible method which satisfies the requirements for spatiotemporal resolution, sensitivity, multi-physical sensing capability and long-term viability. Here we present a super-resolution-based quantum biosensing approach, namely Super-resolution Multi-physical field Imaging with Deconvolution, implemented in our custom-built setup which integrates nitrogen vacancy center-based quantum sensing with structured illumination microscopy. This enables quantitative, super-resolved, and long-term tracking of intracellular physical fields, featuring spatial resolution of 136 nm, temporal resolution of 150 ms, and field of view of 180×180 μm 2 . We further perform super-resolution multimodal imaging in a live cell, revealing the spatially heterogeneous reactive oxygen species dynamics under external stimulation. Our work enables the dynamic assessment of localized physiochemical dynamics under super-resolution quantum biosensing.

title: A dual-attribution framework reveals how foreign investment and trade redistribute cobalt availability
abstract: Global resource allocation is increasingly shaped by foreign direct investment (FDI) and international trade, yet their combined effects on distribution of critical mineral availability across countries remain poorly quantified. Here, we develop a dual-attribution framework covering 193 countries and 36 territories that attributes primary cobalt availability according to corporate ownership and secondary availability according to international trade. We compare these estimates with a combined baseline scenario using geographic-production and pre-trade perspectives to assess how ownership and trade reshape country-level cobalt availability. Relative to this baseline, total cobalt availability is higher in 63.6% of countries, while 72.7% show a positive composite change when primary and secondary availability are equally weighted. Although these mechanisms do not alter the global total amount of cobalt available, they reduce its concentration across countries. Our findings highlight how FDI and trade reshape cobalt distribution and support resource-governance policies that account for both host and exporting countries.

title: PRPF19 drives hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis via PKM2-mediated glycolytic reprogramming
abstract: Activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) is a pivotal event driving fibrogenic remodeling of the injured liver. However, the upstream regulators that integrate post-translational signaling with metabolic reprogramming during HSC activation remain poorly defined. Here, we identify pre-mRNA processing factor 19 (PRPF19) as a ubiquitination-linked metabolic regulator that promotes HSC activation. PRPF19 expression was elevated in human and murine fibrotic livers, enriched in activated HSCs, and positively correlated with fibrosis severity. Conditional deletion of Prpf19 in HSCs ( Prpf19 flox/flox ; Lrat -Cre ERT2 ), but not in hepatocytes ( Prpf19 flox/flox ; Alb -Cre ERT2 ), attenuated HSC activation and liver fibrosis in vivo. Integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses indicated that PRPF19 sustains glycolytic flux and transcriptional programs associated with HSC activation. Mechanistically, PRPF19 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2), facilitating its nuclear translocation and hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α)-dependent transcription of glycolytic and fibrogenic genes. These findings support a role for the PRPF19-PKM2 pathway in metabolic regulation during HSC activation and liver fibrosis.

title: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities
abstract: The corpus callosum is the largest commissure in the mammalian brain and has been implicated in supporting cognitive processes required for adapting to complex environments. Individuals born with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis, characterized by malformations of the corpus callosum, commonly exhibit deficits in social navigation, abstract problem-solving, decision-making, and self-awareness. Metacognition is a key cognitive process that supports these functions; however, it has yet to be tested comprehensively in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis. Over three experiments, and three Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis cohorts, we examine perceptual accuracy, confidence judgments, and metacognitive efficiency in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis using two variants of a Random Dot Kinematogram task within lab, online, and virtual reality conditions. We find that individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis typically display normal perceptual accuracy but fail to adjust their confidence judgments in line with task difficulty. Computational modeling reveal that this difference is characterized by lower metacognitive efficiency concomitant with lower metacognitive sensitivity. Together, these results provide evidence that the corpus callosum is consistently associated with reduced metacognitive efficiency.

title: A self-limiting mechanotransduction feedback loop ensures robust organ formation
abstract: Organ morphogenesis uses mechanotransduction feedback loops to convert forces into gene expression changes that regulate cell mechanics. How these loops integrate with developmental programs to ensure robust outcomes remains unclear. We show that Yap mechanotransduction establishes a self-limiting positive feedback loop for semicircular canal formation in zebrafish. Canal development proceeds through bud initiation, extension, and fusion within the otic epithelium. Local swelling of hyaluronan-rich extracellular matrix (ECM) in the bud activates Yap in a spatial pattern. Yap increases the expression of its target, ccn1l1 , promoting further ECM expansion to sustain bud extension. This feedback loop confers developmental robustness: graded ccn1l1 knockdown reduces extension rate, yet canal formation persists and fails only with strong disruption. Critically, the loop contains its own termination mechanism. During bud fusion, PKA signaling, activated by the adhesion GPCR Adgrg6, downregulates ccn1l1 , ending the loop. These findings reveal how mechanotransduction loops with built-in termination provide developmental control by integrating mechanical forces, transcriptional responses, and morphogenetic outcomes.

title: Extensive genomic diversity in Desulfovibrio reveals species-specific functional traits associated with disease
abstract: Desulfovibrio spp. are associated with inflammatory diseases and human health, yet limited representative genomes and isolates hinder our understanding of their role in disease. Here, we assembled a comprehensive database of 2658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases and 32 countries, including 24 human isolates. Genomic analyses showed extensive species diversity and revealed disease-associated functional traits, including flagellin and adaptation-associated genes (i.e., ureases). Flagellin-mediated Toll-like receptor 5 activation was species-specific and D. desulfuricans flagellin downregulated TGF-beta signalling in murine small intestinal organoids, suggesting impaired immune tolerance. Additionally, we investigated genomic capacity for hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) production, a main Desulfovibrio metabolite. While health- and disease-associated Desulfovibrio spp. mainly encoded dissimilatory sulfate reduction, tetrathionate metabolism-encoding bacteria were exclusively detected in inflammatory bowel diseases, including Proteus mirabilis and Morganella morganii . Overall, our study provides a comprehensive genomic Desulfovibrio resource and identifies new links associating strain variation, functional traits and H 2 S-production with inflammatory diseases.

title: Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy
abstract: Individuals with disabilities may experience disparities in cancer diagnosis, but population-based evidence remains limited. We conduct a population-based cohort study using linked cancer registry and administrative healthcare data for digestive system cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2021 in Northern Italy, examining diagnostic routes and one-year survival according to pre-existing impairments. Individuals with impairments are more likely to be diagnosed following emergency presentation compared with those without impairments (51.8% compared with 37.9%; adjusted odds ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval 1.23–1.61), particularly those with impairments of mental and neuromusculoskeletal functions. They also have higher one-year mortality (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.26–1.46), independent of socio-demographic and clinical factors. Here, we show that disability-related disparities in emergency cancer diagnosis and survival persist across multiple impairment categories, providing population-based evidence from a European setting on differences in diagnostic pathways across heterogeneous disability groups.

title: Transposable element-mediated structural variations shape gene expression and agronomic trait diversity in Brassica napus
abstract: Brassica napus is a globally important allotetraploid oilseed crop with a complex genome and extensive structural diversity that remains incompletely characterized. Here, we present gap-free reference genome assemblies for Zhongshuang 11 (ZS11) and Westar, and assemble six additional accessions. We harmonize gene annotations across 22 genomes and develop BnaScope ( https://rgmi.hzau.edu.cn/bnascope ), a gene-centric functional genomics platform. Gene-based and graph-based pan-genomes identify 123,107 non-redundant gene clusters and 188,218 structural variants, including 112,417 transposable element-mediated structural variants (TEMSVs). TEMSVs show asymmetric distributions between An and Cn subgenomes and are associated with increased homoeolog expression imbalance, particularly for CDS-TEMSVs. SV-based genome-wide association analyses identify candidate genes underlying seed quality traits, and functional analyses demonstrate that BnaPYRDs negatively regulate seed glucosinolate content. These findings establish structural variation as an important contributor to homoeolog regulation and seed-quality variation in B. napus .

title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities
abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is a crucial urban source of HO x radicals, promoting surface ozone (O 3 ) and secondary fine particle (PM 2.5 ) formation, yet its long-term evolution and air-quality impacts remain poorly constrained. Here, using a deep neural network established on worldwide field campaigns, we reconstruct global surface HONO distributions. Typical megacities exhibited contrasting trends in 2005–2021, marked by a sharp decline in Beijing (−47.4% in 2013–2021), an increase in Delhi (+10.0% in 2005–2018), and slight decreases in London, New York and Los Angeles. These HONO changes are identified as major driver of O 3 and particulate nitrate variations, outweighing contributions of conventional NO x and volatile organic compounds abatement in Beijing and Delhi, while showing comparable impacts in the remaining cities. A fused data-driven framework further uncovers regime-dependent HONO reduction strategies, prioritizing NO x control in summer and co-reduction of NO x , PM 2.5 and direct combustion emissions in winter, to accelerate O 3 and PM 2.5 joint mitigation.

title: Giant step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2
abstract: Control of magnetization reversal is crucial for spintronic memory and logic devices. Previous studies on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnets have largely treated magnetic regions in isolation, leaving the roles of step boundaries comparatively unexplored. Here, we investigate step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped Fe 3 GaTe 2 using Kerr microscopy, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, and micromagnetic simulations. Our results indicate that step boundaries can serve as preferential sites for premature nucleation, giving rise to two distinct regimes. In Type I, reversal initiated in a thicker region propagates rapidly across the step boundary, reducing the coercivity of an adjacent thinner region by up to 59.3%. In Type II, stripe domains originating from the thicker region progressively enter the thinner region, shifting its critical switching field polarity and transforming its hysteresis loop from square to slanted, accompanied by a transition in the dominant reversal mode from rapid domain-wall motion to stripe domain growth. Similar behavior in Fe 3 GeTe 2 suggests that step-boundary-mediated modulation may occur more broadly in layered van der Waals ferromagnets. Our findings highlight step engineering as a potential non-invasive strategy for designing efficient and thermally stable vdW spintronic devices.

title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields
abstract: Multimodal fluorescence and phase imaging provides complementary information about biological samples. However, existing simultaneous fluorescence-phase techniques primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin specimens, restricting their use in thick tissues and in vivo applications. Although multiphoton microscopy enables deep-tissue fluorescence imaging, combining it with three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) imaging remains challenging because few methods can reconstruct the RI of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. Here, we introduce fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT), which reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free and fluorescence-labeled objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. FDT uses the transport of intensity equation and a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared with state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, this approach improves computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. We demonstrate FDT in two experimental regimes: reconstructing the 3D RI of label-free tissues up to 300 μ m thick placed on a fluorescent substrate, and reconstructing the 3D RI of fluorescence-labeled, 3D-cultured cells without transmission-side access using fluorescence emitted by the cells themselves. FDT establishes a foundation for accessible reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems.

title: Structural basis of ammonium transport and coordinated regulation of AMT1;1 in Arabidopsis thaliana
abstract: Efficient ammonium uptake is essential for plant growth and nitrogen-use efficiency, yet the structural basis of ammonium transport and regulation in plant AMTs remains unclear. Here, we determined multiple cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Arabidopsis thaliana ammonium transporter AMT1;1 in apo, ammonium-bound, methylammonium-bound, low-pH and phosphomimetic states. These structures reveal a conserved ammonium conduction pathway comprising an aromatic recruitment vestibule, a Phe-gate/Twin-His-containing pore, and a polar intracellular exit region. We further identified a conserved extracellular N-terminal disulfide bond required for oligomer stability and transport activity, suggesting potential redox-dependent regulation. On the cytoplasmic side, phosphorylation modulates C-terminal interactions with intracellular loops, revealing an allosteric regulatory mechanism. Comparison with the bacterial ammonium-sensing protein Sd -Amt1 uncovers a conserved ammonium-recognition region in At AMT1;1 that contributes to transport activity but lacks the signaling module and ligand-dependent conformational switching observed in Sd -Amt1. Together, these findings provide structural insight into ammonium transport and coordinated regulation in plant AMT transporters.

title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
abstract: Sensory inputs reach cortical and subcortical areas in parallel, but how they coordinate to guide decisions remains unknown. We examined the roles of the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the superior colliculus (SC) in mice performing whisker-mediated tactile detection. While inactivating S1 contralateral to the stimulus increased detection threshold, inactivating ipsilateral S1 decreased it. These opposing effects reflected shifts in choice bias rather than sensitivity. Unilateral SC inactivation produced similar directional effects, whereas bilateral inactivation of either S1 or SC neutralized bias. Furthermore, SC lesions impaired detection performance, and combined S1 inactivation caused no further impairment, indicating that S1-mediated shifts in bias were SC-dependent. S1 inactivation also decreased sensory-evoked neural activity in SC, and choice decoding revealed that behavioral impairment was more closely associated with changes in SC population activity than with loss of sensory encoding in S1. Thus, S1 shapes perceptual bias by modulating SC-dependent circuits that transform sensory evidence into perceptual decisions.

title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
abstract: Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

title: CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons
abstract: Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Using mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation, we show that CREST is essential for motor neuron maturation by activating mature neuronal genes and repressing progenitor genes. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.

title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio ( R GD ) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. While the chlorophyll-increase phase has lengthened by 2.3–5.5 days, the post-peak chlorophyll-decline phase has extended disproportionately by 5.7–6.2 days. Environmental sensitivity analyses reveal distinct hemispheric patterns in the statistical associations between phenological variability and multiple co-varying physical and biogeochemical factors, consistent with contrasting nutrient regimes between the Northern and Southern high-latitude oceans. We further show that these shifts are associated with spatially heterogeneous changes in marine chlorophyll accumulation patterns. Our results identify bloom asymmetry as an important dimension of marine phenological change, providing an observational baseline for evaluating future links between chlorophyll phenology, ecosystem timing, and polar biogeochemical processes under climate change.

title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. Oleylamine ligands adsorbed on NiMoO 4 sub-nanowires act as mild reductants, selectively reducing Ni 2+ to spatially confined metallic Ni domains and forming coherent Ni/NiMoO 4 heterointerfaces. Experimental and theoretical analyses suggest that the Ni/NiMoO 4 interfaces modify the local electronic structure and facilitate the adsorption and activation of hydrogen evolution intermediates. The resulting catalyst requires an overpotential of 14.4 ± 2.9 mV to reach 10 mA cm −2 in 1 M KOH and delivers 2 A cm −2 at 1.62 V in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer at 80 o C, with stable operation over 2200 h at 25 °C. These findings provide insights into the construction and interfacial regulation of sub-nanometer heterostructures through in situ reduction.

title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
abstract: Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract: Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03 , a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -( G03 )- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity.

title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
abstract: Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.

title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. We further show that these trends in Atlantic NICs are primarily driven by changes in near-inertial wind forcing, particularly those associated with mesoscale weather systems, while variations in mixed-layer depth playing a minor role. This observed intensification of Atlantic NICs may have important implications for ocean transport and mixing, and needs to be properly represented in the current generation of climate models.

title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. We apply OSAR to 34 low- to medium-GC bacterial NRPS clusters (7–78 kb) and successfully assemble 31. Expression in Bacillus subtilis yields 29 peptides from 10 clusters. Several products arose from cryptic biosynthetic behaviors such as potential module skipping and premature release. OSAR provides a practical workflow for assembly and refactoring of NRPS clusters and may facilitate the translation of sequence information into natural products.

title: Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
abstract: Identifying targets to enhance tumor immunity is an urgent need. Although nucleic acid sensors play critical roles in promoting tumor immune clearance, their exceptionally low mutation rate in cancers suggests potential unexplored roles in tumor progression. Here, we demonstrate that the RNA sensor melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5) promotes immune evasion, and its high expression is strongly predictive of poor survival and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in patients. Targeting MDA5 reshapes the tumor microenvironment, strengthening immune memory responses and enhancing effector CD8⁺ T cell activity in preclinical models in female mice. Mechanistically, MDA5 deficiency triggers unfolded protein response driven immunogenic cell death through induction of damage-associated molecular patterns, leading to enhanced dendritic cell-mediated antigen engulfment and T cell activation. Additionally, MDA5 loss primes the ASK1-JNK/P38 signaling pathway, sensitizing tumor cells to TNF-α/IFN-γ, further amplifying this process. Consequently, targeting MDA5 enhances the efficacy of ICB therapy across multiple cancer types, positioning it as a promising therapeutic target.

title: Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
abstract: Plant invasions are threatening the long-term sustainability of ecosystem functions. Yet, how plant invasions impact the temporal stability of community cover across spatial scales remains poorly understood, hindering effective invasion management. Using the National Ecological Observatory Network dataset, we examine how plant invasions influence multi-scale stability of total community abundance (used total community cover) via altering community functional diversity, as well as growth and dispersal strategies. We find that invasion-associated losses of functional α diversity and functional shifts toward acquisitive strategies, reduce species asynchrony and species stability, respectively. These changes ultimately lead to lower temporal stability at the local scale (α stability). Meanwhile, invasion-associated functional shifts toward acquisitive seed dispersal strategies weaken functional β diversity, which reduces asynchrony community dynamics among local communities (spatial asynchrony). These concurrent declines in α stability and spatial asynchrony collectively destabilize metacommunity-scale stability. Our findings reveal that plant invasions may trigger destabilizing effects across spatial scales, associated with changes in functional diversity as well as growth and dispersal strategies, underscoring the need for a multi-scale invasion management framework focusing on both local diversity and the connectivity among local communities.

title: ETSAM: effectively segmenting cell membranes in cryo-electron tomograms
abstract: Cryogenic Electron Tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging experimental technique used to visualize cell structures and macromolecules in their native cellular environment. Accurate segmentation of cell structures in cryo-ET tomograms, such as cell membranes, supports the study of cellular organization and function. However, several inherent limitations in cryo-ET, including the very low signal-to-noise ratio, missing wedge artifacts from limited tilt angles, and other noise artifacts, collectively hinder the reliable identification and delineation of these structures. In this study, we present ETSAM, a two-stage Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2)-based fine-tuned AI method that effectively segments cell membranes in tomograms. It is trained on a diverse dataset comprising 83 experimental tomograms from the CryoET Data Portal (CDP) database and 28 simulated tomograms generated using PolNet. On an independent test set of 17 experimental tomograms for which ground-truth annotations are available, ETSAM outperforms other deep learning based methods by robustly identifying cell membranes with high sensitivity while also maintaining better precision.

title: Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers
abstract: Sleep consolidates episodic memory through a hippocampus-dependent process in adults. Whether and how sleep supports memory consolidation during early life, when hippocampal function is immature, remains unclear. Here, we examined effects of sleep on the consolidation of spatial context, a core component of episodic memory, in toddlers aged 2–3 years. Toddlers were familiarized with two spatial contexts, followed by a ~ 90-min nap or equivalent wake period. Afterwards, using a hide-and-seek game we tested their ability to relocate toys within these contexts. Only after post-familiarization sleep, toddlers showed significant context memory and formed stronger associations between toys and specific contexts compared to wakefulness. Contextual memory was positively correlated with spindle density and slow oscillation–spindle phase-amplitude coupling during non-rapid eye movement sleep. Here, we show that, despite hippocampal immaturity, memory effects in the sleeping toddler’s brain are accompanied by thalamo-cortical oscillatory dynamics that are also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
abstract: Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe 48 Mn 32 Co 10 Cr 10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
abstract: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response.

title: Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
abstract: Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. Here, we show that actively-melting grounding zones are required to reproduce nearly three decades of observed retreat, thinning, and acceleration of Thwaites Glacier in a calibrated ice-sheet model, with successful reconstruction occurring only when grounding zones are represented as 2-5 km wide regions. Extending this model forward, we show that grounding-zone processes govern glacier’s detachment from stabilizing seafloor ridges, enabling unpinning as early as 2038 and producing up to 30 ± 6 mm of global mean sea-level rise by 2100 - approximately double previous projections even without additional climate warming.

title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
abstract: We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition–specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA–protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.

title: Exocomets in a planet nursery
abstract: Evidence for exocomets has been found in PDS 70, a young planetary system where planets are still forming. The discovery extends exocomet studies into an earlier stage of planetary evolution, when planets, planetesimals and protoplanetary discs coexist.

title: Author Correction: UNCOVERseq enables sensitive and controlled gene editing off-target nomination across CRISPR-Cas modalities and systems
abstract: In the version of the article initially published, the graphs in Fig. 2a were missing and have now been reinserted in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: KMT2B facilitates long-range gene regulation through LINE1 elements
abstract: Transcriptional regulation is tightly linked to chromatin organization, with H3K4me3 marking active and bivalent promoters. In embryonic stem cells, KMT2B deposits H3K4me3 at bivalent promoters, yet loss of H3K4me3 at these sites leaves developmental gene transcription largely unaltered. Here, we show that, in both mouse embryonic stem cells and during differentiation, the primary role of KMT2B is not to counteract Polycomb-mediated repression at bivalent promoters. Instead, we uncover a distinct regulatory function for KMT2B at the CG-rich 5’UTR of young LINE-1 elements. KMT2B binds LINE-1 5’UTRs and maintains their active chromatin state (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H4K16ac) while preventing repressive H3K9me3 accumulation. Using complementary genomic methods and targeted deletions, we show that KMT2B-bound LINE-1 elements act as enhancers modulating neighboring gene expression in embryonic stem cells and, particularly, during differentiation. Our findings define KMT2B regulatory functions at LINE-1 repeats and highlight transposable elements as key components of long-range gene expression control.

title: DigiDent: integrated bristle-level sensing and AI for contact-aware toothbrushing assessment
abstract: Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing, the most common preventive practice, remains largely unguided and unquantified, contributing to the global burden of oral diseases. Current smart toothbrush systems fundamentally fail to capture the critical fine-scale biomechanics at the bristle-tooth interface, which is essential for evaluating clinical adherence and preventing gingival damage. Here we present DigiDent, an AI powered sensing to interpretation system that renders brushing micro-biomechanics computationally interpretable by measuring in-situ contact dynamics at bristle-tooth interface with an embedded E-Bristle sensor. DigiDent fuses bristle-level contact sensing with inertial sensing through a dual-stream neural inference architecture, converting contact-rich brushing behavior into quantitative and interpretable metrics of force, duration, contact-motion pattern, and fine-grained coverage. In validation experiments, DigiDent achieved >99% recognition of motion-contact patterns and 99.84% classification accuracy across 21 brushing subregions. Pilot user-operation verification further demonstrates the feasibility of DigiDent for real-use brushing monitoring and quantitative feedback. These results establish embedded co-deformation sensing and AI-based interpretation as a technical foundation for future personalized toothbrushing assessment and coaching.

title: An international multicenter study of MASLD prevalence among children and adolescents assessed by VCTE
abstract: The worldwide prevalence of pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains uncertain. Using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE), we estimate the prevalence of MASLD among children and adolescents in community and hospital populations and conduct additional analyses of hepatic steatosis and fibrosis severity grades. In this international multicenter study, we include 9352 children and adolescents aged 6–18 years from 38 centers across 17 countries on five continents. In the overall population, the median age is 12.0 years (IQR: 8.5–15.1), and 5471 (58.5%) are male. The prevalence of MASLD is 17.60% (95% CI: 16.63–18.61) in the community population and 58.03% (95% CI: 56.34–59.70) in the hospital population, with corresponding age-standardized prevalences of 20.97% and 52.34%, respectively. The prevalence of MASLD in the community population is highest in South America (47.92%), followed by North America (25.05%) and Asia (13.96%). MASLD prevalence among adolescents is significantly higher in 2021–2024 compared to 2017–2020, except among those with normal weight or below. Older age, obesity, and elevated serum aminotransferase levels are independently associated with hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, whereas steatosis (grades S2 and S3) is independently associated with greater hepatic fibrosis. Our findings provide useful contemporary data for estimating the epidemiology of pediatric MASLD across diverse populations.

title: Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing
abstract: Understanding how wild populations undergo rapid phenotypic evolution requires linking phenotypic change to its underlying genomic architecture over contemporary timescales. Here, we leverage a 30-year study of Swiss barn owls ( Tyto alba ) to examine long-term changes in two melanin-based traits (plumage coloration and spottiness) that have previously been linked to multiple fitness-related traits. We document a consistent temporal shift toward darker and more heavily spotted individuals and show, using whole-genome sequencing of 3,102 individuals, that these traits are controlled by a small number of loci of major effect with partially overlapping architectures. Temporal allele frequency analyses reveal subtle but consistent changes at these loci. By comparing empirical trajectories to simulations, we show that genetic drift alone is insufficient to explain the observed patterns at one major locus, indicating a role for selection. Our results demonstrate how selection acting on a small number of loci can contribute to rapid phenotypic evolution of continuous traits in the wild and highlight the value of long-term genomic and phenotypic monitoring for disentangling evolutionary processes.

title: Structures and molecular mechanisms of RAD54B in modulating homologous recombination
abstract: Genome stability is essential for cellular viability yet constantly threatened by DNA-damaging agents. Among these, DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are particularly harmful and in S/G2 phases are faithfully repaired through homologous recombination (HR). The RAD51 recombinase forms nucleoprotein filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) that performs critical functions in HR. The efficiency of HR depends on precise regulation of RAD51 filament dynamics by accessory factors, including RAD54B, a double-strand DNA-dependent ATPase. Here, using cryogenic electron microscopy, mutagenesis, and biochemical assays, we show that RAD54B stabilizes RAD51–DNA filaments, inhibits RAD51 ATPase activity, and promotes D-loop formation and strand exchange. RAD54B contains two main RAD51-interacting sites and a β-domain that bridges RAD51 protomers, is positioned to contact donor dsDNA, and regulates RAD54B’s ATPase activity. Cellular assays reveal that the RAD51-interacting sites are required for repairing DSBs by HR in human cells. Our findings uncover a modular architecture and mechanistic framework for RAD54B’s critical role in genome maintenance.

title: Hysteresis of extreme precipitation in East Asia under various CO2 removal pathways
abstract: Extreme precipitation poses severe societal and economic risks under elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), yet current understanding of how it will respond to various future CO 2 removal scenarios remains limited. Focusing on East Asia, a region highly vulnerable to monsoonal dynamics and anthropogenic influences, here we assess the hysteresis of extreme precipitation responses under four CO 2 concentration thresholds and two emission reduction rates using climate model simulations. The extreme precipitation indices based on intensity and frequency exhibit an increase during the CO 2 peak, but fail to fully return to their initial states even after CO 2 levels decline to their initial levels. This hysteresis behavior is amplified by delayed and slower emission reductions. The hysteresis is linked to increases in mean monsoon precipitation associated with hysteresis in tropical Pacific warming patterns and subsequent atmospheric teleconnections. Moisture budget analysis further indicates that enhanced precipitation is attributed to increased moisture transport into East Asia, driven by early-summer rises in specific humidity (thermodynamic factor) through mean circulation and late-summer intensification of monsoon circulation (dynamic factor). These findings reveal the mechanisms shaping East Asian extreme precipitation under different carbon removal pathways and highlight the critical role of both timing and pace of emission reductions in determining regional climate outcomes.

title: Author Correction: Nuclear condensates formed by truncated mutant NEK1s impede ribosomal RNA biogenesis and drive motor dysfunction
abstract: In the version of this article, a citation and discussion of relevant prior work (Georgiadou, P. et al. FEBS J . https://doi.org/10.1111/febs.70487 (2026)) was not included and now appears in the second to last paragraph of the Discussion in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: Neuronal signatures of successful one-shot memory in mid-level visual cortex
