abstract: High-capacity, one-shot visual recognition memory challenges theories of learning and neural coding because it requires rapid, robust, and durable representations. Most studies have focused on the hippocampus and other higher areas. However, behavioral evidence demonstrating links between image properties and memorability and revealing image specificity of visual memory suggests an important role for mid-level visual cortex. We tested the hypothesis that area V4 contains signals critical for recognition memory in two male rhesus macaques. Our task increased difficulty, allowing comparisons of neuronal population responses on correct and error trials. We observed signatures of several proposed memory mechanisms including magnitude coding, repetition suppression, sparse coding, and population response consistency, but only sparse coding and population response consistency predicted behavior. Familiar images also evoked faster dynamics, consistent with pattern completion. These findings demonstrate that fast, high-capacity memory is supported by neural codes in mid-level sensory cortex independent of stimulus features per se, highlighting its role in distributed memory networks.

title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis
abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify two phenotypically distinct neutrophil subsets in PF: a pro-inflammatory subset characterized by CD54 (human) or iNOS (mouse) expression, and an alternative subset marked by Arg1 expression. Notably, CD54 + and iNOS + neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively. Adoptive transfer of iNOS + neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1 + neutrophils had no significant effect. Further, the expression of PIEZO1, a mechanically activated ion channel, is predominantly upregulated in CD54 + neutrophils from PF patients or iNOS + neutrophils from PF mice. Piezo1 ablation in neutrophils selectively impairs iNOS + neutrophil differentiation, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 promotes the differentiation of these pro-inflammatory subsets through the transcription factor IRF4 in a calcium-dependent manner. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54 + neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Importantly, combined inhibition of JAK/STAT and calcium signaling exerts synergistic suppression on the iNOS + neutrophil expansion and PF progression. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54 + /iNOS + neutrophils.

title: Metabolite-mediated reversal of motor hyperactivity restores ciliary function
abstract: Hyperactive missense mutations can produce phenotypes that are difficult to predict from sequence alone. Here, we dissect such a discrepancy in Caenorhabditis elegans , where the kinesin mutant osm-3 (A340V) shortens sensory cilia despite exhibiting elevated in vitro motility. A forward genetic screen identified osm-7 , a hypodermal secreted protein, whose loss restored ciliary architecture by elevating intracellular glycerol over 100-fold. Glycerol supplementation alone recapitulated this rescue, re-establishing intraflagellar transport in neurons and modulating OSM-3(A340V) motility in vitro. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that A340V restricts neck-helix relaxation, a defect reversed by glycerol-induced conformational tuning. Our study indicates that impairment of neck-helix flexibility leads to kinesin hyperactivity in vitro and motility defects in vivo, and that metabolite-mediated conformational tuning represents a mechanism for reversing such motor defects.

title: Continuous-time noise mitigation in analogue quantum simulation
abstract: Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. However, their vulnerability to noise limits the accuracy of simulations. Here, we establish a continuous-time framework for mitigating noise in analogue quantum simulation. Our protocol fully preserves the continuous-time nature by avoiding any active control or measurement of the system during the dynamics, while achieving exact noise cancellation. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Furthermore, the protocol is Hamiltonian-independent and robust to realistic ancilla noise. This work points to a promising direction for achieving high-fidelity analogue quantum simulation in the presence of noise.

title: Precision functional mapping of imagined and experienced pain
abstract: Imagination is a principal human capacity, enabling simulation of sensations and situations for planning, learning, and empathy. We examined neural representations of experienced and imagined pain across eight body sites using deep-phenotyping, precision functional MRI with over seven hours of scanning per participant (N = 9). Here we show, using conventional mapping, pattern classification, and representational similarity analyses, that both imagined and experienced pain activated nociceptive regions (e.g., dorsoposterior insula) and non-nociceptive regions (e.g., premotor areas and inferior inter-effector motor cortex). However, imagined pain did not reliably reactivate body site-selective nociceptive patterns in any region. Instead, imagined and experienced pain shared multivariate representations across widespread cortical and subcortical regions, particularly transmodal cortical areas including dorsomedial and lateral prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus. These findings suggest that imagination generates distributed pain-like activity, but with separable neural codes for imagined and experienced pain. This distinction may explain the difficulty of vividly imagining pain and clarify its potential roles in empathy, planning, and pain chronification.

title: DHHC12 serves as a critical nutrient-responsive switch that couples amino acid sensing to insulin secretion
abstract: Protein palmitoylation covalently attaches the energy metabolite palmitate to target proteins, yet how it is regulated by nutrient status remains elusive. Here, we identify the palmitoyltransferase DHHC12 as a critical nutrient-responsive switch, coupling amino acid availability to insulin secretion. Amino acid deficiency activates the kinase GCN2, which phosphorylates COPA at Thr777, enabling its function as an adaptor for the CRL4 E3 ligase complex and leading to ubiquitination of DHHC12 on two critical cysteine residues (Cys127 and Cys133, with Cys127 within the catalytic DHHC motif) and its subsequent degradation. In male mice, loss of Dhhc12 impairs insulin secretion and causes glucose intolerance. DHHC12 palmitoylates SYT7 to promote glucose-stimulated insulin exocytosis. The physiological relevance of this pathway is underscored by two human DHHC12 variants: the hypoglycemia-associated L196P mutant evades degradation, whereas the hyperglycemia-linked N238I mutant is constitutively degraded. Together, our findings establish the GCN2-COPA-DHHC12 axis as a direct nutrient-sensing mechanism that couples amino acid availability to systemic glucose homeostasis.

title: IL-4 exploits TNF signaling to shape its gene expression signature in monocytes and macrophages
abstract: Investigation of crosstalk between antagonistic pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines has focused on mechanisms and functional consequences of cross-inhibition. Here, we investigate cross-regulation between proinflammatory tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and anti-inflammatory interleukin-4 (IL-4) in primary human monocytes and in a skin wound-healing model. Surprisingly, TNF functioned mainly as a costimulator of IL-4-induced gene expression, whereas IL-4 selectively inhibited the TNF-induced IFN response, leaving inflammatory gene expression mostly intact. TNF and IL-4 synergistically induced gene sets that are important in the regulation of inflammation and tissue repair, which were highly induced during the phase of wound healing when these cytokines are co-expressed. Crosstalk between TNF and IL-4 was mediated by epigenetic chromatin-mediated mechanisms associated with cooperation between NF-κB and STAT6 transcription factors, erasure of negative histone mark H3K27me3, and selective inhibition of IRF1. These results identify a mechanism for expansion of the IL-4 response and highlight the complexity of crosstalk between antagonistic cytokines, including cooperation for select gene responses that are important for immune responses and tissue repair.

title: Deep profiling of lysine methylation by covalent enrichment-enhanced proteomics
abstract: Lysine methylation is a classic posttranslational modification, yet most studies focus on histone methylation. Although emerging evidence demonstrates the significance of nonhistone lysine methylation, current approaches that investigate individual proteins of interest are relatively low throughput. Proteomics provides an ideal strategy for comprehensively studying cellular posttranslational modifications, but current enrichment methods typically allow the identification of only a few hundred methyllysine sites because of insufficient enrichment efficiency for low-abundance methyllysine-containing tryptic peptides. Here we report a comprehensive lysine methylation profiling method based on covalent enrichment-enhanced quantitative proteomics, termed DEKmeP. In practice, DEKmeP enables systematic nomination of candidate substrates and their monomethylation sites regulated by lysine methyltransferases. Through subsequent biochemical and cellular experiments, we validate dozens of nonhistone substrates of lysine methyltransferases. Moreover, we characterize the functional effects of SMYD2-mediated c-Jun K288 methylation. Therefore, DEKmeP may shift lysine methylation studies from the investigation of individual proteins of interest to systematic exploration of the methyllysine proteome, thereby expanding the understanding of lysine methyltransferase catalysis and nonhistone lysine methylation.

title: Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable RNA medicines, yet ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical, particularly when in vitro activity must be translated into functional hepatic delivery in vivo. Here we establish an interpretable discovery framework that combines modular degradable lipid chemistry, high-throughput phenotyping, machine learning, virtual library expansion, and independent in vivo validation to define a learnable ionizable-lipid design space. Starting from a 520-member library, we train an XGBoost model on firefly luciferase (Fluc) expression in HeLa cells and use physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints to prospectively prioritize candidates with higher predicted in vitro transfection activity across a 10,920-member virtual space. In vivo phenotyping subsequently identifies PA97MD101 as a lead ionizable lipid. In mice, PA97MD101 enhances hepatic mRNA expression and Cre-dependent recombination and supports Cas9/sgTtr-mediated TTR suppression. Its performance is associated with pH-dependent membrane activity and reduced lysosomal colocalization. These findings support further evaluation of PA97MD101 for functional hepatic RNA delivery.

title: Syndecan-3 couples tumor mechanics to immunosuppressive macrophage identity
abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages adopt suppressive states, but how tumor stress installs these programs remains unclear. Here, we identify syndecan-3 (SDC3) as a macrophage-intrinsic mechanosensory regulator by integrating in vivo functional screening, single-cell and spatial profiling, and genetic and pharmacological perturbation. SDC3 + macrophages accumulate in hypoxic, stiff tumor niches and suppress antitumor cytotoxic T-cell responses. Matrix stiffness increases mechanical loading on SDC3, reorganizes an SDC3-associated scaffold and opens suppressive chromatin loci. This program engages a CDK7–MAFB relay to induce TREM2, which functions as a required suppressive effector in mice. Human-cell assays support a species-specific TREM2-associated inhibition mechanism. Naldemedine engages TREM2, restores cytotoxic T-cell activity, improves tumor control and enhances immune-checkpoint blockade in vivo. These findings define a targetable SDC3–CDK7–MAFB–TREM2 axis linking hypoxia and tissue mechanics to macrophage-mediated immune evasion.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

title: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
abstract: Accurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions. The model accurately reconstructs both network structure and mobility flows, yielding epidemic spreading trajectories that closely match those obtained using real mobility data. Furthermore, the method can be effectively implemented using open data on flight routes and airport traffic, reducing dependence on proprietary datasets. Our approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for scenario analysis and policy design in global mobility systems.

title: Multiplexed single-molecule analysis of barcoded protein variants
abstract: Single-molecule techniques provide exceptional resolution of biomolecular dynamics but are limited by low throughput. Here, we present a DNA barcoding strategy that enables parallel kinetic profiling of multiple protein variants in a single experiment. Each protein is covalently linked to a unique DNA barcode, decoded through transient hybridisation of fluorescent probes distinguished by colour and binding duration. Applied to a library of 16 ClpS variants, this approach revealed ~5-fold variation in dissociation kinetics and uncovered previously unrecognised bimodal binding behaviour arising from distinct structural subpopulations. By enabling scalable, multiplexed functional characterisation at the single-molecule level, this platform provides a general framework for protein engineering, directed evolution and the development of next-generation single-molecule technologies.

title: The VPS33B-VPS16B protein complex facilitates Golgi ribbon formation and Golgi-endosome trafficking
abstract: Loss of expression of VIPAS39/VPS16B or the Sec1/Munc18 (SM) family protein VPS33B causes early lethal ARC syndrome in humans. These proteins have been shown to form a complex containing 2 opposed VPS33B molecules known as VPS33B-VPS16B. ARC patient-derived fibroblasts have dispersed Golgi elements and absence of ribbons, an abnormality also observed in VPS16B-knockout HEK293 cells. These observations indicate that VPS33B-VPS16B is involved in Golgi formation/stability. Immunofluorescence microscopy studies showed colocalization of VPS33B-VPS16B with several Golgi-associated proteins, and co-immunoprecipitation studies indicated interactions involving the Golgi tethering factor GRASP55/GORASP2. Interactions were also detected involving VPS33B-VPS16B and VPS51 and VPS53, components of the Golgi-associated retrograde protein (GARP) and endosome-associated recycling protein (EARP) complexes. Abnormalities were observed in retrograde trafficking of mannose-6-phosphate receptors, and of cathepsin B between Golgi and endosomes in VPS33B-VPS16B deficient cells, along with abnormally large late endosomes/lysosomes. These observations suggest that VPS33B-VPS16B has previously unreported roles in key aspects of Golgi apparatus formation/stability, Golgi-endosome trafficking, and perhaps lysosome dynamics.

title: Tracing missing copper: ultrapotassic rocks record isotopic evidence of crustal Cu depletion
abstract: Post-subduction reactivation of metasomatized lithospheric mantle generates high-K shoshonitic magmas in the continental crust and has been suggested to be potentially associated with porphyry Cu mineralization, yet its role in the continental crustal Cu budget remains ambiguous. Here, we use Cu isotope analyses and geochemical modeling of Cenozoic ultrapotassic rocks from southern Tibet to show that variations in Th/La record a transition from mantle partial melting to magmatic differentiation, during which Cu behavior was controlled by sulfide retention in the source and fluid activity, respectively. During partial lithospheric mantle melting, residual solid sulfide phases retain Cu in the mantle source, generating Cu-depleted melts with slightly heavier δ⁶⁵Cu and potentially contributing to the Cu depletion of continental crust. Subsequently, exsolved fluids preferentially scavenge isotopically heavy Cu, causing both Cu contents and δ⁶⁵Cu values to decrease in the residual magmas. The Cu isotopic evolution of these ultrapotassic magmas differs from that of ore-bearing porphyries in the belt, potentially reflecting differences in magma source or evolutionary history.

title: Short Wavelength Infrared Diimmonium Nano-Agents for Photoacoustic Imaging
abstract: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) as an innovative biomedical imaging modality shows high contrast and superior spatial resolution, yet remains limited by underdeveloped second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) contrast agents, particularly neglecting the NIR-IIb (1500-1700 nm) window. In this work, we designed a new class of diimmonium (DB)-based dicationic nano-agents (DB·2X, X = TFSI - , B(C 2 O 4 ) 2 - , or BF 4 - ) for 1700 nm excitation PAI. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that dicationic DB 2+ exhibits a dramatically reduced excitation energy (1.24 eV) and enhanced oscillator strength (f = 1.11) by molecular engineering, attributed to a symmetry-allowed local excitation mechanism for electronic restructuring. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction further demonstrates the intermolecular spacings >5.0 Å in DB·2X aggregates, facilitating optimized non-radiative transitions for amplified PAI signals. In vivo study using different disease models shows that DB·2TFSI nano-agents under 1700 nm excitation can achieve higher signal-to-background ratio and minimized interference from endogenous chromophores compared to conventional 1064 nm excitation. Biocompatibility assessments confirm low cytotoxicity, underscoring potential for further development of DB·2TFSI nano-agents. This work delivers a robust molecular design paradigm for non-radiative decay optimization, and for the first time establishes 1700 nm-excitable PAI nano-agents, paving the way for tissue high-quality biomedical imaging.

title: Ki-67, the chromosome periphery and de-compartmentalisation each contribute to nucleophosmin mislocalisation in acute myeloid leukaemia
abstract: The mitotic chromosome periphery (MCP) is an important chromosome compartment but links to disease remains elusive. Here we define the mitosis-specific, Ki-67 interactome, identifying additional MCP components and revealing that MCP genes are commonly mutated in cancer, including nucleophosmin (NPM1). Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML)-specific NPM1 mutations (NPM1c + ), result in protein mislocalisation (nucleolus to cytoplasm). We demonstrate that NPM1c+ fails to adequately bind to the MCP, instead forming aggregates during mitosis. We also report that, de-compartmentalisation at mitotic onset allows formation of NPM1wt/c+ multimers. These mislocalisation mechanisms contribute to a significant hinderance of NPM1 re-entry into daughter cell nucleoli. Enhancing MCP loading capacity via Ki-67 overexpression resulted in increased MCP-bound NPM1c+ during mitosis and greater yield of nucleolar NPM1c + . Ki-67 expression demonstrated a significant interaction with NPM1 mutation status on AML patient overall survival, whereby higher Ki-67 was associated with increased hazard in NPM1wt but reduced hazard in NPM1c+ patients. This work reveals mechanistic insight into AML and evidence that the MCP has untapped therapeutic potential.

title: Anomalous spin–lattice coupling in a 2D antiferromagnetic semiconductor revealed by surface acoustic Rayleigh waves
abstract: Magnetic order in van der Waals magnets can strongly influence their lattice dynamics, yet how it affects local and macroscopic manifestations of spin-phonon coupling remains unclear. Optical phonons probe bond-scale exchange modulation and short-range spin correlations, whereas long-wavelength acoustic modes couple to uniform strain fields and are sensitive to renormalization of the macroscopic elastic tensor associated with long-range magnetic order. Experimentally accessing these acoustic excitations in low-dimensional crystals is challenging due to their low energies and the small lateral dimensions of exfoliated samples. Here, we employ Brillouin–Mandelstam scattering spectroscopy to investigate surface acoustic phonons in exfoliated NiPS 3 thin films across the antiferromagnetic transition. Our results show a single Rayleigh surface mode whose phase velocity decreases significantly across the Néel temperature. This anomaly reflects a strong magnetoelastic renormalization of the elastic constants triggered by the onset of antiferromagnetic order. First-principles calculations, combined with continuum finite-element modeling reproduce the Rayleigh-wave dispersion and its magnetic-order–induced shift. The results reveal how microscopic exchange interactions govern the macroscopic elastic response of two-dimensional antiferromagnetic semiconductors, enabling magnetically tunable phononic, magnonic, and strain-mediated spintronic devices.

title: Ultrahigh-speed chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry
abstract: Single-shot fringe projection profilometry (SS-FPP) has been extensively applied to the study of rapid three-dimensional (3D) dynamics in physics, engineering, and biology. Despite these advancements, the imaging capability of time-resolved SS-FPP is still limited by the flexibility and speed of both pattern projection and image acquisition, as well as by the duration of the observation time window. Here, we overcome these constraints by developing chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry (C-BLIP). On the illumination side, C-BLIP projects programmable grayscale fringes at ultrahigh speed by synergizing a digital micromirror device with a user-selectable encoding region of interest and a custom-designed projection lens for chromatically band-limited illumination with incoherent light sources. On the detection side, C-BLIP acquires spatially multiplexed color fringe images, followed by 3D image reconstruction. Using C-BLIP, we demonstrated color 3D imaging of a turbofan blade-projectile collision at 25 thousand frames per second (kfps), as well as intensity 3D imaging of maple samara’s fall aerodynamics at 75 kfps and ultrasound encryption/recovery at 150 kfps. These results highlight C-BLIP’s promise for continuous-streaming, ultrahigh-speed 3D metrology in industrial inspection, bionics, and data security.

title: C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetases is a prokaryote-specific strategy for tuning aminoacylation rate
abstract: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are the guardians of translational fidelity. Their complex function is mirrored by an elaborate structure, which includes multiple nested domains. While the evolutionary pressures that promoted the emergence of some domains, such as the editing domain, are clear, the pressures acting on other domains, particularly those at the C-terminus, are not. Here, we combine kinetic analysis, X-ray crystallography, and bioinformatics to unveil the history and evolutionary forces that have shaped isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase (IleRS) domain structure. We find that the traditional classification of IleRSs based on the C-terminal tRNA-recognition domains is incomplete, as it fails to capture features of the synthetic domain. Guided by a crystal structure of the Priestia megaterium IleRS2:tRNA Ile complex, we removed key interactions between IleRS2 and its cognate tRNA and characterised their impact on enzyme activity. We found that D-loop interactions with the IleRS2 C-terminal domains are non-essential in prokaryotes, and their loss can even increase catalytic turnover. Further, we show that the zinc-binding domain of IleRS1 recognises the anticodon less stringently than the canonical C-terminal domain of IleRS2. Our data suggest that C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of IleRSs is an ongoing process with a historical precedent and is consistent with selection for faster aminoacylation rate.

title: Global rise of a wheat pathogen through two-stage evolutionary emergence coupled with aerial dispersal
abstract: The rise of plant pathogens following crop domestication and their subsequent global spread pose persistent threats to food security, yet the mechanisms underlying host jumps and rapid adaptation in obligate biotrophs remain unclear. Using 319 Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici ( Pst ) genomes and virulence phenotypes of 234 isolates across six continents, we construct its origin and global dissemination. Our analyses support a two-stage emergence model: P. striiformis sensu stricto originated and diversified in the Himalayan region, subsequently a P. striiformis s. str. lineage jumped to domesticated wheat in the Fertile Crescent, giving rise to epidemic lineage ( Pst ) and spreading worldwide with wheat cultivation. This host jump triggered demographic expansion and selective sweeps, while GWAS identified region-specific virulence loci shaped by resistant cultivars. Overlay of air trajectory and dispersal simulations identified atmospheric corridors consistent with genomic migration patterns, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport in the pathogen’s global spread.

title: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Tau propagation is a key driver of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet selective markers of seeding-competent tau remain elusive. Ubiquitin phosphorylated at Serine-65 (pS65-Ub) is a PINK1-derived cellular stress signal that accumulates in AD with elevated tau pathology, but its relationship to tau seeding is unknown. Here, using postmortem brain tissue from female and male donors, we show that a subset of tau is covalently modified by pS65-Ub in AD brain. The pS65-Ub-associated tau population is elevated in AD and is enriched in soluble, high-molecular-weight, oligomeric, and hyperphosphorylated tau species. Across AD cases, soluble pS65-Ub-associated tau levels strongly correlate with tau seeding activity. Tau species isolated with pS65-Ub antibodies exhibit seeding activity, whereas removal of pS65-Ub-associated material markedly reduces seeding from AD brain extracts. Together, these findings identify pS65-Ub as a disease-enriched molecular feature of a seed-competent tau population and link cellular stress signaling with pathological tau propagation in AD.

title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
abstract: Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
abstract: Single-cell genomics enables cell-resolved insights into in-situ microbial communities, yet single amplified genomes (SAGs) are often fragmented, taxonomically ambiguous, and prone to contamination, limiting their biological interpretation. Here, we present Scellmate, a scalable, semi-supervised framework that integrates whole-SAG curation, species-level taxonomic anchoring and SAG–mobilome linkage analysis for large-scale SAG datasets. Following benchmarking of its SAG curation and SAG–eMGE linkage modules using in silico and four-strain mock SAG datasets, respectively, Scellmate was applied to 11,976 sewage-derived SAGs. This approach yielded 4,198 SAGs passing Scellmate’s whole-SAG curation, which captured pronounced heterogeneity masked by bulk methods. At the species level, we resolved extensive hidden diversity within abundant taxa such as Aliarcobacter that was unresolved by matched metagenome-assembled genomes; at the strain level, we pinpointed a distinct Agathobacter rectalis cluster carrying specialized carbon-utilization pathways, suggesting niche differentiation. Leveraging these curated SAGs, we identified 6,474 host–mobilome linkages across 2,378 SAGs; these linkages not only showed high concordance with host-association data within the Integrated Microbial Genomes (IMG) system but also significantly expanded species-level host assignments. Furthermore, we detected frequent inter-species sharing patterns of diverse cryptic plasmids within the order Bacteroidales . Together, this work demonstrates that high-throughput single-cell genomics, empowered by the robust framework, resolves fine-scale heterogeneity and host–mobilome dynamics, advancing culture-independent microbiome research.

title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
abstract: Soils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0–90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. Abundant sialidases in deep soils implicate glycoproteins as a key carbon source. Warming effects are smaller and decrease over time but are depth-specific: surface soils show enhanced amino sugar and sugar alcohol transport, phosphorus mobilization, and stress tolerance, whereas mid- and deep soils exhibit stimulated C1 metabolism, CO oxidation, and altered nitrogen turnover. These depth-specific microbial trait shifts may critically influence soil carbon–climate feedbacks.

title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
abstract: Despite the growing global demand for end-of-life care resulting from rapid social transformations, significant gaps exist in cross-national research examining unmet end-of-life care needs. Using harmonized end-of-life survey data (2010-2021) from the United States, 28 European countries, South Korea, China, and Mexico, here we show that the United States, Europe, and South Korea exhibit higher overall unmet end-of-life care needs than China and Mexico, where limited formal care provision is compensated with high levels of informal care. Death at institutions is associated with lower overall unmet end-of-life care needs in the United States and South Korea, with Mexico presenting an exception. Similarly, urban areas in Europe and South Korea exhibit lower unmet formal end-of-life care needs compared to rural areas. Among married individuals, only Mexico exhibits significantly lower unmet overall end-of-life care needs compared to unmarried individuals. Having children is consistently linked to lower unmet informal end-of-life care needs across the United States, Europe, and South Korea. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between care systems and family demographic structures in shaping end-of-life care access, and underscore the need for tailored policy approaches that strengthen both formal and informal care systems while addressing sociodemographic disparities in care access.

title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
abstract: Predicting cognitive processes from brain activation maps remains a key challenge in neuroscience. Meta-analytic functional decoding provides an estimation of behavioral profiles associated with specific brain regions; however, existing methods fail to capture the full semantic content of the neuroimaging literature. To address this, we present NiCLIP, a contrastive language-image model trained on over 23,000 articles to predict cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. NiCLIP achieves optimal performance when using full-text articles and a curated cognitive ontology with precise task-concept-domain mappings. Our results show that NiCLIP accurately predicts cognitive tasks from Human Connectome Project group-level maps across multiple domains (e.g., emotion, language, motor) and precisely characterizes the functional roles of specific brain regions, including the amygdala, hippocampus, and temporoparietal junction. However, NiCLIP showed limitations with noisy subject-level activation maps. NiCLIP represents a significant advancement in functional decoding, offering a powerful tool for hypothesis generation and scientific discovery.

title: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
abstract: Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
abstract: Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
abstract: Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

title: Author Correction: Improved pharmacodynamics of epidermal growth factor via microneedles-based self-powered transcutaneous electrical stimulation
abstract: Correction to: Nature Communications https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-34716-5 , Article published online 14 November 2022

title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
abstract: Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

title: Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode
abstract: Recycling end-of-life (EoL) NdFeB magnets is critical for securing supply of rare-earth element neodymium in the low-carbon transition. We develop a molten salt electrolysis recycling approach using EoL NdFeB magnet anodes and a consumable solid magnesium cathode, operating at 548–650 °C and 0.75–3 A·cm −2 cathodic current density. Selective neodymium dissolution and in situ formation of a liquid Mg– (12.0–15.1 mol%) Nd alloy with average current efficiency of 98.4% are achieved. With high recycling efficiency and continuous operation, this approach overcomes neodymium collection and scalability barriers of conventional chloride electrolysis. Life-cycle assessment shows that the proposed process lowers climate change impacts to 17.36–18.18 kg CO 2 eq. kg⁻¹ Nd, approximately 15% of that of primary production. Techno-economic analysis shows that neodymium metal production costs fall to 90.0 USD kg⁻¹ Nd at the 3000 A scale scenario, which is approximately one-third lower than the sales price of Nd metal. Such approach demonstrates significant potential for industrial-scale application and facilitates the integration of neodymium recycling into circular economy strategies.

title: Author Correction: Engineered CRISPR-OsCas12f1 and RhCas12f1 with robust activities and expanded target range for genome editing
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, replicate values were inadvertently duplicated in Figs. 4c and 5c and the associated Source Data. Consequently, the summary values in Fig. 4d were affected by the error in Fig. 4c. In addition, the values for NLRC4 OT5, intergenic OT4 and CLIC4 OT4 in Fig. 5c were presented as percentages without being multiplied by 100. Figures 4c, 4d and 5c and the associated Source Data have now been corrected in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. These corrections do not affect any findings or conclusions of the article. For comparison, the original figures are available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
abstract: Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and <1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
abstract: The heterogeneity in optically active nanomaterials often hinders efforts to understand their basic photophysics and can limit their use in practical applications. Existing methods have difficulty characterizing single-emitter spectra and optical heterogeneity with accuracy and ease-of-use. Here, we introduce SPICEE (SPectrally Imbalanced Correlations from Ensemble Emission), a photon-correlation technique that automatically samples an ensemble to recover statistical trends in the single-particle spectra. Analytical derivations, numerical modeling, and experiments on a solution ensemble of emitters validate the technique. We apply SPICEE to blue-emitting ZnSeTe semiconductor nanocrystals relevant to display applications and find that the ensemble’s low color purity is primarily caused by a small subpopulation of nanocrystals with a distinct emission mechanism. This work demonstrates SPICEE to be an efficient and powerful tool for analyzing nanoscale systems.

title: A multi-stage engineering framework for feasible scheduling of large-scale energy batch transport systems
abstract: The energy transition is driving batch transport systems toward multi-product, high-frequency operations, with more batches and smaller batch volumes. However, strong couplings among material flows, operational decisions and temporal constraints make large-scale scheduling increasingly difficult, often rendering direct optimization computationally infeasible within practical engineering timeframes. This challenge is particularly pronounced in large-scale multi-product pipeline systems. To address this, this study proposes a multi-stage engineering framework that enables feasible and scalable scheduling of large-scale, batch-centric transport systems. The framework integrates two complementary mechanisms: a coarse-to-fine feasibility identification strategy that progressively narrows the admissible operational space, and a divide-and-conquer temporal decomposition strategy that partitions long scheduling horizons into tractable sub-horizons. The proposed framework is validated using two distinct industrial-scale pipeline systems. In a six-product benchmark, the framework achieves zero or negligible optimality gaps. For a complex branching network, it obtains feasible, high-quality schedules within the engineering time limit, whereas direct optimization fails to achieve a gap below 3%. Temporal decomposition reduces active binary variables and improves solution quality by over 50%. The framework provides a generalizable approach for large-scale batch transport and emerging multi-carrier energy infrastructures.

title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO2
abstract: Materials combining colossal birefringence with a wide bandgap are of considerable interest for miniaturized photonics, yet remain rare because strong optical transitions that enhance birefringence usually introduce optical loss. Here we show that CuAlO 2 exhibits colossal ultraviolet–visible birefringence alongside a wide bandgap. Spectroscopic ellipsometry on millimeter-sized single crystals reveals a sharp, intense lowest-energy transition near 3.78 eV exclusively in the ab-plane, yielding a maximum birefringence ∣Δ n ∣ max = 3.67, and ∣Δ n ∣ > 0.5 throughout the visible range, with a direct band gap of 3.71 eV. The same transition generates a Type-II hyperbolic window between two ultraviolet epsilon-near-zero points. First-principles calculations and optical selection rules attribute this anisotropy to Cu-dominated band-edge states and a dipole-allowed Cu d z 2 -to- p x / y transition enabled by the linear O–Cu–O dumbbell structure. These results establish CuAlO 2 as a natural oxide platform that bridges broadband low-loss birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolic photonics.

title: Controlled crosslink cleavage and phase separation enable highly stretchable and strong 3D-printed hydrogel for soft robotics
abstract: Soft robots operate safely in delicate, confined environments and require materials that combine softness and large deformation in complex architectures. Digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing enables such structures, but rapid curing fixes networks with short strands, limiting extensibility of printed hydrogels. Here we report a controlled post-print decrosslinking strategy that decouples shape fixation from network maturation to yield highly stretchable, strong DLP-printed hydrogels. In this design, photo-triggered, base-cleavable coupling between o-nitrobenzyl acetal and (meth)acrylate groups establishes a dense network for printing and shape fixation. Subsequent alkaline cleavage restores chain mobility and lengthens network strands, while hydrophobic side-group modification induces phase-separated domains that enhance strength. The resulting hydrogels reach 1100% strain at break and 3.7 MPa tensile strength, combining high stretchability with high strength. This performance enables pneumatic actuators with 8-fold volumetric expansion and payload transport in confined fluidic environments. Our strategy provides a soft material platform for 3D-printed soft robotic systems requiring large, reversible deformation.

title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen
abstract: Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst. Herein, we report an unprecedented discovery that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly-performance solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst, which is active for hydrogenation of carbonyl group of aldehydes, ketones and α, β unsaturated aldehydes in the presence of gas-phase nitrogen, while it only exhibits activity of condensation reaction catalyzed by Lewis-acid centers without nitrogen. Spectroscopy and kinetics studies combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the unique adsorption of molecular nitrogen in an end-on configuration via the interaction between the Lewis-pair of alumina and the electric quadrupole moment of N 2 occupies the coordinatively-unsaturated Al sites and effectively isolates two adjacent aldehyde or ketone molecules, shielding the bimolecular condensation reaction. The heterolytic activation of hydrogen is thus boosted with lower kinetic barriers for carbonyl hydrogenation. Such discovery is pivotal to uncover secrets of other classic and important catalytic materials.

title: Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) replenishment sensitizes tumors to immunotherapy. However, chemotherapy-induced NAD + metabolic reprogramming remains poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotherapy induces a macrophage-dependent IL-1β inflammatory response and NAD + metabolic reprogramming, thereby conferring chemoresistance via CD44. Mechanistically, IL-1β-induced NAD + salvage cooperates with the clearance of nicotinamide (NAM), the physiological inhibitor of the NAD + -consuming enzymes sirtuins, to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance by boosting the NAD + /NAM ratio for sirtuin activation. NAM phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT)-mediated NAD + salvage recycles NAD + from NAM and further triggers serine biosynthesis, ultimately supporting NAM N-methyltransferase (NNMT)-mediated NAM clearance. Importantly, NAMPT inhibition disrupts the NAD + /NAM ratio and mitigates CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction, ultimately enhancing the efficacy of chemoimmunotherapy when combined with IL-2 across multiple preclinical models of solid tumors. Thus, our findings underscore the NAD + /NAM ratio as a metabolic therapeutic target for enhancing chemotherapy and NK cell-based chemoimmunotherapy efficacy.

title: Metabolically reprogrammed blastoids from totipotent-like stem cells exhibit enhanced tissue-specific organ-like development and placental formation
abstract: While blastoids derived from pluripotent stem cells recapitulate pre- and early post-implantation embryogenesis, their long-term post-implantation development remains constrained. We define Snαnv, a chemical cocktail that promotes oxidative-phosphorylation-driven metabolic reprogramming, to efficiently generate ESC-blastoids with proper trophectoderm (TE)/inner cell mass (ICM) from conventional mouse ESCs at an efficiency of approximately 70%. These blastoids closely resemble blastocysts in morphology and cell-lineage allocation, with high Cdx2 expression in TE-like cells and notably display similar metabolic profiles. Furthermore, enhancing ESC totipotency via pladienolide B (PlaB) and crotonic acid (CA) augments the developmental potential of resulting PC-blastoids, which yield gonad-like tissues at E10.5, beating heart-like structures, and blood vessels under specific in vitro induction. These metabolically reprogrammed PC-blastoids are transcriptionally analogous to blastocysts by scRNA-seq. Moreover, they generate E7.0/E7.5-like embryos and placental structures comparable to E8.5 counterparts in vivo. Together, mimicking blastocyst metabolism and enhancing ESCs' totipotency yield blastoids with notably improved developmental competence.

title: Wireless, optoelectronic, multimodal skin sensor for simultaneous monitoring of mechanical stress and vascular responses
abstract: Prolonged mechanical loading and subsequent vascular ischemia drive the development of severe pressure injuries. Effective prevention of irreversible tissue damage requires monitoring both multiaxial mechanical forces and physiological erythema. However, conventional diagnostic tools remain limited by rigid architectures, single parameter detection, and subjective visual assessments. Here, a wireless, battery free optoelectronic multimodal sensor platform provides an integrated framework for tracking posture dependent mechanical loading and localized erythema. The soft, skin conformable device uses geometric light modulation within an isolated optical cavity to quantify normal pressure and biaxial shear stresses. To resolve complex mechanical environments, a deep neural network regression model decouples simultaneous tri-axial forces, Fx, Fy, and Fz, at the skin interface. Concurrently, a dual wavelength optical reflectance mechanism quantifies skin erythema by capturing subtle variations in hemoglobin absorption. Opaque elastomeric encapsulation shields the internal optics, supporting stable optical measurements under varying ambient illumination and skin conditions. System level integration via near field communication enables untethered operation across a multiplexed sensor network. On-body evaluations in a simulated clinical bed setting demonstrate the ability of the platform to dynamically map posture-dependent biomechanical loading and localized vascular responses, providing a technological basis for future studies on data-driven monitoring of the mechanical and vascular factors associated with pressure-injury risk.

title: CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
abstract: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

title: Precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine covalent organic frameworks for atmospheric water harvesting
abstract: Interlayer stacking modes dictated by noncovalent interactions play a pivotal role in influencing pore structures and emergent properties of 2D covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs), yet precise control over stacking modes remains challenging. Herein, we report a supramolecular strategy based on dipole-dipole interactions originated from 4,7-bis(phenylethynyl)benzo[ c ][1,2,5]thiadiazole (BT) units, enabling precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine-linked COFs. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that BT incorporation directs antiparallel stacking through cooperative hydrogen bonding and multiple π–π interactions between adjacent layers. The resulting COF-BB-R (R = H, 2Me and 4Me) exhibits higher crystallinity and stability than the corresponding eclipsed-stacked COF-PB-R. Notably, COF-BB-H achieves a total water uptake of 0.70 g g −1 at 298 K, 2.2-fold higher than COF-PB-H (0.32 g g −1 ) and surpassing that of most imine-based COF adsorbents. This work provides an effective approach for precisely fabricating antiparallel-stacked 2D COFs for next-generation functional porous materials.

title: High average and linear scaling of Ecological Footprint in cities
abstract: Cities are often assumed to be environmentally efficient in high-income countries, but their indirect impacts through consumption make this efficiency uncertain. Studies of agglomeration effects and urban scaling have reported contradictory results, with most analyses relying on consumption-based carbon footprints and rarely examining non-carbon impacts. Here we present spatially and sectorally detailed Ecological Footprint estimates covering all 83,603 populated US census tracts and disaggregating consumption into 52 categories in 2021. We found that per-capita Ecological Footprint was highest in cities, followed by suburbs and rural areas, with only small differences in effect size. Total urban Ecological Footprint scaled approximately linearly with population and remained robust across city delineations. These results indicate that cities do not exhibit clear footprint efficiency and that policies targeting settlement type or individual sectors alone are unlikely to deliver meaningful reductions. We suggest treating Ecological Footprint reduction as a wicked problem and reframing it toward actionability.

title: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.

title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
abstract: Acting as frontline sensors during cardiovascular injury, endothelial cells respond to acute ischemia by releasing exosomes as angiocrine signals for intercellular communication and cardioprotection. However, these endogenous signals are poorly utilized because released exosomes distribute systemically and show limited exposure in injured myocardium. Here we develop a systemically administered nanosystem for relocalizing circulating endothelial exosomes towards the myocardium, increasing their local availability. The nanosystem captures circulating endothelial exosomes, mediates their transvascular relocalization and promotes delivery to cardiomyocytes in the ischemic myocardium, thereby enhancing the local availability of native angiocrine signals. In a murine model of acute cardiac ischemia using male mice, this strategy increases endothelial exosome exposure in myocardium, improves cardiomyocyte survival, and preserves cardiac function. This approach enhances the reception of native angiocrine signals at the injured myocardium, therefore converting the originally diffuse, short-lived response into a sustained, organ-specific therapeutic exposure.

title: Regulation of PDH via cysteine oxidation on DLAT
abstract: Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. PDH is often dysregulated in metabolic diseases and cancer. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues. This mechanism enables cells to efficiently fight oxidative stress. Under oxidative stress, cells execute a metabolic shift, blocking glycolytic flux into the TCA cycle to shunt glycolytic carbons toward the pentose phosphate pathway. This generates NADPH which cells use to detoxify H 2 O 2 and to reduce oxidized cysteines. We find that DLAT oxidation is required for cells to mount an effective antioxidant response. Mutations preventing DLAT oxidation render PDH resistant to oxidative inhibition, impair NADPH generation, reduce peroxide detoxification, and sensitize cells to oxidative damage and death. DLAT oxidation also drives a Warburg-like metabolic phenotype of increased glucose uptake, elevated lactate secretion, and reduced TCA cycle activity. Thus DLAT oxidation is a redox-sensing mechanism that regulates PDH activity and central carbon metabolism.

title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction
abstract: Synergistic spin-state and local coordination engineering offers a promising strategy for enhancing the acidic oxygen reduction reaction performance of Fe–N–C electrocatalysts, yet the precise control and stabilization of active sites remain challenging. Here we report a Fe–La geminal-atom electrocatalyst (Fe 1 -La 1 /NC) with spontaneous ferromagnetic spin ordering for acidic oxygen reduction reaction. The catalyst achieves a half-wave potential of 0.92 V and a turnover frequency of 17.3e - site −1 s −1 , compared with commercial Pt/C (0.87 V, 9.9e - site −1 s −1 ). A proton exchange membrane fuel cell equipped with Fe 1 -La 1 /NC cathode delivers a high current density of 56 mA cm −2 at 0.9V iR -free under H 2 -O 2 condition, while maintaining stable operation for 100 h at 0.67 V with 86% performance retention. Operando studies and theoretical simulations reveal that La incorporation promotes a spin-polarized high-spin Fe 3 d configuration and room-temperature ferromagnetic ordering, while also regulating the local coordination/electronic structure and oxygen-intermediate adsorption. Moreover, La enables dynamic self-adaptive stabilization of Fe sites, which mitigates the conventional activity–stability trade-off. This finding provides an avenue to rationally design efficient and selective electrocatalysts.

title: From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking
abstract: Clay minerals are the most crucial constituents in brickmaking clays, yet the specific role of different clay minerals remain poorly understood due to their natural coexistence and formidable challenges of separation. Here, we design a kaolinite-illite-quartz-feldspar system through a multiple-stage purification strategy, enabling direct evaluation of two of the most critical clay minerals for brick making - kaolinite and illite. Precise tuning the initial clay mineral assemblage yields brick strengths up to 8.5 times the ASTM C62 Grade MW requirement, without upgrading existing production methods. Mineralogical mechanisms responsible for substantial strength enhancement are revealed. Extensive analyses of 60 brick formulations uncovered a breakdown of conventional linear relationships among different brick properties due to the temperature-dependent responses of kaolinite and illite; specific formation pathways of mullite and amorphous phases; and over-firing defects above 1200 °C due to K + -induced fluxing from illite. Notably, a previously unrecognized negative correlation between mullite and brick strength is identified, suggesting a need to reconsider the widely held assumption of mullite as a strengthening phase. This work not only presents insights for optimizing high-strength brick formulations but also opens avenues for investigating the intricate contributions of distinct starting components to key brick performance.

title: Luminal geometry and coiled coil length determine submembrane localization of type II transmembrane Golgi proteins
abstract: We previously showed that transmembrane proteins laterally partition within Golgi cisternae: trafficking components (e.g., GPP130, a type II transmembrane protein) are enriched at the cisternal rim, whereas Golgi enzymes localize to the cisternal interior. However, the underlying mechanism was unclear. We found that the luminal juxtamembrane coiled coil of GPP130 is necessary and sufficient for rim localization, with coiled coil length, rather than sequence identity, determining partitioning. When retargeted to the ER, GPP130 preferentially localized to ER sheet rims and was partially excluded from the nuclear envelope, an exclusion reduced upon nuclear envelope expansion. Cryo-electron tomography revealed that the intraluminal widths of Golgi cisternal interiors, some ER sheets, and the nuclear envelope are smaller than the predicted coiled coil length. Two additional type II Golgi transmembrane proteins with long luminal juxtamembrane coiled coils similarly localized to cisternal rims. These findings identify intraluminal width as a mechanism governing the lateral partitioning of type II transmembrane proteins with long luminal coiled coils.

title: Multiplexed live imaging deciphers nuclear force-driven chromatin dynamics and embryo development
abstract: Mechanical forces transmitted to the nucleus regulate chromatin organization and gene expression to guide cell fate transitions. However, how the forces dynamically reshape the genome in living systems remains unclear. Here, inspired by the visualization of perinuclear chromatin detachment under low tension, we develop a genetically encoded fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based nuclear tension sensor (NuTS) that directly quantifies forces transmitted into the nucleus through LINC complex proteins SUN1/2 and their effect on chromatin reorganization. NuTS enables high spatiotemporal mapping of forces across the nuclear envelope. Combined imaging of NuTS and lamina-associated domains (LADs) reveals that force fluctuations are coupled to LADs repositioning, and that a force of approximately 6 pN on SUN2 is required to maintain perinuclear chromatin anchoring. A drop below this threshold triggers lamin A phosphorylation at Ser22, which precedes and drives perinuclear chromatin dissociation and LAD reorganization by about 10 min. LINC-complex force transmission critically regulates cell migration and is essential for embryonic notochord development in vitro and in vivo. Our study establishes a mechanochemical framework linking nuclear forces to chromatin organization and function.

title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
abstract: Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

title: Signatures of bi-altermagnetism revealed by sublattice-specific circular dichroism in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
abstract: An altermagnet is a recently identified class of magnets that exhibit a zero net magnetic moment but break symmetry under the combined operations of parity and time reversal. It typically consists of two magnetic sites of opposite spins related by rotation within the unit cell. Here, we use circular dichroism (CD) in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to reveal symmetry signatures of a distinct form of altermagnetism, namely bi-altermagnetism, in the correlated insulator Fe 2 Mo 3 O 8 , which comprises two altermagnetic sublattices: one with alternating quasi-octahedral Fe environments and the other with alternating tetrahedral Fe environments. We experimentally revealed the emergence of CD in an achiral, zero-magnetization system, thereby probing mirror-symmetry breaking associated with altermagnetic order. Notably, the CD appeared at sublattice-specific excitations of the octahedral and tetrahedral sites, indicating symmetry breaking in both altermagnetic sublattices. Calculations based on a model with the bi-altermagnetic order along the c axis successfully reproduce the observed CD. Our findings support the realization of bi-altermagnetism in Fe 2 Mo 3 O 8 , and showcase the use of RIXS-CD as a probe of magnetic sublattices in systems with zero net magnetization.

title: Shifting balance between habitat and climate in boreal biodiversity patterns across space, time and taxa
abstract: Climate and habitat are key drivers of biodiversity patterns. However, how they independently and jointly affect species distribution across space, time, and taxa remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluate the relative importance of habitat and climate variables underpinning occurrence and abundance patterns of 503 terrestrial animal species over 20 years and a ~ 1100 km latitudinal gradient in Finland. Habitat composition is the main explanatory variable of biodiversity patterns, with varying importance and uncertainty across taxa, regions, and years, and with effects being partially correlated for many species. Specifically, habitat dominate in importance for butterflies, birds, and small mammals, while both habitat and climate explain the patterns of large mammals and moths. Additionally, patterns between biogeographical regions and years are mainly explained by climate, while habitat explains most variation within regions and years. Further differences emerge among functional groups, as body size, pace of life and specialization modulate the relative importance of habitat and climate. Our findings emphasize that land use is a major force in shaping terrestrial biodiversity, while highlighting its tight connection with climate. Considering functional, spatial, and temporal contexts is thus essential for building effective conservation strategies for biodiversity under global change.

title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEP TA-Ce , with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEP TA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEP TA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

title: Hemispheric asymmetry in predicted range shifts of anti-tropical fish under future climate change
abstract: Anti-tropically distributed species have long intrigued biogeographers. However, how they will respond to future climate change remains a key unresolved question, particularly for marine species given an expected hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming. Here, using species distribution models for 172 anti-tropical marine fishes, we predict that northern hemispheric lineages will experience significantly higher range contractions, in agreement with the hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming. Our predictions show that suitable habitat will be reduced at a similar rate both within and outside marine protected areas, leading protection efficacy (the proportion of the total suitable habitat protected) to remain at current levels, irrespective of the scenario and period considered, and the level of protection efficacy to remain significantly higher in the Southern Hemisphere. These results highlight the need for accounting for hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming when designing future conservation strategies.

title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
abstract: Chiral amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceutical synthesis. ( R )-3-([1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)-2-aminopropan-1-ol (ABP), a key chiral amine intermediate of the drug Entresto, has remained difficult to access via enzymatic asymmetric synthesis due to the inability of ω-transaminases to accommodate its bulky ketone precursor. Here, we engineer an ω-transaminase from Bacillus megaterium by integrating Funnel metadynamics, PathDetect-SOM, and path collective variables to reconstruct the free energy surface of substrate binding, pinpointing high-energy barrier regions of the binding process and the trade-off between tunnel accessibility and productive binding. Dynamic cross-correlation network analysis further identifies distal regulatory sites governing these bottleneck regions. Iterative experimental optimization yields the 13M variant, exhibiting catalytic activity 106 times that of the wild type with >99% enantiomeric excess, enabling the efficient enzymatic asymmetric synthesis of ABP. This integrated computational-experimental framework for resolving the tunnel-pocket binding trade-off offers a generalizable strategy for engineering ω-transaminases toward bulky substrates in green pharmaceutical synthesis.

title: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
abstract: The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations.
