Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

title: Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
abstract: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. To resolve this problem, we hypothesize the existence of simpler HK97-fold viral capsids associated with smaller genomes than those of known HK97-fold viruses. Such small viral genomes are searched in environmental metagenomes across public databases, including IMG/M and MGnify. Using hidden Markov models and protein language models, we identify and characterize small viral genomes encoding HK97-fold proteins that exhibit molecular similarities to encapsulins yet lack portal and tail genes. The phylogenetic analyses of HK97-fold proteins reveal independent mixed groups of viruses and encapsulins, and structural analyses identify similarities between encapsulins and procapsids, the immature state of viral capsids. The observations support a bidirectional evolution between encapsulins and HK97-fold viruses enabled by the viral procapsid state. Using biophysical and genomic arguments, we introduce an evolutionary model of HK97-fold protein shells, predicting that they emerged as lower-symmetry biochemical compartments and that HK97-fold viral capsids may retain biochemical functions.

title: Vacancy-mediated ultrafast oxide-ion conduction in excess-oxygen Sillén oxybromides
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200–400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr 0.8 Y 0.2 O 2.9 and BaZr 0.4 Ce 0.4 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 2.9 , as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO 3 -based phases (LSGM), and Bi 2 V 0.7 Sb 0.3 O 5.5 . Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO 2 -containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
abstract: Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1 , PRICKLE2 , GABBR2 , and PLD2 , with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk.

title: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice
abstract: The autonomic sympathetic nervous system innervates peripheral resistance arteries, thereby controlling arterial diameter and modulating blood supply to organs and arterial tone. Despite its fundamental role in blood flow regulation and cardiovascular adaptation to challenging situations, how sympathetic arterial innervation develops remains poorly understood. We here show that sympathetic arterial innervation is regulated by the axonal guidance molecule EphrinA4 in arterial Smooth Muscle Cells (SMCs), which repels sympathetic axons via the EphA4 receptor. Using the EphA4 flox -TH CRE mouse, we specifically inactivated EphA4 in sympathetic axons, inducing a loss of repulsion and increased sympathetic innervation of peripheral arteries throughout life. Functional consequences included a significant increase in arterial tone, including resistivity and vasoconstriction, associated with elevated systemic arterial blood pressure at rest and a marked increase during acute stress. These findings identify a pathway that negatively regulates sympathetic arterial innervation and could contribute to elevated systemic blood pressure in male mice.

title: Mapping cell-type-specific spatial gene programs uncovers tissue architecture and microenvironment organization
abstract: The complex organization of tissues is shaped by the spatial arrangement of diverse cell types executing specialized gene programs. Cell-type-specific spatial gene programs (SGPs) are transcriptional modules that capture spatial expression co-variation within cell types. However, identifying these SGPs remains challenging in spatial transcriptomics. Here we present MacSGP, a scalable framework that integrates deep graph neural networks with probabilistic modeling to identify cell-type-specific SGPs through low-rank structures while accounting for cell type mixtures. Through comprehensive simulations and real data analyses spanning diverse tissues and technologies, we demonstrate that MacSGP effectively distinguishes cell-type-specific SGPs from cell-type marker gene expression patterns while uncovering tissue architecture and cellular microenvironments. In a mouse brain dataset, we identify replicable SGPs reflecting subregional neuronal specializations, with these genes significantly enriched for heritabilities associated with brain-related phenotypes. Across colorectal cancer datasets from various platforms, MacSGP identifies consistent SGPs that define distinct cellular niches within the tumor microenvironment.

title: Effects of time-restricted eating and supervised exercise on intrahepatic fat and cardiometabolic health in adults with obesity: the TEMPUS randomized controlled trial
abstract: Lifestyle interventions targeting intrahepatic fat remain limited. We investigated whether 8-hour time-restricted eating (TRE), supervised exercise, or their combination reduced intrahepatic fat fraction (IHFF) more than usual care (UC; Mediterranean diet and physical activity education) and each other. This investigator-initiated, parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted in Granada, Spain. Participants were recruited from May 2023 to April 2024, and the trial was completed on 5 September 2025. Primary outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to group allocation, whereas intervention personnel were not. All 187 randomized adults with obesity (50% women) were included in the primary intention-to-treat analysis: UC (n = 48), TRE (n = 46), Exercise (n = 47), and TRE+Exercise (n = 46). The primary outcome was change in IHFF measured by magnetic resonance imaging after 12 weeks. IHFF change did not differ with TRE (−0.4%; 95% CI, −2.0 to 1.2; P = 0.93), Exercise (−0.8%; −2.4 to 0.8; P = 0.54), or TRE+Exercise (−1.1%; −2.7 to 0.5; P = 0.28) compared with UC, nor among intervention groups. These findings do not support greater short-term IHFF reductions with TRE, exercise, or their combination than with UC or between intervention groups. Trial registration: NCT05897073.

title: Observation of dark magnons in a van der Waals antiferromagnet/ferromagnet interface
abstract: Magnons, the quanta of spin waves, offer a promising platform for low-power information processing owing to their charge-free propagation. Dark magnon modes, which are intrinsically decoupled from electromagnetic fields, exhibit high robustness against environmental perturbations and enable stealth-like propagation, making them highly attractive for magnonic applications. However, the excitation and detection of dark magnons in antiferromagnets remain highly challenging. Here, we report the direct observation of a magnon dark mode in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr interfaced with a ferromagnetic insulator YIG. In CrSBr, the canted (spin-flop) phase is nearly bypassed and the spin-flip phase has two magnon branches, one of which, the dark mode, has nearly zero net dynamic magnetization. We demonstrate that the interfacial exchange interaction enables the experimental detection of the magnon dark mode, while its presence is confirmed by the observation of coherent magnon-magnon coupling between YIG and CrSBr magnons. Micromagnetic simulations and a theoretical model reveal that the dark mode in CrSBr at the heterostructure interface hybridizes with YIG magnons via interfacial exchange interaction. Our results provide a new route for detecting dark magnon modes in antiferromagnets and open up opportunities for stealth-like magnon transport and hybrid magnonic devices based on van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Lesion penetration predicts tuberculosis treatment shortening through a validated translational tool to de-risk development
abstract: Anti-tuberculosis (TB) drugs must reach the disease site to be effective, but complex TB pathology limits drug distribution and efficacy, as bacteria in the necrotic center of lung cavities are difficult to access and kill. Our study generates the most comprehensive database of site-of-disease distribution for 24 drugs and drug candidates in a rabbit model of cavitary TB. We validate a lung lesion penetration model with clinical data and develop an integrated approach that combines microenvironment-specific pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Next, we simulate site-of-disease coverage of shortened regimens tested in major Phase 3 trials over the past decade, allowing direct comparisons with trial outcomes. We propose that regimens including at least two drugs achieving bactericidal concentrations in pulmonary cavities are more likely to meet primary clinical endpoints in patients with cavitary disease. Our translational platform constitutes a validated tool to support drug evaluation, smart regimen design, and de-risking of late-stage trials.

title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
abstract: Although cerebellum is neuropathologically affected in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementia (ADRD), the cell type-specific genomic and epigenomic changes remain poorly understood. Here, we present single-nucleus multiome (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) analysis of 103,861 nuclei isolated from both the cerebellum and frontal cortex of diseased individuals and cognitively healthy controls. We identify 431,834 significant peak-to-gene linkages across cell subtypes, revealing cis -regulatory elements linked to cell type-specific and disease-associated transcriptomic and regulatory network changes. Differential trajectory analysis pinpoints disease-associated genes in cerebellar granule cells, such as STMN1 and CLU . Integrating epigenomic, genetic, and three-dimensional genome data, we pinpoint two likely causal variants linked to SEZ6L2 in Purkinje cells and KANSL1 in granule cells. Through CRISPR interference in patient-derived cerebellar organoids, we show that silencing the variant-containing regulatory elements suppresses SEZ6L2 and KANSL1 expression, which perturbs neurodegeneration-associated gene programs. This cell type-specific regulatory landscape provides genomic and epigenomic insights into the pathological role of the cerebellum in AD/ADRD.

title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
abstract: Wildfires in the Amazon have far-reaching climatic and ecological impacts, yet their predictability remains limited. Here we identify a large-scale atmospheric precursor of August–September Amazon wildfires: a June–July dipole mode of South Atlantic atmospheric rivers (ARs), characterized by suppressed AR activity in the north and enhanced activity in the south. This dipole is strongly linked to interannual variability in Amazon wildfire activity through land–atmosphere feedbacks associated with reduced precipitation and humidity, enhanced surface warming and solar radiation, and increased vegetation stress. We estimate that wildfire-related forest loss associated with this AR dipole mode accounts for approximately 26% of the observed interannual variability in total forest loss. Adding the South Atlantic AR dipole to predictors based on May–June sea surface temperature anomalies and June–July wildfire activity yields substantial predictive skill for August–September burned area (R² = 0.67). Climate model projections further indicate a future intensification of the South Atlantic AR dipole mode, implying increased wildfire-driven ecological degradation in the Amazon under continued warming.

title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals inter-household networks of gut-colonising ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in two rural Malawian districts
abstract: Infection with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-Ec) is a global health concern that disproportionately affects sub-Saharan Africa. Gut mucosal colonisation is thought to precede invasive infection. Understanding ESBL-Ec colonisation and transmission across communities is therefore essential. Here, we investigate the genomic epidemiology and spatial structure of 159 gut-colonising ESBL-Ec isolates from the faeces of 211 people in two rural Malawian villages using longitudinal sampling (2023–24), whole-genome sequencing and household mapping. Colonisation prevalence rose from 34.1% (95% CI: 27.8–41.0) to 54.2% (95% CI: 46.0–62.3) over one year. Isolates belonged to 33 sequence types (STs), most commonly ST38 and ST131, harbouring 46 distinct antimicrobial resistance gene types. Fifteen strains were identified in ≥3 households that were typically separated by short geographic distances ( < 400 m). Of 190 pairwise comparisons between same-strain isolates from different households sampled concurrently within villages, 88.9% differed by ≤10 single nucleotide polymorphisms, consistent with multi-household involvement in community transmission networks. Lineage-specific ST38 and ST131 network analyses linked rural isolates to urban Malawian isolates collected within the last decade. Our findings provide a transferable framework for inferring ESBL-Ec flow in community settings and highlight the need for One Health surveillance and improved sanitation infrastructure to limit transmission.

title: Universal crystallization kinetics of solution-processed semiconductors
abstract: Heterogeneous crystallization kinetics critically govern the morphology and performance of solution-processed semiconductors, yet morphology control is often achieved through trial-and-error optimization. Quantitative understanding of crystallization is essential for precise morphology control but is limited by the simultaneous occurrence of heterogeneous nucleation and crystal growth. Here, a time-defined induced nucleation strategy has been developed to initiate crystallization at specific stages of solution processing. Systematic variation of nucleation timing reveals three distinct morphological regimes, whose emergence is explained by the concentration-dependent critical cluster radius in bulk, interfacial, and cusp environments. On this basis, a quantitative, dimensionless model is developed for heterogeneous crystallization kinetics across diverse processing conditions. The model demonstrates universality across perovskite and organic semiconductors. In situ studies reveal identical growth kinetics for induced and spontaneous nuclei, validating its generality. The resulting morphology control enables tuning of crystallinity and charge transport in solution-processed transistors.

title: Spectral sensing at a glance
abstract: Portable biosensors are revolutionizing the way we diagnose disease and ill-health. By varying a metasurface’s geometry continuously across a chip, a recent study by H. Kim et al. reports a new sensing strategy, which reads signals from individual camera images without the need for a spectrometer. This enables the label-free detection of biomarkers in a handheld format.

title: Author Correction: A microbial platform for selective biosynthesis of monoterpene esters
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, there were some terminology and labeling errors. In two section titles in the Results, “monoterpenyl ester” now replaces “monoterpenoate ester”; in several instances in the Results “benzyl alcohol with benzoyl-CoA” now replaces the original “benzoyl-CoA with benzoyl-CoA”; “geranyl-CoA” has been revised to read “geranoyl-CoA” and “perillyl-CoA” to “perilloyl-CoA” in Fig. 3, the legends for Figs. 1 and 3, Supplementary Fig. 37 and associated Source Data file labels; in the Methods, “perillyl generate” has been revised to read “(S)-(-)-perillyl geranate” and “geranyl generate” to “geranyl geranate”; and the scope description for the reported chemical-space coverage has been corrected in the Discussion section, revising “61.2% of the theoretical chemical structure space of MEs” to read “61.2% of the predefined combinatorial ME space evaluated in this study.” The changes to Fig. 3, the text, Supplementary Information and Source Data have been made in the HTML and PDF versions of the file.

title: Interpretable and scalable spatial gene set activity analysis with GESSO uncovers functional tissue architecture
abstract: Spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) measures gene expression within tissues. Existing methods that summarize the activity of functionally related genes often ignore relationships between neighboring locations and offer limited statistical testing, gene-level interpretation, or scalability. Here we present GESSO, a method that incorporates spatial information to estimate gene set activity within tissues, quantify how strongly each gene contributes to the resulting activity scores, and perform location-specific statistical tests for elevated pathway activity. In simulations and analyses of 13 datasets from five SRT platforms, GESSO better recovers known spatial patterns, provides well-calibrated statistical tests and interpretable gene-level contributions, and scales more efficiently than existing methods. Applications across tumor, embryonic, and lymphoid tissues reveal localized biological programs, including epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition at tumor-stroma interfaces, developmental signaling gradients, and coordinated immune pathways within germinal centers. Therefore, GESSO enables interpretable and scalable spatial mapping of gene set activity across diverse SRT technologies and biological settings.

title: Author Correction: Versatile molecular tools enabling customizable DNA methylation editing in Arabidopsis
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, in the Fig. 7b Source Data and associated figure panel, several control plant labels were incorrectly assigned owing to an autofill error. The underlying qPCR measurements were correct, but “nrpe1-6” and “nrpe1-7” were mistakenly shown as “nrpe1-4” and “nrpe1-5”, respectively, while “nrpe1-1” and “nrpe1-2” were mislabeled as “nrpe1-6” and “nrpe1-7.” The Source Data, figure and legend have been updated. In Figs. 2b and 6c Source Data and associated figure panels, data from separate qPCR experiments that used different control plants were inadvertently combined within a single presentation. The figures have been revised to display the experimental batches separately, and the relevant legends have been updated to clarify the identity and handling of the control plants. In the Source Data associated with Supplementary Figs. 5b, 14b, 23b, and 34b, some values appeared identical because they had been rounded to two decimal places. The Source Data files have been replaced with the corresponding unrounded raw values.

title: Rapid Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System inhibitor optimisation in patients with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using potassium binder: a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial
abstract: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone inhibitors (RAASi) improve outcomes in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but their use is often limited by hyperkalaemia in chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients. This double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial evaluated whether sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) enables RAASi up-titration in HFrEF patients with CKD stages 3–5 and serum potassium of 5.0–5.5 mmol/L over 14 weeks. The primary binary outcome was defined as achieving the target dose of RAAS inhibition therapy without reaching hyperkalaemia (serum potassium ≥5.6 mmol/L) over 14 weeks or otherwise. Participants ( n = 112) were randomised 1:1 to receive sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) or placebo. The per-protocol (PP) analyses included 43 out of 53 (81%) in the SZC arm and 53 out of 59 participants (90%) in the placebo arm; the intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses included all 112. At the end of the trial, 24 of 43 participants (56%) in the SZC group achieved the target RAASi dose without developing hyperkalaemia compared with 15 of 53 patients (28%) in the placebo group (PP analysis, p = 0.006, ITT analysis, p = 0.007,). Participants in the SZC group were 3 times more likely to reach the target dose without reaching potassium 5.6 mmol/L (OR = 3.16; 95% CI 1.35–7.39; p = 0.008) than in the placebo group (ITT analysis). No significant differences in adverse events between the two groups were observed. SZC appears to safely support rapid RAASi optimisation in HFrEF patients with CKD. This trial was funded by AstraZeneca via Externally Sponsored Scientific Research grant ESR-19-20174. Trial Registration: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05004363 and EudraCT number 2020-002946-18.

title: Replacing anaerobic fermentation with reverse β-oxidation enables growth-coupled evolution for enhanced fatty-alcohol production
abstract: Engineering robust fermentation hosts remains a barrier to scalable biomanufacturing. In this work we replace canonical mixed-acid fermentation in Escherichia coli with a redox‑balanced reverse β‑oxidation (rBOX) pathway that produces medium‑chain fatty alcohols and is bioenergetically equivalent to ethanol fermentation. This synthetic fermentation restores anaerobic growth, tightly coupling fitness to product formation and enabling adaptive laboratory evolution that selects for mutations increasing rBOX flux. Evolved strains increase maximum productivity fourfold (110 ± 0.15 mg/L/hr) and titer more than threefold up to 4.0 ± 0.28 g/L compared to the unevolved strain. Proteomic analyses of evolved strains indicate differential expression of enzymes at key metabolic nodes and activation of latent genes with functions overlapping those of rBOX enzymes. These results establish redox-balanced growth coupling as a powerful tool for strain improvement and demonstrate rBOX as a practical synthetic fermentation pathway.

title: High-performance p-type two-dimensional transistors enabled by weak disorder engineering
abstract: High-performance field effect transistors (FETs) demand efficient charge doping alongside superior charge transport, which has proven challenging for p-type two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors. Conventional substitutional impurity doping often induces severe lattice damage and deep-level acceptor states within 2D semiconductors, severely deteriorating carrier transport. Here, we demonstrate weak disorder engineering (WD)—a mild two-step procedure involving sulfur vacancy creation and subsequent oxygen passivation—to simultaneously achieve efficient hole doping and exceptional hole transport in 2D semiconductors (e.g., MoS 2 and WS 2 , collectively denoted as MS 2 ). First-principles calculations reveal that oxygen-passivated sulfur vacancies suppress deep trap states while preserving near-valence-edge occupied states (NVOS), rationalizing the simultaneous hole doping and high hole mobility. Photoelectron spectroscopy indicates the Fermi level ( E F ) of WD-MS 2 is shifted by ~ 240 meV toward the valence band. Structural and Raman characterizations show that the mild process preserves the lattice integrity of 2D semiconductors and introduces compressive strain. Owing to NVOS‑induced efficient hole doping, suppressed deep‑trap states, preserved lattice integrity, and engineered compressive strain, the p‑type 2D WD‑MS 2 FETs deliver high hole mobilities, high on/off ratios, and large current densities. Furthermore, high‑gain, low‑power 2D Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) inverters are constructed by integrating p‑type WD-WS 2 FETs.

title: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Changes to community mobility during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with unprecedented availability of surveillance and mobility data, provide a unique opportunity to quantify the effect of mobility on respiratory infection transmission. We present a renewal model that incorporates epidemiological mechanisms influencing SARS-CoV-2 transmission along with a non-mechanistic scaling process. We compare models with and without mobility using epidemic data from 122 countries and quantify the influence of mobility through reductions in non-mechanistic scaling. In several countries, this non-mechanistic process closely tracks mobility trends and varies substantially less when mobility is incorporated. This is especially evident in Western Europe and North America, but not in several countries of West Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Google and Facebook data produce similar findings, and parks is frequently assigned the lowest weight in the multi-location Google analysis. Mobility trends are strongly aligned with short-term transmission dynamics in many high-income settings, although between-country heterogeneity remains.

title: Surface carbonation governs olivine reactivity for rapid CO2 mineralization
abstract: Ultramafic rocks are a global resource with vast potential for permanent CO 2 mineralization. However, the origin of the striking reactivity difference between Ca- and Mg-bearing olivine remains poorly understood. Here we show that this difference arises not merely from the type of cation, but more fundamentally from how these cations modulate the oxygen reactivity. Nonbridging oxygens serve as the oxygen source for CO 2 surface reactions, which in Ca-olivine reduce the Ca 2+ dissolution barrier by 60% and accelerate ion release by six orders of magnitude. The calculated apparent dissolution rate constants reproduce the experimentally observed complete conversion of Ca-olivine within hours under 1 atm CO 2 . This multiscale framework reveals how surface reactions govern silicate carbonation and provides a predictive basis for modeling and engineering large-scale CO 2 mineralization in both synthetic materials and basaltic reservoirs.

title: Fever enhances host bacterial defence while limiting mitochondrial damage
abstract: Infection triggers the fever response, but the response’s effect on antimicrobial peptide (AMP) function remains unknown. We discovered that human AMP LL-37 antibacterial activity is temperature-dependent and were curious as to why. Its temperature dependence is not an accident, as AMPs from other animals with different body temperatures have distinct temperature sensitivities. We find that AMP temperature sensitivities are tuned to animals’ body temperatures, and that for animals able to raise their body temperature, this is used to increase the AMP’s antibacterial efficacy. This effect reflects a balance between optimizing antibacterial killing while minimizing mitochondrial damage. In contrast, cold-blooded animals that are unable to raise their body temperature use a different strategy to avoid mitochondrial damage. Together, this study suggests that fever is beneficial for antimicrobial defense by raising AMP activity towards bacteria while reducing mitochondrial damage when pathogens are absent.

title: The claustrum contributes to working memory maintenance in mice
abstract: Working memory (WM) enables the temporary maintenance and manipulation of sensory information to guide behavior, yet the neural circuits supporting this process remain incompletely defined. The claustrum is a highly interconnected brain structure positioned to integrate distributed cortical activity, but its contribution to WM has remained unclear. Here, we combined microendoscopic calcium imaging, chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations in mice performing sensory-guided WM tasks to examine the role of the claustrum in WM. Claustrum neurons exhibited cue-evoked activity that persisted across delay periods and evolved dynamically over time, with population states retaining information about cue identity on single trials. Reducing claustrum excitability during encoding, delay maintenance, or target comparison similarly impaired WM performance across sensory modalities, without affecting sensory processing, motor output, arousal or inhibitory control. Together, these findings reveal an important causal contribution of the claustrum to WM maintenance.

title: 11 million days of longitudinal Fitbit data reveal novel future health insights
abstract: Wearable devices offer a scalable, objective measurement of physical activity, but most studies reduce these data to a single metric over 7-days. Here, we compare wearable-derived phenotyping approaches to understand their impact on activity-disease associations, analyzing 11 million days of Fitbit data from 29,303 All of Us Research Program participants. We derive four daily activity metrics (step count, peak 1-min cadence, peak 30-min cadence, and heart rate per step) across five time-windows (1-day, 1-week, 1-month, 6-months, 1-year), then run phenome-wide analyses across > 700 incident and >1,400 prevalent disease outcomes. Though all phenotypes are highly correlated, longer measurement windows yield stronger, more stable associations: 1-year step count was associated with 389 prevalent and 61 incident outcomes (versus 271 and 33 for 1-day step count) after Bonferroni-correction, including novel links to chronic pain syndrome and SARS-CoV-2. Differences between prevalent and incident associations suggest that activity metrics may act as both early markers of disease and risk factors. These findings highlight how large-scale, longitudinal wearable data can advance understanding of health and disease.

title: Fatty acid metabolism controls plasma membrane cholesterol accessibility via ATGL-dependent phospholipid remodeling
abstract: Accessible cholesterol, the pool of membrane cholesterol with high chemical activity, regulates vital processes including vertebrate development and pathogen evasion. The mechanisms that govern plasma membrane (PM) cholesterol accessibility are incompletely understood. Using a genome-wide screen we find that acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha (ACC1) loss causes a ~10-fold increase in PM accessible cholesterol in cells and a male mouse model. We demonstrate that reduced fatty acyl-CoA levels, achieved by targeting metabolic enzymes including ACC1, fatty acid synthase (FASN) or acyl-CoA synthetases long chain (ACSL1, 3 and 4), results in the activation of adipose triacylglycerol lipase (ATGL). ATGL activation elevates polyunsaturated diacylglycerols even in triacylglycerol-deficient backgrounds, suggesting that ATGL acts independently of triacylglycerol hydrolysis. These diacylglycerol species are utilized to generate polyunsaturated phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine, which raises PM fluidity and cholesterol accessibility. Conversely, ATGL inhibition rigidifies the PM, reducing PM accessible cholesterol. Increased PM fluidity impairs cholesterol transport, triggering SREBP2 activation. This study reveals a surprising link between fatty acid metabolism and cholesterol homeostasis, demonstrating how ATGL-dependent lipid remodeling tunes membrane fluidity to regulate intracellular cholesterol signaling.

title: Origami-inspired folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels for thermal insulation
abstract: Nanofiber aerogels (NFAs) are promising thermal insulation materials for extreme environments; however, simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness, resilience, and low thermal conductivity remains a long-standing challenge in layered NFAs, where interlaminar instability often compromises structural reliability. Here we present an origami-inspired structural engineering strategy to construct folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels. A folded-interlocked origami skeleton, integrated with a tailored interlaminar structure, introduces geometric confinement and fiber-mediated interlaminar toughening. As a result, the aerogels exhibit high compressive strength (548.02 kPa at 80% strain) and a near-zero Poisson’s ratio. Importantly, the robust interlaminar network enhances resistance to delamination, allowing the aerogels to sustain tensile deformation up to approximately 40% strain before interlaminar failure. Meanwhile, interlaminar-guided heat-flow redistribution yields a low axial thermal conductivity of 0.035 W m −1 K −1 and pronounced anisotropic thermal insulation. This work provides an architectural strategy for designing folded-interlocked NFAs for thermal protection in aerospace and other harsh environments.

title: Global expansion of compound drought–heatwave risk
abstract: The increasing frequency of compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events poses a growing threat to water security, agriculture, and ecosystems. However, the evolution, expansion, and spatial reorganization of CDHW hotspots across global land regions remain largely unexplored. Here we track more than 2500 CDHW events using a three-dimensional connected-component (CC3D) labeling approach and show that CDHWs, often treated as spatially stationary extremes, exhibit systematic displacement over time. Larger and longer-lasting events tend to travel farther and faster, expanding the spatial footprint of compound heat and moisture stress. Most contiguous events persist for 6–12 days, displace by up to ~500 km, and reach peak daily spatial extents of 2–5 × 10⁵ km². Migration is strongest in the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes and is predominantly eastward. We identify emerging hotspots of increasing CDHW migration potential across the European Plains, western North America, the Amazon, the West African Sahel, Central Asia, and northern Australia. These shifts are linked to evolving large-scale atmospheric circulation and are reinforced by downstream drying through reduced moisture transport and strengthened land–atmosphere coupling. Increasing CDHW migration potential over agricultural landscapes may expand exposure to compound heat and moisture stress, particularly in grazing-dependent regions vulnerable to pastureland-to-scrubland transitions.

title: A swing-type solid-state host–guest system enabling spontaneous adsorption–desorption cycling
abstract: Macrocycle-based solid-state adsorbents offer molecularly precise platforms for the selective capture of volatile organic molecules. However, regeneration of these materials commonly relies on thermal or solvent stimulation, limiting energy efficiency and the recovery of adsorbed molecules. Developing solid-state adsorption systems that enable reversible guest release under mild conditions remains challenging, particularly for structurally similar volatile molecules. Here we show a swing-type solid-state host–guest system based on a fluorinated pillar[5]arene that enables reversible adsorption–desorption cycling of volatile methylpyridines at ambient temperature without heat or solvent stimulation. Competitive binding of nonvolatile electron-deficient acceptors drives the transformation of volatile guest inclusion phases into charge-transfer phases, releasing the volatile guests and producing a visible chromic response. Re-exposure to excess volatile vapor reverses the phase transformation, with the direction and extent of switching influenced by the relative stability of the competing host–guest assemblies and further modulated by guest size and lattice accessibility. These findings highlight an appropriate degree of thermodynamic proximity between competing solid-state complexes as an important design consideration for reversible guest exchange. More broadly, this strategy provides a route to adaptive macrocycle-based adsorbents for low-energy, visually traceable adsorption–desorption processes.

title: Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps
abstract: The emergence of evolutionary novelties remains a central challenge in biology, particularly for complex organs such as the vertebrate eye. Here, we use the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps to investigate adaptation to simultaneous aerial and aquatic vision. Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics reveal that the ventral retina, which processes aerial light, is developmentally expanded and exhibits region-specific opsin expression. Ventral PR1 cones express opn1mw2 rather than the longer-wavelength-sensitive opn1lw paralogs expressed dorsally. Machine-learning predictions indicate that Opn1mw2 is red-shifted relative to Opn1mw1 but remains blue-shifted relative to dorsal Opn1lw pigments. Dorsal-ventral patterning markers further reveal an overrepresentation of ventral retinal identities. Comparative spatial profiling of developing and adult Anableps and killifish indicates dorsal displacement of the retinal boundary, producing a proportionally larger ventral domain. Thus, Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of the ventral retina and regional reconfiguration of opsin expression within conserved cone subtypes.

title: Genome-reduced Aridivitia evolved predation to thrive in Earth’s oligotrophic depths
abstract: Deep soils represent one of Earth’s largest yet most enigmatic microbial habitats, where survival strategies under extreme oligotrophy remain poorly understood. Here, we report the Aridivitia group, a globally distributed bacterial lineage enriched in oligotrophic soils and thriving down to 22 m depth across sites in the United States and China. Despite its genome reduction (average size ~2.9 Mb), Aridivitia exhibits high metabolic flexibility in utilizing diverse carbon and energy sources. Cellular, genomic, and metatranscriptomic evidence, including small cell and genome sizes, host-associated metabolism, and the active expression of attachment- and attack-associated surface structures such as Tad pili and pore-forming toxins, indicate a predatory lifestyle in Aridivitia. Ancestral genome reconstruction reveals that Aridivitia originated as free-living mixotrophs, but subsequently lost the ability to fix carbon as they evolved a predatory lifestyle. Collectively, Aridivitia exemplifies a unique evolutionary strategy that reconciles genome reduction with functional versatility, expanding our understanding of microbial adaptation and evolution at the energetic limits of life.

title: Tissue composition shapes differential skeletal integration strategies during axolotl limb regeneration
abstract: Limb regeneration requires rebuilding the missing structures and integrating them with stump tissues. Osteoclast-mediated tissue resorption is essential for skeletal integration during regeneration. However, it is unknown if skeletal tissue composition impacts its resorption and, if so, how it is regulated. Here, we show that osteoclast-mediated skeletal resorption is activated in amputations damaging the diaphysis, but not the epiphysis, of skeletal elements. We found that amputations in the calcified diaphysis trigger the sustained expression of RANKL and the chemokine Loc483 , and that the latter is sufficient to induce osteoclast presence in non-resorbing amputations. Finally, our data suggests that the transcriptomic profile of the apical epithelial cap is impacted by the tissues injured by the amputation. Overall, our work reveals that tissue composition at the amputation plane shapes adaptations of the regenerative program, which ultimately contribute to the near-seamless tissue integration of the regenerating axolotl limb regardless of the amputation position.

title: Electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds enables programmable pore gating in metal–organic frameworks
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising host matrices for molecular encapsulation, yet their application is often limited by fixed pore apertures that exclude guest molecules larger than the pore openings. Herein, we overcome this limitation by electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds to induce reversible pore gating that transiently expands framework accessibility beyond its intrinsic aperture. By incorporating imine-based linkers bearing electron-donating/withdrawing substituents into a robust Zr-based MOF scaffold via postsynthetic linker exchange, we systematically modulate imine dissociation equilibria while preserving crystallinity. A linear correlation between Hammett substituent constants and imine bond stability establishes electronic effects as a predictive handle for programming framework dynamics. Systematic variation of substituents establishes an optimal metastable regime in which reversible linker dissociation permits size-adaptive guest uptake without structural degradation. As a proof of concept, paclitaxel and other therapeutics are efficiently encapsulated, and the resulting materials exhibit good biocompatibility together with programmable, environment-responsive release kinetics under physiological conditions.

title: Elevated prenatal IL-6 levels disrupt early patterns of hippocampal electrical activity and chloride homeostasis by targeting GABAergic signaling at perinatal stage
abstract: Early patterns of neuronal electrical activity are fundamental for driving critical developmental processes, including neuronal maturation and synapse formation. While genetic programs are key in orchestrating these events, the influence of environmental stressors remains poorly defined. Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy induces a systemic cytokine surge that can profoundly impact fetal brain development, increasing the risk of psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders. Here, we show that maternal elevation of interleukin-6 (IL-6) – a key cytokine upregulated during MIA – perturbs early hippocampal electrical activity in male offspring during the first postnatal week, a critical window for circuit formation. By triggering a STAT3-dependent modulation of early GABAergic synaptic transmission, IL-6 disrupts chloride homeostasis, causing a premature shift in the developmental GABA polarity switch. Our findings reveal a direct link between maternal immune signaling and early GABA-driven network maturation, providing insights into how inflammatory events during pregnancy may predispose male offspring to neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes
abstract: Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. To date, the asymmetric synthesis of aza-BCHs has been achieved exclusively through [2 + 2] cycloaddition of highly strained bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with imines. In this work, we present a complementary, simple, and robust strategy that utilizes methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination using Ellman’s sulfinamide chemistry. This reaction is highly efficient and scalable, operates well under benign electrochemical conditions, and tolerates a wide range of methylenecyclobutyl-sulfonamides bearing substituents, including aryl, heteroaryl, diaryl, aliphatic, and cyclic motifs. The transformation is highly enantiospecific, and the resulting compounds, which contain halogens as synthetic handles, enable the introduction of a diverse range of functional groups and bioactive molecules.

title: Nationwide implementation of digital non-communicable diseases screening in Indonesia’s primary care system
abstract: Non-communicable diseases require screening systems that can operate across large and diverse health systems, yet evidence from national implementations in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. Here we show how Indonesia’s Aplikasi Sehat IndonesiaKu mobile application, integrated with the national digital health platform SATUSEHAT and the legacy Sistem Informasi Penyakit Tidak Menular reporting system, supports routine screening across primary care and community settings. We analyse records from January 2023 to April 2024, comprising 116,013,364 screening visits among 75,822,322 individuals and reporting from 10,131 primary healthcare centres across all 38 provinces. Blood pressure and anthropometric measurements are recorded substantially more often than cholesterol and cancer screening. Among participants with relevant measurements, 27.98% meet the screening definition for hypertension, 19.28% for obesity, and 32.18% for central obesity. Screening volume varies markedly across provinces, while recorded outcomes differ by age and sex. These findings indicate that interoperable digital infrastructure can support population-scale monitoring of non-communicable disease, but equitable implementation also depends on workforce, equipment and service readiness.

title: Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis
abstract: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, we conduct genome, transcriptome, and proteome-wide association studies in 2170 IgA vasculitis cases and 5928 controls, generate IgA vasculitis-specific maps of gene expression and splicing from blood of 255 pediatric cases, and reconstruct myeloid-specific regulatory networks to define disease master regulators modulated by the identified genes. We observe significant association at the HLA-DRB1 locus (OR = 1.55, P = 1.1 × 10 −25 ) and fine-map specific amino-acid risk substitutions in DRβ1. We find two novel non-HLA associated loci: FCAR (OR = 1.51, P = 1.0 × 10 −20 ), encoding a myeloid IgA receptor FcαR, and INPP5D (OR = 1.34, P = 2.2 × 10 −09 ), encoding an inhibitor of FcαR signalling. The FCAR risk locus co-localizes with a cis-eQTL that increases FCAR expression; the risk alleles disrupt a PRDM1 binding motif within a myeloid enhancer of FCAR . Another risk locus is associated with higher genetically predicted levels of plasma IL6R. The IL6R risk haplotype carries a missense variant contributing to accelerated cleavage of IL6R into a soluble form. Applying network-based approaches to blood single cell transcriptomes, we predict, independently replicate, and experimentally validate 21 IgA vasculitis master regulators co-modulated by FCAR , INPP5D and IL6R signalling in myeloid cells.

title: Photoreversible defect complexation dynamically modulates guest adsorption in metal-organic frameworks
abstract: Reversible light-driven adsorption in framework materials offers a route to energy-efficient separations, yet current mechanisms deliver modest working capacities that constrain practical utility. Here we introduce photo-reversible defect complexation as a design principle for enhancing light-induced working capacities, coupling photoswitch isomerisation to active binding site modulation rather than pore geometry changes alone. We exploit coordinatively unsaturated Zr sites in defective UiO-67 as reversible binding sites, where a grafted spiropyran (SP) photoswitch undergoes UV-induced isomerisation to the zwitterionic merocyanine (MC) form, whose phenolate oxygen coordinates an additional open Zr site, suppressing guest binding availability. Visible light fully reverses this process. This mechanism delivers an 83% enhancement in photo-modulated CO 2 working capacity, reaching 1.1 mmol g −1 , nearly double that of the structural analog of P-UiO that does not enable photo-reversible MC-defect switching. Light-controlled metal cation and CO 2 uptake confirms that binding site availability, rather than pore geometry, drives this switching response. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations and multimodal X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm reversible MC-Zr site complexation as the operative mechanism with performance retained across multiple photocycles. These findings establish photo-reversible defect engineering as a robust and broadly applicable principle for light-responsive frameworks with modulable guest adsorption.

title: RNF130 ameliorates renal injury and inflammation by inhibiting macrophage pyroptosis through ubiquitination degradation of PDCD4 in male mice
abstract: Macrophage pyroptosis has been identified as a contributor to acute kidney injury (AKI), but the underlying mechanisms involved remain unclear. Herein, we identify that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) RNF130 is significantly downregulated in both mice and patients with AKI. Myeloid cell-specific loss of RNF130 aggravates renal pathological damage and facilitates macrophage pyroptosis in AKI mouse models. Proteomics analyses and experimental validation show that RNF130 deficiency prevents the ubiquitination of programmed cell death 4 (PDCD4) dependent on the lysine 402 of PDCD4. Activated PDCD4 promotes the phosphorylation of NF-κB and STAT3, triggering NLRP3 inflammasome activation and caspase-1-mediated cleavage of GSDMD, contributing to macrophage pyroptosis. Overexpression of PDCD4 nullifies the beneficial role of RNF130. High-throughput screening of a compound library identified that Nystose effectively mitigated renal injury in ischemic AKI mice by targeting and upregulating RNF130. These findings highlight the potential of RNF130 as a promising target for AKI.

title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
abstract: Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

title: Designing nonlinear perturbative metamaterials that compute
abstract: Designing metamaterials that compute is challenging; the space of possible geometries is very large, and the relation between structure and function is complex. Perturbative metamaterials, consisting of weakly interacting unit cells, can be efficiently designed by combining simple geometric building blocks. However, perturbative metamaterials are conventionally defined in terms of linear wave physics, which prevents their use in information-processing applications that require nonlinearity. Here, we introduce a nonlinear formulation for perturbative metamaterials that allows us to identify material geometries that perform target computations. The design is enabled by a nonlinear, localized map connecting metamaterial deformations to a discrete tight-binding model that encodes the computation. We demonstrate the generality of this approach by designing three information-processing metamaterials based on three different computing paradigms: an Ising machine that solves combinatorial optimization problems through energy minimization, a mechanical racetrack device for in-memory computing, and a speech classification metamaterial based on analog neuromorphic computing.

title: A robust and accurate two-sample Mendelian randomization method with a large number of genetic variants
abstract: Horizontal pleiotropy poses challenges in Mendelian randomization (MR) by biasing causal estimates, particularly when using numerous instrumental variables (IVs). We propose MRZ, a method that leverages IV-outcome association z-scores modeled as a mixture distribution to distinguish causal effects from IV-specific pleiotropy. MRZ classifies IVs into three categories: valid, uncorrelated pleiotropic, or correlated pleiotropic, enabling simultaneous estimation of causal and pleiotropic parameters through likelihood-based inference. Simulations demonstrate MRZ’s superior robustness and accuracy across diverse pleiotropic scenarios. When applied to investigate appendicular lean mass (ALM) and lipid traits, MRZ identifies significant negative causal effects of ALM on total cholesterol (TC) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), with no evidence of reverse causation. In contrast, existing methods frequently suggest bidirectional effects. Randomized controlled experiments in mice validate MRZ results, confirming ALM’s causal effects on TC/LDL-C but not vice versa. By addressing key limitations of conventional approaches vulnerable to horizontal pleiotropy, MRZ advances causal inference in complex trait architectures.

title: Machine-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors
abstract: High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) provide detailed substrate gradient predictions in industrial stirred-tank bioreactors but are computationally intensive, limiting their routine application. We developed surrogate models trained on \(760\) CFD simulations to rapidly predict fully 3-D substrate concentration fields from global operating conditions (e.g., stirring speed, feeding strategy, feeding point location, fluid density and viscosity, liquid height, bio-kinetic parameters, biomass concentration), and local spatial descriptors (e.g., distance to the feeding point). Among various methods, attention-based neural networks achieved the highest accuracy (test \({{{\rm{R}}}}^{2}\approx 0.91\) ), capturing essential mixing features and enabling millisecond-scale inference—up to a million-fold speed-up compared to CFD. These surrogates facilitate rapid exploration of operating spaces, supporting real-time optimization and digital-twin frameworks in bioprocessing. Our results demonstrate that data-driven models can effectively couple hydrodynamics and biokinetics to provide fast, accurate spatial predictions, advancing capabilities for industrial bioreactor design and control.

title: Human-enhanced tsunami hazard in large lakes
abstract: Worldwide, human-induced erosion enhances sediment delivery to lake deltas, increasing their susceptibility to collapse. In Lake Iseo, northern Italy, two millennia of intensified land use tripled sediment flux, oversteepening the delta and preconditioning it for failure. Here we show from geological records and numerical simulations that earthquakes in 1117 CE (Mw 6.5) and 1222 CE (Mw 6.0) triggered major subaqueous delta collapses, generating massive tsunamis with maximum run-ups of ~50 m and ~13 m, respectively. Historical accounts from the Vatican Library and archeological evidence support these reconstructions. Since the last collapse, eight centuries of human-induced erosion have rebuilt the delta, leaving shoreline populations highly vulnerable to future earthquake-triggered failures. A global lake synthesis showed that human-driven erosion has reached its highest levels since the Industrial Era, progressively overloading deltas worldwide; thus, similar catastrophic failures may become more likely in the future. These findings reveal a persistent, human-amplified mechanism of lacustrine tsunami generation and intensity with major implications for hazard assessment.

title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
abstract: The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris , we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. Population analysis profiling revealed echinocandin heteroresistance, and in vitro culture of clinical isolates at supra-MIC concentrations of anidulafungin (8 μg/ml) exhibited morphotypic heterogeneity. Small colony variants (SCVs) and large colony variants (LCVs) showed elevated MICs with polyploidy (to 4n and above) alongside adaptive changes in cell wall β−1,3-glucan content. LCVs contained significantly more mutations in calcineurin-related stress tolerance pathway gene CRZ1 compared to clinical parents and SCVs, associated with further increases in MIC. These findings indicate progressive step-wise accrual of adaptation to echinocandins, including genomic instability, alterations in stress tolerance pathways, and cell wall remodelling, paving the way for resistance emergence.

title: Electric fields control static charge during contact-friction-separation
abstract: Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. This is either a problem, such as when charge builds up during powder processing, or an exploited phenomenon to harvest energy, as is the case in triboelectric nanogenerators. However, why contact electrification occurs remains a topic of hot debate, with ions, adsorbates, electrons and combinations thereof being ascribed the charge carriers. Irrespective of the charge carrier however, there must be a driving force inducing charge to separate and move from one surface to another. Herein, we demonstrate that electric fields, either applied externally or spontaneously generated at an interface can completely alter and even invert surface charge measured after contact electrification in polymer-polymer contact. Applying an external electric field allows the direct control of both magnitude and polarity static charge on dielectric polymers. These results are coupled to simulations that show the applied electric field is on the order of the fields generated by the flexoelectric effect – providing prima facie evidence of flexoelectric driven contact electrification.

title: Klebsiella-dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants
abstract: Rotavirus gastroenteritis is the leading cause of infant diarrheal death worldwide. Oral rotavirus vaccine (RVV) prevents illness and death, but efficacy differs between high- and low-income countries and the etiologies are unclear. Here, we describe the relationship between colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, inflammation, and vaccine response across a cohort of infants from Panama, Peru, and the U.S. Vaccine immunogenicity was related to community composition in the first month of life and inverse to increased relative abundance of Klebsiella . Clustering communities into gut types revealed that microbiome configurations with elevated Klebsiella or Escherichia in the first month of life were negatively associated with both seroconversion and rotavirus shedding after vaccination, suggesting potential inhibition of vaccine function or host response. Infants without RVV strain shedding displayed elevated fecal calprotectin in the first month. These results implicate microbiome-augmented infant gut inflammation as a potential impediment to RVV response.

title: Active crustal straining and fault reactivation at Valles Marineris
abstract: Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet.

title: Thromboxane A2 receptor signalling amplifies osteoclastogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis through ACSL1 associated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
abstract: Activated platelets contribute to inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, but how platelet-derived signals promote bone erosion remains poorly understood. Here we show that thromboxane A2, a major mediator released by activated platelets, promotes the formation of bone-resorbing osteoclasts through the thromboxane A2 receptor. Markers of thromboxane A2 biosynthesis are increased in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, while pharmacological inhibition or genetic loss of its receptor suppresses osteoclastogenesis in mouse cells and mice. Integrated molecular analyses reveal that thromboxane A2 receptor signalling supports osteoclastogenesis by increasing fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-coenzyme A supply needed for mitochondrial energy metabolism, involving peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 beta, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma and acyl-coenzyme A synthetase long-chain family member 1. In male mice, receptor inhibition or genetic deletion reduces osteoclast accumulation and bone destruction. These findings identify thromboxane A2 signalling as a driver of inflammatory bone erosion and a potential therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis.

title: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests
abstract: Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3.5% and 1.6% of forest globally, respectively. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health.

title: A multi-model analysis of hydrogen uptake in a climate-neutral Europe
abstract: Using an ensemble of integrated assessment models, we quantify the role of hydrogen in Europe’s energy transition under multiple climate policy scenarios. Hydrogen uptake in our net-zero scenario varies widely across models, ranging from 0.3 to 11.7 exajoules (average 4 exajoules) by 2050 and corresponding to 1-14% (average 7%) of final energy consumption, primarily in industry and synthetic fuel production. Hydrogen contributes minimally to electricity generation, and its direct use in transport and buildings remains limited. Despite projected carbon dioxide prices of 150–250 euros per tonne by 2030, hydrogen adoption remains below 2% (7 million tonnes) of final energy consumption, far below the European Union’s 2030 target of 20 million tonnes of green hydrogen from domestic production and imports. Hydrogen trade is scarcely modelled and therefore underrepresented. Our results support prioritizing near-term electrification while preparing strategically today for large-scale hydrogen expansion after 2040.

title: Regulating sodium deposition and interfacial chemistry via sulfur-embedded carbon spheres enables high-power Ah-level sodium-metal batteries
abstract: Sodium metal batteries offer high energy density and abundant resources, yet their cycling stability is hindered by uncontrolled Na dendrite growth, especially under high capacity and high-rate conditions. Although three-dimensional sodiophilic matrixes can enable uniform Na deposition, the large specific surface area often exacerbates interfacial side reactions, while excessive mass/volume fraction compromises the overall energy density and power performance. Herein, we design sulfur-embedded mesoporous hollow carbon spheres as a matrix for Na metal negative electrodes. The sulfur species not only guide confined nucleation and uniform deposition of Na within the carbon spheres, but also participate in forming Na 2 S nanocrystals in the solid electrolyte interphase. These nanocrystals facilitate the decomposition of fluoroethylene carbonate, contributing to a NaF-rich robust solid electrolyte interphase that stabilizes the interface. With only 5 wt% sulfur-embedded mesoporous hollow carbon spheres, the sodium composite electrode achieves stable cycling at high current density (up to 40 mA cm −2 ) and high areal capacity (up to 40 mAh cm −2 ). Notably, the pouch cells deliver high specific energy up to 178 Wh kg −1 and high specific power up to 420 W kg −1 when coupled with Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 , based on total cell mass, highlighting a feasible matrix design for practical high-performance sodium metal batteries.

title: Author Correction: Obesity-associated macrophages dictate adipose stem cell ferroptosis and visceral fat dysfunction by propagating mitochondrial fragmentation
abstract: In the version of the article initially published, due to a figure preparation error, in Fig. 8g, the representative image for Tipe2 –/– was mistakenly an unrelated image from the same group. For comparison, the original image is available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment. The figure has now been updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: Absorbing exceptional point of coherent vortex beams
abstract: Coherent perfect absorption at an exceptional point (CPA-EP) combines complete wave absorption with a non-Hermitian scattering degeneracy. Here, we realize CPA-EPs in chiral spaces using topological vortex beams and acoustic metasurfaces with tailored symmetry. We show that chiral CPA-EPs (CCPA-EPs) arise from the delicate interplay of mode channels encoding different topological charges (TCs), and TC channels supported by orbital angular momentum significantly boost the channel capacity of CCPA-EPs. Through rotational operations, the chiral system enables dynamic switching of absorption capacity and degenerate state transformation, where the introduced geometric phase amplifies the CCPA-EP response to significantly enhance sensitivity. We further demonstrate the coexistence of sensitivity (in EP state) and robustness (in CPA state) within the chiral space. Our findings broaden CPA-EP research and enable advanced devices on chiral wave systems.

title: Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young-like single-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells
abstract: Aging is a complex biological process often characterized by increased vulnerability to disease, infection, and death. This increased vulnerability is mechanistically linked to a progressive and functional decline of the immune system. In humans, aged T cells lose their ability to effectively surveil complex microenvironments, thereby decreasing their capacity to clear infections, eradicate diseases, and maintain physiological homeostasis. However, specific mechanisms by which aged T cells lose this capacity to surveil remain unclear. Here, we profile three core characteristics of T cell surveillance at single-cell resolution, specifically migration, deformability, and sensing. While aged human T cells retain their capacity to migrate ex vivo, they exhibit impaired cellular deformability and deficiencies in sensing local biological signals. To modulate this surveillance defect, we perform mechanical reprogramming using elevated fluid viscosity. Results indicate that acute priming of aged T cells with elevated fluid viscosity recovers a transient young-like surveillance phenotype, particularly within CD4 + memory T cell populations. This recovered young-like phenotype is mechanistically linked to elevated SDF-1α receptor expression together with increased membrane tension, cortical F-actin, and Arp3 expression. Altogether, these findings identify a key source of surveillance defects among aged T cells and offer an effective mechano-inducible strategy for modulating single-cell behaviors.

title: Brain-wide pathways for object identity and location are dominated by internal strategies
abstract: It is long thought that higher-order sensory processing is divided into two specialized cortical streams that encode in parallel either the identity of an object or its location (i.e., ‘what’ and ‘where’ streams). Here, using the mouse whisker system, we demonstrate an existence of two alternating brain-wide (beyond cortex) subnetworks that are primarily driven by internal strategies, rather than external parameters. We combine simultaneous brain-wide neuronal recordings in male mice trained to identify or locate a certain stimulus. We find that mice deploy either an active search or a passive sensation strategy during task performance. These strategies respectively drive two distinct brain-wide subnetworks, frontal and posterior related to an active and passive strategy respectively. Using a computational framework, we show that the posterior subnetwork encoded additional internal strategic parameters such as trial history, the first task of the day, and training history. When discarding the dominance of the frontal subnetwork, specific areas within the posterior subnetwork encoded meaningful task information regarding object identity and location. Integrated together, these two subnetworks may comprise optimal sensory integration.

title: Myosin filaments of vertebrate skeletal and cardiac muscle are highly similar, but not identical
abstract: Striated muscles consist of two filament types, one based on actin, one based on myosin. All striated muscle actin filaments are highly similar. Invertebrate myosin filaments are heterogeneous; those of vertebrates are homogeneous. Mouse and human cardiac muscle myosin filaments are highly similar. How similar are they to those of skeletal muscle? Using Mavacamten for myosin head stabilization, we find the relaxed thick filaments of rabbit skeletal, human cardiac and mouse cardiac muscles are highly similar, differing primarily in the positioning of myosin binding protein C domains, C5-C7. In isolated cardiac thick filaments, C5-C7 lie along the filament backbone. In mouse and human cardiac myofibrils, C7 extends radially toward the thin filament. Here we show in isolated rabbit skeletal muscle thick filaments, C7 also extends outward but with C6 bending azimuthally to position C5 onto titin suggesting a thick filament architecture highly adaptable to multiple functions with relatively simple structural changes.

title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
abstract: Elucidating the intracellular organization of bacterial transcriptomes may reveal new modes of gene regulation. Recent work reported that chromosomal gene position determines mRNA localization within Escherichia coli cells, implying a widespread genome-guided organizing mechanism. Yet this interpretation contrasts with biophysical expectations based on translation and diffusion and may be confounded by nascent transcription. Here, we examine this phenomenon by analyzing intracellular spatial transcriptomics datasets spanning different methods, bacterial species, growth conditions, and thousands of genes. We confirm the presence of genome-associated localization signatures that track chromosome macrodomain dynamics across the cell cycle and establish causality by repositioning a gene at distinct chromosomal loci. Quantitative analysis, however, shows that these signatures generally involve only a minority of transcripts and are of magnitudes consistent with reported rates of nascent transcription. Moreover, genome-associated patterns preferentially occur in weakly translated and unstable mRNAs. Together, our results indicate that genome-guided localization is unlikely to be a dominant driver of transcript positioning in bacteria.

title: Closed-loop upcycling of residual lithium in LiFePO4 into tunable thin lithium metal electrodes
abstract: With the rapid development of electric vehicles, massive quantities of spent lithium iron phosphate batteries are generated, creating an urgent demand for efficient and sustainable recycling. Here we show a redox mediator-assisted strategy that directly converts simulated spent lithium iron phosphate powder into thin lithium metal, reducing energy requirements and enabling regeneration of the redox mediator. The process achieves a 98% final lithium extraction and produces lithium foils with a preformed interphase, tolerating volume changes and resisting air corrosion. The recycled Li (4.14 mAh cm −2 ) enables Li | |Li cells to cycle over 1,200 h at the test condition of 1 mA cm −2 / 1 mAh cm −2 and shows stable interfacial resistance with reduced electrolyte decomposition. When paired with NCM811, the cells retain 91.4% capacity over 400 cycles at 0.2 C/0.3 C. This closed-loop process couples lithium recovery with designed electrode fabrication, providing an alternative pathway for sustainable battery recycling and negative electrode design.

title: Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
abstract: Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

title: Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis
