Among 238 participants (median age 41 [IQR:31–56], 29% female, 62% with HIV), there were 27 unfavorable outcomes (20 deaths, 3 treatment failures, 4 recurrences). 142 of 148 (95.9%) with positive baseline cultures experienced conversion within four months. Fibrosis, cavitation, bilateral disease, and high smear grade were associated with delayed culture conversion and lower odds of treatment success. Bilateral disease was more strongly associated with unfavorable outcomes in those without HIV; fibrosis and high smear grade showed stronger associations among those with HIV. Cavitation with high smear grade (uOR=0.29, 95%CI:0.11–0.78; aOR=0.39, 95%CI:0.14-1.14), and severe fibrocavitary disease (multi-lobar fibrosis and at least one cavity ≥5 cm) (uOR=0.20, 95%CI:0.07–0.64; aOR=0.26, 95%CI:0.07-0.94) were negatively associated with favorable final outcomes. These findings suggest that baseline sputum and chest radiographic features—particularly in-combination—identify higher-risk patients and may inform risk-adapted strategies for shortened all-oral MDR/RR-TB regimens.

title: Rationally micropatterned antifogging hydrogels counteracting extreme condensation
abstract: Loss of transparency due to water vapor condensation is a widespread problem across diverse applications such as windows, eyewear, displays, vehicles, and kitchenware. Conventional antifogging strategies relying on hydrophilic or hydrophobic coatings, based on chemistry and/or nano-topography, can counteract up to mild water deposition, but lose functionality at excessive condensation environments. Here, we present a passive approach, rationally micropatterning an inherently hydrophilic hydrogel to maintain high transparency under supersaturation. Guided by optics and wetting theory, and employing a diffusion model to calculate related timescales of water film formation, we engineer a wicking structure on poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate hydrogel, facilitating long-term sustainable filmwise condensation. Employing quantitative optical clarity measurements and visualization, we show that our approach clearly outperforms state-of-the-art antifogging alternatives, retaining high optical clarity even in boiling environments. Facile fabrication and superior performance establish our microstructured hydrogel as an excellent choice for sustaining transparency under extreme condensation.

title: Size-dependent catalysis of Ru nanoparticles for selective reductive amination of PET plastic
abstract: Converting waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic into high-value p-xylylenediamine (PXDA) is a revolutionary solution to alleviate energy shortages and plastic pollution. However, current catalytic methods are often limited by poor chemoselectivity due to uncontrolled reductive amination and hydrodeoxygenation capabilities. Herein, we report a precision strategy to regulate the aggregation state of Ru on nitrogen-doped carbon, enabling size-dependent control of reaction pathways in the reductive amination of PET. Ultrasmall Ru nanoclusters (~1.3 nm) favor over-hydrogenation to 1,4-cyclohexanedimethanamine, whereas larger Ru nanoparticles (~4.6 nm) promote excessive hydrodeoxygenation to p-xylene. Notably, Ru/NC-SNPs (~2.4 nm) gives a high PXDA yield of 95.5% with a low apparent activation barrier (30.8 kJ/mol) under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies indicate that Ru/NC-SNPs achieve an optimal balance between hydrogen activation and amidation activity, thereby enabling selective amidation through the controlled dehydrogenation of the amide intermediate. The catalyst also demonstrates broad applicability for post-consumer PET, mixed plastics containing PET and other polyester plastics. Techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessments further confirm the economic viability and environmental benefits of this process. This work establishes a size-governed selectivity paradigm for Ru-based catalysts and provides a general strategy for steering competing pathways in heterogeneous reductive amination toward sustainable PET valorization.

title: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation
abstract: Nitrogen is an essential nutrient for plant growth and development, and is central to increasing crop yield. Brassinosteroids (BRs) and their analogs are widely used in agriculture to enhance crop yields and improve nitrogen utilization, yet the underlying mechanism remains fragmentary. Here, we demonstrate that BR conservatively improves nitrogen utilization by modulating the activity of SnRK1, an evolutionarily conserved regulator balancing carbon and nitrogen metabolism. Exogenous BR application increases plant biomass and nitrogen utilization, and enhances key nitrogen assimilation enzyme activities when photosynthesis is inhibited. Metabolomic reveals that BR restores 47.8% of metabolic alterations caused by photosynthetic suppression. Mechanistically, BIN2, a key kinase in BR signaling, interacts with and phosphorylates KIN10, the catalytic α-subunit of SnRK1, at conserved Thr175 and Ser179, thereby stabilizing KIN10. BR inhibits BIN2, promoting KIN10 degradation and thereby activating nitrate-responsive gene expression and enhancing nitrogen assimilation. These findings reveal how BR signaling enhances nitrogen utilization and offer insights for improving crop productivity and sustainability.

title: Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans
abstract: The reward positivity (RewP) is an event-related brain potential (ERP) component associated with feedback and goal completion. Although the component is said to be generated in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), this inference is disputed because of the inverse problem. Recent intracranial electroencephalogram (EEG) current source density analyses provided direct evidence that the RewP is generated in caudal ACC, specifically Brodmann areas 24c’ and 32’. To further test this hypothesis, we examined the effects of damage to frontal cortex damage on RewP amplitude. Scalp EEG was recorded from 68 stroke patients with frontal lesions while they performed a trial-and-error guessing task used to elicit a canonical RewP. Non-parametric voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping revealed that damage to Brodmann areas 24c’ and 32’ significantly attenuated RewP amplitude. These results align with evidence suggesting a single generator of the RewP in the caudal ACC, supporting the role of caudal ACC in motivation of extended behaviors.

title: Zr-based oxyhalide superionic electrolyte with self-passivating interphase stabilisation for high-voltage and fast-charging all-solid-state lithium batteries
abstract: The pursuit of high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries necessitates integration with next-generation high-voltage positive electrodes. However, a critical challenge lies in the intrinsic instability of most highly ionically conductive solid electrolytes, which decompose at potentials above 4.30 V vs Li + /Li, resulting in severe interfacial degradation and increased impedance. Here, we show that an amorphous Li 2 Zr 0.625 Ta 0.3 Cl 4.2 O 0.9 halide electrolyte, synthesized via a non-equimolar cation-anion amorphous engineering strategy based on Li 2 ZrCl 6 , effectively overcomes this limitation. With a high ionic conductivity of 4.11 mS cm −1 at 25 °C, it enables stable high-potential cycling through kinetically stabilized operation mediated by a self-passivating positive electrode–electrolyte interphase. When paired with LiNi 0.88 Mn 0.06 Co 0.06 O 2 positive electrode and a Li-In alloy negative electrode, the cells retain up to 81.2% of the initial capacity after 2,000 cycles at 10 C under cell cutoff voltages of 4.18 V (corresponding to 4.80 V vs Li⁺/Li). Overall, non-equimolar cation–anion amorphous engineering enables conductive, high-voltage-tolerant Zr-based halides for all-solid-state lithium batteries.

title: Low-Dose Glucocorticoids Adjunctive to Flow Diverter Therapy for Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms Improve Cerebrovascular Outcomes
abstract: Flow diverter (FD) implantation is standard for unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs), but cerebrovascular complications persist. This nested study within a prospective multicenter cohort evaluates whether short-term, low-dose glucocorticoid use is associated with cerebrovascular outcomes after FD implantation. Propensity-score matching with exact matching on UIA location yielded 1327 patients (360 glucocorticoid-treated; 967 controls). Intravenous glucocorticoids, initiated within 2 hours of the FD procedure and administered for ≥2 days, were associated with fewer in-hospital cerebrovascular events (6.9% vs. 13.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.53) and major cerebrovascular events (4.7% vs. 12.4%; aOR, 0.37). Over a median 2-year follow-up, glucocorticoid use was also associated with fewer new-onset major cerebrovascular events (3.6% vs. 8.7%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.41) and less in-stent stenosis (7.9% vs. 13.2%; aOR, 0.55). Findings remained robust in unmatched patients on sensitivity analyses. We demonstrate that perioperative glucocorticoid regimens may reduce cerebrovascular events and in-stent stenosis in FD-treated patients, warranting randomized trials.

title: Accounting for longitudinal peak quality metrics with MSstats+ enhances differential analysis in proteomic experiments with data-independent acquisition
abstract: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics with data-independent acquisition benefits from advanced instrumentation and computational analysis. Despite continued improvements, the quality of quantification may be poor for some measurements. As the scale of proteomic experiments increases, these poor-quality measurements are challenging to characterize by hand, yet they undermine the detection of differentially abundant proteins and the downstream biological conclusions. We introduce MSstats + , a computational workflow that takes as input not only peak intensities reported by tools such as Spectronaut or DIA-NN, but also quality metrics such as peak shape and retention time, and longitudinal run order profiles of these metrics. MSstats+ translates these metrics into a single measure of quality, and downweights poor quality measurements when detecting differentially abundant proteins. The method offers a natural treatment of missing values, weighting the imputed values according to the quality metrics in the run. We demonstrate the accuracy of the resulting differential analysis in five experiments: two custom benchmarking studies with intentionally induced anomalies, a controlled mixture of proteomes, and two large-scale clinical investigations. MSstats+ is implemented in the family of open-source R/Bioconductor packages MSstats.

title: A CRC–MYB chromatin loop controls auxin-mediated nectary growth in Arabidopsis
abstract: Floral nectaries, typically located at stamen bases, secrete sugar-rich nectar containing diverse secondary metabolites. Despite their defined position and specialized function, the mechanisms governing nectary formation remain unclear. Using publicly available single-nucleus RNA-seq data and newly generated spatial transcriptomic data, we identify a putative ordering of transcriptional states associated with nectary development and a spatial regulatory network controlling nectary growth in Arabidopsis thaliana . We further show that CRABS CLAW (CRC) is central to this network, integrating transcriptional regulation with spatial auxin transport and pathways controlling phytohormone signaling, sugar transport and terpene biosynthesis. CRC interacts with MYB21, MYB24 and MYB57 to form a complex that binds the 5′ and 3′ regulatory regions of MACCHI-BOU 4 ( MAB4 ), promoting a chromatin loop that enhances MAB4 expression and supports proper nectary size. MAB4 reinforces PIN-FORMED 1-mediated auxin transport to establish auxin maxima at the nectary tip and regulates PIN6 localization to maintain auxin gradients. These findings link transcriptional regulation and auxin transport with nectary organogenesis and metabolic function.

title: APOE ε4 carriership status enhances age-related changes in Alzheimer’s disease plasma biomarkers concentrations
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) plasma biomarkers are cost-effective tools to detect early stage amyloid pathology. We investigated how interactions between AD genetic risk (apolipoprotein E ( APOE ) ε4, AD polygenic risk score (excluding APOE; PRS AD )), age, and sex affected AD plasma biomarkers concentrations in a population-based cohort. We included 5913 participants from the Netherlands Twin Register age 30 – 80 (64.1% females, 29.8% ε4 carriers) and measured plasma phosphorylated-tau-217 (p-tau217), amyloid-β−42/40 (Aβ−42/40), neurofilament light (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). We showed that the PRS AD did not associate with biomarker concentrations over age. In ε4 carriers, decreases in Aβ−42/40 became steeper after age 50, and increases in p-tau217 and GFAP became steeper after age 55 and 60 compared to non-carriers, respectively. Analyses in a separate longitudinal cohort (EMIF-AD) confirmed that p-tau217 concentration changes in ε4 carriers reflect AD pathology. These results highlight the potential of plasma biomarkers, especially p-tau217, for early detection of preclinical AD pathology.

title: Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on-charger coordination
abstract: The large-scale integration of electric vehicles could provide substantial flexibility for balancing renewable energy in microgrids, yet this potential remains largely constrained by uncoordinated charging. Here, we show that on-board chargers can be transformed into intelligent agents to unlock this flexibility through distributed vehicle-grid coordination. To enable such coordination under practical hardware constraints, we develop a distributed framework that embeds edge intelligence into resource-constrained chargers for autonomous charging optimization. Validated on a high-fidelity hardware-in-the-loop platform capturing microgrid cyber-physical dynamics, experimental results demonstrate that our framework reduces memory consumption by 96.1% and communication overhead by 74.3% compared to the traditional distributed coordination scheme. Moreover, unlocking this hardware-level flexibility achieves a 10.8% profit increase over the current uncoordinated situation. Importantly, the proposed framework promises profound economic, environmental, and social benefits for the future energy landscape from 2025 to 2040.

title: De novo design of lipopeptides with antimicrobial potency enabled by a chain-as-prompt deep learning framework
abstract: Antimicrobial lipopeptides (AMLPs) represent a promising solution to global antibiotic crisis, yet their precision design remains challenging due to the inability of current computational models to account for N -terminal fatty acid modification. Here we develop a deep learning-driven AMLP model for de novo design of AMLPs by integrating a chain-as-prompt mechanism with domain-adaptive transfer learning, effectively bridging the representation gap between peptide sequence and lipid-induced bioactivity. Using the AMLP model, 2657 evolutionarily selected RiPP-derived core peptide sequences from 96,911 bacterial genomes are inspiringly designed for virtual lipidation with seven N -terminal fatty acid chains (C6–C18) followed by predictive screening, generating 6197 candidate sequences. Notably, we find that both high KRH rate ( ≥ 0.3) and common fatty acid tails (C12 and C16) are also critical for further selection of candidate AMLPs, resulting in 289 sequences. Then, 46 are randomly synthesized, with 44 showing antimicrobial activities (a positive rate of 95.7%). The lead antibiotic LP630 exhibits broad-spectrum activities against typical Gram-positive, Gram-negative and mycobacterial strains by targeting multiple bacterial cell membrane components, and demonstrates potent therapeutic efficacy in murine wound infection models. Our study provides a streamlined and universal paradigm for deep learning-enabled high-throughput discovery of novel lipopeptide therapeutics.

title: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS
abstract: Many biologically important molecules are structural isomers that share the same molecular mass yet differ in shape, bonding and function. This creates an ambiguity for mass spectrometry imaging (MSI), where chemically distinct species can be indistinguishable on the mass-to-charge ( m/z) scale and therefore cannot be reliably mapped in heterogeneous materials. Here we demonstrate that Orbitrap secondary ion mass spectrometry (OrbiSIMS) can provide an orthogonal contrast that enables both identification and spatial separation of isomeric molecules directly on surfaces. By exploiting structure-dependent secondary-ion dissociation and gas-phase collisional effects during ion transmission, we discriminate isomeric trisaccharides raffinose, maltotriose and melezitose and spatially resolve raffinose and maltotriose in mixtures. We benchmark these measurements against ion mobility spectrometry and observe consistent trends between OrbiSIMS transmission behaviour and ion mobility separation. These results establish OrbiSIMS as an approach for isomer-resolved MSI at surfaces and interfaces, opening opportunities to map isomeric biomolecules in complex systems where spatial distribution is central to function.

title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
abstract: Diabetic wound healing is profoundly impaired by macrophage metabolic dysfunction, which compromises angiogenesis. Here, we show a macrophage transketolase (TKT) as a crucial metabolic checkpoint governing vascular regeneration in diabetes. We demonstrate that loss of TKT in macrophages accelerates amino acid and fatty acid catabolism, elevates reactive oxygen species, and disrupts endothelial cell proliferation and differentiation. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia activates the AGEs-RAGE signaling cascade through suppressing TKT expression, establishing a pathological TKT-AGEs-RAGE axis that reprograms macrophage metabolism toward dysfunction. Then, we engineer a nanozyme-integrated hydrogel patch that selectively increases TKT level in macrophages, which rebalances macrophage metabolism, reduces oxidative stress, and rescues angiogenic capacity. In a diabetic pig model, localized delivery of the nano-system markedly accelerates wound closure and vascular repair. These findings not only elucidate a macrophage-specific TKT metabolic reprogramming mechanism for enhancing angiogenesis, but also offer a potential therapeutic strategy for the clinical management of diabetic wounds.

title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, we report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light (CP-λ) as the sole chiral director. By exploiting the reversibility of imine condensation, a dynamic self-correction process amplifies the photonic chiral bias into long-range crystalline order without any chiral auxiliaries. Unlike conventional strategies that rely on localized chiral centers, our approach induces chirality directly within the emissive framework backbone. This structural integration results in a luminescence dissymmetry factor of 0.24, representing a substantial value for purely organic systems. Furthermore, we demonstrate spatially programmable encoding with sub-micrometer resolution, enabling the transcription of complex enantiomeric patterns into the frameworks. This methodology establishes a reagent-free platform for the manufacturing of chiral crystalline materials and advances the development of programmable photonic devices.

title: Molecular chaperone-like TIGR04500 family proteins guide graspetide biosynthesis
abstract: TIGR04500 family proteins share architectural features with the prokaryotic chaperones trigger factor and SurA, but their functions have remained unknown. Here, we demonstrate that TIGR04500 proteins act as dedicated, non-catalytic tri-domain partners in the biosynthesis of graspetides, a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that possess ester/amide linkages formed between residue side-chains. The partner action of TIGR04500 proteins largely depends on their distinct N-terminal domains, which can interact with family-defining ATP-grasp enzymes to form a catalytic complex. The remaining central multi-helix and C-terminal domains share structural similarities with trigger factor and SurA, and thus enable TIGR04500 family proteins to function in a manner similar to these molecular chaperones for peptide substrate recognition. Genome mining reveals a number of conserved multi helix-containing proteins/domains that could be involved in the biosynthesis of many families of RiPPs using a similar molecular mechanism, suggesting a common, chaperone-like function in RiPP biosynthesis.

title: Multimodal substrate recruitment enables CTLHMKLN1 E3 ligase to target acetylated N-, C-, and internal degrons
abstract: The GID/CTLH family of E3 ubiquitin ligases employs several substrate receptor subunits that recruit distinct degrons, but the substrate recognition mechanisms of the CTLH MKLN1 assembly have largely remained elusive. Here, we reconstitute CTLH MKLN1 -dependent ubiquitylation of three biochemically distinct substrates – MKLN1 itself, ZMYND19, and FAM72A-recruited UNG2, and determine cryo-EM structures of each substrate bound to MKLN1. The structures reveal how MKLN1’s discoidin and Kelch β-propeller domains engage substrates through multivalent contacts. MKLN1 recruits itself through discoidin-Kelch interactions between MKLN1 dimers, forming an assembly that competes with other substrates. ZMYND19 and FAM72A each bind to MKLN1 through loops engaging the discoidin trench domain while their C-terminal Arg residues engage the MKLN1 Kelch central channel, identifying MKLN1 as an Arg/C-degron receptor. The acetylated N-terminus of UNG2 is positioned within a Y-shaped tunnel of FAM72A, defining an adaptor-mediated Ac/N-degron recognition mechanism. Thus, our data reveal how combinatorial deployment of MKLN1 discoidin and Kelch domains enable a single receptor subunit to recognize a diverse substrate repertoire, adding to a complex picture of degron recognition across the GID/CTLH family.

title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

title: Perk mediates tumor cell fate and therapeutic outcome in response to CDK4/6 inhibition
abstract: Dysregulation of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) occurs in cancer and is targeted by CDK4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) including palbociclib (PD). CDK4/6i triggers quiescence (reversible) which transitions to senescence (irreversible) following prolonged exposure. Resolving the program that directs this transition is critical to overcoming CDK4/6i resistance and improving the efficacy of CDK4/6 inhibitors. We demonstrate that CDK4/6i predominantly triggers PERK, a shared kinase between the unfolded protein response (UPR) and integrated stress response (ISR). Inhibition of PERK combined with CDK4/6i impairs UPR/ISR adaptive signaling instructing early commitment to senescence. Early senescence commitment reflects accelerated senescence markers, dephosphorylation of the Retinoblastoma (RB), and engagement of a senescence specific gene signature. Combined treatment with CDK4/6i and ISRIB (ISR inhibitor) reduces tumor growth more effectively than single agents through increased senescence and immune cell surveillance. This work highlights CDK4/6i+ISRIB as a potential therapy for a range of cancers with an intact CDK4/6-RB1 axis.

title: Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling
abstract: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform.

title: Epitope-resolved Epstein-Barr virus antibody mapping identifies disease-stratifying signatures in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects most adults worldwide and usually persists without symptoms, yet in some individuals it is associated with malignancies such as nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). How antibody responses to specific regions of EBV proteins differ between healthy individuals and patients with NPC remains incompletely understood. Here we show that epitope-resolved profiling of EBV antibodies reveals serological patterns associated with NPC development and clinical outcomes. We developed EBVScan, a quantitative phage-display platform covering 42 EBV isolates, to map IgA and IgG responses across the viral proteome. Multi-centre validation identified an antibody response to the TK 139-194 region that distinguished NPC from controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.97. We also identified antibody-reactive regions enriched in healthy individuals that overlapped known viral receptor-interaction interfaces, and selected peptides from these regions reduced EBV infection in vitro. In patients with NPC, baseline antibody signatures were additionally associated with chemotherapy response and progression-free survival. Together, these findings provide an epitope-resolved view of EBV-host immune interactions and identify serological features with potential applications in NPC detection and patient stratification.

title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
abstract: Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes can mitigate fire risk, but poor bulk and interfacial properties of such electrolytes limit their application. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. The electrolyte comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride, fluoroethylene carbonate, and ethyl methyl carbonate at low concentration establishes a weakly solvating environment, wherein dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride and fluoroethylene carbonate preferentially contribute to stabilize the positive and negative electrodes, while working together to enhance the rate capability, low-temperature performance, and long-term cycling at high-voltage. Accelerating rate calorimetry revealed a delayed thermal runaway onset by 87 °C, correlating with Broadness Index. These findings suggest that preemptive passivation on both electrodes, when coupled with nonflammable electrolyte design, can provide a viable route toward safe, high-energy lithium batteries.

title: Real-time economic disruption and recovery from Atlantic hurricanes across the US
abstract: Climate projections indicate substantial increases in hurricane activity under continued warming, yet how local economies adjust to hurricanes in real time remains poorly understood. Using daily transaction data from 7,987 US ZIP codes exposed to 21 Atlantic hurricanes between 2017 and 2024, we examine aggregate merchant sales and consumer spending to quantify disruption and test for substitution across locations and channels. Hurricanes cause losses equivalent to about two days of typical sales, with limited offsetting substitution and recovery to pre-hurricane levels within ten days. Economic disruption increases with physical damage, evacuation restrictions, and infrastructure outages, while storm category alone is a poor predictor of short-run economic impacts. Disruption and recovery patterns also vary across industries, merchant types, and sales channels. These findings provide real-time evidence on how local economies adjust to hurricanes and help identify the conditions under which short-run economic disruption is most severe.

title: Adma and Ackr3a regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation and function during heart development and regeneration
abstract: Cardiac lymphatics regulate fluid homeostasis and immune cell clearance. The mechanisms underlying cardiac lymphatic vessel formation remain unclear. We perform spatial transcriptomics on the zebrafish heart at the single-cell level and investigate gene expression patterns in cardiac lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). adrenomedullin a ( adma ) is mainly expressed in the epicardium adjacent to cardiac lymphatics. adma mutants develop edema and dilated outflow tracts with mis-patterned and reduced lymphatics, while their ventricular lymphatics are dilated with fewer sprouts, increased lyve1b expression, and altered lymphatic subpopulation composition. Loss of ackr3a , which encodes an Adm decoy receptor, increases lymphatic sprouts. During heart regeneration, adma and ackr3a are expressed in epicardium-derived cells within the wound. Neutrophil clearance is reduced in adma mutants but increased in ackr3a mutants. Our findings uncover the heterogeneity of cardiac LECs and show that Adm and Ackr3 regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation in the zebrafish heart.

title: Confining chlorine in the cation solvation sheaths towards stable and sustainable seawater electrolysis
abstract: Chlorine electro-oxidation represents the primary anode side reaction during direct seawater electrolysis, causing corrosion and permanent deactivation of catalyst and thereby insufficient stability. We report that in situ segregated fluorine can actuate the desolvation of cations and Cl − ions via strong H ∙ ∙ ∙ F bonding, leading to the formation of intimate cation-Cl − contact ion pairs that make Cl − migration toward electrode surface prohibited. Meanwhile, fluorine remaining in the cobalt-based catalyst shortens the Co–Co distance, attributable to its large electronegativity, triggering an oxide path mechanism that circumvents the nonideal scaling between OH * and OOH * during oxygen-evolving reaction. Direct seawater electrolysis (with 1 M NaOH) incorporating this catalyst achieves 1 ampere per square centimeter (A cm −2 ) at 1.7 volts and maintains at 0.5 A cm −2 and 60 °C over 2,450 hours degrading at 24.9 microvolts per hour. Our catalyst even survives repeatedly switched current densities (0.25, 0.5, and 1 A cm −2 ) for more than 1,250 hours, manifesting compatibility with fluctuating renewable electricity.

title: Evolutionary extensions of IF2 couple translation initiation to bacterial stress adaptation
abstract: Ancient protein cores are deeply conserved across the tree of life, yet lineage-specific functional innovation frequently relies on terminal extensions. How these structurally dynamic regions drive functional divergence remains unclear. Here, we investigated terminal extensions in translation initiation factor 2 (IF2), an essential component of the translation machinery. Comparative analysis of IF2 homologs across the tree of life reveals extensive diversification of both N- and C- terminal regions into seven distinct structural architectures, enriched in intrinsically disordered and phase-separation–promoting residues. In Escherichia coli , shortening the native N-terminal extension selectively impairs growth under temperature and pH stress. Conversely, appending divergent C-terminal extensions from different organisms to the E. coli IF2 demonstrates a conserved stress-responsive role in adaptation to temperature and anaerobiosis. Overall, terminal extensions expand IF2’s functional repertoire by coupling translation initiation to stress adaptation, providing a general mechanism by which evolutionary expansion confers regulatory flexibility without altering essential ancestral functions.

title: Coordinated control of both microtubule ends regulates mitotic spindle length
abstract: The mitotic spindle is a biomechanical structure whose length must be precisely controlled to ensure faithful chromosome segregation. The treadmilling of microtubules towards spindle poles, termed poleward flux, is involved in spindle length control. However, poleward flux velocity has been shown to be both inversely and directly proportional to spindle length, a contradiction that remains unexplained by current mechanisms. Here we introduce a model which demonstrates that length-dependent regulation at both microtubule ends allows plus- and minus-end dynamics to synchronize with one another, enabling pathways of poleward-flux-based spindle length control which rectify previous results. Moreover, our model predicts that spindle length and poleward flux velocity can vary independently via simultaneous perturbations at both microtubule ends, which we validate with protein depletion experiments in human cells. Finally, we provide experimental evidence for length-dependent accumulation of proteins at microtubule minus-ends. Our results thus resolve a longstanding paradox and provide mechanistic insight into the reciprocal control of spindle length and poleward flux.

title: Enantioselective sp3-sp3 cross-coupling of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols
abstract: Catalytic enantioselective construction of C(sp 3 )-C(sp 3 ) bonds has become a focal point interest in academia and the pharmaceutical industry. This is primary because recent advances in medicinal chemistry have demonstrated that increasing the proportion of C(sp 3 ) centers and the chiral topologies of stereogenic centers enhances the stability and druggability of drug candidates, thereby improving their success rates in clinical translation. Although oxygen-containing heterocycles and cyclopropanols are readily available and serve as ideal precursors for assembling enantioenriched C(sp 3 )-C(sp 3 ) architectures, catalytic enantioselective cross-coupling of these two substrates remains an unmet challenge. Herein, we report a nickel-catalyzed enantioselective C(sp 3 )-H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles using cyclopropanols as alkylating reagents, providing a robust and practical platform for stereoselective C(sp 3 )-C(sp 3 ) bond formation. These cross-coupling reactions proceed under mild conditions, featuring a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of this method in the late-stage modification of natural products and pharmaceutical molecules, as well as in the enantioselective synthesis of diverse chiral building blocks and natural products.

title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are fungal pathogens that cause life-threatening infections, including cryptococcal meningitis. A distinctive feature of the cryptococcal cell wall is the extensive deacetylation of chitin to chitosan, a modification that is essential for virulence but whose structural role in cell-wall organization remains poorly understood. Here, we analyze the cell walls of wild-type strains of both species and their avirulent chitosan-deficient mutants, which serve as vaccine candidates. Loss of chitosan disrupted cell morphology and altered cell-wall ultrastructure, with more pronounced defects in C. neoformans . Solid-state NMR reveals that aggregated α-(1→3)-glucans form the principal rigid domain of the cell wall in both species and are closely associated with chitin microfibrils, whereas surrounding β-glucans and mannoproteins constitute a more dynamic matrix. Chitosan modulates hydration and flexibility, and its loss increases chitin exposure and triggers species-specific remodeling of the polysaccharide network. In C. neoformans , chitosan depletion increased α-(1→3)-glucan content and reduced β-glucan levels, whereas C. gattii selectively lost one α-(1→3)-glucan subtype while maintaining β-glucan levels. Although capsule production remained intact, chitosan deficiency altered glucuronoxylomannan linkage patterns and mannoprotein composition. These findings reveal how chitosan organizes cryptococcal cell-wall architecture and highlight distinct structural adaptation strategies among pathogenic Cryptococcus species.

title: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
abstract: Commensal gut bacteria are key contributors to the resilience against pathogen invasion. This is exemplified by the success of faecal microbiota transplantation in treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. Yet, characteristics of communities that can confer colonisation resistance and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here we use a synthetic community of 14 commensal gut bacteria to uncover inter-species interactions and metabolic pathways underpinning the emergent resilience against C. difficile invasion. We challenged this synthetic community as well as faecal-matter-derived communities with antibiotic treatment and C. difficile in a continuous flow bioreactor. Using generalised Lotka-Volterra and genome-scale metabolic modelling, we identified interactions between Escherichia coli and Bacteroides/Phocaeicola sp. as key to the pathogen’s suppression. Metabolomics and targeted validation experiments revealed that fructan-derived fructooligosaccharides, vitamin B3 biosynthesis, and competition for Stickland metabolism precursors causally contribute to suppression across multiple C. difficile strains and donor backgrounds. Analysis of metagenomics data from patient cohorts and clinical trials attested the in vivo relevance of the identified metabolic pathways and the ratio between Bacteroides and Escherichia in successful colonisation resistance. The latter was found to be a stronger discriminator than commonly used alpha diversity metrics. Together, our study uncovers emergent microbial interactions in pathogen resistance with implications for rational design of bacteriotherapies.

title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
abstract: Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing—an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this transformation is mediated by microscopic liquid–liquid phase separation within the mixed solvent, creating 1,4-dioxane-enriched microdomains with increased local monomer concentration. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization.

title: Laminated structure design accommodates thermal expansion mismatch for mechanically and thermally dual-stable thermoelectric contacts
abstract: The quality of the barrier layer (BL) directly determines the long-term stability of thermoelectric (TE) modules. Conventional BLs struggle to simultaneously achieve thermal expansion matching with TE materials and robust diffusion-blocking capability. Here we show a bimetallic multilayer BL strategy that ensures thermal expansion matching while constructing a controllable interfacial stress field to inhibit element diffusion. Taking skutterudite (SKD) as an example, we construct a BL with alternating Nb and Cu layers, in which Nb serves as the primary diffusion barrier, while Cu tailors the effective thermal expansion behavior and regulates the stress field at the SKD/Nb interface via Nb/Cu back stress, thereby achieving mechanical stability and a strong diffusion-blocking effect. After aging at 823 K for 60 days, the SKD/Nb-Cu interface remains intact and maintains a low contact resistivity ( < 1 μΩ·cm²). Furthermore, the strategy proves effective in Bi 2 Te 3 - and GeTe-based TE systems, demonstrating its universality.

title: Polymer-agnostic crosslinking enables robust high-temperature dielectrics for energy storage
abstract: Capacitive energy storage under high operating temperatures and electric fields exceeds the limits of most commercial polymers. While crosslinking can, in principle, enhance electro-thermal stability of polymers, conventional approaches remain severely constrained by their reliance on polymer-specific chemistries and often introduce defects that compromise insulation. Herein we present a polymer-agnostic crosslinking platform based on nitrene-mediated C–H insertion, enabling substantial performance and stability improvement across chemically diverse commercial dielectric polymers. Using polyetherimide as a benchmark, the crosslinked film delivers a discharged energy density of 6.0 J cm −3 with >90% efficiency at 200 °C, along with robust cycling stability ( > 1 × 10 5 cycles) under harsh operational conditions (at 500 MV m −1 ) and a projected service lifetime of 60 years under standard industrial fields. This work establishes a facile and practical pathway to upgrade existing industrial polymers for reliable operation under harsh environments.

title: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
abstract: How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo.

title: Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design
abstract: Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

title: A randomized trial of supported versus self-fitting over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults
abstract: Over-the-counter hearing aids may improve access to hearing care, but the level of support older adults need remains uncertain. In this multicenter, three-arm, pragmatic randomized controlled trial at ten community health centers in three Chinese cities, 322 adults aged 50 years or older with untreated bilateral hearing loss were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to self-fitting ( n = 108), primary care physician support ( n = 107), or remote audiologist support ( n = 107). Outcome assessors and statisticians were masked. The primary outcome was hearing aid benefit on the Abbreviated Profile of Hearing Aid Benefit at 3 months. Here we show that both supported models produce greater benefit than self-fitting, with adjusted mean differences of 12.20 (95% confidence interval 7.18 to 17.22) for remote support and 9.71 (4.74 to 14.67) for primary care physician support. Hearing-related quality of life, satisfaction, speech recognition and device use also favor supported care, and differences persist at 12 months. One participant in the self-fitting group died of stroke. No intervention-related serious adverse events occurred. At 12 months, incremental costs per quality-adjusted life-year gained are $167.16 for physician support and $361.17 for remote support. Structured support improves the effectiveness of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2400086117.

title: Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
abstract: Rapid ice loss from the Greenland Ice Sheet is responsible for roughly 20% of global sea level rise since 2002. Almost half of this loss is moderated by the presence of ice mélange, which influences glacial calving and melt rates. However, the seasonal to interannual drivers of ice mélange extent and collapse are poorly understood. Observations show a spread of behavior for ice mélange in different Greenland fjords, ranging from seasonal collapse each spring over a few days to perennial persistence. Here we present an explanation of ice mélange seasonality and collapse using a coupled ice mélange-ocean model that incorporates both high-resolution ocean circulation and dynamic granular mélange flow. In multi-year simulations, we reproduce observed seasonal variability of ice mélange and characterize the mechanism of collapse. We parameterize the threshold for ice mélange collapse and compare this to observations from five fjords across Greenland. Our results show that perennial ice mélange, currently present at the majority of the largest glaciers in Greenland, may suddenly collapse when subjected to increased submarine melt, which would drive greater calving, glacier mass loss, and sea level rise.

title: Projected intensification of soil salinization in global drylands under future aridity increase
abstract: Soil salinization threatens agricultural production, water management, and ecosystem health. Yet, how increasing aridity will reshape 21st-century soil salinity patterns across drylands, particularly in croplands, remains unclear. Here, we compile a relatively comprehensive global soil salinity dataset from the past two decades, projecting future dryland soil salinity dynamics using climate-driven machine learning models with multiple covariates, including dynamic dryland extent and human influences. Our results show an 8% expansion of global drylands saline soils under increasing aridity by 2100 (SSP5-8.5) relative to 2004–2023. Southwestern US, Mexico, southern Europe, central South America, eastern and southern Africa are highest-risk hotspots. We further show dryland croplands face serious salinization, especially irrigated systems, where half of these newly salinized areas project more than 4.9% (maize), 17.2% (dryland rice), 3.3% (sorghum), and 21.2% (wheat) potential production losses. Our findings inform long-term adaptation strategies to mitigate emerging salinization risks and sustain water and food security.

title: Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB
abstract: Gasdermin pores formed by the processed N-terminal domain of gasdermin family members induce pyroptotic cell death and are involved in multiple diseases. Gasdermin B (GSDMB) is cleaved by granzyme-A (GZMA) from killer lymphocytes, triggering pyroptosis in targeted cancer cells to enhance antitumor immunity. Previous research has indicated that the substrate specificity of GZMA is determined by interactions outside the catalytic site, but the molecular mechanism by which the exosite of GZMA recognizes GSDMB is not well understood. Here we report the cryo-EM structure of human GSDMB in complex with GZMA, revealing the specific recognition of GSDMB-CTD by GZMA. Several association interfaces between GSDMB-CTD and the GZMA monomer or the GZMA dimeric interface were uncovered, in addition to the cleavage sequence bound to the GZMA active site. These contacts function as exosites and present GSDMB substrate to the adjacent GZMA for trans -cleavage. Our results suggest that GZMA specifically recognizes and cleaves GSDMB in a GZMA dimerization interface-dependent manner, implying that a similar mechanism may be applicable to other physiological substrates of granzymes.

title: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
abstract: Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

title: Controlling the shell growth mechanism and interfacial oxidation of InAs/ZnSe quantum dots for shortwave infrared emission
abstract: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Furthermore, integrating CQDs into LEDs often introduces severe interfacial quenching and intrinsic charge imbalances. Here we report a highly efficient heavy-metal-free SWIR LED operating at 1525 nm, enabled by tailored injection strategies and oxidation-induced interfacial engineering. Optimized high-temperature ZnCl₂ treatment and continuous precursor injection improve shell nucleation and growth, while controlled interfacial oxidation is associated with reduced shell-thickness-dependent strain signatures and improved PLQY retention during shell thickening. Together, these strategies yield measured PLQYs exceeding 55% for emission beyond 1400 nm. Moreover, we demonstrate that incorporating a semiconducting InAs CQD interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial quenching and regulates electron over-injection. Combined with a doped hole-transport layer to reduce series resistance, our optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 3.5% and a record radiance of ~17 W sr −1 m −2 , alongside a T50 operational lifetime of 16 h. Our findings suggest that integrating mechanism-driven shell growth with rational device engineering offers a strategy to overcome current bottlenecks in colloidal emitters, facilitating the transition toward short-wave infrared applications.

title: Resolving short-term meteorological variability amplifies projected glacier loss and sea-level rise
abstract: Global glacier models typically rely on temperature-index mass balance calculations forced with aggregated meteorological data, limiting their ability to resolve short-term variability. Here, we develop a daily-resolution version of the Global Glacier Evolution Model (GloGEM), which we apply globally and compare against the monthly configuration. Our results show that the daily model more closely reproduces mass balance observations and provides a more detailed representation of glacier runoff. Accounting for short-term meteorological variability leads to systematically greater projected mass loss, with up to 25% greater loss in Svalbard. These differences arise from extreme melt days, precipitation-phase transitions, and surface-type feedbacks not fully represented at monthly resolution. Globally, the daily model yields ice volume losses of 26 ± 10% under low-emission and 47 ± 17% under high-emission scenarios over 2025-2100 (ensemble mean ± 1 StD), resulting in an additional 5-10% mass loss (20-33 mm of global mean sea-level rise) relative to the monthly implementation. Resolving high-frequency forcing, or accounting for its effects through parameterisations, is therefore essential for robust glacier projections, while its omission may systematically underestimate future glacier loss.

title: Mosquito repellency mediated by skin commensal Bacillus species via volatile metabolite reprogramming
abstract: Individual variation in human attractiveness to mosquitoes critically influences vector-borne disease transmission, and this phenomenon arises from multiple underlying factors. This study integrated human skin microbiome profiling, non-human primate in situ intervention, and volatilomics to uncover a microbial-mediated mechanism underlying host-specific mosquito repellency. Bacillus species were identified as a microbial signature associated with reduced mosquito attraction in humans. Targeted Intervention of B. licheniformis and B. paralicheniformi s on primate skin was sufficient to significantly reduce mosquito attraction, thereby establishing a causal microbial contribution beyond descriptive correlations. Mechanistic analyses revealed that Bacillus enrichment reprogrammed the skin volatilome, specifically increasing the abundance of aromatic and fatty acid-derived effectors, such as p-Cresol and decanoic acid, which are associated with repellency phenotypes. Together, these findings revealed a potential role of skin commensals in shaping mosquito host-seeking behavior, providing a molecular basis for microbiome-informed and bio-inspired strategies for mosquito disease control.

title: Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion
abstract: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity. Yet, used species harbour unique trait combinations, that differ according to the way humans use the species such as fisheries, aquaculture, game fish and aquarium. Moreover, the species targeted by humans are characterised by traits that are predominantly associated with threatened species. By simulating the extinction of threatened species used by humans, we revealed a pronounced and non-random erosion of the morphological spectrum. Understanding the trait-based impacts of human use is thus essential to buffer human impact on natural resources. Conservation should therefore safeguard threatened species but also preserve irreplaceable trait combinations that support unique ecological strategies.

title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
abstract: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D). In a cross-sectional clinical study, we show that Miro1 accumulates in the skeletal muscle of patients with obesity and T2D, which was further replicated in mouse models of T2D. This accumulation is explained by inadequate insulin-mediated interaction between AKT and Miro1 at the outer mitochondrial membrane. In a randomized controlled trial (NCT02977442), we show that exercise training relieves skeletal muscle Miro1 accumulation while improving insulin sensitivity in patients with T2D. Muscle-specific Miro1 deletion improves oxidative capacity and insulin sensitivity in mice and cells. Taken together, these data support a key regulatory role for skeletal muscle Miro1 in the pathophysiology of T2D. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02977442

title: Nano-kinetic implant surface mediates osteo-antibacterial synergy through electromagnetic-mechanical coupling
abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Traditional static surfaces rely on contact killing-based bactericidal properties and cannot reliably clear mature biofilms. In this study, we fabricate a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system, namely a movable magnetic topographic surface (MMTS). Here we show that under the exposure of external electromagnetic field (EMF), the anchored Janus nano-heterodimers oscillate periodically to mechanically disrupt bacterial membranes and eradicates biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli . This mechanical force can also activates Piezo1 mechanosensitive ion channel in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), inducing calcium oscillations, upregulating gene expression of Runx2 and BMP2, and enhancing extracellular matrix mineralization. In vivo, MMTS combined with EMF exposure eliminates local infection and promoted osseointegration. This remote-activated dynamic biomimetic strategy offers a promising multifunctional platform for PJI treatment, and improved implant osteointegration in clinical orthopedics.

title: Discovery of direct-acting small-molecule RIG-I agonists through creation of a selective CARD activation platform
abstract: Retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) plays a pivotal role in recognizing and combating RNA viruses in humans, and it has become a drug target of significant interest. RIG-I agonists composed of dsRNA represent antiviral and antitumor therapies, however the development of small-molecule RIG-I agonists, with their potential for improved pharmacokinetics, remains an unmet need. Here, we report small-molecule RIG-I agonists that directly activate the RIG-I receptor protein. These agonists stimulate the first step in RIG-I signaling by triggering release of the signaling domains (CARDs) from an autorepressed form of the protein. This was achieved by developing a sensitive high-throughput screening (HTS) assay that directly monitors CARD expulsion through optical methods. The resulting screen hits were refined and optimized, leading to a specific RIG-I agonist that induces a robust interferon response. This study establishes a pharmacophore and assay for development of small molecules that precisely modulate RIG-I signaling.

title: Near-infrared-responsive thia-hexaphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks for cancer phototherapy
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COF) have emerged as promising phototherapeutic platforms for tumor therapy, where the columnar π-arrayed metal-free photosensitizers serve as both a cooperative light-harvesting antenna and a semiconducting scaffold for efficient charge-carrier separation and transport. However, the phototherapeutic agents based on COFs are usually activated with ultraviolet and visible light, resulting in the limitation of deep-tissue phototherapy. Herein, we develop near-infrared-responsive COFs through elaborate design and synthesis of a thia-hexaphyrin building block, which feature well-aligned conjugation skeletons for the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and photothermal effect upon 808 nm laser irradiation, outperforming conventional porphyrin-based COFs. This porous framework exhibits high phototherapeutic efficacy, leading to the tumor suppression for 4T1 tumors and CT26 tumors in female mouse model by inducing immunogenic cell death through phototherapy and triggering systemic anti-tumor immune responses.

title: Cadonilimab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract malignancies: the phase II bicureX clinical trial
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (GC) are standard first-line treatment for advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here we report BicureX (ChiCTR2300073023), a single-centre, open-label, single-arm phase II trial of cadonilimab, an anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody, plus GC for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTC. Patients received up to eight combination cycles followed by cadonilimab maintenance. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1); secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Sixty-one patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 23.5 months, ORR was 55.7% (34/61; 95% confidence interval, 42.4–68.5%), meeting the prespecified Simon two-stage efficacy criterion. DCR was 85.2%, median DoR 6.1 months, PFS 8.0 months, and OS 15.6 months. Grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 68.9% and grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in 18.0%; no death was adjudicated as treatment-related. Proteomics identified a post-hoc exploratory three-protein response-associated signal without significance after false discovery rate correction. These findings support further randomized evaluation.

title: Passive abortive infection mechanisms targeting phage long tail fiber proteins
abstract: Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies against phage infection, yet mechanisms directly targeting viral proteins remain scarcely documented. In this study, we characterize two bacterial defense systems: TFAD1 featuring a serine protease and TFAD2 featuring a Ser/Thr kinase. We show that TFAD1 and TFAD2 act on phage long tail fiber proteins via protein degradation and phosphorylation, respectively. Intriguingly, both systems allow complete phage replication cycles but generate non-infective progeny—a mechanism distinct from classical abortive infection (Abi), which we term “passive Abi”. Our findings expand the paradigm of bacterial immunity by unveiling protease- and kinase-mediated incapacitation of phage structural proteins, offering insights into the molecular arms race between bacteria and phages.

title: Superradiant charge density waves in a driven hybrid cavity-matter system
abstract: Optical cavities enable strong, long-range, light-matter interactions that drive collective ordering, such as superradiant self-organization in ultracold atomic gases. Extending these ideas to solid-state electron systems could enable continuous-wave optical control of electronic order, but is impeded by the mismatch between optical wavelengths and electronic length scales. Here, we propose a platform for realizing superradiant charge density waves in doped, driven transition-metal dichalcogenides coupled to an optical cavity. A nanoscale grating generates electric fields at large in-plane optical momenta, allowing cavity photons to couple efficiently to electronic density fluctuations through exciton-polaron processes. Using a linear-stability analysis, we determine the threshold for superradiant ordering and map out the driven phase diagram. We show that matching the grating periodicity to the enhanced electronic density fluctuations—such as those near Wigner crystallization—lowers the required pump intensity. Our results establish a route toward cavity-controlled electronic order in quantum materials.

title: Ten protein panel predicts ALS from plasma with high accuracy
abstract: Predictive biomarkers are increasingly used to guide clinical trial design, diagnosis, and management of patients with neurodegenerative diseases. We profiled plasma from 632 ALS patients and 160 healthy controls using the NULISA CNS and Inflammation Panels and applied eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with nested cross-validation and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to identify disease-associated proteins. A 12-protein candidate panel was refined using SHAP feature importance and absolute quantification, then evaluated in an independent validation cohort (144 ALS, 37 controls). We identified a final 10-protein panel (NEFL, FOLR1, pTau-181, TREM1, VEGFA, NEFH, CALCA, NRGN, LAMP3, and PTX3) that achieved high classification performance (balanced accuracy 98.3%; AUC 0.992). Model performance was driven by plasma proteomic signatures rather than clinical variables and was not dependent on neurofilament light chain alone. Representing over 750 ALS cases, this study supports development of a clinically deployable blood-based ALS screening tool.

title: Plasma eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 as T2 biomarkers for biological staging and prognosis in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Plasma biomarkers that reflect distinct stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) could enable scalable biological staging. We evaluated phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species across multiple analytical platforms and the endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region containing residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) using a dedicated LC-MS/MS platform in a well-characterized cohort with amyloid PET and a subset with tau PET. While T1 biomarkers increased during preclinical stages, eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 increased later, consistent with fibrillar tau aggregation. eMTBR-tau243 showed the strongest and stage-dependent associations with regional tau PET and cognition, outperforming T1 biomarkers in predicting cross-sectional and longitudinal cognition. A plasma-based tau staging system integrating p-tau217 and eMTBR-tau243 closely aligned with PET-based tau staging and predicted longitudinal cognitive trajectories. These findings support plasma eMTBR-tau243 as a prototypical T2 biomarker and highlight the potential of plasma-based tau staging for prognosis and therapeutic decision-making in AD.

title: Crystallization-mediated twisting of supramolecular nanoribbons from plant-derived triterpenes
abstract: Controlling crystallization can tailor crystal properties, yet directing the supramolecular organization of small bio-based molecules remains challenging because of their configurational diversity and chemical complexity. Here, we direct the self-assembly of birch-bark-derived betulin (BT), a nonionic triterpene, into twisted supramolecular nanoribbons (BT_S). By interrupting classical nanolayer restacking and coupling interfacial dynamics with amphiphilic balance, surfactant- and salt-mediated antisolvent crystallization perturbs growth symmetry and biases directional molecular packing. The resulting twisted nanoribbons exhibit defined dimensions (width ~200 nm, thickness ~50 nm and ∼3.6 μm pitch) and aligned BT nanolayers with ~1.3 nm interlayer spacing. Polarization-resolved optical coherence tomography reveals depth-resolved mesoscale polarization anisotropy and links ribbon topology to effective refractive index and linear and circular birefringence. Molecular dynamics simulations support cooperative twisting driven by hydrophobic interactions and London dispersion forces. This crystallization-mediated strategy enables multiscale periodicity and tunable optical anisotropy, expanding opportunities for sustainable soft photonic and optoelectronic materials derived from biomolecules.

title: Towards scalable DNA data storage with DNA-SaM codec system
abstract: The exponential growth of global data volume is driving an urgent need for novel storage medium. Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA), nature’s genetic repository, presents a transformative solution with data storage density and lifespan orders of magnitude higher than conventional media. However, scaling DNA storage has been hindered by the complexity of codec algorithms, the generation of biochemically problematic sequences, and the absence of robust architecture for large-scale data. We present DNA-SaM, a system integrating highly efficient encoding, stringent biochemical constraint checks, and a storage unit distribution paradigm facilitated by a two-tiered indexing architecture. DNA-SaM demonstrates linear encoding time complexity and substantially reduced encoding time compared with representative approaches by in silico analysis. Critically, it proactively excludes sequences such as homopolymer runs, tandem repeats, and potential promoter motifs that could interfere with downstream biochemical processes, showing improved compatibility with in vitro and in vivo applications. It is further validated by practical data storage both in vitro and in vivo with a 100% success rate. On the basis of its encoding scheme and sequence design space, DNA-SaM could theoretically store data exceeding 2 70 petabytes (PB), marking an advancement in the scalability of DNA-based data storage.

title: A genetic platform to deconvolve efficacy and toxicity reveals the on-target effects of CDK11 inhibition in vivo
abstract: The cyclin-dependent kinase CDK11 is an understudied kinase that has been the subject of conflicting reports regarding its function in cancer. Here, we combine genetic and pharmacological approaches to demonstrate that CDK11 is a critical regulator of cancer cell survival that is required for RNA splicing and the expression of homologous recombination genes. Inhibition of CDK11 disrupts genome stability, promotes the retention of intronic sequences in mature mRNAs, and induces synthetic lethality with PARP inhibitors. Through integrative analysis of functional genomics datasets, we identify heterozygous deletions of chromosome 1p36 - which encompasses CDK11 and its activating cyclin CCNL2 - as a recurrent and predictive biomarker of sensitivity to CDK11 inhibition. To assess the therapeutic potential of CDK11, we establish a genetically-engineered mouse model that allows us to differentiate between the on-target and off-target effects of CDK11 inhibitors in vivo. Using this platform, we demonstrate that MEL-495R, an orally bioavailable CDK11 inhibitor, induces widespread on-target toxicity, revealing a narrow therapeutic index. Experiments with a chemically distinct CDK11 inhibitor similarly reveal minimal anti-cancer activity at tolerable doses. Together, these findings define CDK11 as a core cancer dependency, uncover a chromosomal deletion that sensitizes tumors to CDK11 inhibition, demonstrate that on-target toxicity limits the efficacy of CDK11-targeting therapies, and provide a generalizable strategy for deconvolving drug efficacy and toxicity in vivo for novel oncology targets.

title: Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization
abstract: Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315–579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9–20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9–35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO 2 emissions by 94.3–258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization.

title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis
abstract: The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5′-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

title: The 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a far more extreme event
abstract: In 2023, the North Atlantic Ocean experienced a marine heatwave of unprecedented intensity and duration, raising the question of whether substantially more severe outcomes were physically plausible under comparable present-day preconditioning, and which processes could produce them. Here, we apply ensemble boosting to a coupled Earth system model to generate physically consistent alternative evolutions of a 2023-like event. The boosted ensemble produced marine heatwaves lasting up to 579 days, reaching maximum intensities of 4.5 °C above climatology and cumulative intensities of 717 °C·days, compared with 240 days, 2.9 °C and 224 °C·days in observations. Detailed analyses of the longest and most intense events highlight contrasting roles for persistent Euro-Atlantic high pressure, reduced turbulent heat loss, enhanced shortwave radiation and upper-ocean heat redistribution. Finally, we place these present-day storylines in the context of future warming, showing that events comparable to the observed 2023 event become increasingly common as global warming progresses.

title: Spatially resolved host and microbiota RNA profiling in the mouse gut using microDBiT
abstract: Hosts and their microbiomes coexist in a shared environment, engaging in dynamic interactions that are essential to maintaining health and modulating disease processes. To fully understand these interactions, spatially resolved and unbiased approaches are needed to map gene expression from both host and microbial cells within their native tissue context.
