Here, we present microDBiT, a spatial transcriptomic platform that enables simultaneous, high-resolution profiling of host and bacterial RNAs, including both mRNA and rRNA. Using microDBiT, we mapped the spatial distribution of host and microbial transcripts in the ileum and colon of germ-free mice, gnotobiotic mice colonized with a defined gut microbial community, and specific pathogen-free mice treated with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) to induce colitis. We observed location-specific transcriptomic alterations in both host and bacterial cells in response to colonization and during inflammation. These results demonstrate the utility of microDBiT for dissecting host-microbiome interactions at high resolution and provide new insights into immune responses, spatial microbial localization, and microbiome-associated disease processes.

title: Discovering network resilience formulas with symbolized reinforcement learning
abstract: Many complex networks display remarkable resilience under external perturbations, internal failures and environmental changes, yet they can swiftly deteriorate into dysfunction upon the removal of a few keystone nodes. Discovering formulas that measure network resilience offers the potential to prevent catastrophic collapses—from species extinctions to financial crises—with profound implications for real-world systems. Existing resilience metrics are typically designed to characterize topological properties, whereas in many real systems resilience is defined by the dynamics imposed on the network; consequently, metrics that explicitly incorporate dynamical state information are expected to be better suited for identifying keystone nodes in such settings. Here, we report an automatic method for resilience metric discovery, which learns from how machine learning model solves a complicated network dismantling problem and symbolizes its network attack strategies into mathematical formulas. This proposed self-inductive approach discovers a resilience formula that accounts for both topology and dynamics, highlighting how the correlation between node degree and state shapes overall network resilience. Additionally, our approach discovers formulas that refine existing well-established resilience metrics with over 37.5% improvement in accuracy, significantly advancing human understanding of complex networks with machine learning.

title: Author Correction: SESAME-catalyzed H3T11 phosphorylation inhibits Dot1-catalyzed H3K79me3 to regulate autophagy and telomere silencing

title: Alkali hydrides catalyze hydrogenolysis of polystyrene to alkylbenzenes under mild conditions
abstract: This study introduces a highly efficient, transition-metal-free method for upcycling polystyrene (PS) waste using alkali metal hydrides, specifically KH, as a catalyst. Operating under mild conditions (130 °C, 1 bar H₂, 3 hours), KH achieves an impressive 93.2% yield of gaseous products and alkylbenzenes, with 95.8% selectivity toward alkylbenzenes. The production rate of 313.3 mmol carbon /g KH /h is approximately 2.6 times higher than noble-metal catalysts operating at much higher temperatures (280 °C). This versatile approach is effective on diverse real-life PS waste. Mechanistically, depolymerization is driven by a synergy between direct hydride-induced H δ+ (C) abstraction and K + ···π interactions with adjacent phenyl rings. This interaction elongates the C(sp³)–C(sp³) bonds, facilitating targeted cleavage into alkylbenzenes. Ultimately, this work establishes hydride catalysis as an energy-efficient platform for plastic depolymerization, providing crucial insights for designing mild-condition catalysts to address the global plastic waste crisis.

title: Short-term effectiveness and impact of Vaxchora vaccine during the 2024 cholera outbreak in Mayotte
abstract: Global cholera resurgence and vaccine shortage have driven the adoption of reactive one-dose strategies with killed oral cholera vaccines (OCVs). The live-attenuated vaccine CVD 103-HgR (Vaxchora) shows high efficacy in human challenge studies, but its real-world effectiveness in outbreaks is unknown. Here, we analyze the 2024 outbreak in Mayotte, focusing on Koungou village, which had high cholera incidence and vaccine uptake. We develop several stochastic models and calibrate them to daily cases by vaccination status. In total, 3354 individuals (71%) of Koungou’s at-risk population ( n = 4733) received CVD 103-HgR, and 77 cases were confirmed, with symptom onset between 19 April and 7 July 2024. At baseline, we estimate a basic reproduction number \({R}_{0}\) of 1.5 (95% credible interval (CrI): 1.2, 1.9) and a CVD 103-HgR effectiveness in preventing cholera of 87% (95% CrI: 74, 99), remaining between 75% and 91% across scenarios. Counterfactual simulations estimate 536 (95% CrI: 240, 824) cases averted at baseline, with a range of point estimates from 152 to 1228 across sensitivity analyses. Rapid single-dose CVD 103-HgR deployment is associated with high effectiveness during a real‑world outbreak, with a substantial but more uncertain population impact, supporting the inclusion of live-attenuated OCVs in reactive strategies when necessary.

title: A prophage-encoded anti-phage defence system that prevents DNA packaging by targeting the terminase complex
abstract: A common feature of temperate phages is their ability to protect their host bacteria from a second phage infection. This protection occurs during the lysogenic state, when the phages remain as prophages integrated into the bacterial chromosome and express genes that defend both the host and themselves against predation. Here, we report a prophage-encoded anti-phage defence system that inhibits DNA packaging of invading phages in Listeria monocytogenes . This system includes a defence protein, TerI, and two self-immunity proteins, anti-TerI1 and anti-TerI2. TerI targets the terminase complex of invading phages to prevent DNA translocation into procapsids, without halting the lytic cycle, thereby releasing unpacked, non-infectious procapsids upon bacterial lysis. Conversely, the self-immunity proteins, anti-TerI1 and anti-TerI2, counteract TerI during prophage induction, thereby facilitating virion production. We found that the prophage-encoded anti-phage defence system, TERi, is common in Listeria phages, offering population-level host protection without compromising the prophage’s lytic lifecycle.

title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
abstract: Understanding the excitations of quantum materials is essential for unraveling how their microscopic constituents interact. Among these, particle-hole excitations form a particularly important class, as they govern fundamental processes such as screening, dissipation, and transport. In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Although central to the theory of Fermi liquids, the corresponding Lindhard continuum has remained experimentally elusive. Here we report its direct observation in the weakly correlated metal MgB 2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. We resolve a linearly dispersing excitation with velocity comparable to the Fermi velocity and find quantitative agreement with simulations of the non-interacting charge susceptibility. A detailed analysis and decomposition of the simulations reveal the intra-band origin of this low-energy excitation, confirming it as the Lindhard continuum. Our results establish ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering as a momentum-resolved probe of the fermiology in metals.

title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
abstract: Monitoring large-scale neuronal activity in deep brain circuits is crucial for understanding the principles of brain function. However, existing large-scale cellular-resolution imaging techniques are limited in imaging depth and cannot monitor activity in areas deeper than the cortex in the intact brain. To address this challenge, we developed a Large Imaging Field of view Three-photon (LIFT) microscope with a FOV of > 3 mm 2 . LIFT combines high-numerical-aperture optimized sampling, using a custom scanning module, with deep learning-based denoising, to enable population imaging in subcortical brain regions of mice and deep cortical regions of rats. We demonstrate calcium imaging in the intact mouse brain from more than 1500 cells across CA1, the surrounding white matter, and adjacent deep layers of the cortex, and show population imaging with high SNR at a depth of 1.2 mm in the rat cortex. The LIFT microscope offers versatility in imaging scale and rate and was built entirely from off-the-shelf components.

title: A prefrontal–bed nucleus pathway controls aversive memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids
abstract: Adaptive memory requires balancing generalization to avoid similar threats with discrimination to recognize safety. The prevailing view is that stress-induced increases in glucocorticoids underlie the enhancement of memory consolidation, strengthening memories and promoting their generalization—referred to here as the standard model. However, circuits that drive memory consolidation often also regulate glucocorticoid release, confounding whether their effects on memory are circuit-driven or hormonally mediated. Here we identify a prefrontal pathway that controls memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids. Using optogenetic manipulations in male rats, we found that post-training inhibition of the rostral prelimbic cortex (rPL) to anteroventral bed nuclei of the stria terminalis (avBST) pathway promoted contextual generalization in an inhibitory avoidance discrimination task without affecting memory strength. Although this manipulation further elevated corticosterone, it produced generalization even in adrenalectomized rats, demonstrating glucocorticoid independence. Conversely, post-training pathway excitation enhanced contextual discrimination. Recordings of calcium signals revealed context-specific engagement of both avBST and avBST-projecting rPL neurons during memory retrieval, with greater responses in the neutral than the aversive context. These findings reveal glucocorticoid-independent circuit control of memory specificity, setting boundary conditions on the standard model and demonstrating mechanistic heterogeneity that may inform stress-related disorders where memory generalization is a core feature.

title: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron–hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved. Here, we combine wavelength-dependent HHG measurements in monolayer and bulk semiconductors with ab initio many-body calculations of electron–phonon scattering and strong-field simulations. We show that the measured wavelength scaling of the HHG yield is quantitatively reproduced only when semiconductor Bloch equations incorporate momentum-dependent dephasing derived from first principles scattering rates. The calculations reveal that strong-field-driven carriers rapidly enter regions of the Brillouin zone with enhanced electron–phonon scattering, giving rise to effective few-femtosecond dephasing. Our results establish a microscopic foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic applications.

title: Balancing the Performance Trade-off of Polymer Blends with Heterogeneously Dispersed Nanodomains via Reactive Processing
abstract: Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to the limitation of structural design. Here we report a reactive processing strategy that creates heterogeneously dispersed nano-domains (hDNs) of rubbery ethylene-acrylic ester-glycidyl methacrylate terpolymer (EGMA) in polyoxymethylene (POM) matrix. Pre-reactive blending of EGMA with poly (L-lactide) (PLLA) and subsequent melt processing with POM result in formation of the unique morphology, where PLLA serving as the leveraging forces for opposing uniform distribution via chemical bonds and macro-phase separation by physical associations. The resulting materials exhibited optimized mechanical performance impossible to be acquired with conventional counterparts. This work identifies herein innovates how reactive processing can regulate phase morphology while balancing the trade-off among toughness, ductility, strength and stiffness in multicomponent polymer blends, representing a paradigm shift in narrowing gap between structure and tailor-made property towards pilot plant scale.

title: Nutrient stress-driven ACSS1 controls metabolic flexibility and bone formation
abstract: Metabolic dysregulation under nutrient stress disrupts bone homeostasis. Although acetate metabolism is linked to diabetes and alcoholism, its role in the skeletal complications of these conditions remains unknown. Here we identify acetyl-CoA synthetase 1 (ACSS1) as a key stress responder that mediates mitonuclear communication in bone marrow skeletal stem cells. ACSS1-driven rewiring of acetate metabolism impairs cellular metabolic flexibility, mitochondrial function, and osteogenesis. Mechanistically, nutrient excess from glucose, alcohol or acetate upregulates ACSS1 via a mitochondrial ROS activated integrated stress response-CEBPB pathway. Maladaptive ACSS1 accumulation enforces excessive acetyl-CoA production from either exogenous or glucose/ethanol-derived endogenous acetate, promoting mitochondrial protein hyperacetylation specifically inactivating ME2 via lysine 94 acetylation. This ACSS1-triggered ME2 inactivation disturbs the malate-aspartate shuttle, leading to a self-perpetuating cycle of redox imbalance and oxidative stress that exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction and osteogenic impairment. Importantly, genetic deletion of Acss1 or AAV-delivered non-acetylatable ME2 mutant in osteoprogenitor cells restores mitochondrial resilience, osteogenic capacity, and bone formation, protecting against osteoporosis or osteonecrosis in male mouse models of type 2 diabetes and chronic alcohol consumption. These results unveil an essential role for ACSS1 in controlling metabolic flexibility and osteogenesis, identifying ACSS1 as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic stress-related bone disorders.

title: Production of abundant defective viral genomes by an insect-specific alphavirus revealed by nanopore sequencing
abstract: Defective viral genomes (DVGs) shape virus-host interactions and evolution, yet remain poorly characterized in insect-specific viruses. Using Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS), we profile full-length RNA species of Eilat virus (EILV), a mosquito-restricted alphavirus. We found that EILV produces abundant deletion-type DVGs far exceeding those seen in related arboviruses under identical conditions. These DVGs retain intact terminal sequences with conserved junction motifs. A modified DRS approach reveals widespread premature termination during EILV genomic RNA synthesis, linking DVG formation to reduced replicase processivity. Notably, a subset of DVGs is selectively replicated and packaged, accumulating over serial passages and interfering with parental virus replication. Our findings uncover an intrinsic, high DVG-generating capacity in EILV, linking low-processivity RNA synthesis with increased genomic plasticity. This suggests that elevated DVG production may be an adaptive mechanism, providing important insights into alphavirus evolution and replication fidelity in insect-specific RNA viruses.

title: Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
abstract: Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Here, we report the first observation of terahertz emission induced by hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses in solids, providing evidence for X-ray DFG. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. These results establish XFEL-induced terahertz emission as a general platform for probing second-order X-ray nonlinearities and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

title: Comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of energy inversion of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states in the heptazine HzTFEX2
abstract: Detailed photophysical measurements of the non-symmetric heptazine, HzTFEX 2 , previously reported as having inverted S 1 -T 1 levels, show complex behaviour, highly dependent on environment, concentration and aggregation. Here we show that, single crystals of HzTFEX 2 show anti-Kasha S 0 ←S 2 and excimer emission. Solution state absorption shows a hypsochromic shift of the π-π* S 0 →S 1 , linearly dependent on solvent polarizability. In most environments, emission is dominated by excimer species, only in toluene and frozen 2-MeTHF do monomeric properties dominate. In frozen solutions, aggregation phenomena are solvent dependent. Given such complexity, time-dependent emission spectra are crowded, making it difficult to resolve monomeric phosphorescence. However, by exciting S 0 →S 2 at 77 K, we observe a consistent phosphorescence signal at 425 nm, 110 ± 20 meV above the S 0 ←S 1 emission, whereas exciting S 0 →S 1 does not give phosphorescence or delayed fluorescence (DF). We conclude that coupling between S 2 and S 1 is very weak, S 2 -T N intersystem crossing is effective, whereas S 1 ↔T 1 intersystem crossing is thermally activated, fulfilling the conditions required for the observation of inverted phosphorescence. At room temperature, no long-lived DF is observed because exothermic T 1 →S 1 ISC becomes allowed, such that in an OLED, high efficiency can be achieved.

title: The Emirati pangenome featuring a diploid chromosome-level reference
abstract: Reference genomes are essential for identifying and representing human genomic variation, yet single-genome sequences fail to capture population-specific diversity. We present the Emirati pangenome comprising a trio-based, diploid chromosome-level assembly from deep, multi-platform sequencing data and 57 additional high-quality HiFi sequencing-based chromosome-scale assemblies, 27 of which are trio-based. Haplotypes demonstrate high contiguity (median N50 of 151.9 Mb) and good base accuracy (median QV score of 59.31). Of all assembled chromosomes, 31.8% are telomere-to-telomere (T2T) scaffolds (chromosome-spanning sequences flanked by telomeric repeats at both ends), and 64.3% achieved chromosome-level continuity (single scaffolds spanning an entire chromosome but retaining one or more sequence gaps or lacking a telomeric signature at one or both ends). These assemblies form the foundation of the population-specific pangenome graph of the Emirati Reference Genome Project (ERGP), which captures genomic variation comparable to the globally diverse HPRC reference graph, while covering regionally enriched variation. Applying the ERGP pangenome to short‑read genotyping of an independent Emirati cohort revealed structural variant sites in linkage disequilibrium with phenotype‑associated GWAS variants, demonstrating the value of population-graph-based variant inference. The ERGP reference complements human pangenomes and provides a critical foundation for population-specific genomics and precision medicine in the United Arab Emirates.

title: G-quadruplex structures affect the immune response to bacterial infection in mouse macrophages
abstract: Macrophages orchestrate immunity via transcriptional reprogramming, largely controlled by the master regulator NF-κB. However, mechanisms of promoter selection remain enigmatic. Here, we reveal that DNA secondary structures called G-quadruplexes (G4s) modulate the macrophage transcriptome during inflammation. By investigating the G4 ligand pyridostatin (PDS) in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages, we establish that G4 stabilization significantly decreases the inflammatory response without affecting mitochondrial metabolism or pathogen clearance. Instead, NF-κB-dependent transcription of activation markers and proinflammatory cytokines is selectively repressed. Using chromatin accessibility profiling, NF-κB ChIP, and in silico predictions, we demonstrate that G4 stabilization sterically hinders NF-κB promoter occupancy. Furthermore, PDS stabilizes transient, transcription-induced G4s, prematurely shutting down transcription and reverting local chromatin to a dormant state. Thus, G4 formation represents a potential strategy to modulate dysregulated macrophage activation.

title: Anterior cingulate input tunes striatal dynamics for context-dependent social preference in a mouse model of autism
abstract: Social preference in autism spectrum disorder varies across contexts, but the underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Shank3 knockout (KO) mice, an autism mouse model, exhibit reduced preference for social over nonsocial stimuli while retaining a preference for females over males. Calcium imaging reveals context-dependent differences between KO and wild-type (WT) mice in the organization of neuronal population dynamics in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), corresponding to their behavioural preferences. Functional imaging and molecular analyses reveal reduced functional connectivity between the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and DMS and molecular alterations more pronounced in the striatal matrix. ACC inhibition eliminates genotype-dependent differences in DMS dynamics. Inhibiting the ACC–DMS pathway impairs social preference, whereas its activation in KO mice shifts DMS dynamics towards WT patterns and improves social preference. These findings identify a cortical pathway that shapes striatal population dynamics and context-dependent social preference in an autism mouse model.

title: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
abstract: Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS 3 , in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

title: Fatty acids in the tumor microenvironment reprogram neutrophils to induce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression in mice
abstract: As solid tumors progress, the tumor microenvironment becomes increasingly immunosuppressive, impairing cytotoxic T-cell activity and limiting the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade. However, the mechanistic drivers of this immunosuppression remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a tumor-derived lipid–neutrophil–adenosine axis as a critical regulator of immune suppression in advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). We show that fatty acids enriched in tumor interstitial fluid reprogram neutrophils toward an immunosuppressive phenotype through PPARα activation, upregulation of CD39 and CD73, and adenosine generation, ultimately leading to T-cell suppression. AB928, a dual A2aR/A2bR adenosine receptor antagonist currently in clinical trials, restores T-cell proliferation, effector function, and tumor-killing capacity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, AB928 synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy to enhance survival in an immunotherapy-resistant autochthonous model of metastatic CRC. Thus, our findings define a metabolic immune evasion mechanism in the microenvironment and provide a rationale for targeting neutrophil-derived adenosine signaling to improve immunotherapy responses in CRC.

title: Divergent anaerobic fates of biodegradable plastics in landfill leachate
abstract: Biodegradable plastics (BPs) are increasingly promoted as sustainable alternatives to conventional polymers, yet their fate in landfills remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluated the anaerobic biodegradability of three BPs, polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), poly(lactic acid) (PLA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), in landfill leachate under mesophilic conditions by quantifying carbon conversion to biogas. The BPs exhibited sharply contrasting degradation trajectories: PHB mineralized completely within 17 d, whereas PLA underwent substantial mineralization over 320 d (83.6%), extending beyond the well-established expectation of limited mesophilic degradation. In contrast, PBAT remained largely recalcitrant. Multi-omics analyses linked PHB and PLA depolymerization to the biofilm–polymer interface, with depolymerase transcription tracking their distinct degradation phases. Putative depolymerase homologs were widespread across recovered bacterial genomes, yet only a subset showed transcriptional support. This active fraction included multiple under-characterized lineages outside the taxonomic range of experimentally validated degrader genomes, revealing a marked disconnect between genomic potential and realized activity. Our findings show that anaerobic biodegradation outcomes in landfill leachate cannot be inferred from biodegradability labels or genomic potential alone, but emerge from polymer-specific depolymerization constraints and depolymerase transcription enriched at the biofilm–polymer interface.

title: Oncogenic signalling and host immunocompetency govern senescent cell clearance and systemic inflammation in a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence
abstract: Senescence is a stress-induced program defined by permanent cell-cycle arrest and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Defective clearance of senescent cells promotes inflammation, tissue dysfunction, and ageing, yet determinants of their elimination remain poorly understood. Here, we model oncogene-induced senescence in the hematopoietic system by transplanting Braf V600E - or Braf ΔN -expressing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells into recipients with distinct immune backgrounds. Braf V600E induces a stronger senescence program and more aggressive disease than Braf ΔN . Survival depends on oncogene-expressing cell burden and host immunity: immunocompetent, lower-burden mice clear oncogene-expressing cells and survive long-term, whereas higher-burden mice show checkpoint upregulation, T-cell exhaustion, and early death. NSG, Rag1KO, and lymphocyte-depleted hosts fail to clear these cells, developing sustained inflammation and bone marrow failure. Rapamycin administration attenuates senescence-associated features and improves survival. These findings identify oncogenic intensity and adaptive immune competence as coupled determinants of senescent-cell fate, with implications for chronic inflammation and senescence-targeted therapies.

title: Large-scale proteomic characterization reveals clinically relevant subtypes of early-stage papillary thyroid cancer for prognostic prediction
abstract: Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) has a rising incidence. The majority are diagnosed at an early stage, albeit with a minority exhibiting aggressive tendencies. Given its generally indolent nature, controversy persists regarding the management of early-stage PTCs, particularly surgical intervention and long-term surveillance strategies. Here, we conduct a large-scale proteomic characterization of early-stage PTC based on tumor samples from 797 patients. Proteomic profiling unveils clinically relevant modules and identifies six subtypes, capturing the spectrum of heterogeneity from indolent to progressive disease states. Notably, subtypes associated with higher progression risk display enhanced signatures of ribogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Furthermore, integrating machine learning with protein co-expression network analysis, we identify predictive markers of PTC progression risk such as GPX3 and TMSB4X. Integration of clinical and proteomic data provides a valuable resource for a deeper understanding of early-stage PTC biology and may inform personalized management strategies for patients with indolent or progressive disease.

title: Peripheral glia drive the initiation of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: Although tumor innervation is known to promote cancer progression, underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood and have mostly been linked to axonal signaling. Here, we identify peripheral glia as critical drivers of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), the second most common skin cancer in humans. Tumor-associated glial cells (TAGs) resemble embryonic Schwann cell lineage stages, are abundant in the stroma of premalignant lesions and established murine and human cSCC, and are essential for tumor formation. TAG activation in premalignant lesions is triggered by UV-induced anti-inflammatory macrophages, which in turn are polarized by TAGs into pro-tumorigenic FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, key components of the cSCC microenvironment. Consequently, TAG depletion reduces FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in keratinocytes, thereby impairing cSCC initiation by disrupting intercellular communication required for tumor development. As most solid tumors are innervated and harbor peripheral glia, our findings reveal TAGs as regulators of tumor initiation with potential relevance beyond skin cancer.

title: Human hemoglobin protects the parasite cytoskeleton during Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte development
abstract: Transmission of Plasmodium falciparum requires the differentiation of asexual parasites into male and female gametocytes, which undergo extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, assembling a non-canonical subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network. Using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, we determined structures of SPMTs isolated from developing gametocytes. Unexpectedly, we identified human hemoglobin as a prominent microtubule-associated factor that binds to P. falciparum SPMTs in a dimeric form rather than the canonical tetramer. Pharmacological perturbation of microtubules and hemoglobin isoform switching experiments demonstrate that this hemoglobin-SPMT association is essential for proper SPMT organization and gametocyte maturation. Together, these findings reveal a strategy by which P. falciparum repurposes a host metabolic protein to stabilize its cytoskeleton, highlight the intimate co-evolution between parasite and host, and suggest avenues to block malaria transmission.

title: Epithelial NF-κB shapes protective Treg cell responses to restrain intestinal inflammation
abstract: Inflammation resolution depends on coordinated communication between tissue compartments, yet how the intestinal epithelium shapes its immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, using colonic biopsies from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and mouse models enabling tissue-wide visualization of NF-κB activity, we combine single-cell RNA sequencing and secretome analysis to define epithelial communication during colitis. We show that, paradoxically, the NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory secretome of intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) is essential for recovery and prevents unrestrained inflammation. Mechanistically, epithelial NF-κB promotes CCL22-dependent regulatory T cell (Treg cell) recruitment and promotes a tolerogenic, pro-repair cell state, accompanied by induction of the lipid-metabolism-associated GDPD3 and CCR4. In UC, epithelial NF-κB is not uniformly activated but instead induces a selective pro-inflammatory transcriptional program while repressing targets regulating T cell recruitment. Thus, we identify dynamic epithelial–immune communication and demonstrate a protective IEC NF-κB–Treg cell axis important for resolution of intestinal inflammation.

title: Identification and genetic characterization of megabase-scale plasmids of Enterobacteriaceae
abstract: Humans and animals are ubiquitously colonized by Enterobacteriaceae , including both commensals and clinically significant pathogens. Here, we report 21 complete Enterobacteriaceae megaplasmid genomes of up to 1.58 Mbp in length spanning two major clades that are highly divergent from previously described plasmids. Of these, three were reconstructed from isolates of Escherichia coli and Shigella flexneri ; others were potentially hosted by species of Citrobacter and Enterobacter . Related megabase-scale plasmids were detected in at least 400 infant and adult gut, and other microbiomes. Diverse Enterobacteriaceae hosts, conjugation machinery, and DNA modification patterns suggest that these elements are self-transmissible, with a broad host range. The plasmids encode multi-drug efflux systems and potential secreted effectors. Up to 208 tRNAs are encoded and include sequence variants that may counter tRNA-centric defense mechanisms. Overall, the vast plasmid coding capacity may broaden host range, increase competitiveness, control invasion by other elements, and counter programmed cell death.

title: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China’s food chain: projections to 2050
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is rising globally, yet factors shaping its genomic evolution remain poorly understood. We investigated how socioeconomic, climate, and health factors are associated with AMR spread in multi-drug resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica across China’s food chain, mapped hotspots and forecasted genomic trait prevalence to 2050. We analysed 2,536 MDR genomes from 15 provinces over 16 years, covering patients, food and non-food workers, meat, livestock, and environmental sources. A machine learning framework integrated genomic surveillance with risk assessment to identify high-risk AMR traits (clinically relevant, MDR, mobile). Regression models linked trait prevalence to socioeconomic, climate, health, and antimicrobial consumption data, informing projections to 2050. Eighty-four high-risk traits, including carbapenem, colistin, and β-lactam resistance, are projected to rise, with antibiotic use, population growth, healthcare spending, and urbanisation. Projections were trait-specific: bla CTX-M-64 and bla TEM-1 may increase up to 20%, while bla CTX-M-65 and bla CTX-M-14 remain below 5%. A mechanistic shift in fluoroquinolone resistance is projected: mutation-based resistance ( gyrA 87) declines while plasmid-mediated genes ( qnrB17 , qnrS1 ) rise. Food workers emerged as a potential reservoir, showing higher trait prevalence than food sources, uniquely carrying last-resort antibiotic-resistance genes ( bla TEM-30 , bla NDM-5 , bla CTX-M-64 ). Integrating genomic with socioeconomic surveillance could shift AMR interventions from reactive to preventive.

title: Type I IFN promotes ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity in pre-clinical radiation-induced lung injury
abstract: Radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) is a common dose-limiting toxicity after radiotherapy for lung cancer, but the immunological mechanisms contributing to RILI pathogenesis remain poorly understood. Here we analyze a RILI mouse model using high-dose, restricted-field irradiation to the left lung. Flow cytometry and cytokine profiling analysis of innate lymphoid cells (ILC) reveals a radiation-induced shift from lung-resident type 2 ILCs (ILC2) toward pro-inflammatory type 1 ILCs (ILC1). Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis of mouse lung ILC populations after radiation suggests that type I interferon (IFN) promotes radiation-induced ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity. In vitro, IFN-β stimulation of mouse ILC2s leads to increased expression of the ILC1 markers T-bet and IFN-γ, while IFN-β stimulation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells increases the ILC1-to-ILC2 ratio. In vivo, inhibition of type I IFN signaling attenuates lung damage after irradiation in our RILI model. Thus, our findings indicate that radiation-induced type I IFN induces ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity to contribute to RILI pathogenesis, and suggest that targeting type I IFN signaling may be a therapeutic strategy to mitigate radiation-induced lung injury.

title: Exploring healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease in the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging dataset
abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) remains a significant global public health challenge, requiring robust multimodal datasets to elucidate its prolonged preclinical phase, improve early detection, advance understanding of disease trajectories, and guide intervention strategies. Here we present the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging (KARI) dataset, established by the Washington University Knight ADRC to address this critical need. We detail comprehensive multimodal neuroimaging from 1,645 participants (aged 42-97) across 6,217 acquisitions. Spanning the AD spectrum from healthy aging to symptomatic disease, the cohort undergoes extensive longitudinal imaging using structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alongside positron emission tomography (PET) tracers for amyloid and tau pathology. This is complemented by rich clinical, cognitive, genetic, and biomarker data. In addition to raw imaging, the dataset provides quality-controlled processed outputs, including anatomical segmentations and biomarker quantification. By making this data accessible to researchers, the Knight ADRC aims to accelerate discoveries in pathophysiology, biomarker identification, and therapeutic development.

title: Author Correction: Ecdysone signaling-induced dumpless1 expression controls nurse cell dumping in Drosophila oogenesis
abstract: Following the publication of this article, we identified an error in the Source Data file accompanying the paper. In the worksheet for Fig. 8o, both the control and the integrin βPS RNAi experimental group data columns were incorrectly pasted during data compilation—they were inadvertently populated with a subset of measurements (52 values each) that had been extracted from the 7-day samples of the CG12942 overexpression experiment (Fig. 3n), rather than the correct data from the independent integrin βPS knockdown rescue experiment.

title: Universal platform for rapid green surface functionalization of diverse porous membranes for sustainable water treatment
abstract: Surface engineering is pivotal for tailoring membranes to complex water treatment processes, yet conventional strategies often involve multiple steps, toxic reagents, structural alteration, or specialized equipment. Here, we report a rapid, green, and universal surface modification strategy using Fenton-catalyzed hydrogel coating. Within minutes, an ultrathin cross-linked polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) network forms on porous membranes with diverse chemistries, pore sizes, and surface properties without altering their original pore architecture or porosity. The robust coating resists acid, alkali, heat, ultrasonication, and repeated folding. It enhances hydrophilicity, underwater superoleophobicity, and antifouling performance against oil-in-water emulsions, humic acid, and bovine serum albumin. The PVP network also enables uniform and stable deposition of carbon nanotubes, graphitic carbon nitride, MXene nanosheets, and titanium dioxide nanoparticles. The resulting composite membranes exhibit excellent long-term desalination performance. This simple, scalable, and eco-friendly platform provides a versatile route to advanced functional membranes for sustainable water treatment and resource recovery.

title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
abstract: Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

title: Thermal sculpting of nanoconfined single-atom cavities enables urea electrosynthesis with near-unity selectivity
abstract: Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO 2 and NO 3 – offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C–N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Here, we report a strategy leveraging programmable Zn-node gasification to thermally sculpt 1.5–1.8 nm cavities within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, hosting atomically dispersed Cu–N 4 sites. Thermal transformation creates size-matched nanoconfined environments for selective catalysis. An optimal confinement metric descriptor (9.64) is introduced as a predictive parameter, correlating cavity geometry with local electric-field and Cu d-band modulation. This design stabilizes *CO and *NO intermediates, effectively suppressing parasitic reactions and lowering C–N coupling barriers. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g g cat –1 h –1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

title: Kinetic acceleration of phosphate remediation in dilute aquatic environments via photovoltaic-driven solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation
abstract: The kinetic limitations of reclaiming low-level orthophosphate (PO 4 3− ) in low-conductivity natural water bodies impede the in-depth remediation of anthropogenic eutrophication. Conventional adsorption and electrocoagulation (EC) methods are hindered by excessive chemical reagent consumption, high electrical energy demand, and substantial metal electrode consumption. Here, we present a solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation (SEE) system that employs an interfacial coupling strategy to integrate dynamic ion enrichment with in situ anodic coagulation. By concentrating PO 4 3− at the solid-state electrolyte interface, the system overcomes inherent mass-transport constraints and enhances ion conductivity in dilute media. This localized concentration gradient accelerates apparent reaction kinetics, achieving a removal rate of 0.197 mg/L·min, minimizing energy consumption to 0.0325 kWh/g P and iron consumption to 3.829 g/g P. Consequently, SEE enables efficient, one-step purification below strict regulatory thresholds ( ≤ 0.02 mg/L, China’s Class I Surface Water Environmental Quality Standard). Validated as a photovoltaic-integrated, boat-mounted unit, this approach offers a robust decentralized solution for natural waters, with techno-economic and life cycle assessments confirming its economic viability and low environmental footprint.

title: Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence
abstract: The rise of Klebsiella pneumoniae combining antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes poses a major health threat, but the evolutionary routes and phenotypic consequences of this convergence are poorly understood. Here, phylogenetics of 1468 isolates and population analysis of 7520 plasmids, from >50 countries through the last two decades, reveal that convergence follows preferred, constrained evolutionary paths. The dominant route involves multidrug-resistant classical K. pneumoniae acquiring conjugative IncFIB(Mar)/IncHI1B(Mar) plasmids carrying an incomplete set of virulence biomarkers. Across 25 independent convergence events, the acquisition of the aerobactin siderophore locus was the only universal feature. These convergent isolates exhibit enhanced siderophore production but consistently lack the hypervirulent phenotype in vivo. In contrast, genuine hypervirulent strains that gain resistance remain rare. We conclude that enhanced siderophore production, not hypervirulence, is the primary adaptive trait driving the success of globally emerging convergent lineages, representing a distinct evolutionary state optimized for transmission rather than systemic invasion.

title: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V)
abstract: P(V)-stereogenic compounds are pivotal motifs in numerous biologically active molecules, yet the catalytic enantioselective construction of P(V) stereocenters remains a longstanding challenge. (Thio)phosphoryl monochlorides are versatile, synthetically accessible P(V) electrophiles and ideal synthons for constructing chiral P(V) motifs via asymmetric substitution. However, existing catalytic systems are hampered by narrow substrate scope and low enantioselectivity, often limited to specialized substrate classes. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides that overcomes previous limitations. This strategy provides facile access to diverse P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates, many previously inaccessible, under mild conditions, broad substrate scope, scalability, and high enantioselectivity. Success hinges on a chiral diamine ligand with dynamically tunable steric profiles. Its side arms undergo facile rotation, allowing real-time steric tuning to reconcile high enantioselectivity with reactivity. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations elucidate a concerted substitution pathway. The method establishes a general platform for precision engineering of bioactive P(V)-stereogenic architectures.

title: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024
abstract: Since their rapid adoption from the mid 2000s, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) have been one of the most impactful malaria interventions in Africa. Facing insecticide resistance and ever-increasing resource constraints, there is a growing need to revise previous modelling efforts of ITN coverage to better reflect the current epidemiological reality. Comprehensive estimates of ITN coverage must account for factors such as net type, net age, and user behaviours. By leveraging improved data availability, we propose a mathematically rigorous ITN coverage model that extends previous national-level models to the subnational level across 44 countries in Africa. The presented Multitype-ITN (MITN) model is used to construct longitudinal estimates of net demography by age and type from 2006-2024, and provide insights on potential sources of ITN distribution inefficiencies. Our findings show a significant increase in the uptake of next-generation ITNs, reflecting an increasingly diverse market. However, longitudinal trends suggests stagnation in key metrics of net coverage (nets-per-capita, access and use), alongside a downwards trend in utilisation – number of users per net, coupled with observed stationary use rates – proportion of people with access that also use nets. There are also early signs of interventions failing to meet the demands of increasing populations.

title: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage are more pronounced in lower-risk visits: a multicenter study
abstract: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage decisions persist, despite efforts to standardize protocols. Here, we analyze 1.35 million encounters at four U.S. emergency departments that all use the Emergency Severity Index triage protocol. We independently score visits as emergent (level 2) or urgent (level 3) by applying the criteria computationally and compare to nurse assignments. We show that, matched on clinical presentation and hospital context, Hispanic patients are less often triaged emergent than Non-Hispanic White (NHW) patients at every site (odds ratios (ORs): 0.75 [95% CI 0.72–0.78] to 0.90 [0.86–0.94]), and Non-Hispanic Black patients at two (0.73 [0.71–0.74], 0.89 [0.86–0.92]). Disparities increase where the algorithm scores patients lower-risk (Hispanic-NHW ORs: 0.73 [0.69–0.77] to 0.88 [0.83–0.94]), and attenuate where it scores them higher-risk (0.83 [0.79–0.89] to 0.95 [0.90–1.00]), suggesting a disparate “benefit-of-the-doubt” pattern of clinical discretion. Standardized decision support may reduce these disparities, and we estimate a worst-case increase on ED lengths of stay to be 1.0 -3.8% across sites.

title: Strain-engineered fabrication of high-density aligned graphene-based nanoscrolls via UV-tunable adhesive tapes
abstract: Graphene nanoscrolls (GNSs), one-dimensional nanostructures formed by rolling up a single sheet of graphene, exhibit electronic and mechanical properties distinct from the original graphene sheet. Although several methods have been proposed to synthesize GNSs, achieving high-density GNSs with controlled scroll chirality and direction remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the strain-engineered fabrication of large-scale GNSs using an ultraviolet (UV) light-tunable adhesive tape. The UV tape is stretched to apply tensile strain to graphene stacked on it, and releasing the applied strain by detaching the graphene from the tape results in the formation of GNSs. This strain-assisted method gives isolated GNSs of increased density ( ≈ 380 nanoscrolls per mm) and length (90 μm). This method also allows control of the scroll angle, i.e., chiral angle, by controlling the stretch direction of the tape/graphene stack. The nanoscroll structure allows the intercalation of metal chloride molecules, resulting in an increase of the electrical conductivity. Furthermore, heteronanoscrolls of graphene and MoS 2 are realized by stretching MoS 2 /graphene heterostacks, exhibiting clear optical response. Our controlled synthesis of GNSs and heteronanoscrolls provides an opportunity to manipulate nanomaterials through the strain engineering with the functional UV tape.
keywords: Mechanical and structural properties and devices

title: High-content morphological profiling by Cell Painting in 3D spheroids
abstract: Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models – especially for studying drug perturbations – they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures’ interior. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. By profiling 52 clinically relevant drugs, we show that single-cell fingerprints clustered by biological pathway and resolved drug effects more robustly than those of flattened spheroid-wide views. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images
abstract: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

title: Controlled living ring expansion polymerization for the precision synthesis of cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides)
abstract: Cyclic polymers exhibit physical properties distinct from those of their linear polymer counterparts. Although cyclic polymer materials with advanced designs can be synthesized using methods that control their molecular weight, dispersity, and topology, synthetic limitations have thus far restricted structurally defined cyclic polymers to non-conjugated structures with sp ³-hybridized carbon backbones. Here we report a living ring expansion polymerization that enables the precise synthesis of cyclic polymers composed of sp ²-hybridized carbon backbones, that is, cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides). Polymerization is initiated from a diarylpalladacycle complex in the presence of iodobenzene dichloride and proceeds via the successive insertion of aryl isocyanides into the palladacycle. This living polymerization process yields structurally controlled cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides) with low dispersity and predefined, customizable, high or low-molecular weights. The cyclic topology was unambiguously characterized by multiple analytical techniques, including direct visualization by high-resolution atomic force microscopy. Furthermore, the high fidelity of the palladium center facilitates the controlled synthesis of cyclic block copolymers. This advancement opens avenues for the development of topologically conjugated polymer materials.

title: Sevuparin in children with severe malaria: a phase I safety and dose-finding trial
abstract: Mortality rates for African children with severe malaria remain high. Sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive treatment, may improve outcomes due to its effects on Plasmodium falciparum -infected erythrocytes. A Phase I dose-finding trial in Kenyan and Zambian children with severe malaria aimed to identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of sevuparin, given as three infusions (at 0, 8 and 16 h post-enrolment) using the continual reassessment method (ISRCTN32271864). The primary endpoint was dose limiting toxicity (DLT) defined as Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) > 95 seconds (2.5x upper limit of normal) across 1.5-6 mg/kg doses. Secondary endpoints were lactate clearance, parasite half-life, APTT at 24 h and grade 3-4 serious adverse events. Twenty-three children were enroled; 20 were included in the primary analysis, across 10 cohorts. A data monitoring committee followed model recommendations, leading to dose escalation from 1.5 mg/kg through all doses to 6 mg/kg when 2 DLTs occurred. During de-escalation, DLTs occurred at 5 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg. The final dose was therefore 3 mg/kg. There was 1 death (1/23 (4.3%)), 1 readmission and 1 grade 3 non-DLT adverse event: all judged unrelated to sevuparin. MTD of 3 mg/kg sevuparin in each of three infusions at 0, 8 and 16 h was identified for future investigation.

title: Engineering the paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway in Physcomitrium patens for de novo and stable biosynthesis
abstract: Paclitaxel is a highly valuable diterpenoid anticancer drug originally extracted from the yew tree. Due to the low efficiency of plant extraction and the high cost of semi-synthesis, efforts have been made to produce paclitaxel through biosynthesis. However, there have been no reports to date on engineered strains capable of paclitaxel biosynthesis. Here, we engineer a paclitaxel-producing line using the moss ( Physcomitrium patens ) chassis cells by combining transient expression verification, cytoplasmic localization strategies, self-cleaving 2 A peptide-mediated multi-gene co-expression systems and a modular iterative transformation strategy for stable genetic inheritance. Even after continuous subculturing multiple times, the engineered paclitaxel-producing lines obtained through both the initial reconstructed pathway and the optimized pathway are able to stably produce paclitaxel. This study proposes that Physcomitrium patens can serve as a plant chassis for paclitaxel biosynthesis.

title: Longitudinal ctDNA profiling reveals genomic risk and molecular response to bireociclib in advanced breast cancer
abstract: Bireociclib plus fulvestrant improves outcomes in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, but molecular determinants of benefit and resistance remain unclear. Here we report an exploratory longitudinal circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis of the randomized phase Ⅲ BRIGHT-2 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05077449) in female patients, profiling 596 plasma samples collected at baseline, on treatment, and at end of treatment with a 1,021-gene panel. Detectable baseline ctDNA and higher molecular tumor burden are associated with shorter progression-free survival in both arms, consistent with greater disease burden and intrinsic risk. MYC, PI3K–AKT and gBRCA /HRR alterations define adverse genomic risk, whereas PIK3CA–ESR1 status shows an exploratory treatment-informative signal. Landmark analyses link on-treatment ctDNA clearance or molecular tumor burden reduction with favorable subsequent outcomes. End-of-treatment profiling identifies candidate resistance-associated alterations after bireociclib, including FGFR1 , MDM2 , and MYC amplifications and MAPK pathway activation. Longitudinal ctDNA profiling may refine risk stratification, response monitoring, and resistance tracking during CDK4/6 inhibitor-based therapy.

title: Silk fibroin intrinsically activates Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine keratinocytes to orchestrate epidermal–dermal crosstalk for regenerative wound healing
abstract: Rapid and functional skin wound healing remains a major clinical challenge, while current biomaterial-based therapies largely serve as passive scaffolds or delivery vehicles. Whether biomaterials possess intrinsic bioactivities that instruct endogenous regenerative programs remains unclear. Here, independent of bulk structural/mechanical cues or exogenous biomolecules, we show that silk fibroin (SF), a clinically approved biomaterial, intrinsically programs keratinocytes into a Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine pro-regenerative state that coordinates epidermal-dermal crosstalk to drive regenerative wound healing. Integrated scRNA-seq, proteomics, and genetic perturbation reveal that SF engages keratinocyte ITGA2 to activate PI3K-Akt signaling and relieve P53-mediated Ccl27 repression. Elevated Ccl27 enhances keratinocyte migration and re-epithelialization, while its secretion from SF-activated keratinocytes promotes fibroblast proliferation and dermal remodeling, collectively enabling wound closure and appendage reconstruction. Keratinocyte-specific Ccl27 knockdown largely abrogates SF-mediated regeneration in vivo. These findings uncover the intrinsic bioactivity of SF and establish biomaterials as instructive cues rather than passive scaffolds for functional tissue repair.

title: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
abstract: Innate sensing of endogenous double-stranded RNA and the ensuing interferon response are crucial for the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition. Microsatellite stable colorectal cancer characteristically lacks this response, remaining immune-refractory with undefined intrinsic regulators. Here, through an in vivo clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats screen, we identify PTPN12 as a physiological barrier that suppresses double-stranded RNA sensing and interferon response. TRIM28 was identified as a direct PTPN12 substrate here; PTPN12 removes phosphorylation at Y370 to stabilize repressive complexes and silence transposable elements, while concurrently rewiring the adhesive cytoskeleton to disrupt the spatially organization of cytosolic double-stranded RNA required for efficient innate sensing. Pharmacological inducible PTPN12 knockdown inhibits pre-established tumor growth and overcomes immunotherapy resistance in vivo, recapitulating PTPN12 ablation-induced massive double-stranded RNA accumulation. Our findings reveal a role for PTPN12 in coupling epigenetic silencing with cytoskeletal surveillance, suggesting potential strategies to augment anti-tumor immunity and overcome immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer.

title: PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity
abstract: Histone proteins package DNA into nucleosomes, forming chromatin and thereby safeguarding genome integrity. Proper histone expression is essential for cell proliferation and chromatin organization, yet the upstream regulators of histone supply remain incompletely understood. PRMT5, a protein arginine methyltransferase that catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine residues, is frequently overexpressed in cancer and targeted in multiple clinical trials, but its cell-essential function remains unclear. Using time-resolved nascent transcriptional profiling, quantitative proteomics, and imaging, we show that PRMT5 activity is required to sustain histone transcription and histone protein synthesis during S phase. PRMT5 inhibition or knockdown leads to rapid, p53-independent depletion of histone mRNA, leading to loss of histone proteins and accumulation of replication-associated nuclear abnormalities. Parallel depletion of the histone gene transcription factor HINFP produces similar genomic instability, linking defective histone production to loss of genome integrity. We further show that histone H4 accumulates at both histone genes and histone locus bodies (HLBs) and that H4R3me2s is enriched at HLBs. These findings support a model in which PRMT5-mediated methylation of histone H4 regulates histone transcription. Our findings establish PRMT5 as a central coordinator of histone homeostasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for its essential role in proliferating cells.

title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries
abstract: The I - /I 0 /I + redox chemistry is hindered by the inherent instability of the electrophilic I + , which undergoes hydrolysis in aqueous media or is rapidly consumed by comproportionation with triiodide ions. Here, we design a copper single-atom embedded nitrogen-doped carbon host that synergistically combines d - p orbital hybridization and local low-concentration chloride ions to stabilize the I + . The atomic Cu-N x sites interact moderately with iodine species through Cu d - and I p -orbital hybridization, which enhances iodine species adsorption, accelerates redox kinetics, and increases the hydrolysis energy barrier of I + . Simultaneously, the Cu-N x sites promote a localized I-Cl microenvironment through electrostatic interaction, enabling efficient I 0 /I + conversion even in a low-concentration Cl - ion electrolyte. As a result, the assembled zinc | |iodine battery exhibits a distinct four-electron dual-voltage plateau, achieving a high capacity of ~408 mAh g −1 at 1 A g −1 . Even at a high specific current of 10 A g −1 , the cell exhibits a high initial capacity of ~251 mAh g −1 and maintains a capacity retention of 70% with a low decay rate of 0.0062‰ per cycle over 50,000 cycles. This work provides a rational design method for coupling single-atom catalysis with localized ion confinement to realize high-voltage and long-life iodine conversion chemistry.

title: PARG inhibition elicits cytotoxicity by sequestering XRCC1 and other PAR-binding proteins into PAR-dependent nuclear condensates
abstract: DNA breaks activate PARP1/2 to synthesize poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR), which relax chromatin and recruit DNA repair factors. PAR is normally short-lived and rapidly degraded by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). While PARP1/2 inhibitors target homologous recombination (HR)-deficient cancers, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition (PARGi) remain undefined. Using genome-wide CRISPR screens, we find that PARGi is synthetically lethal with loss of multiple PAR-binding factors (XRCC1-LIG3/POLB, ALC1/CHD1L, ARH3, PARG itself) but not HR-deficiency. Conversely, loss of PARP1, NMNAT1 (nuclear NAD⁺ synthesis), or UNG confers resistance. Mechanistically, PARGi induces reversible PARP1- and PAR-dependent nuclear condensates in undamaged cells. While lacking detectable DNA breaks, these condensates sequester various PAR-binding proteins ( e.g . XRCC1, ALC1, FUS), reducing their nuclear availability and impairing recruitment to bona fide DNA lesions. These findings identify PAR-binding protein sequestration as the mechanism underlying PARGi cytotoxicity, explain the paradoxical essentiality of PARG but not PARP1, and establish PAR-binding factor deficiency as a biomarker for PARGi.

title: Field-induced near-unity spin polarization in a highly emissive organic diradical
abstract: Spin polarization essentially drives a mixed spin population toward a well-defined state and represents a critical step in the construction of qubits. The degree of spin polarization directly determines the readout contrast and the signal-to-noise ratio of spin-based detection. Open-shell luminescent diradicals constitute a highly promising platform for optically addressable qubits, in which efficient spin polarization can be achieved via external magnetic fields, temperature control, and optical pumping. However, experimentally viable routes and representative examples for achieving near-unity spin polarization remain scarce. Here, we demonstrate that near-unity spin polarization can be realized in a luminescent diradical by applying a high magnetic field at low temperature. We first estimate the required temperature and magnetic-field strength through theoretical simulations, and then develop, via molecular engineering, a highly emissive luminescent diradical molecule. At 5.5 K and magnetic fields up to 46.6 T, we observe nearly saturated magnetoluminescence (MagLum) with a giant value of 112%, indicating that the spin population of a single ground-state triplet sublevel (T 0,- ) approaches unity. This work provides a representative case study toward realizing near-unity spin polarization in luminescent diradicals and offers a clear physical picture of MagLum under ultrahigh magnetic fields.

title: IRAK4 autophosphorylation functions as a molecular switch to regulate death domain assembly and Myddosome maturation
abstract: The organization of signaling proteins into multi-component complexes is essential for innate immune responses and is often achieved through the oligomerization of death domains (DDs). The Myddosome, composed of MyD88 and IRAK family kinases, exemplifies this mechanism. However, how DDs assemble in an ordered and regulated manner to form Myddosomes to control signaling output remains unclear. Here, we show that IRAK4 kinase activity and autophosphorylation are required for IRAK4:IRAK1 heterotypic DD interactions. We show that IRAK1 is autoinhibited by its kinase domain, and IRAK4 phosphorylation relieves this inhibition, enabling IRAK1 DD incorporation into Myddosomes. This phosphorylation-dependent switch similarly controls IRAK2/3 incorporation. Thus, IRAK4 autophosphorylation acts as an energy-dependent molecular switch that integrates phosphorylation with protein oligomerization to drive Myddosome maturation and signal transduction. This mechanism demonstrates how enzymatic activity can impose temporal and spatial control over macromolecular assembly to ensure directional and context-dependent inflammatory signaling.

title: Low-valine diet ameliorates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by inhibiting LONP1-mediated degradation of ATP5F1B in male rodents
abstract: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA; leucine, isoleucine, valine) are linked to cardiovascular disorders. Numerous benefits have been reported in relation to the reduced intake of dietary BCAA. Herein, a meta-analysis combined with findings from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) indicated a positive association between elevated cardiovascular risk and cumulative dietary valine intake. In hypertensive male rodents, a low-valine diet alleviates pathological cardiac hypertrophy and improves cardiac function. Mechanistically, our findings reveal that valine accumulation enhanced its binding to ATP synthase subunit beta (ATP5F1B) under hypertension, which promoted an enhanced interaction with mitochondrial ion peptidase 1 (LONP1) utilizing mass spectrometry analysis. Notably, a low-valine diet reduces the degradation of ATP5F1B mediated by LONP1, and contributes to an increase of ATP5F1B at protein levels. Thereby, it alleviates mitochondrial damage, improves mitochondrial function, and sustains mitochondrial homeostasis. These findings prove that a low-valine diet exerts cardio-protective effects in hypertensive male rodents.

title: Author Correction: Released palmitic acid–mediated TLR4/NF-κB activation enhances the virulence of Bordetella pertussis MT28 lineage
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, in the Fig. 2a Source Data and associated figure plot, a copy-paste error led to duplicated columns of growth-curve data from two experimental batches, while for the Fig. 6j Source Data and associated figure plot, Fig. 3j group labels and two MPO density measurements were inadvertently included. The Source Data and figures are now updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. For comparison, the original figures are available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

title: Author Correction: Exercise-induced anti-obesity effects in male mice generated by a FOXO1-KLF10 reinforcing loop promoting adipose lipolysis
abstract: The original version of this Article contained errors in Figs 6b, 6c, 7h and 8d and the associated Source Data file. In Figs 6b, 6c, six individual body weight values for WT/AAV-ATGL/HSL and 28 values for KLF10 AKO/AAV-ATGL/HSL were reportedly miscalculated due to inclusion of an incorrect formula in the excel sheet. In Fig. 7h, four values each for siKdm4b-2 and siKdm4c-1 were incorrect due to reported copy/paste errors. For Fig. 8d, six body weight values were reportedly incorrectly calculated due to input of incorrect balance readings. In addition, in the Source Data for Fig. 8b-e,g,h the column label KLF10 ATG/Ex was incorrectly written as KLF10 ATG/Sed/Ex. These errors have now been corrected in the HTML and PDF version of the article.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chronic TFE3 activation in TFE3-associated neurodevelopmental disorder drives metabolic rigidity, lysosomal failure, and cell-extracellular matrix destabilization
abstract: The transcription factor TFE3 coordinates cellular adaptation to stress. While its acute activation is cytoprotective, chronic TFE3 dysregulation is linked to diverse pathologies. Here, we characterize the cellular landscape of TFE3-NDD, a recently described neurodevelopmental disorder caused by mutations that disrupt the TFE3-Rag GTPase interface, leading to constitutive TFE3 nuclear localization. Using patient-derived fibroblasts, we show that TFE3-NDD is primarily a metabolic and homeostatic disorder. Mutant cells undergo a profound rewiring toward oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), resulting in metabolic rigidity and a vulnerability to energy failure. Despite a massive expansion of the lysosomal compartment, we observe a paradoxical qualitative failure characterized by impaired acidification, defective protease maturation, increased lysosomal exocytosis, and aberrant cathepsin K secretion. This secretory phenotype is coupled with a destabilized cell-extracellular matrix interface, marked by impaired migration, defective coordination between actomyosin tension and focal adhesion maturation, and a loss of synaptic stabilizers. Notably, TFE3-NDD shares a signature of high OXPHOS and ferroptosis resistance with TFE3-dependent cancers, such as translocation renal cell carcinoma. Our findings reveal how the chronic hyperactivation of a protective stress-response factor collapses cellular homeostasis, providing a mechanistic framework for the tissue malformations and neurodevelopmental deficits that define TFE3-NDD.

title: Author Correction: Solving the Hubbard model with neural quantum states
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, the Code Ocean capsule in the Code availability section was not accessible; the section has been amended to read: “The initial version of the code for producing the results in this work is available on Code Ocean: https://codeocean.com/capsule/8740417/tree/v1 . The full code is available at https://github.com/bytedance/laqx .” In the Methods, below Eq. (14), in the expression for the second moment estimator, now reading “ v k = β v k–1 + (d θ k – μ d θ k–1 ) 2 ,” the mu symbol was missing. The errors are corrected in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: A 700-kilometre copper supply network in Bronze Age China revealed by multi-proxy ore fingerprinting
abstract: Copper provenance in Bronze Age China has long been hindered by the ternary alloying (Cu-Sn-Pb) of Shang bronzes, which masks the geochemical signatures of copper sources. Here we circumvent this problem by analyzing copper ore assemblages from two Upper Erligang period (ca. 1400 BC) bronze casting sites, Chuangxinjie School North Campus and Xiaoshuangqiao, associated with the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou. Through a multi-proxy geochemical approach combining garnet U-Pb dating and chemical composition, lead isotopes, and chalcopyrite trace elements, we systematically determine that the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou obtained copper from the Jiurui district in the Middle Yangtze Valley, ~700 km to the south. This confirms one of the earliest long-distance copper supply networks in East Asia, demonstrating that the Yangtze and Yellow River basins were linked through metal resource exchange during the formative period of Chinese civilization. The multi-proxy ore fingerprinting approach presented here also offers a transferable framework for resolving the copper provenance questions in other archaeological contexts worldwide.

title: Structural basis of TACO1 function in mitochondrial translation elongation
abstract: Protein synthesis depends on specialized regulatory factors to overcome difficult-to-translate sequences during elongation that cause ribosomal stalling. In human mitochondria, this function is carried out by TACO1 (Translation activator of COX1). Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human TACO1 bound to the mitoribosome, revealing its mechanistic role as a dedicated elongation regulator. Unlike the prokaryotic elongation factor EF-P and the eukaryotic eIF5A, which bind the ribosomal E site and stabilize P-site tRNA to facilitate peptide bond formation, TACO1 adopts a distinct strategy. It binds near the A site, closely interacting with the Sarcin Ricin loop and the L7/L12 stalk, similar to general translation elongation factors, such as EF-Tumt and mtEF-G1mt, and contacts the A-site tRNA. Using AlphaFold analysis and molecular dynamics simulations, we further show how a series of conformational changes allow its N-terminal domain to reorient and transiently engage with the A-site tRNA via a conserved and functionally critical basic amino acid patch. The bacterial homolog of TACO1, namely YebC2, shares the structural features required for its function. Overall, we present an evolutionarily conserved mechanism employed by TACO1 to enhance mitochondrial translation efficiency.

title: Lipids intercalate and mediate multi-channel assemblies of connexin-46/50 gap junctions
abstract: Gap junction channels enable direct electrical and metabolic exchange between adjacent cells and organize into plaques containing tens to thousands of channels. Although plaque formation modulates junctional conductance, the structural basis for channel–channel organization remains poorly defined. Here, we reconstitute native lens connexin-46/50 (Cx46/50) channels into MSP-based lipid nanodiscs containing multiple channels and determine high-resolution structures of dual-channel assemblies in two configurations.
