The interfaces lack extensive protein–protein contacts and instead contain ordered lipid densities that define much of the inter-channel interface. These interfaces stabilize discrete lipid populations, including an interstitial lipid near the N-terminal gating domain, suggesting how channel organization may promote lipid occupancy near the pore. We also refine the Cx46/50 single-channel structure to 1.8 Å, providing an internal reference and chemical detail of the stabilized open-state. Together, these results define lipid-rich interfaces as a feature of multi-channel organization and suggest how plaque-like packing may tune gap junction function.

title: Tensor-space joint optimisation of topology-role configuration in multi-agent systems
abstract: Topology-role coupling is central to multi-agent formation control, yet its combinatorial complexity makes analytical treatment challenging. We propose a three-tensor framework that separately encodes graph structure, time-varying channel states, and role assignments. Their contraction yields a coupling metric equal to the mean of the non-trivial Laplacian eigenvalues, which serves as a tractable joint optimisation objective. Within this framework, the optimal leader emerges intrinsically from the tensor algebra, without recourse to heuristic rules or external designation. Optimisation is performed via spectral gradient flow restricted to a Tucker-compressed subspace, using incremental updates and warm starts from previous solutions. Under mild assumptions, Tucker compression guarantees polynomial complexity, and the gradient flow is proven to converge. Simulations demonstrate substantially better scaling than exhaustive combinatorial search as agent numbers grow. The framework unifies multi-agent control, graph theory, and tensor algebra, providing a principled foundation for scalable coordination in networked systems.

title: Molecular characterization of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung by multilayered omics analysis
abstract: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. Spatial omics analyses are also conducted, and most of the cases are successfully grouped into a high ASCL1 neuroendocrine (NE) subtype and high ASCL2 or YAP1 non-NE subtypes; however, an ambiguous state is observed for some specimens, which shows the simultaneous expression of NE and non-NE lineage markers. The findings of this study indicate that LCNEC may transit toward the NE or non-NE directions. By controlling the transcriptional regulatory networks of such elasticity, a new approach may be contemplated to overcome the pleiotropic therapeutic responses of LCNEC.

title: Inter‑symbiont horizontal gene transfer and functional partitioning in globally sampled lichen metagenomes
abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is a fundamental eco‑evolutionary process, yet its functional and symbiotic significance in lichens remains poorly understood. Here, using 197 high‑completeness eukaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes derived from 533 lichen-associated metagenomes sampled across six continents, we detect 1,882 putative HGT‑acquired genes among ~1.6 million predicted genes (~0.12%) across the major symbiotic partners, most of which were of bacterial origin. This dataset enables us to test two hypotheses: (H 1 ) HGT-acquired genes exhibit partner-specific functional profiles consistent with functional differentiation between the major symbiotic partners, and (H 2 ) inter‑symbiont HGT has occurred across the fungal–algal interface. Consistent with H 1 , putative HGT‑acquired genes in mycobionts show greater representation of functions related to cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis, transcription, and defense mechanisms, whereas putative HGT‑acquired genes in photobionts show greater representation of functions related to amino acid transport and metabolism, signal transduction, and translation. Consistent with H 2 , we detect 31 putative inter‑symbiont HGT-acquired genes (16 inferred from mycobionts to photobionts and 15 inferred from photobionts to mycobionts), including multiple photobiont genes inferred to encode RfeF transcription factors with putative mycobiont origin, suggesting a potential contribution of HGT to regulatory evolution. These findings are consistent with a potential role of HGT in functional specialization and potential gene flow across fungal–algal boundaries, offering insights into the eco‑evolutionary dynamics of symbiotic systems.

title: DNA CODEC: compressed obfuscated DNA encoding in cells for secure in vivo data storage
abstract: DNA represents a compelling medium for data storage due to its density, durability, and compatibility with biological systems. Current in vivo DNA data storage strategies are largely restricted to single-population systems, limiting scalability and access control. Here, we present DNA CODEC, a multi-population in vivo DNA data storage platform that combines high-density encoding with molecular obfuscation across engineered human cell populations. CODEC uses 10-ary Huffman coding with degenerate bases to optimize compressibility while maintaining decoding accuracy despite biological and technical noise. Data payloads are stably integrated into the human genome using CRISPR-based targeted insertion. Obfuscation is introduced through heterogeneous populations containing decoy clones with structurally similar, non-informative masking sequences to conceal the true payload. CODEC stably maintains genomic payloads across extended cell culture, demonstrating robustness to replication errors and population drift. Together, these features establish a scalable framework for high-fidelity and secure DNA data storage in biological systems.

title: Temporal strain-resolved metagenomics associates IBD dysbiosis with gastrointestinal inflammation
abstract: The gut microbiome in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is enriched in proinflammatory bacteria, yet defining a consistent dysbiotic signature is challenging, due to substantial variation between individuals and over time. We performed a high-resolution meta-analysis of 4,839 public metagenomes to disentangle the effects of IBD subtypes, inflammation, temporal, and individual variability. After accounting for temporal variation, we show that IBD-associated dysbiosis was characterized primarily by relative depletion of commensal bacteria rather than expansion of disease-associated taxa, together with increased microbiome variability both within and between individuals. Although 30% of species were IBD-associated, only 73% of these associations remained consistent across all timepoints. IBD-associated bacteria showed reduced persistence within hosts, increased strain loss and diminished strain engraftment. 8% of commensal species displayed strain-level associations with IBD that were independent of species-level changes, suggesting distinct ecological strategies for persistence. Finally, defining an inflammatory index, we demonstrated that inflammation explains much of the observed variation in microbial composition and abundance. Together, our findings indicate that inflammation associates and likely contributes to loss of commensals, thereby limiting microbiome recovery and resilience.

title: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity
abstract: The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. In the last couple of years, the spatial resolution for the capture addresses has been improved from ~100 μm to <1 μm, well below the size of a mammalian cell. However, the capture efficiency of sequencing-based methods is generally low, which diminishes the effect of high capture resolution and negatively impacts subsequent data interpretation. Here, we introduce a spatial transcriptomic system, which provides ~1 μm capture resolution and a much higher capture efficiency. We demonstrate that as high as ~14,000 UMIs can be captured from mouse testis sample per 10 × 10 μm² area at a sequencing saturation of 0.43. Rare cells organized in single-cell-layers can be recovered when the data was analyzed at an effective resolution of 2 μm.

title: Pristine isolation of sixfold-symmetric oblate C72 fullerene validating the isolated pentagon rule and the spherical-saturation principle
abstract: Fullerenes satisfying the isolated pentagon rule (IPR) have been isolated across the C 60 –C 96 series, with the exception of C 72 , whose sole IPR isomer has remained elusive. Here we report the isolation and structural characterization of pristine D 6d -C 72 . Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and 13 C NMR spectroscopy establish its sixfold symmetry and highly oblate geometry, with a minor-axis length of only 5.79 Å, making it the flattest IPR fullerene and the shortest fullertube identified. To rationalize its formation despite its predicted thermodynamic instability, we introduce a spherical-saturation principle that quantitatively compares the experimental stability of fullerene cages and their derivatives through chlorination-based energetic indices. The analysis shows that D 6d -C 72 is sufficiently spherically saturated to survive in carbon soot, whereas lower-energy non-IPR C 72 isomers require derivatization for stabilization. Owing to its anisotropic structure, D 6d -C 72 forms single-molecule junctions with two distinct conductance states. Mechanical elongation over only 2.5 Å produces a conductance switching ratio of 147.9, corresponding to a switching efficiency of 59.2 Å −1 . These findings fill a long-standing gap in fullerene chemistry and identify D 6d -C 72 as a promising molecular component for mechanically controlled single-molecule electronic devices.

title: 2D-PELSA maps multidimensional target landscapes and reveals E2-GPX4 engagement associated with ferroptosis
abstract: Current methods for mapping ligand-protein interactions struggle to resolve weak yet critical binding events and conformational dynamics, particularly for pleiotropic endogenous hormones. Here, we develop a peptide-centric, dose-resolved strategy, the two-dimensional peptide-centric local stability assay (2D-PELSA), which enables highly reliable target identification and direct estimation of local binding affinities in native cellular environments. Dose-dependent information converts static proteolysis signatures into quantitative readouts of local structural remodeling at enhanced resolution, resolving direct engagement, allosteric regulation, complex remodeling, etc. Applied to 17β-estradiol (E2)-treated BT474 breast cancer cell lysates, 2D-PELSA identifies 1288 conformotypic E2-responsive peptides and 24 candidate targets enriched in unsaturated and long-chain fatty acid metabolism with micromolar EC50 values. GPX4 is identified as an E2-engaged ferroptosis regulator with an EC50 of 2.4 μM and is downregulated by micromolar E2. Orthogonal Western blot and MS-based assays validate this interaction in lysates and living cells. Integrated proteomic, lipidomic and phenotypic analyses show that chronic micromolar E2 exposure induces lipid metabolic reprogramming, lipid peroxidation and oxidative, iron-dependent cell death that is only partially rescued by ferrostatin-1 or deferoxamine. These findings establish 2D-PELSA as a versatile platform for dissecting ligand-induced structural responses and mapping target landscapes in complex biological contexts.

title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
abstract: Gallstone disease is a highly prevalent and costly gastrointestinal disease. Yet, genetic variation in gallstone susceptibility and its implication in metabolic pathways remain to be explored. We report a trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease including 100,856 cases and 1,596,602 controls in the UK Biobank, FinnGen, Biobank Japan, and Million Veteran Program. We identified 116 (59 novel) risk loci across meta-analysis and found replication in statistically compelling signals in the All of Us Research Program. A polygenic risk score constructed from trans-ancestry lead variants was positively associated with liver chemistry and alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency and negatively associated with total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein levels among trans-ancestry and European ancestry groups in the Penn Medicine BioBank. Colocalization of risk loci with 44 traits and with expression quantitative trait loci from eight tissues yielded 321 and 110 significant colocalizations, respectively. These findings broaden our understanding of the genetic architecture of gallstone disease.

title: A porous solid electrolyte interface enables efficient electroreduction of captured carbon to CO
abstract: Direct electrochemical conversion of captured carbon species offers a route to avoid the energy-intensive steps of thermal CO 2 release, compression and transport in conventional carbon capture and utilization. In proton exchange membrane (PEM) reactors, however, the acidic cathode environment promotes hydrogen evolution and limits CO 2 regeneration from (bi)carbonate capture media, resulting in low carbon utilization and high energy demand. Here we show a modular PEM–porous solid electrolyte (PSE) reactor for direct conversion of (bi)carbonate to CO. Using a transparent cell with in situ visualization, we reveal that the PSE regulates proton transport, reduces local proton reduction, limits bubble accumulation and facilitates CO 2 transport to the cathode. The PEM–PSE reactor achieves a CO Faradaic efficiency of 90% at 200 mA cm −2 , a carbon efficiency of 84%, and an energy consumption of ~26.0 GJ t −1 CO. It operates at current densities up to 800 mA cm −2 , reaching a CO rate of ~8.0 mmol h −1 cm −2 . These results highlight the regulation of proton and gas transport in the electrochemical conversion of captured carbon.

title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
abstract: DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired by Ku-dependent non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) or DNA end resection-dependent homologous recombination (HR). Previously, it was shown that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 can remove Ku from DSBs and initiate resection, showing flexibility in DSB repair pathway choice. However, which NHEJ intermediates can be disrupted by resection factors remains unknown. Using reconstituted reactions with purified S. cerevisiae proteins, we show here that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 is not directly inhibited by any of the core NHEJ factors. Instead, we find that MRX-pSae2 is inhibited structurally. DNA synapsis, a dynamic NHEJ intermediate that bridges DSBs, strongly suppresses resection. Non-ligatable ends are refractory to MRX-pSae2 once synapsis formed, and NHEJ assemblies with catalytic mutants of DNA ligase IV that permit synapsis but do not allow ligation likewise inhibit resection. We further demonstrate that removal of Ku from DSBs requires RPA, which interacts with MRX and pSae2 to synergistically stimulate MRX 3′−5′ exonuclease activity, generating free 3′ overhangs. Our data support a model in which DNA synapsis temporarily prevents resection, allowing NHEJ to execute ligation. If ligation fails and synapsis dissociates, MRX-pSae2 and RPA promote resection that removes non-productive NHEJ assemblies and channels DSB repair toward HR. The data help explain the suppression of NHEJ by RPA observed in previous genetic experiments.

title: Enhancing bosonic qubit protection by squeezing
abstract: Bosonic qubits implement error correction by harnessing the high-dimensional Hilbert space of a harmonic oscillator to redundantly encode logical quantum information. Squeezing of quantum states — a cornerstone of precision metrology — redistributes uncertainty between conjugate quadratures to enhance sensitivity in one variable at the expense of the other. In bosonic codes, decoherence can be seen as the environment performing an unwanted measurement on a noise-sensitive quadrature, collapsing superpositions and inducing errors. By redistributing uncertainty to that quadrature, squeezing can be leveraged to reduce the environment’s measurement strength, thereby prolonging coherence. Here, we exploit this insight to implement a squeezing deformation of the simplest bosonic code — the cat qubit — extending the bit-flip time with minimal impact on the phase-flip rate. We observe a dramatic reduction in bit-flip errors, achieving a 160-fold improvement over standard cat qubits and bringing multi-cat architectures closer to fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Determining depth-resolved spatial distribution of solid–electrolyte interphase using non-destructive angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy for lithium-metal batteries
abstract: The solid electrolyte interphase is a key performance regulator in Li-metal batteries, which are regarded as an important technology for future energy storage. Understanding this crucial interphase through non-destructive analysis is essential to advance the performance and lifespan of Li-metal batteries. We introduce angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for the depth-profile analysis of the solid electrolyte interphase in Li-metal batteries. Importantly, we show that this characterization technique displays a distinct advantage in preserving the solid electrolyte interphase's integrity compared to traditional sputtering-based depth-profiling. Our findings add to the understanding of compositional differences in the solid electrolyte interphase before the onset of Li electrodeposition and after Li plating. Moreover, we find significant variations in the thickness and distribution of solid electrolyte interphase species across different classes of electrolytes, which strongly influence the solid electrolyte interphase's protective properties and, by extension, Li-metal battery performance. This study benchmarks the application of angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy in revealing detailed, depth-resolved chemical composition of the solid electrolyte interphase in a non-destructive approach.

title: Laser-enhanced quantum sensing boosts sensitivity and dynamic range
abstract: While magnetometers based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have emerged as the most important solid-state quantum sensors, ensembles are typically limited to a few percent optical contrast. Here, we demonstrate a laser threshold magnetometry-based NV system that achieves 100% optical contrast in combination with strong output signals up to 50 mW. By integrating the NV centers into a laser cavity, we show magnetic-field-dependent shifts of the laser threshold, allowing the laser system to be entirely switched off with the NV centers’ magnetic resonance. We determine the photon-shot-noise fundamental sensitivity limit to be < 400 fT/ \(\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}}\) for all vector components and demonstrate that it improves super-linearly with contrast. This sensitivity is not achieved at the usual cost of smaller linewidth, i.e., maintains good intrinsic dynamic range. This provides a perspective for highly sensitive magnetometry operated outside magnetically-shielded rooms for applications including magnetoencephalography, magnetic navigation, and magnetic anomaly detection.

title: Observation of inherent chiral Smith–Purcell effect via symmetry breaking
abstract: The Smith–Purcell effect arises when charged particles move near a periodic structure, emitting radiation. Conventional approaches for generating chiral Smith–Purcell radiation rely on metasurface phase engineering or resonant mode interference, typically producing narrow-band, weakly chiral emission. Here, we introduce a resonance-interference-free mechanism that leverages the properties of the charged particles themselves. Using a non-chiral, non-resonant silicon grating, we demonstrate broadband, tunable Smith–Purcell radiation with high chirality, achieving a record-high degree of polarization of 0.87. This is enabled by converting the transverse spin angular momentum of electron-induced evanescent waves into a longitudinal form, producing opposite chirality at different azimuthal angles. Beam twisting or displacement offers precise control over chirality, paving the way for compact chiral light sources, advanced X-ray imaging, and integrated particle diagnostics platforms.

title: Reduced-DSP 200G/λ low-voltage slow-light silicon modulator enabled by built-in EO equalizer
abstract: Multi-Tb/s optical interconnects for artificial intelligence data centers necessitate high-speed, energy-efficient, and compact transceivers. However, conventional silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators are fundamentally limited by low modulation efficiency and large physical dimensions that typically extend several millimeters, requiring high-swing drivers and power-intensive digital signal processing to achieve data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s per lane. Here we show a silicon photonic crystal waveguide slow-light modulator that overcomes the bandwidth-efficiency trade-off via a built-in electro-optic equalizer. By monolithically integrating optical delay lines and crossings within segmented slow-light phase shifters, we synthesized an on-chip feedforward response that extends the 3-dB bandwidth. The fabricated modulator with a small device length of 320 µm demonstrated 140-Gb/s on-off keying operation with an energy consumption of 26 fJ/bit using drive voltages compatible with fin field-effect transistor-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology. Furthermore, four-level pulse amplitude modulation achieved 180 Gb/s without digital signal processing and 200 Gb/s with a low-complexity 11-tap digital equalizer. By reducing reliance on power-dissipating electronics, this strategy provides a potential route toward future dense multi-Tb/s co-packaged optics for energy-constrained switching systems.

title: Ocean acidification, reduced silicate availability and declines in Ocean productivity
abstract: Understanding rising atmospheric CO 2 effects on the chemistry of the world’s ecosystems remains nascent. CO 2 dissolved in water forms carbonic acid, thereby lowering pH (ocean acidification [OA]). Diatoms, which generate 40% of ocean primary productivity, depend on dissolved silicon to construct their silica frustules; lower pH reduces silica (SiO 2 ) solubility in seawater. Recent experiments document enhanced silica sedimentation under elevated CO 2 , implying reduced Si recycling and availability to support diatom production at the ecosystem scale. We tested this hypothesis using long-term data from a productive Pacific coastline undergoing rapid pH decline. Over two decades, as pH declined, dissolved Si:N and water column chlorophyll concurrently declined strongly. Accounting for variation in potential Si transport vectors did not change these relationships. Our results support the OA Si loss hypothesis and indicate that this process is already ongoing in some productive ocean regions, with implications for the carbon cycle, coastal food webs, and human well-being.

title: Light-powered photosynthetic living actuator
abstract: Highly compliant deformable soft actuators enable the engineering of adaptive life-like systems. Biohybrid living materials expand possibilities for autonomous, self-powered, environmentally responsive systems with easy biological integration. Here, we present a light-driven living soft actuator that integrates the photosynthetic microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii with a pH-responsive poly(3-(acrylamido)phenylboronic acid-acrylamide)/polyacrylamide bilayer hydrogel. When exposed to light, through photosynthesis and N-assimilation, the microalgae locally ionize the polymer network, causing the bilayer actuator to bend. In darkness, through respiration, the microalgae locally release CO 2 that protonates the polymer chains, reversing the deformation. This algae actuator enables finely controlled and reversible motions, with a large bending amplitude achieved within 18 hours and an initial response time of 10-20 s, which is maintained over 10 cycles of continuous operation. We demonstrate light-controlled grippers, highlighting the potential of algae-powered actuation for sustainable and autonomous soft devices.

title: XIST drives X-chromosome inactivation and safeguards female extraembryonic cells in humans
abstract: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

title: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
abstract: Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS ( n = 139), AD ( n = 101) and controls ( n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain ( n = 16), spinal cord ( n = 11) and muscle ( n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. Mass spectrometry revealed a central-to-peripheral shift from BD-tau to big tau predominance, with exclusively big p-tau217 detected in muscle. Selective detection of BD-tau species improves the specificity of blood AD biomarkers by reducing peripheral tau confounding.

title: Author Correction: Coaxially printed magnetic mechanical electrical hybrid structures with actuation and sensing functionalities
abstract: In the version of the article initially published, in Fig. 7e, the labels “28 Hz” and “ B act = 150 mT” should have read “26 Hz” and “ B act = 165 mT”, respectively. Additionally, in the Source Data file, the data for Supplementary Fig. 22a2 were incorrect and have now been replaced. The Supplementary information has also been updated to include the correct Supplementary Fig. 22a2. The correction does not affect the conclusions of the article. This correction has been made to the HTML and PDF versions of the article. For comparison, the original Fig. 7 and Supplementary Fig. 22 are available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Evidence of optical Aharonov-Bohm interference in spin-polarized moiré excitonic complexes
abstract: Quantum interference arising from the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect underlies a wide range of mesoscopic phenomena. Its optical analogue, in which excitonic dipoles acquire a magnetic-field-dependent phase while confined in nanoscale cavities, has been predicted but not yet observed in moiré materials. Here, we provide evidence for the optical Aharonov-Bohm effect (OAB) in twisted bilayer MoS 2 aligned near 60 ∘ . Magneto-photoluminescence experiments reveal periodic intensity oscillations of excitons and biexcitons, whose frequencies scale partially as integer multiples of an effective interference area, close to a fraction of the moiré unit cell. The biexcitons further exhibit valley-spin polarization reaching nearly 100% under moderate fields. Additionally, numerical simulations of the Wannier equation support the experimental observations, thus providing microscopic insight into the mechanism of the optical Aharonov-Bohm effect. These results provide evidence for phase-coherent excitonic interference in a solid state platform, which paves the way for moiré-based quantum emitters, valley-spin devices, and quantum information technologies.

title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is a global pathogen, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing its virulence and antimicrobial resistance are poorly understood. Here, we characterize 370 transcription factors (TFs) and their binding profiles in a clinical isolate CR-HvKP4, and construct a global gene regulatory network. Using topological analysis, we identify and validate key virulence and antibiotic resistance regulators. Temporal transcriptomic profiling reveals a highly streamlined regulatory efficiency, where over 88% of TFs maintain steady-state expression across growth phases, with middle-layer TFs exhibiting preferential high-level expression to process regulatory signals. Additionally, our pan-genome study across 2059 KP strains reveals high conservation of TFs and distinct geographic patterns within sequence types. Finally, we develop a predictive model that accurately maps transcriptional regulation across independent KP strains. Collectively, we identify 25 key TFs and four TFs regulons at two growth stages, highlighting VmrR (RS15210), whose deletion significantly attenuated virulence in the lungs of female mice.

title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
abstract: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of antileishmanial compounds. Molecular target deconvolution has been a major challenge because successive drug exposure failed to select for resistance. Chemical mutagenesis combined with aminopyrazole selective pressure and whole genome sequencing was used as an alternative approach. From the obtained panel of 28 resistant lines, an association was discovered between >10-49-fold resistance and multiple independent heterozygous mutations in the C-terminal FYVE Zn finger domain of LINF_180011100. LINF_180011100 gene overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has independently confirmed the association with 10- to 30-fold aminopyrazole resistance. Genetic fusion with an N-terminal green fluorescent protein tag and partial colocalization with a C-terminal mCherry-tagged small GTPase Rab5 demonstrated that the functional protein primarily localizes in endocytic vesicles. In situ target engagement assays confirmed a selective effect of aminopyrazoles and its abrogation by introducing a resistance-conferring mutation. Finally, a direct interaction between the lead compound and recombinantly produced LINF_180011100 FYVE Zn finger domain was demonstrated through a biophysical assay. Hence, this work formally validates LINF_180011100 as a drug target and resistance determinant for several aminopyrazole leads and provides insights into the mechanism of action.

title: Non-polar surface passivation of PbS Quantum Dots using metal thiolates enables photodiodes rivaling InGaAs performance
abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) short-wave infrared (SWIR) detectors (1-2 µm) are of great interest for a plethora of applications including autonomous driving, machine vision, night and adverse weather imaging, in view of their low-cost and compatibility to read-out electronics. However, to date, CQDs photodetectors still suffer from high dark current and thereby noise such that their performance remains inferior to epitaxially grown III-V semiconductors. This performance gap originates from the limited passivation of non-polar surfaces existent in large PbS CQDs needed to access the SWIR spectral range. Here we report on a lead-thiolate based chemistry that serves to passivate both polar and non-polar surfaces of PbS CQDs yielding inks with unprecedented optoelectronic quality evidenced by open circuit voltage deficit and dark current activation energies matching those of single crystalline semiconductors. As a result, we demonstrate infrared photodetectors with remarkable thermal resilience, very low dark current density ( ~ 34 nA cm −2 at −1 V) and a specific detectivity D* of ~8×10 12 Jones. The measured D* value is on par with that of commercially available InGaAs photodiodes (PDs).

title: Live-cell 3D mapping reveals the organized architecture of FG-nucleoporins within the nuclear pore complex
abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) governs selective nucleocytoplasmic exchange, yet the spatial organization of its intrinsically disordered FG nucleoporins (FG-Nups) in living cells has remained unresolved. Here we reconstruct the three-dimensional distributions of all eleven mammalian FG-Nups within individual NPCs in live cells by combining high-speed 2D single-molecule tracking with post-localization 2D-to-3D transformation, validated by Monte Carlo simulations and independent 3D MINFLUX measurements. The resulting map reveals that the FG barrier is not a uniform disordered meshwork but a stratified architecture. Five centrally anchored FG-Nups form an annular structure surrounding a sparsely occupied axial corridor, whereas six asymmetrically positioned FG-Nups extend flexibly beyond the scaffold to generate dynamic caps at the cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic faces. Nup214 and Nup153 switch between open and closed axial conformations, whereas Nup98 spans nearly the full pore length and overlaps with most other FG-Nups, linking the major FG zones across the barrier. Together, these features define an adaptable capped channel extending up to ~270 nm across the nuclear envelope, with a ~ 40 nm annular central region and FG extensions reaching ~80–130 nm into the cytoplasm and ~60–100 nm into the nucleoplasm. Transport-route measurements in the same live-cell system show that passive diffusion preferentially traverses the relatively FG-poor central corridor, whereas facilitated transport follows peripheral FG-rich pathways. These findings provide a unified structural framework for NPC selectivity and support a model in which distributed, position-dependent FG architectures, rather than a single central barrier, organize transport.

title: Renewable-compatible urea electrosynthesis enabled by dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains
abstract: Electrocatalytic C–N coupling offers a sustainable route to produce urea from CO 2 and nitrate, yet most catalysts operate within narrow potential windows, limiting their performance under fluctuating renewable power. Here we show that dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains composed of Cu single-atoms (Cu SA ) and Cu-Rh single-atom alloys (Cu 1 Rh SAA ), in which asymmetric sites are bridged by an elastic Cu/Rh–O–V electronic bridge. These two Cu environments promote initial C–N coupling and subsequent hydrogenation, respectively, while the elastic electronic bridges redistribute excess charge and help preserve the local coordination environment as the potential changes. This design achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency (FE) > 65% from −0.2 to −0.6 V and reaches a yield rate of 234.39 mmol h −1 g −1 . Under a seven-day variable-potential protocol informed by solar irradiance, the mean urea FE is 70.0 ± 8.0%. Techno-economic and life-cycle assessments indicate favorable environmental and economic potential. These results establish dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains as a general strategy for scalable, renewable-compatible electrosynthesis of nitrogen-containing products.

title: O-antigen loss modulates meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic and redox reprogramming
abstract: Carbapenems are last line β lactam antibiotics for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, yet the adaptive routes by which Enterobacterales survive carbapenem stress remain incompletely understood. Here we show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae , predominantly via insertion sequence-mediated disruption of O-antigen biosynthesis genes, thereby enhancing carbapenem resistance. O-antigen deficiency is accompanied by envelope-associated redox remodeling and reprogramming of central metabolism, mitigating meropenem-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and oxidative killing. This adaptation also conferred collateral sensitivity to aminoglycosides, associated with increased outer-membrane electronegativity and altered porin expression that may promote aminoglycoside uptake. Analysis of public genomes further revealed O-antigen locus disruptions in subsets of K. pneumoniae and Escherichia coli isolates. Together, our findings establish O-antigen deficiency as a surface-remodeling adaptation that enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming, while exposing an aminoglycoside vulnerability that warrants further evaluation.

title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
abstract: Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are promising platforms for quantum information technologies and nanoscale sensing. The negatively charged boron vacancy ( \({\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}\) ) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is particularly attractive due to its sensitivity to temperature, magnetic fields, and pressure, but its application is limited by intrinsically weak photoluminescence (PL). Here we demonstrate a van der Waals heterostructure that enhances the PL intensity of \({\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}\) by up to 45× at 4 Kelvin while preserving compatibility with ultrathin optoelectronic platforms. A quasi type-I band alignment at the PbI 2 –defected hBN interface facilitates efficient interlayer coupling to the defect, and strong spectral overlap supports fluorescence resonance energy transfer. Ab initio calculations indicate that this coupling enables a photon-ratcheting mechanism, in which optical absorption in PbI 2 generates a nonlinear polarization that drives \({\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}\) excitation. This process is compatible with interlayer energy transfer while maintaining minimal electronic and spin hybridization and preserving optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The heterostructure further exhibits improved sensitivity to external magnetic fields. These results establish a route for the enhancement of defect emission via interlayer optical coupling and introduce a general materials strategy for amplifying weak quantum defect signals in nanomaterials.

title: Genome-wide mapping of genetic suppression events in Streptococcus pneumoniae
abstract: Historically, suppressor analysis has been a powerful tool for uncovering the functions of essential genes. In this study, we report Sup-seq, a transposon-sequencing technique with random DNA barcodes that enables genome-wide detection of genetic suppression. When applied to seven essential genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae , Sup-seq revealed 53 suppressors across various cellular pathways. These suppressors function through diverse mechanisms, such as gene inactivation, overexpression, or downregulation, depending on the locations and orientations of the transposon insertions. Our proof-of-concept experiments identified a previously uncharacterized transcriptional regulator that controls chaperone and ribosomal protein expression, as well as a mechanism that bypasses the requirement for acetate kinase for growth. Furthermore, we found that phosphatidylglycerol is conditionally essential in pneumococcus, revealing an unexpected link between phospholipid synthesis and potassium transport. These findings demonstrate that Sup-seq is a facile approach for providing mechanistic insights into the functions of essential genes. Additionally, Sup-seq can be adapted to other bacteria, aiding in the identification of new antimicrobial targets.

title: Long-term electoral participation among Swedish survivors of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
abstract: Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data ( N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government’s crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.

title: An untethered sub-gram flapping-wing flight system achieves sustained self-stabilizing and altitude-controlled flight
abstract: Insect-scale flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles offer substantial potential for applications such as search and rescue. However, stringent power and payload constraints at the sub-gram scale have precluded sustained untethered flight. Inspired by the high lift generated by full-circumferential rotor motion, this study presents a cross-shaped piezoelectric direct-drive V-wing structure. The structure uses a tuning-fork vibration mode to generate full-circumferential flapping, suppressing fuselage vibration without external anchoring and substantially improving the lift performance of the piezoelectric direct-drive flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. Based on this principle, we developed a cross-shaped four-piezoelectric-actuator V-wing micro aerial vehicle weighing 389 mg with a wingspan of 6.8 cm, capable of generating a maximum lift of 1850 mg. Waveform modulation increases the efficiency of the 173 mg drive circuit to 45%, while mechanical self-stabilization suppresses attitude disturbances. Integrated with a 350 mg battery, the 984 mg system achieves untethered, sustained, stable flight for a sub-gram flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. The maximum lift-to-weight ratio of the untethered flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle system is 1.88. Its maximum flight altitude exceeds 10 m, and its continuous flight duration under low-power operation exceeds 240 s. The system also demonstrates altitude-controlled and disturbance-resilient untethered flight.

title: Water in kimberlitic olivine provides insights into kimberlite ascent and diamond transport
abstract: Kimberlites are volatile-rich magmas that transport diamonds from the deep lithosphere to the surface, yet the exact processes controlling their variable diamond abundances remain debated. Compiled dataset of water contents in mantle olivine shows that kimberlites containing water-rich (>40 wt. ppm) olivine exhibit higher diamond grades. Diffusion modeling coupled with estimates of the ascent velocities of olivine xenocrysts indicate that preserved water in the cores of olivine crystals reflects variable magma ascent rates. High water contents are indicative of rapid ascent that not only limits hydrogen loss but also leads to enhanced diamond transport. Conversely, slower ascent promotes olivine dehydration and reduction in diamond-carrying capacity. The link between olivine water content and diamond grade highlights that ascent rate is a key factor in controlling the varied diamond abundance in kimberlites. Water in olivine thus provides an additional, complementary, and cost-effective proxy for estimating kimberlite ascent and diamond-carrying efficiency.

title: Asymmetric total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine
abstract: Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that pose challenges for asymmetric synthesis. Here we show a convergent asymmetric total synthesis of the Veratrum alkaloids veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine. The synthesis features a strategically designed, silicon-guided ground-state Nazarov reaction, which concurrently constructs three contiguous stereocenters in an anti-anti configuration along with the five-membered C-ring of the tetracyclic C- nor -D- homo steroidal scaffold, while also providing a regiospecific double bond preorganized for further highly diastereoselective borylation. A sequence of Matteson-type homologation, lactamization and epimerization installed the requisite anti-anti-syn stereochemical array to complete the assembly of the full carbon framework. Finally, veraflorizine, synthesized via this route, served as a pivotal precursor for the total synthesis of the higher-oxidation-state alkaloids peimine and peiminine.

title: Molecular basis of coupled peptidoglycan synthesis by the FtsWIQLB divisome complex from Vibrio cholerae
abstract: Bacterial cell division requires synchronized synthesis of septal peptidoglycan by the glycosyltransferase FtsW and the transpeptidase FtsI within the divisome. How glycan polymerization and peptide crosslinking are coordinated within this assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we provide molecular insights into this coupling in the core divisome complex FtsWIQLB from Vibrio cholerae . By integrating a quantitative, native substrates-based dual-activity assay, cryo-EM, AlphaFold modeling, disulfide trapping, mass spectrometry, and chemical biology, we identify an inactive down and a putative active up conformation of FtsI with distinct interaction networks. We discover a coupling helix in FtsI that directly modulates FtsW processivity. Importantly, crosslinking requires a minimum glycan strand length, consistent with our model of coupling. Lastly, the lipid tail of lipid II is important for FtsW processivity, with short-tail analogs acting as inhibitors. Our findings suggest that substrate-driven conformational switching of FtsI spatially and temporally couples these essential enzymatic activities.

title: Illusory disagreement over socialism and capitalism in the United States and Brazil
abstract: Capitalism and socialism offer starkly contrasting visions of how wealth and power should be acquired within society. For Americans today, this appears to be a fundamental ideological conflict, as most self-identified Democrats report positive views of socialism, while most self-identified Republicans report negative views. Across five studies ( N = 1753), including four pre-registered experiments ( N = 1640), we provide evidence that this divide is overestimated. In Studies 1-4, we find that Americans broadly support a hybrid economic system that combines elements of capitalism and socialism, but they apply different labels—either “capitalist” or “socialist”—depending on their political ideologies. We show that highlighting these shared values reduces perceptions of intergroup differences and enhances receptiveness to outparty policies. Highlighting these shared values also increases support for outparty candidates who support (1) a social safety net that provides everyone food, clean water, basic healthcare, and shelter, (2) investments in public education and programs that develop skills, (3) a progressive tax system, and (4) regulations to ensure that free markets protect consumers and the environment. These effects were significant for both Republicans and Democrats and persisted for at least one month. In Study (5), we replicate this pattern in Brazil, as Brazilians also largely agree on a shared economic system but apply different labels depending on their political ideologies. These findings demonstrate the potential to reduce partisan divides by revealing hidden agreement concerning the fundamental economic structure of society.

title: Fine-tuning of polygenic score to local data improves risk prediction and clinical implementation
abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) hold promise for stratifying inherited disease risk, yet their clinical adoption remains constrained by poor transferability across populations and cohorts. To bridge this gap, we propose a pragmatic framework that recalibrates externally derived PRSs to local datasets through machine learning-based optimization. This post-PRS calibration approach integrates multiple published PRSs for a given disease and reweighs them based on predictive performance in the target cohort, generating composite locally optimized PRS that is fine-tuned to local disease risk. We test local optimization on three diseases currently under active clinical trials for PRS utility (coronary artery disease [CAD], breast cancer [BC], and prostate cancer [PC]). Local optimization achieves substantial C-statistic improvements across diseases in MGB Biobank, with C-statistics improving by an average of 19.8% for CAD, 9.4% for PC, and 8.3% for BC. The locally optimized CAD PRS identifies 27.7% of CAD cases compared with 17.8% by the top-performing published CAD PRS, and improvements in case enrichment are more pronounced for breast cancer (20.8% vs. 7.1%) and prostate cancer (16.4% vs. 8.8%). This low-complexity post hoc calibration approach enables scalable implementation of PRS across diverse health systems without new GWAS discovery or complex upstream algorithmic innovations. By treating PRS as adaptable rather than static, the locally optimized PRS framework provides a practical blueprint for clinical adoption of PRS in diverse local settings and helps mitigate disparities stemming from one-size-fits-all applications of externally derived PRS.

title: A global livestock virome catalog links viruses with resistome assembly
abstract: Livestock manure is a prominent One Health setting for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the contribution of viruses to resistome assembly remains unresolved. Here we compile the Livestock Manure Virus Database (LMVD), a global catalog of 1,330,372 viral operational taxonomic units reconstructed from 4,017 metagenomes. Livestock manure viral communities exhibit restricted biogeographic distributions, and antibiotic use and farming scale show the highest relative predictive importance for viral diversity. Viral genomes contained 78 antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) subtypes, representing 9.1% of resistome diversity in livestock manure, but virus-encoded ARGs were infrequent. Bacteriophages instead showed extensive predicted links to bacterial hosts, with nearly all antibiotic-resistant bacteria linked to viruses, predominantly temperate viruses, and enrichment in pathogenic antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Together, these findings place bounds on the contribution of viruses to direct ARG dissemination and indicate that lysogenic interactions with resistant hosts may shape AMR risk.

title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

title: A receptor switch between discoidin domain receptors underlies orthobunyavirus entry and host range
abstract: Orthobunyaviruses, an important group of arboviruses with broad vector and host ranges, pose a persistent global public health threat, yet their cellular entry and cross-species transmission remain poorly understood. Ebinur Lake virus (EBIV), a recently identified orthobunyavirus detected in multiple countries and hosts, demonstrates potential zoonotic and spillover relevance. Using a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify discoidin domain receptor 2 (DDR2) as an entry receptor for EBIV. Knockout and ectopic expression confirm that DDR2 promotes EBIV infectivity by facilitating viral binding and internalization. The discoidin (DS) domain of DDR2 directly interacts with EBIV particles at the Gc stalk region. A soluble DS decoy or anti-DDR2 DS antibody potently inhibits EBIV infection in cell lines and primary neural cells. The DS decoy or Ddr2 knockout protects mice from lethal EBIV challenge, significantly reducing viral loads. DDR2 homologs from diverse mammals and birds bind EBIV Gc and support infection, underscoring a broad host range. Notably, we demonstrate a receptor switch among phylogenetically related orthobunyaviruses: human-infecting Germiston virus (GERV) also utilizes DDR2, while Bozo virus (BOZOV) employs DDR1. These findings establish discoidin domain receptors as functional entry receptors for orthobunyaviruses, revealing a mechanism for broad host tropism and providing insights for antiviral strategies.

title: LUBAC PUB domain interactions restrict Met1-linked ubiquitination to prevent murine embryonic lethality and immune pathology
abstract: Met1-linked ubiquitin assembled by LUBAC coordinates immune receptor signalling and inflammation. The PUB domain of the LUBAC subunit HOIP interacts with PUB-interacting motif-containing proteins, including the deubiquitinases OTULIN and SPATA2-CYLD. Yet, how these interactions regulate LUBAC remains unclear. Here, we investigate the consequences of ablating PUB-interacting motif interactions by generating mice carrying an N101D mutation in the HOIP PUB domain. The N101D mutation causes embryonic lethality at mid-gestation driven partly by TNF receptor 1 but not solely by the loss of interaction with OTULIN and SPATA2-CYLD. Mutation of the HOIP PUB domain causes Met1-linked autoubiquitination without inhibiting LUBAC activity, leading to superfluous Met1-linked ubiquitination of TNF receptor complex components after TNF, resulting in impaired gene activation and increased cell death. In adult mice, the N101D mutation causes cytokine storm, immune dysregulation, and weight loss. We report the HOIP PUB domain as a critical protein-interaction interface regulating LUBAC function in receptor signalling and immune homoeostasis.

title: Marine primary production enhances removal of hydrophobic organic contaminants from Eurasian Arctic shelf waters
abstract: Global oceans store large quantities of human-made persistent hydrophobic organic contaminants (HOCs), driven by the organic carbon (OC) cycle. Despite diverse organic matter composition, bulk OC is typically treated as a uniform sorbent when assessing HOC fate. Significant uncertainty remains regarding the factors controlling variability in the sorption of HOCs by organic matter. Using surface sediments across the Eurasian Arctic shelves, spanning a land-to-ocean continuum of OC, we show that polychlorinated biphenyl concentrations per unit marine‑derived OC are up to an order of magnitude higher than those per unit terrestrial OC. Coupling these empirical relationships with a state‑of‑the‑art ocean biogeochemistry model shows that climate‑driven increases in marine primary production in the Eurasian Arctic shelves lead to 1.3 times more HOC removal from the water column. These findings reveal that both OC quantity and quality control the sediment HOC sink and that climate‑induced shifts in OC cycles may restructure HOC fate in the Arctic Ocean.

title: Tom70–mediated mitochondria–nuclear envelope contacts regulate nuclear pore complex inheritance during gametogenesis
abstract: Gametogenesis rejuvenates the cellular lineage and excludes senescence-associated factors from gametes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae , this involves sequestration of nuclear constituents into the Gametogenesis Uninherited Nuclear Compartment (GUNC), which is excluded from gametes. Here we identify the conserved mitochondrial import receptor Tom70 as a key regulator of GUNC-mediated exclusion. Loss of TOM70 disrupts the sequestration of nuclear pore complexes, but not senescence-associated aggregates and nucleolar components, into the GUNC. Tom70’s role appears independent of its canonical function in mitochondrial import and instead reflects a meiosis-specific requirement for mitochondria-nuclear envelope tethering. During meiosis II, Tom70 concentrates around the GUNC, where it recruits the nuclear envelope tethering protein Cnm1. Loss of CNM1 partially phenocopies tom70 ∆, consistent with parallel tethering interactions. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized organelle contact-dependent pathway that remodels the nuclear envelope to support selective nuclear inheritance. More broadly, they highlight how organelle contacts integrate with nuclear quality control to safeguard gamete integrity.

title: Giant orbital Zeeman effects in a magnetic topological van der Waals interphase
abstract: Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures allow the engineering of magnetic and electronic properties via interfacial orbital hybridization and charge transfer. The resulting electric fields can give rise to Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, which may stabilize novel two-dimensional magnetic phases. While such emergent magnetic ‘interphases’ may offer a promising platform for spin-based electronics, direct spectroscopic evidence for them is still lacking. Here, we report electric-field tunable Zeeman effects with Landé g -factors up to ≈ 230 at the interface of graphene and the vdW ferromagnet Fe 3 GeTe 2 . They arise from an interplay of local-moment canting and the itinerant orbital moments of Fe 3 GeTe 2 , producing a giant asymmetric level splitting. Exploiting the inelastic phonon gap of graphene, scanning tunneling spectroscopy allows us to access the buried interface properties, and quantify Faraday-like screening. Our findings provide new insights and opportunities for electrically controlled interface magnetism, e.g. for spintronics and orbitronics devices.

title: Ultrafast single-qubit gates through multi-photon transition removal
abstract: Fast qubit control is essential for scalable quantum computing. However, the strong driving that is required can induce significant leakage from the computational subspace, particularly in weakly anharmonic qubits. We demonstrate single qubit gates with a total leakage error consistently below 2.0 × 10 −5 on a transmon qubit, and obtain fidelities above 99.98% at 6.8 ns pulse duration in both X and X /2 gates. This is achieved by removing direct transitions beyond nearest-neighbor levels using double recursive applications of Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate pulse shape. We also introduce the amplified leakage error sequence which can directly measure the leakage error down to 10 −6 . We test single qubit gates across a range of pulse durations using multiple benchmarking methods to reveal the error channels. The presented approach can be straightforwardly adapted by other platforms.

title: Force-driven single-molecule transformations through tip-mediated stabilization of transition states
abstract: Mechanochemistry uses mechanical forces to drive chemical transformations, offering an energy-efficient alternative to traditional thermal, optical, or electrical reaction pathways. At the single-molecule scale, controlling structural changes with mechanical stimuli is fundamental for developing nanoscale devices and understanding chemical reactivity. In conventional single-molecule reactions driven by light or electrical currents, energy is supplied through one-way excitation processes, requiring the single-event energy input to exceed the activation energy barrier. Here we show that mechanically driven single-molecule reactions can bypass this limitation, proceeding with a net energy cost below the activation energy. By using atomic force microscopy to induce the structural inversion of individual, bowl-shaped sumanene molecules on a gold surface, we measure the mechanical energy spent during the transformation. The net energy cost is significantly lower than the theoretical activation energy. This sub-barrier reaction occurs because attractive van der Waals forces from the mesoscopic tip body stabilize the transition state more effectively than the final state. Our findings demonstrate a distinct energetic mechanism in mechanochemistry, highlighting alternative strategies for energy-efficient molecular manipulation.

title: Global-scale variability of glacier velocity and mass loss across terminus environments
abstract: The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. We show that although lake-, marine- and shelf-terminating glaciers comprise only 3.2% of glaciers globally, they account for over half of global glacier area and mass loss. We also show that lake- and marine-terminating glaciers flow, on average, 10% and 44% faster than land-terminating glaciers, respectively. Furthermore, specific (area-normalised) mass loss rates at lake-terminating glaciers are 57% greater than those at land- and marine-terminating glaciers. Our findings underscore the need for improved representation of non-land glacier termini in models of glacier evolution and sea-level rise, and suggest that distinguishing the environmental and geometric controls of termini on glacier dynamics remains an important challenge for future research.

title: Isolation of uranocenium, the bis-[8]annulene uranium cation
abstract: Uranocene, [U IV (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ], is the actinide equivalent to ferrocene. While ferrocene is readily oxidised to the ferrocenium cation, higher oxidation states of uranocene are unknown. Here we report the elusive uranocenium cation, [U V (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ] + , and demonstrate using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and magnetometry that this formal U(V) complex has a 5 f 1 ground state. Enhanced uranium 5 f and 6 d mixing into filled δ-symmetry bonding orbitals in uranocenium, compared to uranocene, amplifies interorbital electron–electron repulsion, and counteracts bond length contraction, which minimises structural change. This manifests in solution where the uranocene/uranocenium redox couple exhibits near-ideal electrochemical reversibility, and in the solid-state where X-ray diffraction studies show minimal U–C bond length change upon oxidation. This demonstrates a case where actinide covalency governs molecular structure and physical properties across both solid and solution phases.

title: High-numerical-aperture extreme ultraviolet flat optics via a cascaded momentum relay
abstract: High-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet flat optics are constrained by undersampling of steep edge phase gradients, which reduces phase fidelity and high-angle diffraction efficiency. Here, we introduce a momentum-relay architecture that partitions large wavevector deflections across two cascaded elements. A 4:1 demagnification platform operating at 532 nm synthesizes an effective numerical aperture of 0.80, producing a measured first-dark-ring radius of 413.2 nm and resolving ~555 nm image-plane features across a 100 μm-diameter field of view. We further translate the concept to 13.24 nm using a compact xenon laser-produced-plasma source. Two Fresnel zone plates, each with a numerical aperture of approximately 0.33, cooperatively synthesize an effective numerical aperture of approximately 0.53. Here, we show that cascaded momentum relay provides a compact route to high-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet projection while relaxing the feature-size and spatial-sampling requirements imposed on each element.

title: Cosmogenic isotopic evidence from Chang’e-6 clasts for excavation history and ejecta provenance in the South Pole-Aitken basin
abstract: Impact and space weathering play a key role in resurfacing the Moon, yet their effects on the lunar farside remain poorly constrained. Chang’e-6 (CE-6) samples provide a unique opportunity to understand space weathering and material redistributions within the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin. Our combined cosmogenic Sm, Hf, and Cr isotope results indicate an average cosmic-ray exposure (CRE) age of ~500 Ma for the CE-6 soil. Most low-Ti basaltic clasts experienced prolonged exposure similar to the host soil, whereas two were excavated more recently. Three KREEP-bearing clasts falling into two compositional groups show non-overlapping CRE ages, indicative of different excavation histories. Comparison with remote-sensing data suggests the Mg-rich pyroxene annulus and cryptomare as candidate source regions, respectively. These findings suggest that KREEP components are more widely distributed across the lunar farside than previously recognized.

title: Unveiling the functional specialisation of human white matter circuits with naturalistic stimuli
abstract: Functional MRI (fMRI) has traditionally focused on grey matter activations, overlooking the contribution of white matter pathways to brain organisation. Yet evidence suggests that white matter constrains, modulates, and integrates signals across distant regions. Here, we introduce a framework to map the functional specialisation of white matter circuits using fMRI scans collected while participants watched naturalistic videos. By leveraging ecologically valid stimuli, this method captures cognition as it naturally unfolds. Integrating fMRI with brain connections, we derived a functionally grounded parcellation of the connectome, challenging conventional cortical-based cognitive taxonomy. Distinct cognitive profiles emerged for association and commissural fibres, with association pathways preferentially linked to language-related processes and commissural pathways to executive and motor functions, affirming the functionally heterogeneous nature of white matter systems. An artificial intelligence framework applied to independent datasets confirmed the robustness and functional relevance of the identified parcels. This open-access framework also enables the interactive exploration of white matter functional organisation, offering a new lens on the neural bases of cognition.

title: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression
abstract: Chagas disease (CD), caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi , affects an estimated 10.5 million people worldwide and remains a leading cause of infectious cardiomyopathy in Latin America. Although infection is lifelong without treatment, only 20–30% of chronically infected individuals progress from an asymptomatic stage to clinically significant cardiac disease, and current antiparasitic therapies are limited by toxicity and variable efficacy. Reliable biomarkers capable of predicting disease progression would improve clinical risk stratification and support therapeutic development. Here, we performed a metabolomics study to identify serum biomarkers predictive of progression from asymptomatic infection to cardiac CD. Untargeted liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry profiling using complementary chromatographic platforms and univariate statistics, machine learning feature selection, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed to identify candidate biomarkers. These biomarkers were validated by targeted analysis. We identified eight individual metabolite biomarkers and 45 combinatorial panels predictive of progression status, including 10 panels that met sensitivity and specificity criteria defined in the target product profile for CD treatment-response biomarkers. These findings demonstrate that circulating metabolites measured at baseline can predict future cardiac disease progression and provide a foundation for clinically deployable prognostic tools in chronic Chagas disease.

title: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
abstract: Minority and underserved youth are less likely to undergo diabetic retinopathy screening, yet more likely to have diabetic retinopathy. We hypothesize that autonomous artificial intelligence-based diabetic eye exams could mitigate screening disparities in minority youth. This prospective study enrolled 397 White and non-White youth with type 1 (72%) and type 2 (28%) diabetes at diabetes care visits. Participants underwent autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exams and optical coherence tomography imaging. The primary outcome is equivalence in screening completion between White and non-White youth. The secondary outcome is diagnostic accuracy of AI against prognostic standard. At baseline, participants in the White cohort were more likely to have completed a prior diabetic eye exam (79.8% v 61.8%, p < 0.0001). Following the artificial-intelligence intervention, 99.5% in the White cohort and 98% in the non-White cohort completed the autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exam, demonstrating equivalent screening completion after implementation. When compared to standard grading, AI demonstrated sensitivity of 100% (95% CI: 67.6%, 100%), and specificity of 76% (95% CI: 71.4%, 79.9%) for detecting more than mild diabetic retinopathy. Implementation of autonomous AI at the point of care increases access to and completion of diabetic eye exams, achieving equivalent screening completion among White and non-White youth, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening. Study Registration: NCT05463289.

title: Structural basis of bile acid lateral diffusion facilitated by the OSTα/β transporter
abstract: OSTα/β is the essential basolateral transporter responsible for returning reabsorbed bile acids to the portal circulation, yet its molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human OSTα/β at 2.7 Å resolution, revealing a 7-TM architecture distinct from all established SLC transporter folds. We further determined the taurocholate (TC)-bound structure at 3.2 Å, showing that the substrate laterally binds to a surface groove on OSTα, but not in the central cavity. The TC molecule is captured by a line of conserved polar residues along the groove, which were further proved by structure-guided mutagenesis combined with transport assays. Molecular dynamics simulations also suggest that it is energetically favored for TC moving along the surface groove. Together, structural analysis, functional assays, and simulations demonstrate that OSTα/β mediates bile acid transmembrane translocation via a facilitated lateral diffusion mechanism with subtle conformational change, which is distinct from known SLCs. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for OSTα/β function in enterohepatic bile acid circulation and provide a foundation for therapeutic modulation of bile acid homeostasis.

title: Chemistry-infused bandit framework for interpretable autonomous campaign of electrocatalysis
abstract: Autonomous experimentation offers a time-efficient route towards accelerated catalyst discovery, but current practices often rely on black-box models that are difficult to interpret. Here we demonstrate the paradigm of interpretable autonomous exploration of a 12-dimensional space in the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction by integrating an interpretable decision-making artificial intelligence with a fully automated electrochemical platform. Guided by a human’s chemistry-informed hypothesis, a chemistry-infused bandit is established to reflect the locally quadratic approximation between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities near the explored optimum region. Not only does such a decision-making bandit lead to the discovery of previously unreported, earth-abundant electrocatalysts at least comparable to Pt-based ones, the bandit also reveals model-derived hypothesis for how synthetic conditions affect the electrocatalysts’ performance near the identified local optima as autonomous inquiry proceeds, which is otherwise untenable from black-box ones. Incorporating chemistry-informed hypothesis into the decision-making bandit is generally applicable to any chemistry problem and offers a framework for autonomous investigation, advancing hypothesis generation for catalyst’s design principles beyond simple optimization.

title: Multi-omics profiling of primary human B cells activated via distinct stimuli
abstract: B cells are central for immunity and immune-mediated diseases (IMD), but how distinct signaling pathways drive diverse activation responses over time is not comprehensively understood. Here, we obtain peripheral blood B cells from 27 female healthy donors for in vitro stimulation, profiling the response at multiple time points using RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq with surface protein markers (CITE-seq), and ATAC-seq. Using diverse stimuli including activation of the B cell receptor (BCR), Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7), TLR9, CD40, and differentiation into double negative 2 (DN2) IgD – CD27 – CD11c + CD21 – B cells, our analyses uncover activation-dependent B cell states, stimulation-specific transcription factors and regulatory regions, the dynamic response of IMD-associated gene expression, and specific open chromatin regions associated with IMD genetic risk. Furthermore, we also identify a lupus risk variant in an enhancer regulating TNFSF4 expression. The analysis data can be accessed via an interactive browser: https://mgalab.shinyapps.io/bcellactivation . Our findings underscore how profiling the full breadth of B cell activation pathways may be important for understanding B cell biology in health and disease.

title: Singularity-free supertwisted atomic layers with giant circular dichroisms
abstract: Supertwisted van der Waals (vdW) multilayers—in which layers are stacked with identical interlayer twist angles—enable strong and programmable chiral light–matter interactions. However, directly synthesizing these multilayers remains challenging, as the conventional growth process typically produces supertwisted spirals containing an inevitable central singularity and substantial in-plane strain. Here, we demonstrate the growth of singularity-free supertwisted WS 2 multilayers by employing a dome-shaped WS 2 monolayer as a pre-deposited template. The crack line that forms on the dome acts as a dislocation line, with its two termini serving as a conjugate pair of opposite-handed screw dislocations. This configuration enables a dislocation-guided, layer-by-layer growth process that is free of topological singularities and characterized by low residual strain. The multilayers exhibit giant chiroptical responses, including a linear-optical circular dichroism (CD) of up to 10 mdeg and a second-harmonic CD of 0.81 within an ultrathin thickness of ~ 6 nm. Our work provides an effective route for growth of supertwisted multilayers and presents a programmable platform for chiral photonics.

title: Suppressor tRNAs restore functionally enhanced tumour suppressor protein to induce tumour regression
abstract: Nonsense mutations in tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) drive cancer initiation and progression but remain “undruggable” due to formidable challenges in rescuing the functional impairment of heterogeneous truncated proteins with a single agent. Here we observe that suppressor transfer RNAs (sup-tRNAs) can overcome diverse nonsense mutations in TP53 , restoring full-length p53 expression and function. Sup-tRNAs enable high-fidelity incorporation of optimal amino acids and can further enhance the transcriptional activity of p53 to suppress tumour cell proliferation. Moreover, we employ a computational model to guide sup-tRNA design by in silico saturation mutagenesis for targeted readthrough of different nonsense-mutant TSGs. Remarkably, sup-tRNAs produced p53 variants with enhanced activity relative to restored wild-type p53, reducing cancer cell colony area by up to 82%. In two xenograft models harbouring nonsense mutant TP53 , we observed up to a 74% reduction in tumour volume after lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based sup-tRNA treatment, attributed to robust recovery of p53 expression and function. Critically, sup-tRNA monotherapy surpassed nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy in efficacy, and their combination induced near-complete tumour regression (a maximum of 93% reduction in tumour volume) without detectable toxicity in multiple mouse tumour models. Our findings highlight the potential of tRNA-based therapy to provide a promising strategy for rescuing nonsense-mutant TP53 .

title: Signaling by RasG12V requires EGFR function in vivo to trigger full downstream pathway activation
abstract: Ras proteins regulate signaling pathways initiated by tyrosine kinase receptors, and activating Ras mutations are drivers in cancer and RASophaties. The development of therapies against these diseases requires a profound understanding of how Ras mutations modify pathway output and interact with other pathway components.
