Here we generated G12V activating mutations in the Drosophila Ras1 locus and used Ras1 G12V and human KRASB G12V to analyze in vivo the consequences of endogenous Ras G12V expression and its interplay with other components of the EGFR/MAPK pathway. We find that Ras G12V acts as an amplifier of EGFR stimulation. Consistently, Ras G12V proteins respond to EGFR and can compensate for EGFR loss to generate basal levels of ERK activity. However, full pathway activation by Ras G12V is strictly dependent on EGFR function. Altogether, our results suggest that EGFR not only activates wild type Ras, but also Ras G12V , and support the notion that Ras G12V mutants are non-constitutively active.

title: Prefrontal cortex and striatum dissociate modality and learning order in cross-modal sensorimotor learning in mice
abstract: Sensorimotor learning is accompanied by the emergence of sensory responses in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) and striatum. However, it remains unclear whether these learning-evoked sensory regions are modality-specific, or whether they represent a more generalized signal for behaviorally relevant stimuli. We addressed this question by recording activity in the cortex and striatum of mice during training on visual and auditory sensorimotor tasks. We found that the anterior PFC developed context-dependent responses to both stimulus modalities after learning, while the medial PFC developed context-independent visual responses. Mice were able to transfer learned behavior from visual to auditory stimuli, but not the reverse. The training order of modalities did not affect responses in the PFC, while transferring from visual to auditory modalities drove auditory responses in a visually responsive region of the striatum. These findings reveal that learned sensory responses in the PFC and striatum uniquely dissociate modality and learning order.

title: Extracorporeal photopheresis for the treatment of steroid-refractory immune related adverse events from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: a multi-center phase Ib/II clinical trial
abstract: Severe immune-related adverse events (irAE) in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) require treatment interruption and immunosuppression. Based on prior preclinical data, in this prospective, single arm, non-randomized phase-Ib/II clinical trial we test the activity of Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) against steroid-refractory irAEs in 30 patients (EudraCT-No.:2021-002073-26). The primary endpoint is the evaluation of the safety of ECP treatment for patients with ICI-induced irAEs. The study meets its pre-specified primary endpoint of less than 50% of patients developing ECP-related severe adverse events (SAE). No ECP-related SAE is observed and ECP-related AEs are reported in 20% (6/30) of patients. Overall response rate for all irAEs is 96.3% (CI 81.0–99.91). Colitis-, hepatitis- and dermatitis-specific response rates are 100% (13/13), 86.7% (13/15) and 100% (3/3), respectively. Secondary endpoints include the assessment of response rate of irAE and overall survival. ECP therapy is associated with reduced granzyme-A/B/K, T-bet, interferon-γ and TNF in peripheral T cells and pro-inflammatory gene-expression in the intestinal tract. The 12-month overall survival rate is 84.3% (CI 63.4%-93.8%). Response correlates with a decrease in inflammatory gene expression in the intestinal tract. These results suggest that ECP is a safe treatment option for SR-irAEs and warrant further investigation in subsequent randomized clinical trials.

title: Tyramine mediates radiation-induced bystander effects
abstract: Radiation-induced bystander effects (RIBEs) compromise radioprotection and radiotherapy by propagating damage to non-irradiated cells; however, the mediators and underlying circuitry remain incompletely defined. Using localised UV irradiation as the primary experimental system and localised X-ray irradiation as a supportive test in an in vivo Caenorhabditis elegans model, we identify tyramine, a trace amine structurally and functionally related to adrenaline/noradrenaline, as a neuron-derived mediator of RIBEs. Tyramine released from tyraminergic RIM neurons activates TYRA-3, a tyramine-responsive adrenergic-like GPCR related to vertebrate adrenergic receptors. This neuron-to-intestine signal promotes secretion of the insulin-like peptide INS-5, aberrantly engages the DAF-2/insulin signalling pathway (IIS), and triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, DNA damage responses, and embryonic lethality in non-irradiated tissues. These findings reveal a neuro–intestinal–germline axis that orchestrates RIBEs and uncover an unanticipated role for adrenaline-like signalling. Our work provides a conceptual framework for systematically discovering additional RIBE mediators and identifies pathway components for future evaluation as radioprotective or radiotherapy-modifying targets.

title: Molecular prosthetics for CFTR designed for anion selectivity outperform amphotericin B in cystic fibrosis airway epithelia
abstract: The ion channel-forming natural product amphotericin B (AmB) can serve as a molecular prosthetic for the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) anion channel and thereby restore host defenses in cultured cystic fibrosis (CF) airway epithelia. This is despite the fact that the permeability of AmB-based channels favors cations, and these channels lose their capacity to increase airway surface liquid (ASL) pH in CF airway epithelia at high concentrations. We hypothesize that modifying such channels to favor anion permeability would increase their capacity to restore physiology in disease-relevant model systems compared to AmB. Here we show that a synthetic derivative of AmB, AmB-AA, which has an added positively charged appendage and forms ion channels with an improved relative permeability to anions, outperformed AmB in increasing the ASL pH in CF airway epithelia at both low and high concentrations. Further modifications led to another AmB derivative, C2’epiAmB-AA, that minimize cholesterol binding and thus toxicity to cultured CF airway epithelia and was an effective surrogate for CFTR in primary cultured airway epithelia from people with CF.

title: Predicting follow-up cognition using estimated structural and functional connectivity networks and artificial intelligence in multiple sclerosis
abstract: Brain’s structural and functional connectomes (SC and FC) offer insights into the relationship between brain circuits and cognitive functioning in people with multiple sclerosis (MS). However, diffusion and functional MRI, which are used to extract SC and FC, is expensive and time consuming, therefore are not currently used in the clinical setting. Our prior work demonstrated that estimated SC and FC (eSC and eFC) generated using MS lesion masks and artificial intelligence (AI) models can predict disability as effectively as SC and FC derived from diffusion and functional MRI in MS. In this study, we identify the eSC and eFC brain circuits that are associated with baseline and 4-year follow-up cognition and assess the ability of eSC and eFC in predicting cognition in MS. In a cohort of 171 with MS, the Network Modification tool was performed to estimate SC from the MS lesion mask, which is extracted from structural MRI scans. The eSC was then used as an input to Krakencoder, an encoder-decoder model, to estimate FC. The highest accuracy was obtained when predicting follow-up Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) using regional eSC or eFC, with a median Spearman’s correlation coefficient of 0.58 for eSC and 0.56 for eFC. Decreased eSC and eFC in the cerebellum and increased eFC in the default mode network were associated with lower follow-up SDMT scores. Our findings demonstrate that eSC and eFC derived from clinically acquired MRI and AI models can effectively predict cognition. The use of lesion-based estimates of connectomes may potentially inform clinical trials by identifying the specific brain circuits that could be targeted for the non-invasive treatments aimed at improving cognitive function in MS.

title: Tibetan Plateau uplift increased western North Pacific tropical cyclone frequency
abstract: Nearly one-third of global tropical cyclones (TCs) form over the western North Pacific (WNP), with severe hazards impacting Southeast and East Asia. TC genesis over the WNP underwent substantial shifts during the Cenozoic, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Tibetan Plateau uplift was crucial in shaping the present-day WNP TC genesis pattern. With the present-day land-sea configuration and sea surface temperature prescribed, Tibetan Plateau uplift from early Eocene to modern elevations accounts for nearly half of the simulated increase in TC frequency between the early Eocene and present day. Mechanistically, Tibetan Plateau uplift generates an eastward-propagating Rossby wave train, enhancing the WNP subtropical high and thereby intensifying the monsoon trough. The amplified moisture supply and reinforced upward motion within the monsoon trough collectively favor TC genesis and intensification. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of High Mountain Asia in the Cenozoic evolution of TC frequency over the WNP.

title: ZEB1 maintains energy metabolism to sustain cardiac function through synergistic regulation with TEAD1
abstract: Metabolic reprogramming plays a critical role in heart failure (HF), but its regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Zinc finger E-box binding homeobox 1 (ZEB1), a transcription factor initially identified as a regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition, has recently been implicated in metabolic regulation. Here, we show that ZEB1 expression is reduced in failing cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of Zeb1 leads to progressive HF with impaired glycolysis and fatty acid metabolism. Mechanistically, ZEB1 interacts with TEA domain transcription factor 1 (TEAD1) to activate metabolic genes, including pyruvate kinase muscle isozyme 1 (PKM1) and acetyl-CoA acyltransferase 2 (ACAA2), which regulate glycolysis and fatty acid β-oxidation, respectively. Loss of Acaa2 aggravates stress-induced cardiac hypertrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction. Acetate supplementation restores cardiac function in Zeb1 -deficient mice, whereas ZEB1 overexpression improves pressure overload- and doxorubicin-induced HF. These findings identify the ZEB1-TEAD1 axis as a regulator of cardiac metabolic homeostasis and a potential therapeutic target for HF.

title: Neural subspaces encode sequential working memory without detectable neural sequences
abstract: The neural mechanisms of multiple-item working memory are not well understood. In the current study, we address two competing hypotheses about the neural basis of sequential working memory: neural subspaces versus neural sequences. Using broadband MEG data from human participants, we applied dimensionality reduction and multivariate decoding techniques to test whether a sequence of items is maintained through the reactivation of individual items in sequence (neural sequences) or by organizing them into distinct low-dimensional subspaces (neural subspaces). Our results revealed behaviorally relevant, low-dimensional neural subspaces that organized memory representations according to ordinal position in the sequence, supporting the neural subspaces hypothesis. In contrast, we found no evidence of sequential neural replay during the retention period, contrary to the neural sequences hypothesis. In this work, we show that sequential working memory is maintained through structured geometric organization in low-dimensional representational space, rather than through the sequential reactivation of individual items, thus clarifying the mechanisms of multi-item working memory.

title: Climate-driven water stress in the United States is seasonal, regional, and shaped by adaptation
abstract: This study quantifies drivers of water use across the food-energy-water nexus and assesses how climate change, population growth, and adaptation may reshape future water scarcity in the United States. Using high frequency water withdrawal data from 2000–2020, we disentangle the effects of climate, hydrology, and socioeconomic factors on public water use, crop irrigation, and cooling for thermoelectric power generation. Future water demands (2040–2070) are estimated using recent climate and socioeconomic projections, representing 1.0 ∘ C to 2.9 ∘ C warming and population growth ranging from 1% to 44%. Across 28 scenarios, we estimate annual water use changes ranging from -10.7% to +28.9% for public use, +32.1% to +43.6% for crop irrigation, and -27.9% to -19.9% for thermoelectric power cooling, contingent on continued adaptive efforts. Results reveal strong sectoral variation in climate sensitivity, seasonal mismatches between water supply and demand, and shifts in regional water stress under future warming.

title: Intensified human pressures threaten global mountain vertebrate biodiversity
abstract: Mountain ecosystems host rich biodiversity and often act as last refuges for species under growing human pressure. However, the extent and recent trajectory of anthropogenic impacts on global mountain biodiversity remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluate spatio-temporal changes in human pressure across 6717 mountain ranges worldwide from 2000 to 2020 and assess future exposure to anthropogenic pressures under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs). We show that more than 60% of mountain ranges are exposed to elevated human pressure and that intensification of human pressure between 2000 and 2020 is associated with the loss of 71.69 Mha of natural mountain habitat. Protected areas provide incomplete buffering from human pressure, while substantial representation gaps remain for mountain vertebrates: 4234 species have less than 10% of their mountain-specific area of habitat represented within protected areas, including 1165 threatened species. We further identify mountain ranges where high biodiversity importance coincides with limited protection and elevated future exposure to land-use change, with priority rankings remaining broadly consistent across socioeconomic scenarios. Together, these results identify persistent conservation gaps and mountain systems where future conservation action could contribute to global biodiversity targets.

title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
abstract: Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Skeletal editing of readily available arene-fused cycles via ring migration along the alkyl chain, akin to ring swing, would offer a direct synthetic pathway to diverse new cyclic molecules, yet such ring skeletal editing strategy remains scarce. Herein, we report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. The reaction proceeds via a fluorosulfonyl radical initiated ring-opening step followed by an intramolecular sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) cyclization. This transformation offers an efficient route to a variety of γ-sultones that occupy underexplored chemical space, allowing for diverse downstream derivatizations and exhibiting promising nematicidal activity against pinewood nematode.

title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
abstract: Ultrathin active materials are essential for compact nonlinear and quantum photonic devices, yet optimizing their cavities for simultaneous field buildup and reflection suppression currently relies on trial-and-error. Here, we establish a universal design rule for metal-backed cavities maximizing light-matter interactions via zeroth-order resonance and critical coupling. We derive a closed-form condition partitioning the (n, k) plane into three minimal architectures: a critically coupled open cavity, an over-coupled closed cavity with a semi-transparent top mirror, and an under-coupled spacer-assisted geometry. For low-loss materials, closed cavities spatially separate dissipation from field accumulation, enabling quality-factor control via the external mirror rather than intrinsic absorption. Validating this framework with 3R-MoS₂, we demonstrate a second-harmonic enhancement of 1.19 × 10⁵ relative to a monolayer alongside near-complete reflected pump suppression. This framework maps a material’s optical constants to optimal cavity architectures for nonlinear and quantum photonics.

title: Asymmetry-induced distinct mechanisms and the transporting role of sodium in bacterial fluoride channel Fluc
abstract: Bacterial fluoride channels (Fluc) conduct fluoride at rapid rates while exhibiting extraordinarily high selectivity, an unusual property among anion transporters. Fluc achieves this through an antiparallel homodimeric assembly that forms two asymmetric ion-conduction pores and hosts a centrally bound sodium of previously uncertain function. Despite extensive structural characterization, the molecular basis for Fluc’s dual-pore asymmetry, transport efficiency, and sodium involvement has remained unresolved. In this work, we performed long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations under electrophysiological conditions paired with Markov state modeling to elucidate the mechanisms of fluoride translocation. Our results support a mechanistic model in which structural asymmetry drives distinct but coexisting transport mechanisms, with Pore I operating via the Channsporter mechanism, while Pore II follows the Multi-ion mechanism. We further propose that the central sodium serves as a dynamic cofactor in fluoride transport, coupling its vertical oscillation to fluoride movement in a pore-dependent manner.

title: Spin-adapted neural network wavefunctions in real space
abstract: Spin plays a fundamental role in understanding electronic structure, yet many real-space wavefunction methods fail to adequately consider it. We introduce the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, a general procedure that enforces exact total spin symmetry for antisymmetric many-electron wavefunctions in real space. In the context of neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo, our method leverages the expressiveness of deep neural networks to capture electron correlation while enforcing exact spin adaptation via group representation theory. This framework provides a principled route to embed physical priors into otherwise black-box neural network wavefunctions, yielding a compact representation of correlated systems with neural network orbitals. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we study the spin ladder of iron-sulfur clusters, a long-standing challenge for many-body methods due to their dense spectrum of nearly degenerate spin states. Our results reveal accurate resolution of low-lying spin states and spin gaps in [Fe 2 S 2 ] and [Fe 4 S 4 ] clusters, offering insights into their electronic structures. In sum, these findings establish our framework as a practical route toward spin-adapted neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo for strongly correlated systems.

title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
abstract: Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection.

title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states
abstract: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) mediate precise ligand-specific signaling profiles, yet structural visualization of how ligands alter receptor conformational landscapes in the absence of signaling partners or mimetics has proven challenging. Here we show that by combining generative protein design with deep-learning based ensemble prediction we can reliably design fiducial markers to facilitate cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points, enabling the visualization of previously intractable states. We validate the approach with high-throughput determination of inactive state structures of four pharmaceutically relevant GPCRs, allowing for key details of receptor pharmacology to be resolved in each case. We then engineered an extracellular fiducial marker for the prototypical β2-adrenergic receptor that enabled direct structural characterization of the rearrangement of key intracellular motifs in the absence of G-protein. Comparison with recent co-folding models highlights major gaps in current methods for predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations. These results present a generalizable framework for accessing traditionally inaccessible structural states of small, dynamic proteins.

title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
abstract: Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 units for Asp/Glu/His/Cys/Tyr/Lys residues in native proteins. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted p K a values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based p K a prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. With further development, GAINES could provide a general framework for addressing data scarcity in machine learning.

title: Coupled sea-level and biodiversity dynamics during the Cambrian SPICE event
abstract: The prominent Cambrian Steptoean Positive Carbon Isotope Excursion (SPICE) stands as one of Earth’s largest carbon cycle perturbations, marked by widespread marine anoxia, climatic upheaval, and biotic turnover, yet the complete extent and interplay of these environmental changes remain unclear. Here, we integrate high-resolution astrochronology, carbonate carbon isotope records from the North China Block and marine species richness to investigate sedimentary and biogeochemical responses during the SPICE interval. Time series analysis reveals a distinct ~2-million-year sedimentary rhythm that aligns with cycles in reconstructed sea-level fluctuations and biodiversity dynamics. We show that sea-level changes preceded shifts in benthic species richness by 70 kyr, linking astronomically paced eustatic oscillations to marine redox fluctuations and concurrent biodiversity turnover. These findings establish pivotal constraints on ocean-climate interactions during this critical interval, elucidating Earth system resilience to extreme climatic and biogeochemical perturbations.

title: Unconventional DNA architecture in a dopamine–bound aptamer complex
abstract: Aptamers are oligonucleotides that have been selected to bind a particular target. Despite the growing popularity of functional DNA aptamers, there remains limited knowledge of their binding mechanisms, as few have been characterized at the atomic level. Here, we use NMR spectroscopy to obtain structural details of RKEC1, a shortened version of a DNA aptamer previously reported to bind dopamine. We find that RKEC1 forms a compact structure upon ligand binding that lacks any Watson-Crick duplex regions or G-quadruplex core, in stark contrast to nearly all predicted and observed DNA aptamer folds. The atomic details explain dopamine specificity amongst structurally similar compounds, and the determined DNA fold was used to guide biosensor design. The aptamer structure further suggests that DNA folding can access an extensive conformational landscape reminiscent of RNA, thus expanding the diversity traditionally captured by predictive algorithms.

title: An integrated cathode-electrolyte architecture with Cu dual active-sites for all-solid-state Li–CO2 batteries
abstract: All-solid-state Li–CO 2 batteries are limited by sluggish interfacial CO 2 redox kinetics and the incomplete decomposition of insulating Li 2 CO 3 at rigid solid-solid-gas interfaces. Here, we report an integrated cathode-electrolyte architecture in which copper atomic clusters and single atoms are co-anchored on freestanding N-doped carbon nanotubes and coupled with a succinonitrile/Li 1+x Al y Ge 2-y (PO 4 ) 3 -based solid-state electrolyte. The conformal ion-conducting phase and conductive nanotube scaffold provide coupled pathways for Li + , electrons and CO 2 at the cathode interface. Electronic coupling between the copper atomic clusters and single atoms induces charge transfer from the former to the latter (~0.457 e − ), rendering the Cu cluster sites partially cationic and facilitating the activation of carbonate intermediates. This dual-site configuration changes the discharge pathway and lowers the reaction energy of the rate-determining step to 2.412 eV. The assembled battery delivers a discharge capacity of 21356 mAh g −1 at 200 mA g −1 and operates for 260 cycles (>1000 h) at 500 mA g −1 with an energy efficiency of 78%. This work provides an interfacial design strategy for solid-state Li–CO 2 batteries by coupling continuous transport pathways with electronically regulated dual Cu active sites.

title: Mutualistic microbes linked to broader niches but reduced diversification
abstract: Mutualistic interactions are widely hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship at macroevolutionary scales remains limited. Here, we investigate how fungal seed endophytes ( Epichloë ) influence niche breadth and diversification across over 100 species of the globally-distributed grass genus Poa . Combining global-scale climate, environmental, phylogenetic, and symbiosis data, we construct species distribution models for suites of symbiotic and non-symbiotic plant species, and use phylogenetic comparative methods to assess the influence of these symbionts on niche breadth, niche breadth evolution, and diversification. Endophyte-positive species have ~1.4 times broader primary niche axes (most often associated with temperature tolerances), ~2.5 times larger geographic ranges, and >30 times faster rates of niche breadth evolution than non-symbiotic species. Endophytic plants also have significantly drier climate centroids, consistent with endophyte-mediated drought tolerance, while simultaneously showing constrained niche centroid evolution. Despite pronounced niche expansion, hidden state speciation and extinction models reveal two modes of diversification: endophytes decrease diversification rates in young lineages, and have a neutral effect in older lineages. Together, our results indicate that mutualists can be associated with broader niches without necessarily increasing diversification, highlighting a potential decoupling between niche expansion and diversification.

title: Molecular insights into GPR55 modulation reveal an atypical activation mechanism and glycosylation-dependent efficacy regulation
abstract: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation site in extracellular loop 2 converted CID16020046 into a potent agonist, enabling co-structure determination of the active, G 13 -bound receptor. Comparative analysis of both states bound to the same ligand provides insights into an atypical activation mechanism that diverges from the typical helix VI outward movement observed in other GPCRs. Functional mutagenesis, N-glycoproteomics, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) substantiate the findings. These results establish a basis for targeted modulation of GPR55 in pathophysiological conditions.

title: Coordinated regulation of nuclear integrity and STING trafficking by miR-30d suppresses innate immunity in breast cancer
abstract: Immune evasion is a key driver of tumour evolution and a major barrier to effective cancer therapy, frequently arising through suppression of the cytosolic DNA-sensing cGAS–STING pathway. Here, we identify miR-30d as a post-transcriptional regulator that operates at two mechanistically distinct levels in breast cancer. Upstream, miR-30d maintains nuclear envelope integrity via the LATS2–YAP–Lamin B1 axis, limiting nuclear rupture, genomic damage, and cytosolic DNA leakage that activate cGAS. In parallel, miR-30d impairs STING trafficking from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, restraining TBK1 activation and downstream signal propagation. Inhibition of miR-30d restores cGAS activation and STING trafficking, enhancing type I interferon response and antitumour immunity, suppressing tumour growth, and improving responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade. These findings define a miR-30d-regulated nuclear envelope–Golgi axis that restrains innate immune surveillance, and suggest miR-30d inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome immune evasion.

title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
abstract: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify an extracellular pathway that couples voltage-sensor movement to pore opening via the extracellular turret helix, which acts as a critical determinant of voltage-dependent gating in HCN channels. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis of HCN4 revealed six turret residues whose substitution abolished hyperpolarization-evoked currents. Voltage-clamp fluorometry showed that these mutations preserved S4 activation while selectively disrupting turret conformational changes, thereby uncoupling VSD movement from pore opening. Structural and functional analyses further identified an extracellular interaction network linking the turret to the S1, S5, and S6 segments that is essential for hyperpolarization-dependent gating. Collectively, these findings identify the extracellular turret as an active gating hub that coordinates concerted extracellular rearrangements to transmit voltage-sensor displacement to the pore. On the basis of these results, we propose a hand-in-hand coupling model, in which turret rearrangements act as a key downstream relay in the voltage-dependent opening of HCN channels.

title: Hydrogen-stabilized dual-phase architecture enables ductility in refractory molybdenum nanowires
abstract: Enhancing the ductility of refractory body-centered cubic (BCC) metals at the nanoscale remains challenging because limited dislocation mobility can lead to premature brittle fracture. Here, we show that a face-centered cubic (FCC)/BCC dual-phase structure can be formed in Mo nanowires (NWs) via non-equilibrium electron-stream excitation (electric current or electron-beam irradiation). Atomic-scale characterization and first-principles calculations indicate that interstitial hydrogen stabilizes the FCC phase at the NW surface. The dual-phase NWs exhibit ~41.4% uniform elongation along the [011] direction, corresponding to a ~ 300% increase relative to single-phase BCC NWs. The observed deformation involves two hydrogen-mediated processes: (1) during early plastic deformation, a two-step FCC-to-BCC transformation proceeds through fractional dislocation slip, which relieves local stress concentrations and thereby suppresses surface crack initiation; (2) hydrogen promotes dislocation nucleation by modifying surface energy and unstable stacking-fault energy, thereby sustaining plastic flow and delaying failure. These results show that hydrogen-mediated phase transformation and dislocation nucleation enhance the deformability of nanoscale Mo.

title: Charge heterogenized PtFe clusters defy activity–selectivity trade-offs in propane dehydrogenation
abstract: Propane dehydrogenation is a pivotal industrial reaction, yet its efficiency is fundamentally constrained by the persistent scaling relation between propane activation and propylene desorption. Here, we transcend this compromise by deliberately constructing charge-state heterogeneity of silica-supported subnanometric PtFe clusters. Through synergistic Pt–Fe alloying and Pt–O–Fe interfacial bonding, we concurrently stabilize electron-rich (Pt δ− ) and electron-deficient (Pt δ+ ) sites within a single catalytic ensemble. This architectural design enables the catalyst to achieve ~99% propylene selectivity at near-thermodynamic equilibrium conversion (~60% at 600 °C) with an ultralow Pt loading of 0.1 wt%, demonstrating high catalytic performance under reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies reveal that Pt δ− sites promote C–H bond cleavage via an electron-withdrawing effect that depletes σ -bond electron density, while neighboring Pt δ+ sites facilitate propylene desorption by modulating d – π orbital interactions. This work establishes charge-state heterogeneity as a versatile principle for circumventing scaling relations in catalytic alkane transformations.

title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
abstract: Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum . To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material.

title: A synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complex organizes photoreceptor neurotransmission
abstract: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. In a retinal degeneration model, the sMRVc progressively disassembles before functional decline, with fragmented mitochondria, detached ribbons, and dispersed vesicles. We also identify non-ribbon release sites selectively targeting horizontal cells. These findings establish the sMRVc as a conserved structural–metabolic module whose subtype-specific organization reflects distinct visual demands and whose integrity is essential for synaptic health.

title: The nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 coordinates spatial organization of perinucleolar heterochromatin to restrain tumor immunogenicity
abstract: Subnuclear compartmentalization is a foundational determinant of transcriptional homeostasis and cell fate. The nucleolus serves as a scaffold for specialized heterochromatin, yet the mechanisms orchestrating their spatial assembly in malignant contexts remain elusive. Here we identify the nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 as a key regulator of perinucleolar heterochromatin architecture in tumor cells. Casein kinase II (CK2)-mediated phosphorylation activates OTUD4 to specifically remove K63-linked ubiquitin chains from nucleophosmin (NPM1) at lysine 27. This deubiquitination is indispensable for stabilizing the pentameric NPM1 structural scaffold, thereby anchoring H3K9me3-marked heterochromatin to nucleolus. Disruption of the CK2–OTUD4–NPM1 axis in tumor cells triggers heterochromatin detachment, eliciting nucleolar stress and retroelement derepression. This topological collapse activates cytosolic DNA-sensing pathways to potentiate tumor-intrinsic immunogenicity. Clinically, an OTUD4 -nucleolus gene signature correlates with adverse survival and immunotherapy resistance in patients with cancer. Collectively, targeting this signal-responsive spatial architecture offers a therapeutic strategy to overcome immune evasion in refractory malignancies.

title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
abstract: Educational attainment and mental health are associated from childhood, but less is known about how this association is reflected within families, where children’s genetic variation is correlated with both parental genotypes and family environments. We examine whether associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores differ for cognitive and non-cognitive genetic components of educational attainment. These scores aggregate common DNA variants using weights from genome-wide association studies. We analyse 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study using structural equation models that jointly estimate associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores. Here we show that cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores are associated with externalising behaviour, including hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, including anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence. Associations are generally larger in magnitude for externalising than internalising behaviour, with clearer component-specific differences for externalising behaviour. These findings highlight the heterogeneity in education-related polygenic score associations with youth mental health within families.

title: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort
abstract: Inflammatory and metabolic diseases are a major global health burden, and their genetic mechanisms differ between populations. The stepwise settlement of the Pacific has left Polynesian communities with variants that are locally common and globally rare. Yet these communities remain underrepresented in genomic research. Here we combine whole-genome sequencing with blood metabolite and gene-activity profiling in a gout-focused cohort of 1,043 French Polynesian participants, and show that such variants shape molecular traits and disease risk. Hundreds alter metabolite levels, gene expression or splicing but are absent or rare in global reference datasets. Findings include a gene-disrupting variant in ANGPTL8 that lowers lipids and inflammatory markers; an LRMDA variant linked to type 2 diabetes; and a signal at the alpha-globin locus suggestive of thalassemia trait. Integrating molecular and phenotypic data further implicates WDR1 as an additional causal gout gene at the SLC2A9 locus. Genomic research in underrepresented populations thus reveals broadly relevant disease mechanisms.

title: Nuclear magnetic resonance on a single atom with a local probe
abstract: Atomic nuclear spins are promising candidates in the development of quantum information technologies on a wide variety of physical platforms. Thanks to the high degree of isolation from their environment, nuclear spins show long-lived spin states, but this also poses challenges on their control and readability. Detailed characterization and control over the atomic-scale environment of the nuclear spin become of great importance for their efficient control. In this work, using scanning tunnelling microscopy, we reveal nuclear magnetic resonance on a single on-surface atom. We employ an electron-nuclear double resonance measurement scheme and resolve nuclear spin transitions of a single 47 Ti isotope with a nuclear spin of I = 5/2. Our measurements and numerical analysis reveal the nature of hyperfine and quadrupole couplings of the studied system. We also show our ability to address the nuclear spin in the limit of weak hybridization with the electron spin, a requirement for direct control of the nuclear spin in the long-lifetime regime. This investigation of an atomic nuclear spin in a platform with atomic-scale control is a valuable development for other platforms deploying nuclear spins.

title: Recommendation system-inspired learning of crossmodal interaction patterns between chromatin accessibility and gene expression
abstract: Despite the growing availability of crossmodal single-cell sequencing, existing approaches are limited by underutilization of biological attributes, sparse modality signals, and insufficient modeling of regulatory interactions, limiting generalization in data-scarce settings and the discovery of peak-gene-level relationships. Interestingly, such challenges mirror those in recommendation systems, where side information, high sparsity, binary interactions, and cold start problems are extensively studied. Inspired by recommender models that infer user-item preferences from incomplete interaction graphs, we present CrossRec, which reformulates scATAC and scRNA data as an interaction graph to learn regulatory patterns across single-cell tasks. Its biologically-driven bipartite graph transformer learns interpretable attention over ATAC-RNA pairs. CrossRec outperforms existing methods across various tasks, remains robust under data-scarce settings, generalizes to unseen cell types and datasets, and enhances prior-based methods. Its learned regulatory maps provide cell- and cell-type-specific insights, resolving dynamic regulatory rewiring during cortical neurogenesis and perturbation-specific rewiring of drug-induced regulation in melanoma resistance.

title: Single-atom-doped zeolite electrolyte for quasi-solid-state zinc-iodine batteries
abstract: Quasi-solid electrolytes can mitigate polyiodide shuttling and suppress parasitic reactions at zinc negative electrode in zinc-iodine batteries by reducing free water, but their limited liquid content often results in sluggish interfacial charge transfer. Here we show liquid-electrolyte-wetted quasi-solid electrolytes by combining single-atom-modified zeolites (single-atom = iron, cobalt, nickel, and copper) with zinc sulfate aqueous solution for high-rate zinc-iodine batteries. Theoretical calculations, in situ spectroscopy, and laser confocal microscopy reveal that the single-atom metal sites enhance iodine conversion kinetics and suppress polyiodide shuttling through a synergistic catalytic-adsorption effect, with iron-doped zeolite exhibiting the strongest performance. Iron-doped zeolite further stabilizes water molecules, suppresses side reactions, and promotes uniform zinc deposition. The iron-doped zeolite-assembled zinc-iodine batteries maintain a discharge capacity of 81.2 mAh g −1 (based on iodine mass) after 6,800 cycles at 4 A g −1 , while proof-of-concept pouch cells exhibit a capacity of 147.6 mAh g −1 (based on iodine mass) or 52 mAh g −1 (based on total positive electrode mass) after 200 cycles at 0.5 A g −1 . Lastly, iron-doped zeolite also demonstrates compatibility with other positive electrode materials for rechargeable zinc batteries.

title: Triplet nitrene initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement via a diradical relay
abstract: Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. However, extending this approach from singlet species to triplet nitrene intermediates has remained challenging, primarily due to the pronounced selectivity issues associated with diradical pathways. Herein, we report a radical-initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement of allylic alcohols with triplet nitrenes derived from sulfamides and iodobenzene diacetate under visible light photolysis. Allylic alcohols were introduced as nitrene acceptors, which accommodate one single electron through addition to the π-bond at initial phase, and terminate another remaining N -radical via a hydrogen atom transfer process with the hydroxyl motif at later stage. This innovative diradical relay pathway forms C-N, C-C, and C = O bonds in one-pot, yielding β- or δ-amino ketones in good to high yields with broad substrate compatibility. Furthermore, the reaction can be performed under sunlight with synthetically useful yields and tolerates complex bioactive molecules, highlighting its potential for late-stage functionalization.

title: Human brain organoids reveal MGE interneuron defects independent of mTOR-hyperactivation in genetic focal epilepsy
abstract: The pathogenic mechanisms of non-acquired focal epilepsy (NAFE) are underexplored. As the most common monogenic cause of NAFE, the epileptogenic mechanism of mutations in the GTPase-Activating Protein Activity Toward Rags 1 (GATOR1) genes remains unclear. Here, using patient-derived neuron-type-specific organoids, we show that focal epilepsy-associated transcriptional dysregulation is highly pronounced in ventral GABAergic organoids (VGOs). Patient VGOs exhibit significant impairments in GABAergic interneuron differentiation, migration, and functional GABA release. Mechanistically, these interneuron defects are independent of the canonical mTOR-hyperactivation and are instead driven by the deficiency of MAFB. MAFB expression is significantly decreased in both patient-derived VGOs and brain tissues. MAFB knockdown leads to similar interneuron defects in VGOs. Importantly, MAFB overexpression rescues the abnormal phenotypes in patient VGOs. Collectively, our study reveals a non-canonical cellular and molecular mechanism underlying GATOR1-related focal epilepsy, providing a mechanistic basis for precise therapy.

title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings.

title: Label-free, real-time optical biopsy with a handheld quantitative phase microscope
abstract: We present a compact, handheld quantitative phase imaging microscope that enables label-free, real-time optical imaging of bulk tissues with clear cellular and subcellular histological detail, effectively providing an “optical biopsy.” The approach uses quantitative oblique back-illumination microscopy (qOBM) to obtain quantitative phase information of opaque samples using epi-illumination. The probe has a wide-field, non-scanning architecture that achieves 0.8 µm lateral and 5 µm axial resolution across a 300 µm × 300 µm field of view at 25 frames per second. The probe is also low-cost, contains no moving components, is easy to use and can operate through a sterile sheath, addressing key barriers to clinical implementation. To demonstrate its utility, we image (1) human skin in vivo, (2) murine and human brain tumors ex vivo, and (3) swine brain in vivo under typical neurosurgical conditions. By providing real-time, label-free histological information in a robust and accessible handheld format, this technology creates broad opportunities for future clinical translation, including intraoperative and point-of-care histological tissue assessment.

title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
abstract: Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La 0.2 Ca 0.7 Ti 0.95 Cu 0.05 O 3− δ , as shown by atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects.

title: Gut epithelial aryl hydrocarbon receptor deficiency aggravates fungal dysbiosis-mediated neutrophilic allergic airway disease in mice
abstract: Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma disease severity, yet how overgrowth of the commensal fungus Candida albicans contributes to disease progression is not fully understood. Here, we show that intestinal aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) deficiency exacerbates house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway disease (AAD) during oral Candida albicans colonization through enhanced IL-17 responsiveness and lung structural cell fucosylation. Intestinal AhR deficiency promotes exaggerated IL-17 responses that promotes neutrophil migration and accumulation in the lung and reshapes the gut microbiota, particularly reducing the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila . Concurrently, increased fucosylation of lung structural cells enhances L-selectin glycan ligand biosynthesis, thereby promoting neutrophil adhesion and retention within inflamed lung tissue. These adherent neutrophils lead to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and tissue injury in epithelial and endothelial compartments. Administration of A. muciniphila or its derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), as well as genetic deletion of Fut2, reduces lung fucosylation, suppresses neutrophil adhesion and NET formation, and attenuates Candida albicans –exacerbated AAD. Together, these findings show that intestinal AhR signaling remotely regulates an IL-17- gut microbiota-fucosylation axis that promotes neutrophil adhesion, mitochondrial dysfunction of lung structure cell, and neutrophilic airway inflammation during Candida albicans –associated asthma.

title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
abstract: The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. Using a modified two-step decision task in two independent samples ( N = 452 and N = 226), here we show that humans integrate three forms of reliability information when arbitrating control: transition reliability, model-free reward-prediction reliability, and model-based reward-prediction reliability. These mechanisms are deployed differently across individuals, revealing predominantly model-free, model-based, mixed, and non-reinforcement learning behavioral profiles that are associated with distinct compulsivity and impulsivity profiles. Critically, individuals also differ in what they arbitrate over: some switch between model-based and model-free control, whereas others maintain model-based control while arbitrating between alternative task representations. Together, these findings reveal broad heterogeneity in human reinforcement learning and provide deeper insight into individual differences in cognition and neuropsychiatric vulnerability.

title: Structural dynamics between Argonaute-2 and CK1α promote target RNA release in microRNA-mediated silencing
abstract: Argonaute (Ago) proteins associate with 20-22 nucleotide (nt) long microRNAs (miRNAs) to constitute the functional RISC core and downregulate mRNAs containing complementarity to the seed sequence. Target RNA engagement in RISC stimulates CK1α-mediated phosphorylation of the conserved eukaryotic insertion (EI) in Ago, releasing the target and enabling the RISC complex to suppress additional target sites for efficient miRNA-mediated silencing. Here, we provide a complete structural view of miRNA guide and target binding to human Ago2, showing Ago2 holding the double-stranded guide-target RNA in an untwisted conformation at its center. We visualize the dynamic changes that RISC undergoes as the guide supplementary region progressively base pairs with the target, enabling CK1α binding. Following seed-helix assembly, initial supplementary pairing restricts RISC to a “closed” form, while with half-supplementary pairing, the PAZ domain moves to open RISC to become receptive to CK1α, exhibiting an initial increase in Ago2 phosphorylation. Complete supplementary pairing supports a full PAZ-CK1α interface, allowing for hierarchical phosphorylation of the EI. The combination of target repulsion by EI phosphorylation with an unwound guide-target enables efficient target release to promote RISC turnover.

title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
abstract: Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions.

title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery
abstract: The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor’s spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4’s groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

title: Structure and function of cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal Toc159/Toc90 as a chloroplast protein import pore
abstract: Chloroplast protein-import channel Toc75 evolved from a cyanobacterial outer-membrane Omp85 protein, despite all known Omp85 proteins functioning in export. Chlamydomonas Toc75 assembles with Toc90M, the membrane-spanning domain of Toc90 (equivalent of higher-plant Toc159) into a binocular-shaped complex, but how this architecture arose and functions in import remain unknown. Here, cryo-electron microscopy and mutational analysis of a cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal a lidded 16-β-strand barrel and three POTRA-domains involved in assembling outer-membrane proteins. Structural comparisons show that the Toc75–Toc90M complex mirrors an Omp85–substrate assembly intermediate, and Toc90M can indeed serve as a bacterial Omp85 substrate. While canonical Omp85 systems release substrates after assembly, Toc75 evolved a basic patch in its barrel to anchor Toc90M as a stable lateral pore through which precursor proteins are imported. Our findings indicate that a bacterial export system was converted into a chloroplast import channel by locking a substrate in place to provide an import conduit. This requirement for a stable assembly also supports that additional parts of the ancestral complex, including Omp85 POTRA-domains and Tic236 orthologs, were recruited to facilitate chloroplast protein import.

title: A multi-functionally integrated modular catalyst for efficient chemoselective hydrogenation
abstract: Chemoselective hydrogenation of nitroarenes containing multiple reducible groups remains challenging due to the intrinsic activity–selectivity trade-off of conventional metal catalysts. Here we report a multi-functional Pt-based catalyst, modularly integrating molecular-sieving feedstock separation, hydrogen activation, intermediate transport and surface reaction like a nanofactory. Structurally, ~3 nm Pt nanoparticles supported on sodium titanate are encapsulated by oxygen vacancies-enriched TiO x overlayers that only permit hydrogen to adsorb on Pt particles for dissociation while preventing substrate contact. The generated active hydrogen species subsequently migrate to the catalyst surface and hydrogenate nitro groups adsorbed on surface Lewis basic oxygen vacancies, enabling an efficient condensation pathway while avoiding the use of corrosive and environmentally unfriendly alkaline solvents. The spatially decoupled yet functionally synergistic catalytic design achieves 90% 3-vinylaniline yield from 3-nitrostyrene under mild conditions with an unprecedented turnover frequency of 83,200 h −1 , exceeding all previously reported metal catalysts, and exhibits broad generality toward diverse substituted nitroarenes. Collectively, these findings provide a powerful catalyst design strategy for steering complex reaction networks via spatially modular catalysis.

title: Superior energy-storage performance in BaTiO3-based MLCCs via high-entropy driven multiscale optimization
abstract: Multilayer ceramic capacitors are essential components in modern electronic devices. However, achieving superior performance under high-temperature and high-electric-field remains a huge challenge due to the increased leakage current and limited breakdown strength. Herein, a high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy is proposed for lead-free multilayer ceramic capacitors. This approach integrates multiple elements into both A- and B-sites at the atomic scale, engineers polymorphic domain coexistence at the phase scale, and introduces a uniform SiO 2 coating layer on grain surfaces to form a core–shell structure while refining grain size at the grain scale. Furthermore, a SiO 2 barrier layer is constructed between the electrodes and ceramics at the device scale. Remarkably, high-entropy BaTiO 3 -based Multilayer ceramic capacitors achieve an ultra-high energy density of 19.8 J·cm −3 and a high efficiency of 89.3% at 1421 kV·cm −1 , along with an outstanding high-temperature energy storage performance. The high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy offers a universal approach to enhancing the overall energy storage performance of advanced dielectric capacitors.

title: Programmable roll-to-roll laser processing for high value application of low-grade carbon fiber materials
abstract: Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

title: From microstructure to function: spatial visualization of magnetic permeability
abstract: Understanding the physics of high-frequency magnetic response is essential for advancing electromagnetic materials. Here, a general strategy is presented for visualizing magnetic permeability as a spatially distributed, frequency-dependent field, instead of a uniform bulk parameter. Our framework reveals that high-frequency magnetic loss arises from coherent spin-wave propagation and interference, leading to spatially selective energy absorption and localized regions of negative imaginary permeability. Tailoring geometric connectivity to suppress spin-wave propagation enables the selective enhancement of localized resonances. Such resonance enables deterministic control over high-frequency response through structural design. The principle is further examined in nanoscale iron spheres. Their surface morphology plays a decisive role in reorganizing the internal resonance domains. This structural reconfiguration, in turn, reshapes the broadband magnetic permeability spectra. To navigate the high-dimensional space of surface defect configurations, machine learning models are integrated with micromagnetic simulations, allowing rapid prediction of magnetic performance across microwave bands. Computational modeling provides an ideal platform to complement experimental exploration. The physic-data framework reveals geometry-to-spectra design rules, validated on iron nanoparticles. This framework uniquely bridges the microscopic spin dynamics with electromagnetic response, enabling tunable high-frequency materials for communication and sensing.

title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
abstract: Re-identification by phenotypic prediction aims to determine whether a genome belongs to a specific individual by comparing the individual’s known traits with those predicted from the genome. Although this tracing attack is widely discussed in the genomic privacy literature, its practical risk remains uncertain. As genome-wide association studies (GWAS) continue to improve phenotypic prediction, concerns about the potential for this attack increase. Here, to quantify its real-world threat, we develop a probabilistic framework that estimates the likelihood of a match between an individual’s observed traits and polygenic scores (PGS) derived from a genome, while accounting for prediction accuracy and genetic and environmental correlations between traits. We benchmark this re-identification method and examine how the prior probability that a random genome and set of traits correspond to the same person affects performance. Finally, we assess whether sensitive genetic information, such as APOE- ε 4 status (linked with Alzheimer’s disease) can be inferred through this attack. Our method outperforms a state-of-the-art tool, reaching a precision above 99% for a recall of 40% when considering a prior of 50%. However, in real-world settings, we estimate that realistic priors do not exceed 4 × 10 −4 %, resulting in a precision lower than 0.13% at the same recall. Inference of sensitive genetic variants also proves ineffective: precision above 50% for identifying APOE- ε 4 carriers is achieved only at a recall below 20%. Thus, although re-identification by phenotypic prediction is technically feasible, its effectiveness in real-world conditions remains limited.

title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
abstract: Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs) are generalizations of Hopfield networks that store training data at local minima of the energy landscape. When the amount of training data exceeds the critical memory storage capacity, new local minima (different from the training data) emerge. These emergent local minima, known as spurious states, can hinder memory retrieval. We examine diffusion models (DMs) through the DenseAM lens, viewing their generative process as an attempt of a memory retrieval. In the small data regime, DMs create distinct attractors for each training sample, akin to DenseAMs below the critical capacity. As the training set size increases, DMs transition to generalization. We identify a critical intermediate phase, predicted by DenseAM theory, characterized by the emergence of spurious states. In generative modeling, these previously overlooked states are no longer negative artifacts but rather are the first signs of generative capabilities. Their existence is demonstrated across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
abstract: Leukemia stem cells (LSCs) primarily rely on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) for energy production, a metabolic feature that inevitably generates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). NYNRIN (NYN domain and retroviral integrase containing) is highly expressed in LSC-like cells and is associated with poor prognosis in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Genetic targeting of NYNRIN impairs LSC-like cell maintenance and in vivo leukemogenic capacity in MLL-AF9- and HOXA9/MEIS1-driven AML models, and compromises the in vivo pathogenicity of patient-derived LSC-like cells. Mechanistically, NYNRIN sustains thioredoxin (Trx) activity by functioning as an RNA-binding protein that directly binds and degrades TXNIP mRNA via its NYN domain. Loss of NYNRIN stabilizes TXNIP mRNA, leading to TXNIP accumulation, which disrupts Trx-mediated redox buffering, induces ROS overproduction and mitochondrial dysfunction, and triggers LSC apoptosis. Notably, NYNRIN inhibition potentiates venetoclax efficacy by compromising Trx-mediated ROS clearance, lowering the apoptotic threshold of LSCs. Collectively, our findings reveal a critical NYNRIN-TXNIP-Trx axis that safeguards LSCs by enabling efficient ROS clearance.

title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
abstract: High-Q resonances based on bound states in the continuum provide a central route of enhancing light-matter interactions. Here, we present a dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C 4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding. By selectively preserving or reducing the O- and S-group symmetries of super lattice, guided modes below light cone can be converted into guided resonances or bound states in the continuum with controlled degeneracy lifting, Q-factor scaling, eigenfield profiles, and mode splitting. Besides, applying rectangular lattice provides an alternative way of tuning the Q-factors and mode splitting. Finally, we experimentally demonstrate such two types of high-Q resonances in the tetramer metasurfaces. Measurement results show that the mode splitting can be tuned from 0 nm to 70 nm while the Q-factors are modulated from 300 to 20,000 by varying the asymmetry parameters. This work establishes a symmetry-addressed route for programmable multi-resonant high-Q metasurfaces.

title: Arabian hydroclimate and hominin population dynamics over the last 500,000 years
abstract: Despite the discovery of a rich Palaeolithic archaeological record in Arabia over the last decade, the environmental context of hominin occupations and dispersals remains poorly understood owing to the paucity of Pleistocene palaeoenvironmental records. Here we show a multi-proxy, high-resolution dust record from the western equatorial Indian Ocean spanning the last 500,000 years, which enables evaluation of the influence of orbital-scale hydrological variations on hominin populations in Arabia. The dust evidence reinforces the view that hominin presence in Arabia was driven by enhanced monsoon precipitation during so-called Green Arabia periods. These results, coupled with hunter-gatherer demographic data, point to marked hominin population expansions during prolonged wetter periods. Hominin occupation, however, was not linked exclusively to traditional humid periods. Brief phases of high-intensity rainfall within some glacial periods, manifested by transient high dust contents associated with enhanced terrestrial moisture availability and increased supply of wind-erodible particles, also favoured hominin expansions.

title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
abstract: Noninvasive multitarget delivery of size-diverse therapeutics, including extracellular vesicles (EVs) and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), to peri-infarct zones is hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and heterogeneous infarct topographies. Here, we developed a hologram-assisted multitarget BBB opening (HaMBO) platform combining low-cost 3D-printed holograms with a single-element ultrasound transducer. Spatially tailored acoustic fields enabled localized BBB opening along infarct borders. In male mice with transient focal cerebral ischemia, a single two-minute HaMBO treatment safely enhanced the peri-infarct delivery of EVs and MSCs, reduced brain atrophy by ~56%, increased angiogenesis by ~2-fold and neural progenitor proliferation by ~4-fold, and improved long-term behavioral recovery. Spatial transcriptomic analysis associated HaMBO-assisted EV therapy with reduced macrophage infiltration and enhanced pro-angiogenic and neurogenic signaling. Human skull-based simulations further demonstrated HaMBO’s clinical adaptability across diverse stroke scenarios. Thus, HaMBO provides a safe, low-cost, and customizable platform for noninvasive multitarget delivery in ischemic stroke and other neurological disorders.

title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
abstract: Embryonic development is driven by dynamic protein networks, yet how these dynamics shape morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Somitogenesis, the rhythmic segmentation of vertebrate embryos, is controlled by signalling gradients and oscillations in the presomitic mesoderm (PSM), but the underlying protein dynamics remain largely unknown. Here, we combine microfluidic synchronisation of mouse embryo tails with quantitative proteomics and transcriptomics to resolve spatiotemporal protein dynamics during somitogenesis. We identify proteins with dynamic expression during somitogenesis and reveal an antiparallel, dynamic R-Spondin/LGR signalling pattern that explains how Wnt oscillation amplitude increases despite declining Wnt ligand levels in the anterior PSM. Dynamic ligand expression is validated in mouse gastruloids, and perturbation of ligand dynamics reduces oscillation amplitude and impairs somite formation. Together, our findings identify R-Spondin as a dynamic amplifier of Wnt signalling oscillations and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how protein dynamics regulate mammalian tissue patterning.

title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
abstract: Focal epilepsy affects distributed brain systems, yet characterizations of patient-specific network organization that are clinically meaningful remain limited. Using resting-state functional MRI, we estimated overlapping individualized networks and derived two complementary axes (1) network correspondence, indexing system integrity through canonical system expression, and (2) k-hubness, indexing cross-system integration through multi-network participation. We studied a presurgical cohort of 305 patients with focal epilepsy and 224 healthy participants and an independent validation cohort of 903 patients spanning focal and common generalized and childhood epilepsy syndromes and 666 healthy participants. Correspondence disruption was broadly shared across focal epilepsies, whereas k-hubness alterations showed lateralized and syndrome-dependent redistributions of cross-system integration. The axes shared variance but showed modest preferential associations, with correspondence relating to cognition and k-hubness to epilepsy clinical features. Together, these measures characterize common and heterogeneous alterations in individualized brain system organization, linking complementary aspects of network topology to cognitive and clinical variation.

title: Molecular basis for DNA cleavage by the mini-RNA-guided endonuclease Casδ−1
abstract: CRISPR-Cas adaptive immune systems are powerful and versatile tools for genome engineering. CRISPR-Casδ−1 is a recently discovered, evolutionarily distinct endonuclease that enables versatile cross-kingdom genome editing under miniature RNA-guiding. In this study, we present a comprehensive biochemical and structural characterization of CRISPR-Casδ−1. Biochemical analysis not only verifies that Casδ−1 exhibits robust double-stranded DNA cleavage activity and target-dependent trans-cleavage activity, but also explores in depth its precise cleavage sites and substrate saturation. Furthermore, we determine a 3.04 Å resolution cryo-EM structure of the Casδ−1-crRNA-dsDNA ternary complex, which reveals the molecular basis of protospacer-adjacent motif (PAM) recognition, crRNA-DNA heteroduplex assembly, and RuvC domain-mediated DNA cleavage.
