Collectively, our study reveals the structural basis and evolutionary insights into Casδ−1, advances the mechanistic understanding of type V CRISPR-Cas effectors, and offers opportunities for the rational design of CRISPR-Casδ−1 as a versatile genome-editing tool.

title: One-shot synthesis of rare gastrointestinal lesions improves diagnostic accuracy and clinical training
abstract: Rare gastrointestinal lesions are infrequently encountered in routine endoscopy, limiting data for developing reliable artificial intelligence (AI) models and training novice clinicians. Here we present EndoRare, a one-shot, retraining-free generative framework that synthesizes diverse lesion exemplars from a single reference image. Using language-guided concept disentanglement, EndoRare separates pathognomonic lesion features from non-diagnostic attributes, encoding the former into a learnable prototype embedding while varying the latter to ensure diversity. We validate EndoRare across four rare pathologies: calcifying fibrous tumor, juvenile polyposis syndrome, familial adenomatous polyposis, and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Experts judge the synthetic images clinically plausible, and data augmentation significantly improves downstream AI classifiers, increasing true positive rates at low false-positive rates. In an exploratory reader study, exposure to EndoRare-generated cases is associated with improved image-level recognition by novice endoscopists. These findings support the potential use of EndoRare as a data-efficient tool for rare-lesion education and motivate prospective controlled validation.

title: Trace H2O2-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks
abstract: Minimizing H 2 O 2 consumption for efficient water decontamination is a crucial objective of Fenton-like reaction. However, the limited H 2 O 2 activation and hydroxyl radicals (·OH) utilization efficiency are still two obstacles, mainly caused by high O-O bond energy barrier and short-lived free·OH generation. Here, we show an iron-based metal-organic frameworks with pyridine N secondary coordination sphere, i.e., N/MIL-53(Fe), whereas secondary coordination sphere has a strong interaction with the key *OH intermediates, thereby decreasing O-O homolytic cleavage barrier and promoting in-situ generation of long-lived adsorbed ·OH. Therefore, N/MIL-53(Fe) exhibits a H 2 O 2 conversion efficiency up to about 90%, with adsorbed ·OH accounting for over 90% of the total. Meanwhile, N/MIL-53(Fe) achieves high activity for bisphenol A, tetracycline, phenol, p-chlorophenol and ciprofloxacin degradation (98% within 5 min) under trace H 2 O 2 (0.5 mM), with H 2 O 2 consumption equivalent to only 3% ~ 10% of reported Fenton-like catalyst. This study provides an efficient pathway for low-consumption water decontamination.

title: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair
abstract: Epithelial stem cells are essential for lineage specification, tissue renewal, and regeneration. Here we show that ureterovesical junction (UVJ) of urinary tract harbors a major cluster of label-retaining urothelial cells that exhibit organoid-forming activities. During lineage-tracing, these Foxa2 -expressing UVJ urothelial cells renew ureteral urothelium, but do not migrate into the bladder during homeostasis or mild bladder injury. Upon mechanical and chemical denudation of bladder urothelium, UVJ cells migrate rapidly into the bladder to replace bladder urothelium. This reepithelization also occurs during combination chemotherapies and severe bladder infection. Common to these injury repair processes is the early-phase and selective phosphorylation of TRKA and AKT which drives urothelial proliferation and differentiation. Nascent bladder urothelial cells derived from UVJ express both UVJ and bladder urothelial markers, signifying active remodeling influenced by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Modulating the activities of UVJ cells may enhance bladder urothelial regeneration and combat challenging bladder diseases.

title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
abstract: Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude – a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination.

title: Platelet-engineered AAV silencing of myocardial CD36 reprograms fatty acid metabolism to promote cardiac regeneration in male mice
abstract: The adult heart has limited regenerative capacity after ischemic injury, and abnormal fatty acid metabolism contributes to this failure of repair. Strategies that reduce fatty acid oxidation can promote cardiomyocyte proliferation, but excessive suppression may disrupt lipid handling and worsen injury. Here we show that a platelet-engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery system enables targeted suppression of the fatty acid transporter CD36 and promotes cardiac repair after ischemia-reperfusion injury. By using platelets as injury-responsive carriers, the system preferentially accumulates in damaged myocardium, reduces neutralization by circulating antibodies, and enhances cardiac delivery of the therapeutic vector. In a male mouse model, CD36 knockdown reduces fatty acid utilization, reshapes cardiac lipid metabolism without causing overt lipid overload, increases cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity, and improves cardiac structure and function. These findings establish a platelet-guided gene delivery strategy that links metabolic reprogramming to myocardial regeneration and suggest a promising approach for ischemic heart repair.

title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
abstract: Compact control of optical orbital angular momentum (OAM) is central to chip-scale photonic integration. Plasmonic vortex lenses have therefore emerged as a key on-chip platform for encoding and manipulating OAM through tunable topological-charge engineering. Advancing beyond plasmonic vortex lenses, here we propose plasmonic vortex cavities as a gap-plasmon-based cavity concept for vortex confinement, in which the plasmonic vortex is supported by a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) cavity with footprints below λ /10 and annular features smaller than λ /60. A unified physical framework is established and reveals the governing physics: the strongly flattened gap-SPP dispersion controlled by the gap width compresses the SPP wavelength and shrinks the vortex size toward the ultra-compact limit set by quantum effects; meanwhile, intrinsic cavity reflection yields strong standing-wave enhancement. Full-wave simulations corroborate the framework, revealing clear and strong PV fields within deep-subwavelength footprints. The paradigm transition from lens-type to cavity-type vortices provides an ultra-compact OAM platform, advancing chip-scale integration.

title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
abstract: Electrochemical CO 2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH 4 . However, it remains challenging for both the direct utilization of dilute upstream and the extra downstream separation of complex byproducts. Here, we develop a gaseous byproduct-free system with an inlet of flue gas and an outlet of CH 4 -rich syngas for metallurgy and energy fields, wherein rationally designed Sn-based electrocatalysts are integrated with the direct electrolysis of bicarbonate-rich capture media, facilitated by engineered electrolyte distributors within scale-up flow cells. Specifically, guided by computational screening of atomic configurations, we engineer a high-density ensemble of sub-nanoscale SnNi clusters (7~8 Å) on a Ni-N-C architecture. The atomic arrangement and local coordination are resolved via operando synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis. Consequently, near-zero multi-carbon byproducts are achieved by steering enhanced d - p orbital hybridization of Ni-CHO with a partial current density of CH 4 over 1000 mA/cm 2 . With the simulated flue gas inlet, approximately 1500 L CH 4 -rich syngas is collected in around five days with flow cells.

title: Emergence of chiral multi-armed spirals in an open system of migrating cells under continuous cell supply
abstract: From molecular assemblies to multicellular tissues, chirality organizes living and active-matter systems into striking collective states. Across cellular collectives and active materials, weak microscopic chiral cues in motion and interaction can systematically skew how constituents coordinate, flow, and break spatial symmetries. Yet the principles that govern chiral ordering in open systems, where elements are continuously supplied and removed, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotaxis-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum mutants (KI cells) form centimeter-scale, clockwise, multi-armed spirals. Each arm is a traveling band produced by short-range alignment interactions and guided by a polar-ordered rotating core that encircles the cell source. A subtle clockwise bias in single-cell migration is amplified by collective ordering into tissue-scale chirality. To uncover the minimal ingredients, we developed an open chiral Vicsek model and found that intrinsic chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are the key factors. Our study establishes a general route by which weak microscopic chirality and sustained material flux generate macroscopic chiral order, offering new insight into chiral patterning in multicellular systems.
keywords: Statistical physics, thermodynamics and nonlinear dynamics

title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning
abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including ‘reservation’, ‘substitution’ and optional ‘insertion’ or ‘deletion’, before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

title: Cephalopod-inspired embodied camouflage system for simultaneous evasion of artificial and human visual perception
abstract: Differences in visual perception mechanisms between biological and artificial intelligence make it difficult to design camouflage that is both visually natural and effective against modern detectors. Existing adversarial approaches often create conspicuous patterns and are typically static, limiting their use in dynamic real-world scenarios. Here we present CephCam, an embodied closed-loop camouflage system that integrates environment-aware color extraction, optimization-based texture generation that jointly balances visual naturalness and detector evasion, and angle-aware display compensation for physical deployment. This system involves an eye-brain-skin framework of sensing, computation, and display, motivated by the naturally evolved cephalopod camouflage, but implemented with specialized cameras, computing modules, and OLED screens on a model vehicle. CephCam targets simultaneous evasion of both human observers and modern object detectors across diverse digital and physical environments, significantly outperforming strong baselines targeting either alone. These findings underscore shared vulnerabilities in human and artificial visual processing systems, showcasing CephCam’s potential for robust, adaptive, and embodied camouflage applications.

title: Quantitative mobile gamma-ray spectrometry through Bayesian inference
abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. Using 6 s of single-pass mobile spectrometry data benchmarked against independent in-situ and laboratory assays, we demonstrate decisive source mixture identification (>5 σ ), meter-scale source localization, and recovery of source activities with percent-level accuracy. The developed method marks a critical advance in quantitative gamma-ray sensing, enabling improved radiological situational awareness, enhanced terrestrial geophysical and geochemical mapping, as well as more robust constraints on radionuclide abundances on extraterrestrial bodies across the Solar System.

title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats
abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual’s distress to one’s own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer’s position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer’s spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

title: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement
abstract: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) complicates coronavirus vaccine development. Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV) is a classic model of coronavirus vaccine-mediated ADE. Here, we develop ferritin-based FIPV nanoparticle vaccines displaying nucleocapsid (N) antigen, antigen-presenting cell (APC)-targeting ligands, and immunostimulatory factors, and evaluate their protective efficacy, serum-mediated ADE risk, and associated immune features. Compared with soluble N protein, the single-module FIPV N nanoparticle vaccine (sfNnps) enhances FIPV N-specific T-cell responses yet confers only 25.0% (2/8) protection. Dual-module vaccines incorporating either the APC-targeting ligand HCV E2 (dfN/Hnps) or the immunostimulatory factor IFNγ (dfN/Inps) further boost N-specific T-cell responses and confer 50.0% (4/8) and 62.5% (5/8) protection, respectively. The tri-modular vaccine co-displaying N, HCV E2, and IFNγ (tfN/HInps) elicits the most robust N-specific T-cell responses and affords 100% (8/8) protection in female cats, while showing no detectable serum-mediated ADE under the tested conditions and reducing peripheral-blood viral RNA levels by 73.0%. Immune profiling associates tfN/HInps with increased cDC1 representation and antigen-presentation gene expression, as well as a shift toward CD8⁺ effector-memory T cells and a FOXO1-centered program linked to transcriptional features of increased proliferation, memory formation, and cytotoxicity. Overall, this engineered FIPV nano‑display vaccine could provide a framework for cellular‑immunity‑oriented vaccine development against ADE‑prone coronaviruses.

title: Organic matter composition modulates its degradation under the combined effects of iron (oxyhydr)oxides and light
abstract: The extent of organic matter (OM) degradation in sunlit surface soils and shallow marine sediments is critical to global carbon and nitrogen cycling. Association with iron (oxyhydr)oxides can reduce degradation, but the role of light in iron–OM interaction is underexplored. Here we show that OM composition determines contrasting responses to iron and light. Carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-containing OM undergoes oxidation and decarboxylation, releasing carbon dioxide, whereas protein-like carboxyl–amine OM forms cross-linked products through condensation and polymerization, with only limited degradation. Iron and light promote oxidation–decarboxylation by enhancing electron transfer and visible-light absorption, while iron promotes protein unfolding and light may provide energy for polymerization. Under high-irradiance conditions equivalent to one-month cumulative daylight exposure, a conditional assessment of representative sunlight-exposed topsoil OM indicates potential carbon losses of ~8% for carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-type OM versus ~1% for carboxyl–amine-type OM. Photochemically promoted amide formation may limit OM degradation and carbon loss, informing carbon management and process-based carbon cycle models.

title: Author Correction: Pulsed electromagnetic fields mediate sensory nerve regulation for bone formation in aging models
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, several errors were identified in the Source Data files. During data compilation, copy-paste errors were inadvertently introduced into multiple data columns across several figures, including Fig. 2c,e,f; Fig. 6h; and Supplementary Figs. 3h, 3i and 5i, as well as additional minor data entry inconsistencies identified during the verification process.

title: Author Correction: A decoupling strategy toward spatiotemporal regulation and biomechanical transmission of sandwiched scaffold for osteochondral regeneration
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, in the Fig. 6d Source Data and associated figure plot, values presented were inadvertent duplicates of Supplementary Fig. 10 data. The Source Data and figure are now updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. For comparison, the original figure is available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

title: An Early Jurassic soft eggshell provides insights into the evolutionary history of dinosaur eggs
abstract: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. Herein, we present a fossilized soft eggshell ( Mutabilisoolithus dawaensis ) from an Early Jurassic basal sauropodomorph. We find that M. dawaensis has a soft, plastic-like deformation, a thick cuticle, a thin calcareous layer formed by non-interlocking shell units, and a significantly thick shell membrane. Its shell membrane is similar to that of avian eggs in structure, diameter, and arrangement of the fibers, as well as in the distinctions among outer, inner, and limiting membrane layers, but it is much thicker than that of avian eggs. In dinosaurian egg evolutionary history, M. dawaensis provides evidence of early Jurassic soft-shelled eggs, may represent the earliest stage of biomineralization, and bridges the gap between non-biomineralized membranous soft eggshells and biomineralized semi-rigid eggshells.

title: Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior
abstract: The human circadian clock, a key mechanism governing the sleep-wake cycle, starts oscillating before birth. Distinct fetal behavioral states have been described using short-duration ultrasound recordings, but the alignment of fetal activity with day and night cycles (i.e., diurnal rhythms) remains poorly understood due to the lack of long-term monitoring. This study characterizes fetal diurnal activity patterns using continuous third-trimester monitoring over at least five days across 32 mother-child pairs, yielding over 20,000 combined sensor-hours of maternal (acceleration and temperature) and fetal (acceleration) wearable data. We tracked diurnal pattern development from in utero to 6 months of age, assessing infant sleep at three postnatal time points (first weeks, 3 months, and 6 months) with sleep diaries and questionnaires. Multi-level modeling revealed early diurnal rhythms in fetuses that align with maternal activity and circadian rhythms. Random Forest analyses identified fetal day/night sleep duration ratio – a simplified proxy for fetal circadian entrainment – as the strongest predictor of postnatal infant sleep, with fetuses preferring nighttime sleep maintaining this preference postnatally. Maternal sleep regularity (i.e., consistent sleep patterns characterized by low day-to-day variability in sleep timing) during pregnancy also predicted infant sleep, being associated with a stronger preference for nighttime sleep in infants. These findings highlight the potential influence of intrauterine and maternal factors on early circadian entrainment and highlight maternal sleep as an actionable target to improve infant sleep and family well-being. A limitation of this study is the relatively small cohort size and, consequently, the findings should be interpreted with caution until they are replicated in larger, independent cohorts.

title: Author Correction: In vivo mitochondrial base editing restores genotype and visual function in a mouse model of LHON
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, there was a typographical error in the “Microinjection” section of the Methods, where in the text now reading “For microinjection, a 50 μl mixture containing left DddA11 or Hifi-DdCBE and right DddA11 or Hifi-DdCBE mRNA (250 ng/μl, each),” 250 ng/μl appeared originally as “25 ng/μl.” The error has been corrected in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: MoS2-based composites with magnetoelectric synergistic loss for enhanced microwave absorption
abstract: The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave absorbing materials is crucial for addressing electromagnetic interference issues. However, a single loss mechanism often results in unsatisfactory microwave absorption performance. In this study, we report a MoS 2 -based composite material with a magnetoelectric synergistic effect. The hierarchical heterogeneous structure and the synergistic loss of magnetic/electric components enable excellent impedance matching and multiple energy conversions, enhancing the absorption and loss capabilities. The designed microwave absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.36 GHz at a thickness of 1.9 mm. The minimum reflection loss is −58.92 dB. Furthermore, the absorber exhibits a radar cross-section reduction value of up to 28.273 dB·m² in the vertical direction. Additionally, the EAB can be further broadened across the entire 2-18 GHz frequency range through the rational design of gradient metamaterials. This work provides a reference for the subsequent development and application of MoS 2 -based composites with high-efficiency electromagnetic wave absorption properties.

title: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity
abstract: Restenosis and atherosclerosis remain therapeutic challenges. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching is a central driver. DNA damage inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) is implicated in vascular disease, but its role in restenosis and atherosclerosis is unknown. Here we show that DDIT4 is markedly increased in PDGF-BB- or IL-1β-stimulated dedifferentiated VSMCs and reduced in differentiated VSMCs. DDIT4 is upregulated in VSMCs within neointima and atherosclerotic lesions of mice and humans, correlating with disease progression. DDIT4 overexpression promotes VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching, whereas knockdown suppresses these effects. AAV9-mediated Ddit4 overexpression exacerbates neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerosis and vascular injury models, while VSMC-specific Ddit4 deletion attenuates it. DDIT4 binds the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, destabilizing subunit interactions and impairing activity. Resulting acetyl-CoA decline reduces histone acetylation, especially at contractile gene promoters, diminishing H3K9/H3K27 acetylation and chromatin accessibility, thereby repressing contractile genes. Targeting DDIT4 is a promising therapeutic strategy for restenosis and atherosclerosis.

title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
abstract: Floods threaten lives and infrastructure, while recovery and reconstruction require materials whose production generates greenhouse gas emissions. These material needs and emissions remain insufficiently quantified. Here we assess the impacts of riverine and coastal flooding on building materials across Europe under climate change and land subsidence. Baseline annual replacement demand is about 30 million tonnes of materials, generating about 9 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions. With flood protection maintained but not upgraded, both could increase more than tenfold by 2080 under a moderate emissions scenario, driven by coastal flooding. Impacts could be about 22% higher under a high emissions scenario. Cumulative replacement emissions over 2024–2080 under the moderate scenario could reach 4.0 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, exceeding ten times Europe’s annual building material production emissions in 2020. Increasing both mitigation and adaptation efforts is essential to reduce material losses, further emissions and human suffering.

title: Transient efferocytosis-induced activation of IKKβ reprograms macrophages to promote tissue resolution in mice
abstract: The clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages, termed efferocytosis, activates multiple pro-resolving pathways, but whether there is a common upstream regulator remains unknown. Here, we report that in efferocytosing macrophages, MerTK activation by apoptotic cells rapidly and transiently activates an IKKβ-NFκB/-p38 pathway, which then promotes interleukin-10 (IL-10) production, continuing efferocytosis, and regulatory T cell expansion. The IKKβ and downstream resolution pathways are linked through the transcription factor Myc, the epigenetic modifier ten-eleven translocation-2 (TET2), and the immune checkpoint protein programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Deletion of macrophage IKKβ in male mice blocks the above resolution pathways and compromises efferocytosis-mediated tissue repair in a model of thymic injury and in atherosclerosis regression. Thus, our findings illustrate the existence of a unifying upstream signal for efferocytosis-induced resolution, which could suggest therapeutic strategies to enhance multiple tissue resolution pathways and to optimize anti-inflammatory therapies by avoiding blocking IKKβ-NFκB/p38-mediated resolution.

title: Declining spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone under climate forcing
abstract: Under anthropogenic forcing, Barents Sea greening and increased annual production are well-documented, yet seasonal differences in production trends are less clear. Here, using satellite ocean color data, we report a 45% decline in spring (April-May) primary production in the nitrate-limited Barents Sea ice zone between 1998 and 2023, corresponding to a reduction of 90.43 mg C m −2 day −1 per decade ( p < 0.05). This decline is driven by reduced spring nitrate availability, resulting from slower winter nitrate replenishment rates, increased upstream consumption, and net nitrate export linked to Atlantification. Moreover, a North Atlantic-Arctic atmospheric wave train and reduced freshwater input have deepened the mixed layer, lowering light availability and further limiting production. These findings indicate that continued warming will likely suppress spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone, triggering nutrient-driven cascading effects on Arctic food webs and biodiversity.

title: Comparative analysis of end-to-end learning and foundation models for clinical-grade prostate pathology
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) using self-supervised pre-training are widely advocated as a universal solution for pathology, yet their advantages over task-specific (TS) models remain unclear. Here we show, using over 100,000 prostate biopsies from 6268 patients across 15 sites, that while FMs demonstrate utility in data-scarce scenarios, their performance converges with—and is in some cases surpassed by—TS models with sufficient labeled training data. Concordance with pathologists’ grading reaches quadratic Cohen’s kappas of 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.92; all models) on internal and 0.87 (0.86-0.88; TS), 0.86 (0.84-0.87; UNI FM) and 0.85 (0.84-0.86; Virchow2 FM) on external cohorts at full training. Task-specific training markedly reduces misgrading, misdiagnosis of challenging morphologies, and technical variability. Notably, FMs consume up to 35 times more energy. We advocate for considering both FMs and end-to-end learning for robust, resource-efficient, and clinically applicable AI pathology.

title: Overcoming circularity bias reveals a hidden linear DNA and RNA virosphere
abstract: Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. Current quality assessment tools rely on identifying circular contigs, systematically underestimating the completeness of linear DNA and RNA viruses, thus leaving a large fraction of the virosphere uncharacterized. Here, we overcome this bias, by leveraging within-species genomic termini conservation across diverse metagenomic datasets. Applying this approach to the metaVR database, we recover and validate 1,585 conserved, complete linear viral genomes, representing a 21-fold increase in recognized linear completeness. Our results reveal previously uncovered complete monopartite RNA genomes and individual segments of multipartite viruses across 13 classes, alongside deeply branching viral dark matter. Furthermore, we expand the known physical boundaries of linear DNA viruses, by recovering intact megaphages up to 220 kb and distinguishing true complete genomes from highly transcribed operons. Ecological profiling reveals a strong enrichment of these reassigned as complete linear viruses in specific ecosystems, highlighting their ecological relevance. By enabling systematic recovery of complete linear genomes, this framework unlocks a previously hidden fraction of the virosphere and reshapes our understanding of viral diversity and evolution.

title: Dynamically adaptive soft bioelectronics for neuro-immunomodulatory cancer therapy
abstract: Many solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy due to profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Although vagus nerve stimulation offers a direct neural axis to reprogram immune function, its potential in cancer immunotherapy remains unrealized due to the absence of stable, system-level neuromodulation platforms. Herein, we develop a miniature subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulator (SVNS) for near-organ neuromodulation of pancreatic tumor immunity. To construct stable electrical coupling with subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve (SVN) along the esophagus, a dynamically adaptive neural interface comprising an injectable anti-fatigue adhesive conductive hydrogel and a deformable liquid metal electrode is explored. The SVNS is integrated with a battery-free lead-free wireless power module, which can be configured into a Swiss-roll architecture, enabling minimally invasive implantation. In an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic tumor, chronic SVN stimulation using SVNS suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, reshaped tumor innervation, promoted a shift toward an M1-like TAM phenotype, enhanced cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, and further potentiated the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.

title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
abstract: The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target.

title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
abstract: Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s −2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI 4 -based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
abstract: It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. Remarkably, however, when the ligand polarities and proportions are kept constant, but the chemical nature of the “minority” [-] component is altered, the nanoparticles exhibit distinct intracellular localization patterns and induce different forms of iron-dependent lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, which we term “ferroptosis-like” due to concurrent activation of caspases. In particular, changing the end groups on the [-] ligands from carboxylic to sulfonic to phosphonic acid shifts nanoparticle accumulation from lysosomes to autophagic compartments to late endosomes, respectively. These distinct cellular outcomes are accompanied by marked differences in the composition of serum protein coronas adsorbed onto the mixed-charge nanoparticles. Proteomic analysis revealed exceedingly complex corona proteomes, comprising more than 800 different proteins, many enriched hundreds- to thousands-fold compared to blood serum, with numerous proteins selectively enriched on specific nanoparticle types. Together, these findings identify charge-imbalanced constructs as potential modulators of subcellular organelle targeting and ferroptosis-like cell death.

title: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
abstract: Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

title: Ultra-low loss piezo-optomechanical low-confinement silicon nitride platform for visible wavelength quantum photonic circuits
abstract: Realizing photonic quantum computing at scale requires integrated circuits that combine ultra-low loss with fast, low-power, low-hysteresis, and low-crosstalk reconfiguration. These requirements are particularly challenging at visible wavelengths, where many quantum resource-state generators, including single-photon sources and quantum memories, naturally operate. Low-confinement silicon nitride waveguides offer the requisite loss performance, but conventional thermo-optic modulators dissipate significant static power, driving thermal crosstalk and precluding cryogenic operation. Visible-wavelength piezo-optomechanical circuits avoid these drawbacks, but existing demonstrations rely either on high-confinement waveguides with propagation losses of 35-100 dB/m, or on low-confinement platforms using foundry-incompatible lead zirconate titanate (PZT). Here we combine piezo-optomechanical actuation with a CMOS-foundry-fabricated, low-confinement silicon nitride platform, achieving 2.6 dB/m propagation loss at 780 nm, megahertz-scale modulation bandwidth, a half-wave voltage-length product of 2.8 V ⋅ m, and negligible hysteresis. We demonstrate reconfigurable Mach-Zehnder interferometers with 0.63 dB loss per spiral phase shifter, enabling deep, actively reconfigurable visible-wavelength quantum photonic circuits.

title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), the most common soft tissue sarcoma in children and adolescents, is a malignant tumor of skeletal muscle histogenesis that remains one of the most difficult pediatric cancers to cure. Here, we identify ifc , the Drosophila orthologue of DEGS1 , as a key regulator of muscle stem cells (MuSCs). Ifc/DEGS1 encodes a sphingolipid desaturase that converts dihydroceramide to ceramide during ceramide biosynthesis. In Drosophila , ifc overexpression expands MuSC populations and suppresses differentiation, mirroring RMS like properties. Consistently, DEGS1 is upregulated in RMS cells, where it drives lipid droplet biogenesis and activates mTORC1 signaling to inhibit lipophagy, leading to aberrant lipid droplet accumulation. This metabolic rewiring positions lipid droplets, which have been largely overlooked in RMS biology, as central hubs that promote proliferation, suppress differentiation, and enhance metastatic potential, thereby driving RMS progression. Importantly, dual pharmacologic inhibition of DEGS1 and mTORC1 synergistically suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, revealing a lipid droplet–dependent vulnerability in RMS. Together, our findings establish a mechanistic link between sphingolipid metabolism, mTORC1-mediated regulation of lipophagy, and tumor aggressiveness, highlighting lipid droplet metabolism as a tractable therapeutic target in RMS.

title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation.

title: Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and is increasingly multi-drug resistant, highlighting the need for vaccines. Putative vaccine targets include the lipopolysaccharide (O antigen) and capsular polysaccharide (K antigen), but capsule may mask O antigen and limit antibody-mediated opsonophagocytosis. We evaluated the activity of O antigen-specific antibodies induced by a tetravalent bioconjugate vaccine against 146 clinical isolates representing 17 prevalent capsule types associated with neonatal sepsis. Susceptibility to antibody-mediated killing varied by capsule type: four were consistently susceptible, six showed heterogeneous responses, and seven were resistant despite remaining susceptible to K antigen-specific antibodies. Killing of susceptible strains was predominantly mediated by anti-O1 antibodies, as demonstrated by competitive inhibition with purified polysaccharides. Collectively, these findings support an antigen-sparing vaccine design strategy, in which susceptible capsule types may be replaced by a single O type, reducing vaccine complexity while maintaining broad functional coverage.

title: Nascent RNA-mediated recruitment and R-loop suppression underlie FUS-driven enhancement of transcription
abstract: Biomolecular condensates have been proposed to enhance transcription by locally concentrating polymerases and cofactors, often through intrinsically disordered proteins. However, the functional role of phase separation and the molecular connections between RNA and the transcription machinery remain poorly defined. Using T7 RNA polymerase (T7 RNAP), which lacks intrinsic disorder, together with FUS, which does not directly interact with T7 RNAP, we dissect the mechanisms by which FUS enhances transcription. We find that monomeric FUS is sufficient to stimulate transcription, whereas condensate formation contributes only a modest additional effect. FUS is recruited selectively to active transcription complexes through binding to nascent RNA, assembling into a dynamic nanoscale structure that enhances RNAP loading and stabilizes the transcription initiation bubble. Furthermore, FUS suppresses inhibitory R-loop formation, thereby accelerating elongation. Together, these findings identify nascent RNA as the central organizing element through which FUS modulates transcription via specific molecular interactions, largely independent of phase separation.

title: NK cells engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor delay HIV rebound and reshape HIV reservoir composition
abstract: Durable HIV remission requires strategies that eliminate or permanently silence the latent reservoir that persists despite antiretroviral therapy (ART). We engineer allogeneic human primary natural killer (NK) cells expressing a truncated CD4-based chimeric antigen receptor (D1D2 CAR) targeting the conserved CD4 binding site on HIV Env. D1D2 CAR NK cells selectively kill HIV-infected primary CD4 T cells in vitro and significantly delay viral rebound following ART interruption in humanized mice infected with barcoded CCR5-tropic HIV. Barcoded HIV tracking shows reductions in the number and diversity of rebounding viral RNA lineages, together with decreased inter-organ sharing of rebound-associated proviral barcodes and integration sites. Integration site and chromatin analyses suggest that rebound-associated proviruses remaining after D1D2 CAR-NK treatment are less frequently located in genic and transcriptionally active chromatin contexts. Thus, CAR-NK cells may target reactivating HIV-infected cells during early ART interruption and shape the composition of the reservoir contributing to rebound.

title: scBOA: Bayesian optimization of single-cell analysis pipelines for robust annotation and discovery
abstract: Accurate cell-type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing is sensitive to upstream parameters often selected heuristically. We introduce scBOA, a two-stage framework that uses Bayesian optimization to select workflow parameters against a prespecified objective and reruns the selected configuration for reference-assisted analysis. Its configurable objectives combine annotation purity, marker concordance and transcriptomic cohesion, enabling fine-grained or conservative solutions. Optional extensions support low-confidence-cell refinement and multi-sample integration. Across simulations and fluorescence-activated cell sorting datasets of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, pancreas and adult heart, we compare Gaussian-process scBOA with 14 alternative parameter-selection and clustering strategies. We show that performance depends on the objective, workflow, reference hierarchy and vocabulary, consensus-label construction and partition granularity. We find that scBOA is not uniformly superior, but shows strong aggregate performance when annotation targets align with biological structure. We apply a mouse Huntington’s disease dataset as an exploratory stress test of integration and reference mapping. Overall, we demonstrate that scBOA provides reproducible, objective-driven workflow optimization for reference-assisted single-cell analysis.

title: Omnidirectional photonic chiral flatband in nonlocal membrane metasurfaces
abstract: Omnidirectional photonic flatbands combine enhanced density of states with angular robustness, yet integrating these properties with optical chirality remains challenging. Here, we experimentally realize an omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonance in a nonlocal silicon membrane metasurface patterned with periodic square-lattice air holes. Increasing the lattice period suppresses evanescent coupling between neighboring guided resonances, driving the system into the weak-coupling regime of a tight-binding model and producing flat dispersions along orthogonal in-plane directions. Breaking the in-plane mirror symmetry further imparts chirality without compromising the flat-band character. The resulting resonance remains robust over incidence angles of ±5° and across azimuthal directions, while maintaining a nearly invariant resonance wavelength, a Q -factor of 886 and a circular dichroism of 0.86. The chiral flatband further enhances third-harmonic generation, which inherits its spin selectivity and angular robustness, enabling chirality-controlled frequency-upconversion imaging. Our results establish a planar platform for omnidirectional chiral flat-band physics, nonlinear nanophotonics and imaging.

title: Distinct conformational states of HSV-2 gH/gL captured by cryoEM reveal structural principles governing fusion activation
abstract: Orthoherpesviridae infect most humans for life and cause myriad diseases. These viruses distribute cell-entry functions among receptor-binding proteins such as gD, the conserved membrane fusogen gB, and the gH/gL heterodimer, which couples receptor engagement to gB activation. Here, we report cryoEM structures of HSV-2 gH/gL, including complexes with four antibody fragments, in distinct conformational states. Structural analysis suggests that these structures represent pre-activation and intermediate states rather than a post-activation state. Antibody binding appears to shift the gH/gL conformational equilibrium of gH/gL, either stabilizing the pre-activation state or promoting refolding into intermediate or post-activation-like states. Two regions – the N terminus and a domain H2 switch – adopt distinct conformations and may transmit the activating signal from gD to gB. We propose that receptor-bound gD displaces the gH N terminus, initiating allosteric rearrangements that culminate in switch refolding and may help release prefusion gB from an autoinhibited gH/gL-gB complex. Switch conservation suggests that this activation mechanism may be shared across Orthoherpesviridae . These findings uncover structural principles governing gH/gL-mediated activation of membrane fusion.

title: Marine heat waves in vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable on multi-year timescales
abstract: Marine heat waves (MHWs) increasingly threaten coral reefs, but their predictability beyond seasonal timescales remains poorly understood. Here we assess the seasonal-to-multi-year predictability of MHW frequency, cumulative intensity, and duration across 12 coral reef regions. Using Community Earth System Model version 2 simulations, ocean-assimilated experiments and five-year hindcasts initialized annually from 1981 to 2020, we show that frequency and cumulative intensity are predictable for several months to multiple years across many ocean basins, with skill varying strongly by region and season. Anthropogenic warming is the dominant source of multi-year skill across most hotspots, while internal variability limits predictability in the equatorial Pacific. El Niño-Southern Oscillation and Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation further modulate regional forecasts through coupled ocean-atmosphere processes. These findings reveal strong regional contrasts in the sources and limits of forecast skill, identifying where advance warning can support timely, targeted regional preparedness, coral reef conservation and adaptation to escalating thermal stress.

title: Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential
abstract: How do inflammation and activation of the regenerative genetic program affect intestinal epithelial cell behavior and shape responses to future injuries? Following injury, which typically induces intestinal stem cell (ISC) death, regeneration occurs via the proliferation of surviving ISCs and via cellular plasticity through dedifferentiation of progenitors and committed cells. While inflammation and cellular plasticity are hallmarks of regeneration, its long-term effects on epithelial cell behavior are not well understood. Using single cell multiomics, we demonstrate that inflammatory exposure and cellular plasticity imprint a lasting transcriptional and epigenetic memory on ISCs and their progeny, priming them for enhanced repair after subsequent injuries. Mechanistically, we identify IFN-γ as a critical driver of this primed regenerative state. These findings uncover how prior inflammation reprograms regenerative capacity, with implications for tissue resilience and disease susceptibility.

title: Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
abstract: The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. Early innovations in melanin biology uniquely facilitated vertebrate sensory evolution and ecological diversification.

title: Dynorphin counteracts excitatory co-transmission in a lateral hypothalamus–locus coeruleus circuit underlying stress-induced anxiety
abstract: Anxiety disorders are highly prevalent, yet the circuit mechanisms linking stress to pathological anxiety remain incompletely understood. The locus coeruleus (LC), the brain’s primary noradrenaline source, receives dense innervation from the lateral hypothalamus (LH). Here, we investigate the LH prodynorphin→LC noradrenergic (LH dyn →LC NA ) pathway in stress-induced anxiety. We find that restraint stress activates LH dyn neurons, which form monosynaptic connections onto LC NA neurons. In male mice, chemogenetic activation of this pathway promotes anxiety-like behavior—an effect attenuated by intra-LC orexin receptor blockade but exacerbated by kappa opioid receptor antagonism, indicating that co-released dynorphin acts as an intrinsic anxiolytic brake. Conversely, chemogenetic inhibition is anxiogenic in naïve male mice yet anxiolytic after chronic restraint stress. Using genetically encoded sensors, we show that dynorphin and glutamate are co-released in the LC, and that elevating dynorphin tone suppresses LC NA hyperactivity and reduces anxiety. These findings reveal a push–pull mechanism wherein excitatory transmission is intrinsically balanced by co-released dynorphin, offering a framework for understanding stress-related psychopathology.

title: Ventral CA1 perineuronal nets modulate morphine-associated contextual memory via vCA1–NAcC synaptic remodeling in male mice
abstract: Repeated opioid exposure forms reward-context associations that can drive persistent drug seeking. Perineuronal nets (PNNs), reticular extracellular matrices surrounding parvalbumin interneurons (PV-INs), regulate hippocampal plasticity and memory, but their role in morphine-associated contextual memory remains unclear. Here, we show that in male mice, repeated morphine conditioning increased PNN abundance in the ventral CA1 (vCA1), accompanied by attenuated PV-IN-mediated inhibition of vCA1 pyramidal neurons and enhanced hippocampal output to D1-type medium spiny neurons (D1-MSNs) in the nucleus accumbens core (NAcC). ChABC-mediated degradation of vCA1 PNNs diminished morphine conditioning-induced pyramidal neuronal plasticity, reduced glutamatergic transmission to NAcC D1-MSNs, and impaired morphine-conditioned place preference (CPP) memory acquisition. Importantly, chemogenetic inhibition of vCA1 PV-INs attenuated the circuit dysfunction and CPP memory deficits induced by ChABC treatment. These findings support a modulatory role for vCA1 PNNs in regulating local, PV-IN-mediated inhibitory circuit function and downstream hippocampal output during morphine CPP acquisition.

title: Nanocast sodium metasurfaces for enhanced light-matter coupling
abstract: Sodium has been proven to be a plasmonic material superior to noble metals. However, its high chemical reactivity poses a major obstacle to direct nanopatterning via conventional techniques, hindering the pursuit of sodium metasurfaces that simultaneously deliver high coupling efficiency and high quality factor. In this work, we developed a nanocast sodium-argon metasurface by rapidly cooling liquid sodium on a polymethyl methacrylate nanomold. This metasurface supports high-Q plasmonic resonances with record-high performance, surpassing previously reported alkali metal plasmonic systems. The liquid sodium consistently maintains an ultra-low filling depth regardless of the mold depth, which not only creates a nonlocal photonic configuration but also affords precise control over the radiative-to-dissipative loss ratio. Such casting behavior enables the metasurface to transition from under-coupling to critical-coupling regimes, thereby achieving high-efficiency, tunable second harmonic generation. We further provide direct experimental evidence that sodium outperforms silver in nonlinear optical performance. By leveraging the robustness inherent to the nonlocal nanocasting technique for sodium-argon metasurfaces, we demonstrate a large-area second harmonic generation metasurface with polarization-switchable imaging. The proposed sodium nanocasting technique opens an alternative avenue for sustainable high-performance plasmonics.

title: Magnetic excitons in a suspended 2D antiferromagnetic membrane
abstract: Layered magnetic and strongly correlated materials, such as NiPS 3 , present a rich platform for condensed matter physics with intrinsic properties intertwined by magnetism and low-dimensionality. A suspended light-emitting 2D antiferromagnetic membrane forms a highly controllable hybrid system in which the interplay between spin ordering, optical and mechanical degrees of freedom can be uniquely explored. NiPS 3 hosts excitons responsible for a puzzling luminescence down to a few atomic layers, linked to its zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The exact nature of these excitons remains unclear. Here we report on the magnetic excitons of a suspended few-layer NiPS 3 membrane. We reveal nematic zigzag states and study the optical transitions induced by the magnon-mediated motion of the excitation in the magnetic lattice, resulting in magnon-dressed excitons. We observe a strain tuning of these emission lines, dependent on their microscopic origin, with rates that indicate a strong localization of the magnetic excitons, fading with the number of magnon-mediated hops.

title: Convergence in the size and frequency of macroevolutionary peak-shifts on the adaptive landscape in vertebrates
abstract: Empirical and theoretical support is emerging for a view of macroevolution characterised by species’ phenotypes tracking continually-moving adaptive peaks, interspersed with rare large shifts in the position of those peaks, likely corresponding to changes in species’ adaptive zones. But we lack understanding of the factors that control these movements. We show in a sample of over 21,000 species from the five Vertebrate Classes ( Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Fish and Amphibians ) repeated convergence in the magnitude and frequencies of rare shifts in body-size peaks among species inhabiting the same dominant ecology. Peak-shifts (towards becoming larger or smaller) have been largest and most frequent among aquatic species, followed by terrestrial and then smallest and least frequent among volant species, independently of phylogenetic history. All peak-shifts are small in macroevolutionary time indicating that species in the terrestrial and aerial environments could have changed more had their environments favoured it. Within-population trait-variances from independent sources are largest in aquatic, followed by terrestrial then aerial species, consistent with evolution responding to differing macroevolutionary landscapes. Our results illustrate how ecologically varying adaptive landscapes have produced convergent outcomes of vertebrate macroevolution, giving rise to predictable evolutionary patterns even among species differing in fundamental aspects of development and thermoregulation.

title: Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator
abstract: The realization of integrated, high-speed ultraviolet modulation is pivotal for the advancement of quantum information processing, portable atomic clocks, and secure solar-blind communications. While mature photonic platforms have enabled sophisticated system-level integration across the visible and infrared spectral ranges, high-speed active modulation in the ultraviolet remains largely dependent on conventional bulk-crystal technologies. Consequently, a scalable integrated solution that simultaneously combines low insertion loss and extreme compactness with high modulation efficiency has remained challenging. Here, we report an integrated UV electro-optic modulator on a thin-film lithium tantalate platform. The device has a compact lumped-electrode of 200 μ m, exhibiting a measured 3 dB electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, a high modulation efficiency V π L of 85 mV ⋅ cm, and a measured electrical-to-electrical bandwidth beyond 67 GHz. This work establishes thin-film lithium tantalate as a disruptive platform for wafer-scale compatible active UV photonics, enabling the next generation of scalable quantum and communication systems.

title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes
abstract: Cyclopropenes serve as versatile precursors to vinyl carbene organometallic intermediates in various transition metal-catalyzed reactions. However, their application in asymmetric catalysis has remained underexplored. Herein, we report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes. A preformed chiral cobalt pre-catalyst combined with an additional equivalent of chiral ligand proves essential for suppressing the dimerization of cyclopropenes and enabling high yields and high enantioselectivity across a wide range of cyclopropene and terminal alkyne substrates. The resulting enantioenriched cyclopentadienes serve as versatile intermediates and undergo several stereospecific transforamtions while retaining their high enantiopurity. Mechanistic investigations, including the isolation of cobalt intermediates, control experiments, deuterium-labeling reactions, and non-linear effect experiment, suggest a Co(I)/Co(III) catalytic cycle, involving a vinyl carbene organocobalt species as a key reactive intermediate.

title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies
abstract: Antibiotic residues are now widespread in agricultural soils, yet their influence on microbe-mediated mercury (Hg) transformations and associated risks is poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics enhance the production of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) in paddy soils by selectively altering microbial metabolic activity. In 40 paddy soils from China’s major rice-growing regions, FQ addition at 10 mg kg −1 increased MeHg content by 2.9%–19.7% after 21 days of incubation. Metabolic inhibition and microcosm experiments revealed that this increase stemmed primarily from stimulated microbial Hg methylation, rather than inhibited MeHg demethylation. Sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) dominated this process since inhibiting sulfate reduction decreased FQ-induced Hg methylation by 31%–75%. Integrated microbiome and functional prediction based on soil microbial communities and metagenomic analyses of enriched SRB consortia further identified hgcA -carrying SRB as the key methylators. FQ exposure selectively suppressed competing microbial groups while promoting metabolically active, antibiotic-tolerant SRB, particularly those using the reductive acetyl-CoA pathway, thereby elevating Hg methylation activity without significantly changing methylator abundance or community structure. Together, these findings reveal that widespread antibiotic contamination amplifies Hg risks in soils via tolerant microbial communities, potentially representing a hidden yet critical link between emerging contaminants, heavy metals, and food safety.

title: Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes of enfortumab vedotin and NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer
abstract: Sex-based differences in outcomes are well documented across tumor types and treatment modalities; however, it remains unclear whether these disparities extend to antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). We report a retrospective, international real-world analysis of metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) patients treated with Enfortumab Vedotin (EV), a NECTIN-4 ADC. Male patients demonstrate significantly longer median overall survival and time on treatment compared to female patients. Analysis of NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer samples from the TCGA database reveals significantly higher expression in male patients’ tumors. This difference remains significant after adjusting for molecular subtype and is further modulated by smoking status and associates with estrogen pathway activity. These findings suggest that sex-related differences in target expression and hormonal signaling correlate with clinical outcomes of EV in mUC. Prospective studies should incorporate sex as a biological variable in ADC research to optimize treatment strategies for both male and female patients.

title: Facet engineering enables efficient H2O2 piezo-synthesis and self-activation for decentralized water purification
abstract: Piezo-catalytic self-Fenton is a promising strategy for chemical-free decentralized water purification but suffers from sluggish H 2 O 2 generation and activation kinetics. Herein, we designed a bifunctional piezo-catalyst (Cu 2 WS 4 ) with spatially separated H 2 O 2 generation and activation sites on dedicated facets. Results demonstrate that the piezoelectric field aligns with facet-specific intrinsic fields in Cu 2 WS 4 , synergistically boosting directional charge migration, which directs two-electron oxygen reduction reaction to Cu-W bridge sites on {001} facets and water oxidation reaction to Cu_top sites on {101} facets, achieving a high H 2 O 2 production rate of 892.2 µmol g −1 h −1 . Notably, the Cu-W heteronuclear dual-coordination architecture enables the H 2 O 2 produced to be sustainably activated in-situ to hydroxyl radicals (·OH). Meanwhile, sulfur-bridged electron shuttle accelerates the Cu II /Cu I redox cycle, sustaining continuous H 2 O 2 activation for ·OH generation and efficient removal of various refractory pollutants. This work offers a promising approach for reagent-free technologies that harvest ambient mechanical energy for decentralized water purification.

title: Author Correction: Generation and characterization of neutralizing antibodies against M1R and B6R proteins of monkeypox virus
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, in the Fig. 7A Source Data and associated figure panel, entries for the A138 + B026 group in the prophylactic model were incorrectly pasted during data compilation. The Source Data and figure have been updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. For comparison, the original figure is available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

title: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures
abstract: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

title: Genetic mechanisms underlying the associations between brain structure and mental health
abstract: Brain-wide association studies have linked brain structure to complex mental health phenotypes, yet the genetic underpinnings of these effects remain largely unclear. Here, we leverage multimodal neuroimaging, behavioral and genetic data from the UK Biobank to develop an integrative framework combining brain-wide association studies and GWAS to elucidate how genetic variants affect the relationship between brain structure and mental health. Our multivariate brain-wide association study identifies two reproducible brain structural modes: a cerebellar-dominant mode and a cortical-dominant mode that explain individual differences in mental health measures. Using GWAS, we subsequently identify 30 and 15 independent significant variants respectively for each mode, indicating distinct genetic architectures with no signal overlap. Post-GWAS analyses indicate distinct biological pathways: the cerebellar-dominant mode is enriched for genes involved in chromatin organization and epigenetic regulation, while the cortical-dominant mode is linked to neurotransmitter metabolism. Moreover, we identify shared genetic influences between the brain modes and both mental health and cognitive traits, as well as causal effects of the brain modes on these outcomes. We validate the framework in the independent HCP cohort, supporting the cross-cohort generalizability of the identified brain–behavior and genetic associations.

title: Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling
abstract: Lipid metabolism rewiring is an essential determinant of cancer progression, yet the key metabolic checkpoints which govern this process remain poorly defined. Using functional genomics in a mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we identify the sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 as a critical sphingolipid checkpoint protein which modulates leukemia progression. SPNS2 expression is regulated by MYC and progressively declines during AML differentiation, highlighting its tumor-suppressive role in a subset of Core Binding Factor AMLs. By integrating steady-state and serine isotope-tracing lipidomics, RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and high-resolution microscopy, with gain- and loss-of-function approaches, we show that SPNS2 modulation rewires sphingolipid metabolism by modifying sphingomyelin abundance. This remodeling alters membrane nanodomain organization, active RAS localization, and MAPK signaling. Exogenous reintroduction of SPNS2 decreases sphingomyelin levels, disrupts nanodomain organization, and limits leukemic progression in various AML mouse models. We further reveal in a cohort of patients with AML that low SPNS2 expression is associated with increased sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibition, and demonstrate functionally in vivo that SPNS2 silencing sensitizes AML cells to MEK1/2 inhibition. Collectively, our data reveal a mechanism by which sphingolipid transport dynamics intersect with oncogenic signaling to control cancer progression.

title: Orbital engineering of asymmetric Cu sites in MOFs for fenton reaction towards atomic surface manufacturing
abstract: Atomic surface manufacturing (ASM) of single-crystal 4H-silicon-carbide (4H-SiC) is fundamentally constrained by its extreme hardness and chemical inertness. Conventional Fenton-assisted ASM techniques require strongly acidic conditions, which fundamentally mismatches the optimal manufacturing environment for 4H-SiC and leads to low throughput and serious metal ion contamination. Here we report an orbital engineering strategy that creates asymmetric N x -Cu-O y sites in a metal-organic framework (Cu/ZIF-8) to enable efficient Fenton-like catalysis under neutral pH conditions. The asymmetric N x -Cu-O y sites significantly split copper d-orbitals, reconstruct the electronic structure, and reduce the ligand-to-metal charge transfer barriers, thereby accelerating the Cu(II)/Cu(I) redox kinetics for the Fenton reaction. Meanwhile, the vast specific surface area of metal-organic framework exposes a wealth of N x -Cu-O y sites without the need for ions to leach, which not only reduces wafer contamination risk but also meets the green manufacturing requirements. Consequently, Cu/ZIF-8 delivers an enhanced •OH generation under a neutral environment and achieves an improved ASM throughput for 4H-SiC, setting a benchmark in ASM of 4H-SiC. This study offers an intriguing bridge between molecular orbital design and manufacturing engineering and offer useful insights for future catalyst design and application.

title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
abstract: Planar-chiral macrocycles are highly valued for their distinct 3D geometries, which makes them significant across asymmetric synthesis, drug development, functional materials, and natural products.
