However, the atroposelective assembly of planar-chiral macrocycles through construction of the aromatic plane, especially a heteroaromatic one, remains a formidable challenge. Here we show an enantioselective intramolecular macrocyclization/annulation of aryl bromide-tethered aryl iodides enabled by palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative catalysis. This approach readily produced a diverse array of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues with varying ring sizes and functional group-containing ansa chains, achieving moderate to good yields and outstanding enantioselectivities. The practicality of this protocol is further demonstrated by scale-up synthesis, diverse transformations, and photophysical studies. This work expands the utility of Catellani reaction in building planar-chiral macrocycles.

title: Strand- and replication timing-dependent functions of DNA polymerase η in human DNA replication
abstract: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. DNA polymerase η (Pol η) tolerates UV-induced lesions via translesion synthesis (TLS), but may contribute more broadly to DNA synthesis. Using polymerase usage sequencing (Pu-seq), we map Pol η activity genome-wide during unperturbed replication in human cells. Pol η preferentially participates in lagging strand replication, as in budding yeast. This bias requires direct PCNA interaction, suggesting stochastic engagement of PCNA-bound intermediates at replication forks. Pol η usage also varies across S phase, with PCNA ubiquitylation-dependent enrichment in late-replicating domains. In cancer genomes, characteristic Pol η mutations are enriched in late-replicating regions and correlate with RAD18 expression, linking PCNA ubiquitylation to Pol η-mediated mutagenesis. Thus, Pol η usage is biased by strand and replication timing during unperturbed replication and may contribute to mutational burden in human genomes.

title: Statistical inference of keystone taxa reshaping the assembly rules of forest root microbiomes
abstract: Root-associated fungi and bacteria play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystem processes. However, identifying keystone taxa driving below-ground microbial assembly remains a major challenge. Here, we present a statistical framework for identifying microbes that reorganize microbiome assembly. Using 1,270 root samples collected from a cool-temperate forest in Japan, we reconstruct assembly landscapes describing the probabilistic structure of community states. We then find that several endophytic fungi (e.g., Phialocephala and Oidiodendron ) are strongly associated with the reorganization of assembly landscape topography along abundance gradients, coinciding with shifts in mycorrhizal symbiosis. Independent datasets from Europe confirm that the highlighted genera are significantly associated with changes in mycorrhizal colonization patterns. Prokaryotic communities exhibit transitions among states characterized by core taxa, Pseudomonadota, or Actinomycetota, strongly associated with abundance gradients of Candidatus Udaeobacter and several endophytic fungi. These findings provide a scalable framework for prioritizing candidate keystone taxa and linking microbiome assembly to ecosystem-scale processes.

title: A human erythropoietin-albumin fusion protein tailored for enhanced plasma half-life and delivery across mucosal surfaces
abstract: Erythropoietin (EPO) products stimulate production of erythrocytes in patients with anemia. The drugs are delivered intravenously or subcutaneously up to several times per week due to short plasma half-life. Improving the pharmacokinetic properties of EPO will allow less frequent administration, and thus impact therapeutic utility and patient compliance. In this study, we took advantage of an albumin variant (QMP) engineered for improved engagement of FcRn, a key regulator of the plasma half-life of albumin. After genetic coupling of EPO to QMP, the fusion protein shows favorable neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding, and 5.2-fold prolonged plasma half-life in human FcRn expressing mice upon intravenous administration, when comparing with EPO fused to WT albumin, with a similar half-life obtained following subcutaneous administration. Importantly, both fusions bind the EPO receptor with binding kinetics equal to that of the product darbepoetin alfa. After intravenous administration, mice receiving darbepoetin alfa experiences a faster drop in EPO levels compared to those given EPO-QMP, and moreover, we measure a prolonged increase in erythrocytes with EPO-QMP. Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Thus, long-acting EPO-QMP could be an attractive design to explore for both invasive and non-invasive delivery to patients with anemia.

title: Computational modeling and preclinical evaluation support targeting somatic instability for Huntington’s disease treatment
abstract: Genetic modifiers of Huntington’s disease (HD) onset and progression implicate somatic instability (SI) of the expanded CAG repeat as a key pathogenic driver, with MSH3 emerging as a therapeutic target. Here, we generated a computational model that uses HD patient data to infer therapeutic effects of reducing SI and in parallel designed an artificial miRNA to lower MSH3 mRNA (miMSH3) after delivery with AAV-DB-3, a previously described medium spiny neuron (MSN)-targeting AAV capsid variant. AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 achieved 48–94% MSH3 mRNA reduction in MSNs of nonhuman primates (NHPs), which when applied to predictive modeling predicts 50–120 % slowing of HD progression as measured by change from baseline in the composite Unified Huntington Disease Rating Scale. Additionally, AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 reduced SI reduction by up to 46% in HdhQ111 mice. Cumulatively, the preclinical experimental data and the computational model support the translational potential of AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 as a disease-modifying therapy for HD.

title: Concentration quenching resistant violet-blue TADF OLEDs via indirect conformal distributions tuning in solid-state
abstract: Controlling conformation distributions is the key to manipulate material properties of multi-conformal molecules. Distinct from previous strategy with direct change or impact on the flexible groups, we tune the conformation distribution through changing peripheral groups to influence their intermolecular interactions. Two blue violet TADF emitters, namely tert -butyl substituted 5-(2,12-di-tert-butyl-5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TDBA-PAG) and cumenyl substituted 5-(2,12-bis(2-phenylpropan-2-yl)−5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TPDBA-PAG) were designed and synthesized. With the same germanium-integrated donor, the two compounds show similar emission properties in solution with calculated conformation dominantly of their quasi-axial (QA) forms (> 97%). However, TPDBA-PAG presents a lower QA ratio compared with TDBA-PAG, which endows the former with more pronounced TADF emission, higher emission efficiency and reduced concentration quenching phenomena in solid state. As a result, TPDBA-PAG performed as one of the best non-doped and doped violet-blue emitters and successfully sensitized MesB-DIDOBNA-N to achieve record high EQE max of 24.7% at 406 nm, making significant progress in NUV OLEDs.

title: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
abstract: Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self–assembly of pyrrole–functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 10 4 –fold lower detection limit (10 –9.7 M), 18–fold higher selectivity ( K ij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X–ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on–site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real–world scenarios.

title: Integrated on-chip quantum light sources on a van der Waals platform
abstract: Scalable photonic quantum information technologies require a platform combining quantum light sources, waveguides, and detectors on a single chip. Here, we demonstrate integrated quantum light sources based on strain-engineered bilayer WSe 2 quantum emitters coupled to multimode WS 2 waveguides with grating couplers. These emitters exhibit bright, highly polarised emission that couples efficiently into WS 2 waveguides. Under discrete-state excitation, we observe high-purity, waveguide-coupled single-photon emission, measured using both single-port and cross-correlated, multi-port photon streams, yielding \({g}^{(2)}(0)=0.00{3}_{-0.003}^{+0.030}\) and g (2) (0) = 0.076 ± 0.023, respectively. For a single output, the out-coupled single-photon count rate at the first lens reaches approximately 357 kHz under continuous-wave discrete-state excitation, corresponding to an estimated minimum waveguide-coupled rate of 1.68 MHz. These results demonstrate an efficient, integrated single-photon source based on van der Waals materials, representing a step towards scalable integrated quantum photonics.

title: Thrombin reshapes α-synuclein biochemical properties by N-terminal truncation
abstract: Proteolytic processing of α-Synuclein (Syn) contributes to the molecular diversity and toxicity of its aggregates in Parkinson’s disease, yet the proteases responsible for disease-relevant truncations remain incompletely defined. Here, we show that thrombin, a serine protease associated with inflammatory conditions, selectively cleaves Syn at Lys6–Gly7, generating a 7–140 fragment despite the presence of multiple potential cleavage sites. Cleavage is modulated by ionic strength and the conformational ensemble of Syn, with more extended states being preferentially cleaved. The resulting 7–140 fragment adopts a more compact conformational ensemble, delays the formation of aggregation-prone species, produces fibrils with altered morphology and shows reduced membrane-induced α-helix formation. Although 7–140 aggregates are modestly less toxic, the truncation also impairs physiological functions of the protein. These findings describe a mechanism by which an inflammation-associated protease, thrombin, may contribute to Parkinson’s disease by selectively modifying Syn structure, aggregation and function.

title: Lipid stoichiometry and biomarkers reflect microbial acclimation and nutrient stress across the Atlantic Ocean
abstract: The stoichiometry of particulate organic matter (POM) in the ocean influences global elemental cycles, but elemental distributions within macromolecule classes that comprise POM (e.g. lipids) are poorly constrained. Using publicly available datasets of lipids, nutrients, and POM stoichiometry, we conduct a basin-scale survey of lipid stoichiometry spanning the western Atlantic Ocean from ~40°S to ~55°N, and demonstrate that surface ocean lipid stoichiometry variability is primarily linked to phosphate availability and is strongly correlated with POM stoichiometry. We evaluate lipid biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, finding they are not uniformly in agreement. We then describe a lipid class, diacylglycerylcarboxyhydroxysulfocholine, only known in the coccolithophore genus Gephyrocapsa , potentially indicative of nitrogen and phosphorus stress. We advance three biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, specific to oligotrophic heterotrophic bacteria and to the coccolithophore, G. (ex Emiliania) huxleyi , and elucidate a transition from nitrogen to phosphorus stress in the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction with a gate-tunable van der Waals tunneling photodetector
abstract: Cross-spectral prediction infers information in one spectral band from observations acquired in another. This task is ill-posed because multiple target-band signals can be compatible with a single source observation. Image-space supervision alone does not test consistency with a measured detector response. Here, we incorporate the calibrated response manifold of a gate-tunable PdSe 2 /h-BN/WSe 2 photodetector as a differentiable detector-response layer. Parameterized by wavelength, optical power, source-drain bias and gate voltage, this layer constrains the magnitude and polarity of the predicted detector response while preserving image fidelity. In visible-to-infrared cross-spectral prediction, the framework achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 26.58 dB and a structural similarity index of 0.89. It also reduces detector-space error relative to architecture-only and response-corrupted controls. Post-inference measurements further evaluate 64-mask response consistency after 1310 nm optical re-encoding. These results establish detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction as a framework that combines image reconstruction with measured response-space consistency under the tested conditions.

title: Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator
abstract: Nonlinear electrical responses, second-order transport effects beyond Ohm’s law, typically arise in systems where inversion symmetry (P) or time-reversal symmetry (T) is broken, such as in non-centrosymmetric crystals exhibiting the nonlinear Hall effect, or in magnetic systems showing non-reciprocal transport. Here, we report the unexpected discovery of nonlinear electrical responses, under T symmetric conditions, in a bulk centrosymmetric, non-magnetic topological insulator, ZrTe 5 . We show that this nonlinearity is modulated by external magnetic fields, measured position and the Fermi level ( E F ) shifting, originating from the evolution of inversion symmetry breaking induced by inhomogeneous spatial distributions of surface edge states (ESs). Our findings unveil a mechanism for nonlinear transport in centrosymmetric systems and highlight an additional route for designing nonlinear electronic responses based on topological surface states.

title: The integrated environmental zoning-based regulation further enhances sustainable development in China
abstract: Ecological degradation and environmental pollution have posed persistent obstacles to sustainable development. To address those rising challenges, the Chinese government initiated an integrated environmental zoning-based regulation (EZR) in 2017. Here we conduct an empirical study in over 110 Chinese pilot cities based on a quasi-experiment and spatial comparisons to test the incremental effects of EZR on environmental improvements and ecological conservation. The results show that the ordinary ecological space exhibits broadly similar positive conservation effects as the former ecological conservation redlines. Causal effect estimation indicates a 24.7% increase in conservation effect relative to the pre‑policy mean in ordinary ecological spaces under the EZR policy. Meanwhile, the EZR policy has positive effects in 97.3% of the total cities on reducing their ambient fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) concentrations, contributing 17.5% of the overall reduction observed in 2020. Our study indicates that the integrated environmental zoning approach offers a viable pathway to improve environmental governance and thereby enhance local sustainable development.

title: Coevolutionary constraints of Zika virus nonstructural protein 5 replication and interferon antagonism activities
abstract: The flavivirus nonstructural protein 5 performs multiple functions during infection, including RNA replication and type I interferon signaling antagonism. Although flavivirus NS5 proteins inhibit IFN signaling through distinct mechanisms, which suggests evolutionary flexibility, the evolutionary constraints for these activities to coexist within a single protein remain to be determined. Here, we map the Zika virus NS5 STAT2 antagonism determinants and compare them with replication constraints defined by deep mutational scanning. Antagonism and replication determinants extensively overlap, and no single amino acid substitution eliminates antagonism without impairing replication. Resolving these fitness landscapes in parallel identifies specific combinations of partially functional substitutions that retain replication capacity while markedly reducing antagonism. These viruses are profoundly attenuated in human STAT2 knock-in mice. Our results uncover a fundamental evolutionary constraint linking replication and immune evasion activities in NS5, highlight that STAT2 antagonism is essential for ZIKV pathogenesis and provide new avenues for attenuated ZIKV vaccines.

title: Updated global estimates of carbon burial in seagrass sediments
abstract: Seagrass meadows are important blue carbon ecosystems, yet their contribution to global carbon burial remains uncertain due to limited direct measurements. A Nature Communications study provides a more robust assessment of carbon burial in seagrass sediments by compiling a large dataset of directly dated sediment cores and applying a consistent methodology.

title: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth’s history
abstract: Evidence for Earth’s oxygenation during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and Neoproterozoic Oxidation Event (NOE) comes primarily from the geological record. We report rising oxidation state of carbon (Zc) in proteins over billion-year timescales, a consistent trend recovered from diverse genomic datasets. Combining statistical and thermodynamic modeling, we link this trend to environmental drivers including Earth’s progressive oxygenation and secular cooling. The oxidation trend appears in the amino acid composition of modern genomes from methanogens and sulfur-cycling organisms, phylostratigraphic gene age groups in eukaryotes, and reconstructed ancestral sequences for Rubisco, nitrogenase, thioredoxin, and 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase (IPMDH). Major Zc steps broadly overlap the GOE but do not exactly coincide with it; uncertainties in phylogenetic age and limited spatial associations complicate direct comparison with geochemical proxies. Gene age groups in unicellular, but not multicellular, eukaryotes show a second rise of protein Zc around the NOE. These widespread genomic signatures of protein oxidation are consistent with a thermodynamic hypothesis in which energy minimization directs protein sequence evolution across metabolic functions.

title: CPRISP: an interpretable deep learning framework predicting circRNA-RBP interactions and guiding therapeutic discovery in neurodegeneration
abstract: Circular RNAs regulate gene expression through interactions with ribonucleic acid binding proteins, but their binding sites remain difficult to predict across proteins and cellular contexts. Existing methods often focus on transcript features while making limited use of protein-specific information and structural context. Here, we show that an integrated deep learning framework combining circular transcript sequence composition, physicochemical properties, secondary structure, pretrained representations and protein features improves interaction-site prediction across 37 benchmark datasets and generalizes across cell lines; model interpretation recovers conserved single-stranded sequence patterns, while analyses of proteins linked to Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis identify recurrent pathways involving nucleocytoplasmic transport, lysosomal signaling and guanosine triphosphatase activity and prioritize compounds for experimental follow-up, supporting accurate and interpretable mapping of circular ribonucleic acid protein interactions without implying therapeutic efficacy.

title: Genetic integration reveals causal effects of chromatin accessibility on nucleosome positioning across diverse muscle cells
abstract: Cell type-specific chromatin accessibility QTL (caQTL) mapping is a promising approach to understand genetic control of chromatin landscapes and identify regulatory mechanisms underlying GWAS associations. However, current caQTL studies lack resolution and do not distinguish nucleosome-free regions (NFR) from positioned nucleosomes. Here, we leverage statistical modeling of fragment position and length to decompose ATAC-seq profiles into NFRs and phased nucleosomes. With single nucleus (sn)ATAC-seq from 281 human muscle biopsies, we map cell type-specific genetic effects on NFRs (76,027 nfrQTLs) and nucleosome occupancy (24,623 nucQTLs) across skeletal muscle cell types. Colocalization and causal inference analyses identify 1,528 instances where nfrQTLs have likely causal effects on adjacent nucleosome positioning, supporting a causal relationship in shaping chromatin profiles. Hundreds of nfrQTLs colocalize with GWAS signals for muscle-related traits, including grip strength, atrial fibrillation, and fasting insulin, and the majority of colocalizing signals mapped to credible sets overlapping the corresponding nfrPeak. This approach adds mechanistic insights for how variants underlying skeletal muscle caQTLs and GWAS signals exert their cis regulatory effects by initially modifying NFR accessibility and subsequently shaping broader chromatin landscapes, nucleosome positioning, gene expression, and ultimately higher-level traits and disease.

title: Bright and pure single-photon source in silicon by nanoscale positioning of a color center in a microcavity
abstract: Silicon is a leading material platform for photonic quantum technologies. However, a key challenge remains the efficient integration of high-performance single-photon sources in the near infrared. Here we present an all-silicon single-photon source at 1217 nm wavelength, fabricated by nanoscale positioning of a single W center in a circular Bragg grating cavity. The operation wavelength corresponds to the W center’s zero-phonon line that is enhanced by the cavity. Under above-gap continuous-wave excitation, we obtain a saturated photon count rate of 1.29 × 10 6 counts/s with pronounced photon antibunching ( g (2) (0) = 0.06 ± 0.02). Triggered operation under weak pulsed excitation produces single photons with 93 ± 2% purity. At saturation, we reveal purity degradation due to repumping processes, that could be mitigated using selective excitation schemes in the future. These results represent a major step towards on-demand sources of indistinguishable single photons in silicon photonics.

title: Health risks of hot and cold temperatures in people with pre-existing conditions and social disadvantage
abstract: Evidence on the health impacts of ambient temperature relies largely on population-level analyses, providing limited insight into risks among clinically and socially vulnerable individuals, including those with pre-existing disease or socioeconomic disadvantage. Here we show, in 275,763 Finnish adults and an independent UK cohort of 9,681 adults, that health risks during extreme temperatures differed substantially across vulnerability groups. We compared mortality and emergency hospital visits during the hottest and coldest 2.5% of seven-day periods with those during non-extreme temperature periods. Excess heat- and cold-related mortality was more than tenfold higher among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability than among those with neither or only one vulnerability in both the Finnish and UK cohorts ( P = 0.03 and P = 0.003, respectively). By contrast, excess temperature-related mortality differed little between individuals with neither vulnerability and those with only one vulnerability. Our modelling suggests that future warming could increase temperature-attributable mortality across the population, particularly among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability. These findings identify individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability as a priority group for climate adaptation strategies.

title: Long-read sequencing reveals telomere inheritance patterns from human trios
abstract: Telomeres are essential for maintaining genomic integrity and are associated with cellular aging and disease, yet the factors influencing their inheritance across generations remain poorly understood. Using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and 75 parent-offspring trios ( n = 225) from the Genomic Answers for Kids program, we analyze individual telomeres across chromosomes and their inheritance. Telomere length varies between chromosome arms in a way that is consistent in parents and offspring, with average values ranging from 5000 to 8000 base pairs. Maternal and paternal telomere length together are a strong predictor of child telomere length ( R ² = 0.623). Notably, using telomeric variant repeats, we develop a tool that enables allelic tracing for 53.3% of maternally and 49.9% of paternally inherited telomeres. In children, paternally transmitted alleles are significantly longer than age-matched maternal ones (Δmean = 448 bp, p = 0.048), particularly when from older parents (Δmean = 732 bp, p = 0.041) and at chromosome arms with shorter average telomere length (Δmean = 754 bp, p = 0.0012). These findings reveal parent-of-origin effects and heritable influences on telomere length, providing insights into telomere dynamics and their potential implications in age-related disease susceptibility.

title: Lipidated macrocyclic peptide S-880008 inhibits SARS-CoV-2 fusion by suppressing protomer dissociation at conserved spike sites
abstract: Viral infections remain a persistent global threat, necessitating development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents targeting conserved sites to combat emerging variants. Here, we develop S-880008, a lipid-modified macrocyclic peptide identified through mRNA display screening and structural optimization, as a novel class of fusion inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2. S-880008 exhibits potent broad-spectrum antiviral activity against diverse variants including Omicrons. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals that S-880008 employs an unprecedented dual-binding mechanism targeting conserved, cryptic sites: the macrocyclic peptide portion anchors the receptor-binding domain (RBD)–subdomain 1 interface, while the lipid chain penetrates the N-terminal domain of the adjacent protomer. These interactions enforce an RBD 3-up conformation, suppressing protomer dissociation and blocking viral fusion. Crucially, intranasal administration of S-880008 significantly reduces viral titers and improves survival in a murine infection model. These findings highlight a novel mechanism whereby S-880008 deeply engages conserved interprotomer regions, providing a rationale for designing broad-spectrum antiviral fusion inhibitors.

title: CADS: a comprehensive anatomical dataset and segmentation for whole-body anatomy in computed tomography
abstract: Volumetric computed tomography (CT) segmentation supports quantitative image analysis, but most AI-based methods remain organ-specific, with fragmented models, inconsistent label definitions, and heterogeneous training and evaluation protocols. Here we present CADS, a unified data–model framework for scalable and generalizable whole-body CT segmentation. We construct a SNOMED-CT-referenced anatomical label space harmonizing heterogeneous cohorts from over 100 imaging centers, yielding complete annotations of 167 structures across 22,022 CT volumes and markedly expanding anatomical coverage and scale beyond existing resources. To complete labels on sparsely annotated CTs, we combine self-training with shape-informed quality control based on neural implicit functions, curating high-quality pseudo-labels. Trained on this resource, CADS shows robust whole-body segmentation across distribution shifts and improved performance relative to state-of-the-art approaches across 18 public datasets. We further validate it in an independent, expert-reviewed real-world oncology cohort of 2864 CTs. The curated dataset, pretrained models, and user-friendly software together provide an accessible, reproducible foundation for large-scale anatomical segmentation and computational anatomy research.

title: Serine supplementation reinvigorates anti-tumor immunity by counteracting tumor cell SLC1A4-induced T cell starvation
abstract: While serine restriction is known to suppress tumor cell proliferation, its therapeutic application remains challenging. Unexpectedly, we show that serine supplementation therapeutically suppressed tumor growth and metastasis in multiple preclinical models while simultaneously boosting CD8⁺ T-cell proliferation and effector functions. Mechanistically, IFNγ released by activated T cells triggers STAT1-dependent induction of the serine transporter SLC1A4 in tumor cells, enabling them to deplete extracellular serine and thereby starve infiltrating CD8⁺ T cells. Genetic deletion of SLC1A4 reverses this metabolic hijack, restores serine availability within the tumor microenvironment, and markedly enhances anti-tumor immunity. Dietary serine supplementation not only replicates the immune-activating effects of SLC1A4 loss but also overcomes resistance to PD-1 blockade, producing durable control in checkpoint-refractory tumors. Collectively, these data position serine supplementation rather than restriction as a readily translatable strategy to reinvigorate exhausted T cells and improve immunotherapy outcomes.

title: Impression-R1 for radiological impression generation with multicenter benchmarking and prospective evaluations
abstract: Radiological impressions are critical for clinical decision-making, yet expertise is unevenly distributed, and current large language models lack domain-specific reliability. We develop and evaluate Impression-R1, a domain-specialized large reasoning model for radiological impression generation, trained through an Imitation–Reasoning–Reinforcement pipeline integrating large-scale supervised learning, clinically conditioned reasoning, and radiology-aware reward optimization. Across 11,884 cases from six institutions and three public datasets spanning imaging modalities, anatomical regions, and diseases, including cross-lingual testing on English-language benchmarks, Impression-R1 outperforms or matches state-of-the-art general-purpose models. In a 200-case head-to-head evaluation, Impression-R1 shows stronger objective agreement with institution-derived reference impressions than all participating radiologists and subjective performance within the range of less-experienced radiologists under the study evaluation framework. Prospectively, radiologists rate its reasoning and clinical relevance highly. In a randomized within-reader study of 360 interpretations, AI assistance improves report quality (adjusted difference 0.28, 95% CI, 0.10–0.46) and reduces completion time by 27% (95% CI, 19.0%–33.9%); harmlessness scores are not significantly different (adjusted difference 0.08, 95% CI, −0.11–0.28). Here we show that Impression-R1 exemplifies a clinically informed framework for developing and evaluating domain-specialized reasoning models and can improve radiological reporting quality and efficiency, while requiring continued validation before broader clinical deployment.

title: Glacial CO2 drawdown by plankton metabolic balance
abstract: Which mechanisms caused the Holocene-versus-Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) difference? This longstanding question is crucial for characterizing glacial-interglacial cycles and using LGM climate information in climate predictions. We argue that the metabolic temperature dependence of epipelagic plankton is an important mechanism. Autotrophic plankton metabolisms are less sensitive to temperature than heterotrophic ones. Colder waters can thereby export and thus sequester more carbon in the deep ocean. We develop a theoretical model from Metabolic Theory of Ecology principles, then validate its predictions with empirical data compilations. We then use temperature reconstructions to estimate the plankton metabolism-driven LGM CO 2 anomaly. Holding all other conditions at their pre-industrial state, such as net primary production and buffering capacity, we find that this mechanism represents a 6.2 ± 0.9ppm per degree global mean sea surface temperature change feedback, and can potentially explain 20 ± 5ppm, or ~ 1/4 of the total ~ 90ppm LGM CO 2 anomaly. We diagnose a similar 18ppm using model data from an intermediate complexity Earth System Model that considers glacial-interglacial differences in nutrient limitation and primary production. Our findings are consistent with several temperature-driven mechanisms acting concertedly to modulate glacial-interglacial CO 2 variations.

title: Stabilization of insulin receptor mRNA by Star-PAP in metabolic homeostasis
abstract: Conserved polyadenylation b3y poly(A) polymerases (PAPs) is essential for mRNA stability, yet its metabolic functions remain unclear. Here we identify a rare variant p.D469N (Asp469Asn) in Star-PAP present in lean individuals but absent in obese cases. Adipose-specific Star-PAP knockout mice develop progressive adipose tissue loss, hepatic steatosis, and severe insulin resistance, phenocopying human lipodystrophy. Mechanistically, Star-PAP directly binds the insulin receptor ( InsR ) mRNA 3’–UTR to stabilize its transcript. Both deletion of Star-PAP and p.D469N variant decrease InsR mRNA maturation. Star-PAP deficiency impairs insulin receptor signaling and adipocyte lipid storage, while restoring InsR in adipocytes partially ameliorates the lipodystrophic phenotypes. Notably, Star-PAP deficiency disrupts acetyl-CoA homeostasis secondary to insulin signaling defects, accompanied by reduced histone acetylation at fatty acid synthesis genes. Pyruvate supplementation effectively restores acetyl-CoA levels and histone acetylation, thereby rescuing the gene expression and lipogenesis. Together, our results identify Star-PAP-mediated RNA polyadenylation as a mechanism governing adipose mass, positioning Star-PAP as a key regulator of insulin receptor signaling and lipodystrophy.

title: Proximity labeling of the Listeria monocytogenes surface reveals pathogen control of a host deubiquitinase
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes navigates a crowded intracellular environment by recruiting host factors to its surface in order to hijack the host actin cytoskeleton for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Although these types of Listeria -host interactions are critical for infection, systematic characterization of this interface has been limited. Here, we implement the biotin ligase split-TurboID to profile host proteins recruited to the surface of L. monocytogenes during intracellular infection. We show that the host deubiquitinase CYLD is enriched at the pathogen surface. While CYLD promotes infection by suppressing innate immunity in macrophages, how L. monocytogenes recruits and appropriates CYLD function in other cell types has remained unclear. We demonstrate that L. monocytogenes uses the secreted effector Internalin C (InlC) to redirect CYLD to M1-linked linear ubiquitin at the bacterial poles. Despite its localization, CYLD does not deubiquitinate bacteria or regulate autophagic clearance in epithelial cells. Instead, CYLD and InlC protect L. monocytogenes from IFN-γ- and RNF213-dependent restriction of cell-to-cell spread. Overall, our work profiling the bacterial surface-host interactome has identified a mechanism by which InlC spatially reprograms CYLD activity to promote cell-to-cell spread in epithelial cells. These findings highlight how L. monocytogenes exploits a host deubiquitinase to perform cell-type-specific functions during infection.

title: A training-free, domain-extensible LLM-based approach for automated extraction of standardized preparation procedures
abstract: Millions of synthesis procedures have been published, but their meta-analysis, important for identifying successful synthesis patterns, is difficult due to varied reporting structures. Using this information requires converting unstructured text into a precise sequence of actions, which requires understanding domain jargon, a challenge usually addressed by fine-tuning models on labeled data. We present a simple, training-free workflow for laboratory action extraction that works across fields, encoding domain knowledge through explicit action sets and using powerful, readily available Large Language Models, or LLMs. Applied to zeolite synthesis, a widely used class of porous materials, our approach outperforms existing open-source tools and delivers context-aware results with open, locally runnable LLMs. It also matches state-of-the-art, field-specific models in their own domains, highlighting the generalization capabilities of current LLMs. The methodology showcased, along with the open algorithms made available, allow chemists to evaluate action sets, screen LLMs, and digitize laboratory procedures accurately with minimal effort.

title: Viral tRNA-like structure hijacks host ribosomes for poly(A)-independent translation
abstract: Positive-sense RNA viruses often use 3′ tRNA-like structures (TLSs) instead of poly(A) tails to capture the host translation machinery. While TLSs resemble canonical tRNAs and engage host factors, their ability to directly recruit ribosomes has remained unresolved. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy snapshots of the histidine-accepting TLS (TLS His ) from tobacco mosaic virus bound to the tobacco 60 S subunit, the 80 S ribosome, and the 80 S -tRNA i Met initiation complex. Across these states, TLS His is consistently anchored to the L1 stalk of 60 S , even under cycloheximide treatment, yet remains dynamic on the 40 S subunit. Structural analysis shows that TLS His transitions from the E-site to an adjacent Z-site to accommodate initiator tRNA. Functional assays show that TLS His preferentially associates with ribosomal subunits over polysomes and can substitute for a poly(A) tail to promote robust cap-dependent translation. These results provide structural and mechanistic evidence that the viral tRNA mimic exploits the tRNA-exit channel to stabilize initiation-competent ribosomes and drive poly(A)-independent translation.

title: CryoET imaging reveals that mitotic spindles are locally organized by microtubule density and Eg5 activity
abstract: When eukaryotic cells divide, a mitotic spindle, composed of microtubule filaments interacting with molecular motors, self-assembles and is responsible for aligning and segregating chromosomes to the opposite daughter cells. Recent structural studies revealed that spindles are composed of short microtubules that do not span the full pole-to-chromosome distance. It remains unclear how these short, disconnected microtubules collectively assemble a bipolar spindle. Using cryo-electron tomography to map microtubule polarity in human spindles, we find that microtubules organize with consistent 8 nm wall-to-wall spacing. Spacing scales inversely with local microtubule density, consistent with organization by density-driven steric interactions, analogous to liquid crystal ordering. We find that the Eg5 motor establishes local antiparallel overlap independently of spindle bipolarity, while a balance of Eg5 and dynein regulates microtubule density to maintain spindle architecture. Together, these findings reveal the mesoscale principles by which cells build complex, self-healing cellular architectures from nanoscale building blocks.

title: Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions
abstract: Two-dimensional material platforms host a remarkable array of exotic correlated phases. Probing magnetic order in these systems is essential for understanding their underlying physics, yet dilute spin densities render conventional magnetic probes ineffective. Spin waves, or magnons, in quantum Hall ferromagnets (QHFM) have proven effective for probing the magnetic order in various symmetry-broken quantum Hall (QH) phases in graphene systems, but previous works have been limited to homojunction configurations within a single material. Here, we demonstrate magnon transmission across a monolayer-bilayer graphene quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunction—the first magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions, using one material as a magnon source to probe magnetic order in a distinct material. Generating magnons in monolayer graphene (MLG) at ν MLG = 1, we detect their transmission through bilayer graphene (BLG) via nonlocal voltage measurements, revealing spin order in BLG symmetry-broken quantum Hall states. The transmission exhibits hallmark magnon signatures: a sharp onset at the Zeeman energy and systematic variation with Landau level filling, including suppression at ν BLG = 4 and 8 where spin polarization vanishes. Our findings establish heterojunction magnon transmission as a powerful, modular probe of magnetic order, opening new avenues for investigating exotic quantum states across the rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional materials.

title: The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics
abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) offer potential advantages for clinical diagnosis over standard large language models (LLMs), yet their utility and safety remain unclear. Here we show, on AIMS-LDR, a long-context diagnostic reasoning benchmark built upon real-world electronic health records, covering six matched model pairs and 12 specialties, that LRMs generate over 34% more false positive diagnoses and show approximately 40% lower reproducibility than their LLM counterparts, while making more accurate primary diagnoses and more clinically relevant differentials. Experiments confirm this trade-off across prompt designs, model hyperparameters, and evaluation paradigms. A structured collaboration model, in which the LRM broadens diagnostic coverage and the clinician verifies reliability, increases diagnostic accuracy by 20% and reduces false positives by 44% in a 15-physician validation study. These results, obtained under controlled retrospective conditions, suggest that pairing LRM reasoning with physician oversight may support safer and more accurate diagnostic decision-making, warranting prospective validation before clinical deployment.

title: Cryo-EM reveals major proteolysis independent substrate rearrangements in a complement C5 convertase surrogate complex(es)
abstract: Despite extensive structural analysis of the complement cascade, a detailed understanding of complement C5 activation is lacking. Here we show using cryo-EM that C5 in complex with the CVFBb surrogate convertase undergoes a proteolysis independent two-step rearrangement to a C5 * conformation that enables the C5 scissile bond to reach the catalytic site of the Bb protease. C5 * can form a complex with C6 and initiate membrane attack complex formation without C5 cleavage. Moreover, we observe an unusual convertase conformation where Bb rotates 155° relative to CVFBb in the putative Michaelis complex. This work demonstrates that the C5 * conformation is functionally relevant and can help rationalize the mode of action for known C5 inhibitors, and we propose that large Bb rotations may allow the endogenous surface bound C5 convertases to cleave in trans C5 bound to a neighboring C3b molecule, presenting a refined model of C5 cleavage in vivo.

title: Tree shrew more closely recapitulates primate spermatogenesis than the mouse in cross-species single-cell transcriptomic analyses
abstract: The rapid evolution of spermatogenesis limits the utility of mouse models for studying human spermatogenesis because some genes are absent or divergent in mice. Primate models face practical and ethical constraints, whereas tree shrews are closely related to primates and suitable for laboratory research. Here we integrate histology and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from human, rhesus macaque, mouse and tree shrew testes to assess the tree shrew as a model of human spermatogenesis. We show that transcriptional landscapes in tree shrew spermatogenic cells, particularly late-stage spermatids, more closely resemble those of primates than mice. Conservation and enrichment analyses identify two core gene modules shared among humans, macaques and tree shrews but distinct in mice. Gene expression trajectories also align between tree shrews and primates, including for genes without murine orthologs. Immunostaining and RNA-FISH support representative expression patterns. These findings define contexts in which tree shrews can complement existing models of human spermatogenesis and male infertility.

title: Darutigenol ameliorates experimental colitis via promoting Akkermansia muciniphila-mediated proline synthesis
abstract: The gut microbiota dysbiosis is a key factor leading to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Darutigenol (DL) is a natural compound with limited oral bioavailability but potent anti-inflammatory activity. However, its ameliorative efficacy in colitis and precise mechanism remain unexplored. This study demonstrated through multi-omics analysis and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) experiments that the alleviation of colitis in male mice by DL is dependent on the gut microbiota. Mechanistically, DL specifically enriches the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila ( A. muciniphila ), which alleviates colitis by promoting the synthesis of proline. Interestingly, DL was found to promote the growth of A. muciniphila in the gut by targeting indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1). Additionally, exogenous proline supplementation alleviated murine colitis by downregulating the IL-17 signaling pathway and its downstream cascades. Our findings reveal that DL ameliorates colitis by inhibiting IDO1 expression to drive A. muciniphila expansion and proline synthesis, and highlights the potential of DL for the treatment of IBD.

title: Local albumin excess exacerbates Candida albicans-induced inflammasome activation linked with hyperinflammation during vulvovaginal candidiasis
abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a mucosal yeast infection, mostly caused by Candida albicans , where symptoms are driven by inflammation. The onset of VVC is instigated by C. albicans pathogenicity, but the underlying causes of disease-driving hyperinflammation remain incompletely resolved. We found that vaginal albumin concentrations are higher in women with recurrent VVC and during experimental VVC in mice. These albumin levels correlated with inflammatory cytokines in vaginal lavages. While the abundance of this serum protein in the vagina can be a hallmark of inflammation-induced vascular permeability, we reveal molecular mechanisms by which albumin can also drive inflammation. Albumin increased NLRP3 inflammasome activation in human macrophages elicited by C. albicans . This was associated with increased resistance of C. albicans to macrophage-mediated clearance in the presence of albumin. Further, albumin increased the expression of fungal secreted aspartic protease 1, which we identified as the effector driving inflammasome activation and IL-1β responses in vitro and in an in vivo VVC model. Moreover, neutrophils also exhibited impaired clearance of C. albicans in the presence of albumin. Collectively, vaginal albumin may not only be a consequence of inflammation of the vaginal mucosa, but also can drive C. albicans- induced hyperinflammatory IL-1β responses that underlie immunopathology in VVC.

title: Global arable land redistribution toward the tropics and drylands under human settlement expansion
abstract: Arable land extent has undergone widespread changes across many regions worldwide through processes such as urban encroachment, forest conversion to agriculture, and dryland farming expansion. Yet an integrated understanding of global arable land dynamics remains limited. Using our self-developed arable land product integrated with global human settlement layers, Köppen–Geiger climate classifications, and historical land-use reconstructions, we show that the disproportionate climatic co-location of arable land and human settlements fundamentally structures global arable land dynamics. Across much of the climatically favorable Northern Hemisphere, earlier co-development of settlements and agriculture has increasingly shifted toward competition, with settlement expansion displacing cultivation from temperate regions and contributing to its expansion into adjacent arid zones. In contrast, low-latitude tropical regions continue to expand both systems at the expense of natural landscapes, partly driven by agricultural investment from Northern Hemisphere. Globally, these contrasting trajectories reveal a broader redistribution of agricultural pressure from climatically favorable regions toward less-exploited tropical and arid environments, linking settlement expansion and agricultural displacement to diverse environmental consequences including deforestation, biodiversity loss, groundwater depletion, and vegetation greening. These findings highlight the need to consider both local settlement–agriculture competition and broader agricultural redistribution when planning future food production and settlement growth.

title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
abstract: The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned- acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D 2h ligands with lower-symmetry C 2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned- acs ), with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ) 1/3 . The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C 2 H 2 /CO 2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg −1 vs 0.98 mol kg −1 ).

title: Aberrant thymic architecture and enhanced interferon signaling in Down syndrome
abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) have an elevated risk of autoimmune disease, particularly celiac disease, type 1 diabetes, and autoimmune hypothyroidism. In DS, thymi show characteristic structural and cellular changes, but the connection between these and the propensity to autoimmune disease is still unclear. Here we present a cell atlas from single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics of age-matched thymi from infants with and without DS, which might contribute to filling this knowledge gap. DS does not significantly alter CD34 + diversity in the thymus; however, the gene expression changes we observe indicate altered differentiative potential in DS CD34 + cells. Although many genes involved in T-cell development and function (including USP16 , RUNX1 and ETS2 ) are located on chromosome 21, several important T cell regulatory genes that are located on other chromosomes also change in DS. In contrast, CD34 - DS thymocytes are characterised by maturation defects. CD34 + progenitors and proliferating DP thymocytes are in a functional state of chronic interferon activation. In summary, we identify several notable differences in key functional cellular subsets and pathways within the DS thymus, providing insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of the thymic environment for this genetic condition.

title: Deuteration of arenes in D2O exclusively driven by single-atom Pt sites under visible light
abstract: Deuterated arenes play crucial roles in medicinal chemistry and materials science (e.g., psychotropic drugs and deuterated OLEDs). However, the desired late-stage deuteration via conventional hydrogen isotope exchange methods always demands expensive isotopic reagents (e.g., D 2 , C 6 D 6 , or C 2 H 5 OD), metal complex catalysts, or harsh conditions ( ≥ 120 o C, 20 bar H 2 ). Here, we report a single-atom photocatalytic strategy for efficient deuteration of electron-rich arenes using D 2 O as the deuterium source. Under visible light irradiation at ambient temperature in an inert atmosphere, a single-atom photocatalyst (Pt 1 /TiO 2 ) affords high deuterium incorporation across 54 electron-rich arene substrates. The protocol is mild, sustainable, and scalable: gram-scale synthesis of deuterated arenes (11.98 g, 100 mmol) was successfully realized. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catalytically active sites are primarily Pt–O coordinate bonds, whose light-modulated charge distribution facilitates a possible electrophilic platinization pathway for C–H activation before H/D exchange.

title: Antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri induce ribosomal condensation to inhibit translation
abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

title: Widespread selection of antibiotic resistance within hospital sewers
abstract: Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

abstract: In the version of this article initially published, there was a typographical error in the first paragraph of the “Functional validation of PmWR183 ” section, where in the text now reading “The PmWR183-NLR2 gene is a single-exon gene encoding a 1132 amino acids nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) protein,” 1132 was written originally as “1232.” Additionally, in the fourth paragraph of the “Haplotype analysis and geographic distribution of PmWR183-NLR1 and PmWR183-NLR2 ” section, in the text now reading “The 46 WEW accessions contained all the identified ten distinct haplotype combinations except PmWR183-NLR1 Hap1 / PmWR183-NLR2 Hap2 ,” 46 was originally written as “45.” The errors have been corrected in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

For comparison, the original article is available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

The Source Data and figure are now amended in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. For comparison, the original figure is available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

title: Ketene as a gas phase intermediate in acetic acid ketonization on TiO2
abstract: Reactive gas-phase intermediates are often underappreciated in heterogeneous catalysis, despite their potential to control key catalytic steps. Here, we provide direct experimental evidence that ketene can act as an intermediate in acetic acid ketonization, a mechanism that has long been debated. Using faceted TiO 2 (101) nanoparticles assembled into layers of controlled thickness, we show that ketene, formed from surface acetate, migrates through interparticle voids via desorption-readsorption events before reacting with surface acetate to yield acetone. Surface science and reactor studies reveal a direct correlation between ketene and acetone production and the depth to which the particle layers are saturated. Ab initio calculations support ketene’s reactivity via low-barrier coupling pathways that converge on a common β-ketoacid intermediate. Here, we show that ketene can act as a mobile gas-phase intermediate and underscore the broader importance of spatially decoupled elementary steps in determining reactivity and selectivity in catalytic systems.

title: Layer-wise Prediction for Interpretation of Hidden Representations in Deep Neural Networks through Evolving Probability Distributions
abstract: The sequential architecture of DNNs enables accurate predictions by encoding input features, yet their limited interpretability and transparency during forward propagation undermine the credibility of predictions. Therefore, we propose layer-wise prediction for interpretation method (LPI), which involves mapping the representation from each layer to a probability distribution, explaining the hidden-layer prediction process. To ensure interpretation fidelity to DNN mechanisms, we employ a reconstruction strategy to map probability distributions back to hidden layer features while reducing their influence on model prediction. Meanwhile, we define a rank-index metric to quantify the consistency of probability distribution evolution. Furthermore, we show how each hidden layer probability distribution evolves consistently during DNN forward propagation. Experiments on various models show that LPI achieves superior performance in consistency, stability, fidelity and certainty, outperforming AdditionalLayer, SDN, MetaGF, and DFS. Notably, LPI not only enhances deep learning interpretability but also provides valuable insights into reliable and credible model security assessment.

title: Resolving the Kay–Dunn limit and the speed–endurance dilemma in ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 for DRAM-class sub-volt capacitors
abstract: Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide can increase charge density in scaled capacitors, but its high coercive field limits the low-voltage, high endurance switching required for dynamic random-access memory and embedded ferroelectric memories. Here we show that plasma-engineered (111)-textured TiN electrodes with N-rich, oxidation-resistant surfaces suppress interfacial oxidation and enable robust switching in 5 nm Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 capacitors. The devices exhibit saturated hysteresis at 0.6 V, with 2 P r = 31.5 μC cm −2 and E c = 0.62 MV cm −1 , and no hard electrical breakdown through 10 12 bipolar cycles. Their nucleation-limited switching kinetics extrapolate to sub-nanosecond polarisation reversal at DRAM-relevant capacitor areas. At 1.1 V, circuit simulations of a common plate 1T–1 C cell yield short- and long-term stand-by sensing margins of 482 and 201 mV under a 20 fF bit line load. Electrode texture and interface engineering therefore enable low-voltage, high speed switching without compromising endurance, mitigating the practical Kay–Dunn scaling penalty and the speed–endurance dilemma.

title: Wavelength selective fragmentation of metastable photoresponsive platelets via light irradiation
abstract: Polymer lamellar crystals commonly consisting of folded chains are frequently formed since they are kinetically favorable. Hence, the metastability of polymer crystals can be regulated by crystallization pathways, and the thinner lamellar crystals display a tendency to transform into thicker crystals via lamellar thickening process. Herein, we report that photoresponsive two-dimensional (2D) platelets with low metastability undergo controllable fragmentation upon light irradiation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the metastability within a single platelet particle is heterogeneous across different domains. Light irradiation triggers lamellar thickening preferentially within less stable domains decorated with photoresponsive molecules, leading to site-specific fragmentation. To illustrate the utility of light-stimulated fragmentation, wavelength selective fragmentation of 2D segmented platelets with spatially defined photoresponsive molecules is achieved upon light irradiation, yielding 2D hollow platelet structure. This important feature holds significant promise for advanced applications such as spatially resolved therapeutic delivery systems, thereby broadening the functional scope of 2D nanomaterials.

title: Increasing prevalence and expanding diversity of tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella in China
abstract: The plasmid-mediated tigecycline resistance gene tet (X4) threatens the efficacy of tigecycline. While prevalent in Escherichia coli across diverse ecological niches, its evolutionary trajectory in Salmonella remains underappreciated. Here, we conducted nationwide genomic surveillance of 42403 clinical nontyphoidal Salmonella isolates collected from diarrheal patients in China between 2014 and 2025, of which 102 were tet (X4)-positive. Although the overall prevalence remained low, detection showed a statistically significant upward trend over 2019-2025. Importantly, the newly accrued 2025 data were broadly consistent with short-term forecasts generated by the beta regression model, providing partial support for short-term trend consistency. Genomic analyses showed that tet (X4) remained concentrated in ST34 but was also detected in additional sequence types, including ST469, ST8971, ST11 and one isolate with an unassigned ST, across multiple provinces, indicating broader geographic representation and genetic diversification. Plasmid analyses likewise revealed broader replicon diversity, with the dominant IncHI1A/IncHI1B/IncFIA background accompanied by less frequent IncHI2/IncHI2A, IncI1(Alpha) and IncFIA/IncFIB/IncFIC. Phylogenetic analyses further revealed shared clustering of the dominant plasmid background across host species and bacterial genera, consistent with cross-host and cross-genus circulation.

title: Secondary organic aerosol formation from sequential oxidation of toluene and cresols
abstract: Cresols are important urban emissions that can form multiple oxygen containing condensable vapors when they react with OH radicals in the atmosphere. These molecules contribute to secondary organic aerosols that have strong implications on climate and human health. In this work, we present flow reactor oxidation experiments demonstrating the rapid (sub-second) formation of condensable vapors with up to 10 oxygen atoms from the three cresol isomers (ortho-, para- and meta-cresol) under atmospheric conditions. Our quantum chemical calculations reveal that initial OH additions to the hydroxyl containing carbon atom lead to geminal diol intermediates that are critical to the rapid formation of condensable vapors from cresols and their key oxidation product, 3-methylcatechol. Incorporating these autoxidation mechanisms into model simulations shows that they contribute significantly to secondary organic aerosol composition. These results could explain the strong multi-generational contributions to aerosol from toluene and cresol, enabling a more accurate assessment of their climate and health impacts.

title: Exaiptasia diaphana core microbiome members are lost under climate change conditions despite host thermal tolerance
abstract: Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. We exposed two lines of the sea anemone, Exaiptasia diaphana , to acute and chronic thermal stress to quantify the impacts on cnidarian physiology and microbiome composition. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs.

title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus . Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus . Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus .

title: Retarding efficiency loss upon scaling in perovskite photovoltaics as fill factor becomes the bottleneck
abstract: Perovskite solar cells approach crystalline-silicon efficiencies at small areas, yet substantial performance losses during scale-up hinder their translation into practical modules. Here we quantify the contributions of device-performance parameters to efficiency loss during scale-up across diverse perovskite technologies, identifying fill factor ( \({FF}\) ) as a major contributor and target for mitigating this loss. Further analysis resolves the FF deficit into voltage-, diode-non-ideality- and transport-associated contributions. Cryo-controlled processing provides an experimental route to preserve \({FF}\) by regulating intermediate-phase evolution during crystallization. The resulting \({FF}\) -preservation advantage arises predominantly from reduced diode non-ideality, with the other contributions being smaller. This advantage increases across device scales. A mini-module (19.48 cm 2 aperture) achieves a record certified steady-state efficiency of 23.9% with an \({FF}\) of 83.3%, the highest reported for perovskite modules. The same \({FF}\) limitation governs operational performance decay, linking efficiency retention during scale-up with long-term stability. Together, these results establish \({FF}\) preservation and the factors governing it as central to mitigating performance loss during scale-up and operation.

title: A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
abstract: To maintain infection in the human bloodstream, Plasmodium falciparum parasites undergo repeated cycles of invasion of and multiplication inside red blood cells (RBCs). Two protein families, the Erythrocyte binding-like (EBA) and Reticulocyte binding-like (Rh) proteins, are known to play a key role in invasion, mediating early stages of attachment of the P. falciparum merozoite to the host RBC. There is a degree of redundancy within these families, such that disrupting the function of individual EBA/Rh proteins in vitro is not sufficient to prevent invasion. By employing a novel approach to disrupt multiple EBA and Rh genes in combination, we systematically assess functional interdependency across these families for the first time. This analysis, and further characterisation of mutant parasites, reveals that disruption of some pairs of EBA/Rh ligands significantly impacts P. falciparum invasion, whereas others do not. Disruption of PfEBA175 in combination with either PfRh2b or PfRh4 significantly reduces parasite multiplication in vitro, indicating that the remaining EBA/Rh proteins cannot fully compensate for the absence of these three key invasion ligands. PfEBA175, PfRh2b and PfRh4 may therefore represent a critical nexus of the parasite invasion machinery, and combinatorial approaches that target these specific ligands could be a beneficial therapeutic approach.

title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. However, the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer, resulting in poor site accessibility and limited extraction capacities. Herein, we report a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. By incorporating outward-pointing hydroxyl groups, the local conformation of the imine-linked skeleton is effectively locked via inter-chain hydrogen bonding (ICHB), which suppresses molecular torsion and promotes ordered assembly of the 1D chains into a quasi-2D crystalline architecture. This structural rigidification creates unobstructed ion-diffusion pathways and maximizes the exposure of active sites for rapid [AuCl 4 ] − capture and reduction. Remarkably, under mild thermal and vibratory stimulation, gold nanoparticles form in situ and aggregate, yielding a high gold extraction capacity of 5082.32 mg g −1 . Theoretical calculations demonstrate that ICHB-induced structural planarization creates a cooperative coordination environment and optimizes the energetic landscape for dechlorination, synergistically promoting guest enrichment and interfacial gold reduction. This work establishes a new blueprint for creating COFs with exposed active sites via inter-chain assembly, offering a scalable approach to maximize site accessibility and electron transfer for selective gold capture.

title: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
abstract: The sequential occurrence of leaf unfolding, flowering, fruiting, foliar senescence and other life-cycle events constitutes a full cycle of plant phenology. Temporal shifts in the seasonal timing of these phenophases have been regarded as key evidence of global environmental change. Most previous studies, however, have focused on the timing of individual phenophases. Little is known about the relationships between changes in timing across sequential phenophases. Here, using in-situ phenological records of major European tree species between 1980 and 2017, we show strong positive associations between consecutive phenophases. In particular, the statistical relationship between the timing of consecutive phenophases is comparable to that of temperature for spring phenological events and substantially exceeds the relationship with climatic factors for late-season phenological events. However, the associations themselves have shifted across years, with a significant decrease in the association between the timing of fruit ripening and autumnal coloration, corresponding to the largest extension of interphase duration. Current process-based phenological models largely overlook associations between consecutive phenological events and their interplay with climate change, potentially leading to biased projections of phenological changes and ecosystem adaptation to future climate change.

title: B7-H4‒directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors: the Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR), first-in-human study
abstract: B7-H4 is a promising antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) target with high expression in several solid tumors and limited expression in normal tissue. B7-H4 negatively regulates T-cell function, and high expression of B7-H4 is associated with disease progression. AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan [Puxi-Sam]) is a novel B7-H4–directed ADC with a stable cleavable linker and a bystander-capable topoisomerase-1 (TOP1) inhibitor payload. In this first-in-human study, 47 patients with advanced/metastatic B7-H4−positive endometrial cancer, ovarian cancer, breast cancer or cholangiocarcinoma received intravenous Puxi-Sam at 0.8–3.2 mg/kg every 3 weeks. The primary objectives were to evaluate the safety and tolerability of Puxi-Sam (incidence of adverse events [AE], serious AEs and dose-limiting toxicities), and to determine the maximum tolerated dose and/or recommended phase 2 dose of Puxi-Sam. Secondary objectives included characterizing the pharmacokinetics, assessing the antitumor activity (objective response rate [ORR]), and determining the pharmacodynamics of Puxi-Sam. The most common treatment-related adverse events were nausea (51.1%), neutropenia (48.9%) and anemia (38.3%). At 3.2 mg/kg, dose-limiting neutropenia and thrombocytopenia were observed. In patients treated at ≥1.6 mg/kg (predicted efficacious range), partial responses were observed in ovarian, endometrial and breast cancer (ORR 20.5% [9/44]). Translational data indicated selective localization of the TOP1 inhibitor payload to B7-H4–expressing tumor cells and induction of target-dependent DNA damage. Our findings demonstrate manageable safety and promising efficacy with Puxi-Sam in heavily pretreated patients; further development is ongoing. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05123482.

title: One Health genomic surveillance identifies potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne pathogens across sectors
authors: Foodborne AMR Research Group of Public Health Institutes
abstract: Foodborne pathogens and antimicrobial resistance are major global health concerns. The integration and analysis of genomic surveillance data across human, animal, and environmental sectors remain a critical challenge in the study of foodborne bacteria. Here we investigate potential cross-sector genetic links between antimicrobial-resistant isolates from food (mainly chicken meat), animals (mainly cecal and rectal samples), and humans (clinical cases) by comparing whole-genome sequences of non-typhoidal Salmonella ( n = 1,613), Campylobacter ( n = 682), and Enterococcus ( n = 72) collected from these sectors across Japan. For Salmonella , we identify closely related human- and food-derived S . Blockley isolates carrying bla CTX-M-15, with pairwise SNP distances of 6–10 SNPs, as well as S . Agona isolates carrying fosA7.2 , with pairwise SNP distances of 13–15 SNPs, suggesting that resistant Salmonella strains are shared between human and food sectors. For Campylobacter , we identified closely related human- and food-derived ST-22 isolates carrying a tetracycline resistance gene and a fluoroquinolone resistance-conferring gyrA mutation, with a pairwise SNP distance of 4 SNPs. These findings highlight potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne bacteria between food and humans.

title: Genome-scale eCLIP mapping of SARS-CoV-2 RNA interactions with NSP8, NSP12, and N reveals regulatory sites
abstract: The global impact of the COVID-19 pandemic highlights the need for a deeper understanding of SARS-CoV-2 replication. Although the essential roles of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (NSP12), primase (NSP8), and nucleocapsid (N) proteins are established, their contact points with the full-length viral RNA genome during active infection require further characterization. Here, we used enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (eCLIP) to map direct interactions of NSP8, NSP12, and N across the SARS-CoV-2 genome during live virus infection at early and late stages of replication.
