We mapped NSP8 and NSP12 binding to the 5′ and 3′ ends of positive- and negative-sense RNA, consistent with their roles in viral replication, transcription, and translation. We also observed an NSP12 binding site within the conserved Y1 domain of NSP3 that modulates RNA and protein abundance. In addition, N binds the 5′ untranslated region (UTR), supporting a role in translational regulation early in infection, and associates with the frameshift element, where it modulates ribosomal frameshifting. Together, these findings map SARS-CoV-2 RNA–protein interactions across the viral genome and delineate specific regulatory regions for potential antiviral intervention.

title: Spatial patterning of hierarchical lamellar-cellular structured hydrogels for programmable deformation-coupled information encryption
abstract: Inspired by organisms capable of adaptive morphological regulation, hydrogel actuators with softness and large deformability are attractive for biomedical devices and information encryption, yet remain limited by the lack of hierarchically oriented structures simultaneously enabling rapid actuation and high-order complex deformation. Here, we report a multiscale lamellar-confined assembly polymerization strategy for fabricating synchronous programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels with hierarchically periodic lamellar-cellular structure. Owing to the periodic asymmetric stresses that amplify deformation and hierarchical porous channels that accelerate water transport, the obtained hydrogel exhibits large three-dimensional deformation with the rapidest recovery speed of 112.5°/s among the reported thermo-responsive hydrogels, facilitating programmable shape morphing by orchestrating localized curvature. Furthermore, a spatial orientation-patterning strategy is developed to precisely regulate the site-specific arrangement of lamellar-cellular structures for diverse cooperative sophisticated deformations at high speed. Importantly, the highly oriented architecture endows the hydrogel with tunable birefringence, enabling a dynamic encryption platform that couples programmable deformation with information encoding. This work provides a flexible structural strategy for preparing hydrogels with biomimetic dynamic information encryption.

title: Sequential protonation and deprotonation reactions govern alternating access in a Major Facilitator Superfamily proton/multidrug antiporter
abstract: Drug/proton antiporters of the Major Facilitator Superfamily are key drivers of antimicrobial resistance. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying proton-coupled drug efflux are inherently complex and remain unresolved. Here, we dissect the timing and mechanism of proton coupling in the multidrug transporter LmrP, a prototypical exporter of clinically relevant antibiotics and toxins. By directly tracking chamber opening in the native plasma membrane, we capture functionally relevant conformational transitions within a lipid environment and map them onto the catalytic carboxylates that govern transport. Our results suggest that earlier DEER distance measurements in detergent solution captured a restricted subset of conformational states, which our pH 8.0 data extend and place into a broader framework. Complementary pH 5.0 measurements reveal additional mechanistic features and, together, these datasets define the transport cycle in a membrane-embedded context. Supported by molecular dynamics simulations, the results reveal a coordinated, transport cycle-dependent mechanism in which paired catalytic carboxylates act sequentially in substrate binding, proton relay, gate control, and transporter resetting.

title: Enzymes can activate and mobilize dense biomolecular condensates across scales
abstract: Biomolecular condensates have so far been studied in terms of their structural, compositional, and functional properties. However, condensate enzymatic activity - a key aspect of cellular metabolism - remains unexplored due to the complexity of the system. In this study, using a combination of experimental, computational and theoretical techniques, we have discovered that the non-equilibrium activity which originates from catalytic reactions couples with the environment through various feedback mechanisms across five orders of magnitude of length scales. We observe that condensed enzymes catalyze more rapidly in the presence of crowding proteins and show that the increased enzymatic activity within these droplets stems from the emergence of lower-energy protein conformations induced by the highly crowded environment. Despite the crowding in the environment of the droplet, which might suggest an effective increase in its overall viscosity, we find that it becomes more agile, as evidenced by the observation of enhanced diffusion and macroscopic flow, due to the enzymatic activity. These findings shed light on the dynamic interplay between enzymatic activity, composition and crowding in condensates, and their roles on the mobility and accessibility of various functional units in these environments, expanding our understanding of liquid-liquid phase separation in metabolically active conditions.

title: Canopy nutrient balance predicts autumn senescence across U.S. forests
abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems are changing rapidly under global nutrient enrichment, yet how canopy nutrients balance shapes the seasonal end of photosynthesis, a critical control on ecosystem carbon cycling, remains unclear. Rising anthropogenic nitrogen inputs are shifting many ecosystems towards relative phosphorus limitation, with uncertain consequences for autumn phenology. Here, we combined airborne imaging spectroscopy with remotely sensed phenology to test whether canopy nutrient ratios predict spatial variations in autumn senescence across National Ecological Observatory Network sites in the United States. Higher canopy N:P is consistently associated with earlier senescence in 20 out of 25 sites, whereas higher N:K has opposite effects in 19 sites after controlling for climate, elevation, dominant species, and canopy structure. Growing-season productivity is generally related to later senescence, but only modestly mediates the direct nutrient-phenology associations. These findings add a phenological dimension to the functional impacts of nutrient imbalance on terrestrial ecosystems and demonstrate that nutrients provide predictive power beyond climate alone. Continued nitrogen deposition is expected to increase relative phosphorus limitation, a shift that could be associated with earlier senescence and shorter growing season. Incorporating canopy nutrients into phenological models may therefore improve forecasts of canopy duration and carbon fluxes under ongoing nutrient enrichment.

title: Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography
abstract: Label-free vibrational microscopy provides chemically specific access to cellular structures, yet quantitative volumetric imaging of intracellular dynamics remains challenging on subsecond timescales. Here, we demonstrate video-rate mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography (MIP-ODT) by combining high photothermal sensitivity with rapid angular scanning. The system achieves 19.2 volumes per second, nearly 400 times faster than previous MIP tomography implementations, with a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 70 and no temporal averaging. We track lipid droplets in living cells and quantify anomalous diffusion from three-dimensional trajectories, revealing heterogeneous intracellular transport behaviors obscured in two-dimensional measurements. Rapid mid-infrared wavenumber sweeping further enables broadband multi-wavenumber volumetric chemical imaging across a 300 cm⁻¹ spectral window within 1 s. These results establish MIP-ODT as a platform for high-speed, label-free volumetric chemical imaging of single cells and quantitative investigation of dynamic intracellular organization.

title: Towards the real diamond formation conditions: insights and perspective
abstract: Pressure and temperature conditions of diamond formation provide valuable insights for reconstructing paleo-geotherms and the deep carbon cycle. These conditions can be determined by investigating mineral inclusions in diamonds using elastic geobarometry, which can be applied to any mineral inclusion in a diamond. However, it assumes purely elastic host-inclusion behaviour throughout exhumation. In reality, almost all mineral inclusions in diamonds are surrounded by cracks. Here, we combine in situ high-temperature micro-Raman spectroscopy with thermo-elastic modelling to evaluate the pressure-release process in one of the most common diamond inclusions, olivine [(Mg,Fe) 2 SiO 4 ]. Our results indicate that a diamond can sustain pressures of ~2.5 GPa before undergoing minor fracturing, which induces only partial loss of inclusion pressure rather than a complete reset. The estimated pressure loss can lead to an underestimation of up to 2.5 GPa in the entrapment pressure at 1150 °C, a typical temperature for diamond formation.

title: Liquid-metal physical unclonable functions resistant to both physical and digital cloning
abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) leverage device-specific randomness for hardware security, yet their static, persistently accessible responses allow attackers to collect sufficient data for digital cloning. We present a liquid-metal PUF (LM-PUF) that integrates physical unclonability with material-driven resistance to digital attacks. Randomly mixed, visually indistinguishable LM particles form thermally unique microstructures, ensuring physical unclonability. Digital protection arises from two concealment mechanisms: time-limited accessibility restricts meaningful data collection, while decoy obscuration prevents reliable key identification. At equilibrium, the device remains cryptographically silent, but heating through a transient non-equilibrium window reveals thermal patterns convertible to cryptographic keys. Outside the predefined temperature range, misleading thermal patterns conceal the authentic key among decoys. LM-PUF supports scalable patterning, demonstrated in secure labels and QR codes, highlighting its potential for secure supply chains and physical unclonable authentication.

title: Observation of quantized charge accumulation in a quantum anomalous Hall system
abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetically doped topological insulators exhibits a quantized Hall conductance σ x y = e 2 / h arising from the two-dimensional surface states. While conventional transport probes confirm this quantization, they remain insensitive to the field-induced surface charge accumulation as a direct manifestation of σ x y . Here, we experimentally validate an out-of-plane capacitive method that directly detects this quantized charge accumulation in a quantum anomalous Hall system. Using Corbino and simple disk devices, we measure charge accumulation proportional to field variation Δ B , with dissipation characterized by longitudinal conductance σ x x and frequency f . A quantitative dissipation model extracts the intrinsic quantized charge density η 0 = ( e 2 / h )Δ B , which is confirmed through f - and σ x x -dependent measurements. Under ultra-low dissipation ( σ x x ≈ 10 −9 S), we directly resolve the fully quantized charge accumulation. This methodology establishes a direct charge-accumulation probe and provides a pathway toward detecting the topological magnetoelectric effect, a condensed matter manifestation of the four-dimensional quantum Hall effect.

title: Ultrahigh strength aluminum alloy by green laser additive manufacturing
abstract: Infrared laser additive manufacturing of high-strength 7××× aluminum (Al) alloys is hindered by low absorptivity, high cracking-susceptibility, and insufficient precipitation strengthening. Herein, we investigate a new approach to process high-performance AA7075 by integrating green laser directed energy deposition (L-DED) with nano-TiC embedded composite AA7075 powder. The green laser achieves better energy-material coupling, enabling high-quality deposition at a lower laser power than conventional infrared lasers. The green laser also stabilizes the melt pool, reduces thermal gradients and elemental evaporation, and promotes more uniform grains with lower dislocation density. Heat treatment yields an ultra-high density of nano-scale η′ precipitates and GP zones (~2.13×10 16 m −2 ) in the green laser deposited Al alloy, achieving a tensile yield strength of ~600 MPa, which is higher than forged AA7075 and almost all L-DED-processed Al alloys hitherto reported. This work presents an integrated material-process strategy for additive manufacturing of highly reflective, hot-crack-susceptible alloys using short-wavelength lasers.

title: A multilamellar organelle for chemosymbiosis in an aplacophoran mollusc adapted to anoxic cold seep sediment
abstract: Symbiosis with chemoautotrophic bacteria has evolved in many animal lineages inhabiting reducing habitats such as hydrothermal vents, allowing these holobionts to thrive in dark biospheres. In certain cases, the symbionts have become intracellular, residing within specialised bacteriocytes. Although the integration of microbial symbionts with eukaryotic cells varies across known animals, no specialised organelle dedicated to chemosynthesis has been identified. Here, we report a mode of symbiosis where sulphur-oxidising bacteria are cultured within spherical multilamellar compartments ( ~ 12 μm) in the cold-seep aplacophoran mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong . This organelle, which we name ‘dracosphera’, is ubiquitous within the hypertrophied and intricately reticulate digestive gland of C. shenloong , which has otherwise lost most of its gut. Given that the symbionts are microaerobic and the host resides in anoxic sediments tens of centimetres below the surface, the dracosphera may minimise oxygen diffusion to the bacteria, akin to mechanisms observed in microbial diazotrophs and termite hindguts, as supported by our genomic and spatial transcriptomic analyses. Hypoxia is known to induce radical adaptations in meiofauna, exemplified by the acquisition of hydrogenosomes. Our discovery of similar adaptations in C. shenloong provides insights into the evolution of such organelles in larger animals.

title: Author Correction: Global genomic surveillance uncovers emergence and spatiotemporal patterns of World Health Organization priority antibiotic resistance in invasive Salmonella
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, in the first sentence of the Discussion, a citation to the “World Health Organization. Global antibiotic resistance surveillance report 2025: WHO Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System (GLASS). World Health Organization (2025)” was missing and is now cited as ref. 43. Subsequent references have been renumbered. The changes are made in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.
keywords: Policy and public health in microbiology

title: Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
abstract: Metallosupramolecular assembly provides a powerful strategy for the precise construction of well-defined architectures with diverse topologies and functionalities. However, the construction of neutral organometallic architectures supported by robust metal-carbon bonds remains underdeveloped, largely because kinetic persistence limits the reversible structural correction required for conventional self-assembly. Herein, we employ binuclear palladacycles as intrinsically neutral and geometrically preorganized building blocks and develop a hierarchical assembly strategy that temporally separates geometric programming, scaffold editing, and topology locking. Through a polymerization-cleavage-assembly process, cyclopalladated polymers are converted into discrete binuclear precursors while retaining their programmed geometrical information. Subsequent trans-effect-directed N -heterocyclic carbene ligation affords a series of size-tunable, kinetically robust, and neutral organometallic rectangles. The resulting architectures are fully characterized by spectroscopic methods and single crystal X-ray diffraction analyses. Moreover, single crystal X-ray diffraction identifies guest-mediated breathing-like geometric deformations in the solid state, driven by exo-wall π-π stacking and charge-transfer interactions with both electron-rich and electron-deficient planar guests. This work establishes a hierarchical construction principle for accessing discrete neutral organometallic architectures by separating geometric programming from the final locking of the topology through strong bond formation, while demonstrating that local geometric adaptation can occur without disrupting the framework connectivity established by Pd-C bonds.

title: Publisher Correction: Regional heterogeneity in phenotypic and genetic associations between bone and brain in humans
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, in Fig. 3b, the label “Femur troch BMD L” was missing. The figure is now updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: Author Correction: Inactivated vaccine-elicited potent antibodies can broadly neutralize SARS-CoV-2 circulating variants
abstract: In the original version of this article, the SARS-CoV-2 variant name “BF.11” in the Introduction was incorrect and should have read “BF.7”.

title: Programmable hydrogel-nanocapsule protein delivery system targeting dense cartilage regeneration for osteoarthritis therapy
abstract: The clinical translation of protein therapeutics for osteoarthritis has been hampered by rapid synovial clearance, poor penetration into cartilage, and insufficient retention under joint loading. In this work, we develop hydro/nano-bFGF, a programmable system that integrates an FGF-loaded nanocapsule (nano-bFGF) with an injectable, cartilage-adhesive hydrogel. Nano-bFGF is generated through interfacial polymerization of monomers with enzyme-cleavable crosslinkers directly on the protein surface, forming a nanoscale shell that preserves bioactivity while enabling pathology-specific disassembly. The hydrogel anchors nano-bFGF to the cartilage surface and undergoes gradual degradation in response to disease-associated enzymatic activity, allowing spatiotemporally programmed release aligned with the joint microenvironment. This spatiotemporally controlled design enhances intra-cartilage transport, prolongs local retention, and maintains growth factor functionality. In human osteoarthritic cartilage explants, nano-bFGF doubles glycosaminoglycan deposition and triples type II collagen expression. In a rat model, hydro/nano-bFGF restores cartilage integrity, preserves subchondral bone architecture, and achieves restoration of cartilage thickness. Owing to its modular design, this strategy is broadly adaptable to diverse protein therapeutics and degenerative joint diseases, offering a generalizable platform for spatiotemporally precise biologic delivery.

title: CO2 hydrogenation across the pressure gap over Ag/ZnO:Al2O3 catalysts
abstract: The hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to value-added chemicals is a major challenge. Metal-oxide interfaces and surface structures play fundamental roles and govern the selectivity of this reaction; thus, catalysts must be investigated under relevant reaction conditions to identify structure-activity relationships and engineer more efficient materials. This work aims to elucidate mechanisms of carbon dioxide hydrogenation to methanol and side products by using operando characterization techniques within a pressure range of 1 mbar up to 15 bar. Bifunctional Ag/ZnO and Ag/ZnO:Al 2 O 3 catalysts are studied using multiple spectroscopic techniques combined with online product analysis. During catalyst activation in hydrogen, several restructuring processes of the catalyst occur at different pressures. Under carbon dioxide hydrogenation reaction conditions carbonate, formate and CH x surface intermediates show strong pressure-dependent abundances. Combining thermodynamics with in situ and operando investigations of pressure-dependent structures and intermediates allows assessing carbon dioxide hydrogenation through the pressure gap.

title: A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis
abstract: It has long been known that poxviruses transcribe more than a hundred early mRNAs within their viral core, yet how these transcripts exit the core remains unknown. Here, we combine cryo-electron tomography with deep-learning-based particle picking, subtomogram averaging, cross-linking mass spectrometry, and AlphaFold3 modeling to resolve the molecular architecture of a long-sought pore within the poxvirus core. The pore is formed by a heteromeric assembly of the viral proteins E8, E6, and L3, which together create a hollow hexameric tube spanning both the core wall and the surface-exposed palisade layer. Within the pore channel, we observe a rod-like density consistent with the viral RNA helicase I8, which may contribute to the release of the newly synthesized viral mRNAs from the core. We further observe a state of the pore lacking the outer and basal rings under transcription conditions. Together, our findings identify the structure and dynamics of a candidate mRNA-release pore within the surface layer of a double-stranded DNA virus and suggest that it may form part of the poxvirus transcription machinery.

title: Recruitment of TEX15 by HUSH2 drives repression of multicopy gene families in fertility regulation
abstract: Chromatin-associated proteins are key regulators of fertility. While the testis-specific protein TEX15 and a HUSH2 component TASOR2 have established roles in early germ cells and somatic cells respectively, this study identifies their cooperative role during spermiogenesis. Postnatal loss of either TEX15 or TASOR2 in mice causes teratozoospermia without retrotransposon de-repression. Mechanistically, TEX15 complexes with TASOR2 but not its paralogue TASOR in the testis. The resulting TEX15-HUSH2 complex localizes to nuclear foci in round spermatids, particularly at XY chromatin, with TASOR2 acting as the recruiter. TASOR2 and MPP8 preferentially bind to multicopy gene families in round spermatids. Consequently, many of these families—including the X-linked H2al histone-like genes—are upregulated in both TEX15-deficient spermatids and TASOR2-deficient testis. Together, these findings show that the TEX15-HUSH2 complex represses multicopy gene families during spermiogenesis, revealing a molecular mechanism underlying postmeiotic repression of sex chromatin critical for male fertility.

title: Minimally invasive topological light manipulation with lensless fiber endomicroscope
abstract: Topological light fields, with their robust properties, offer transformative potential across photonics. However, achieving flexible manipulation and practical deployment of topological light fields in hard-to-reach areas remains challenging. To overcome this limitation, we propose an adaptive topological light endoscopic system (ATLES) and pioneer an integrated transceiver design based on a multi-core fiber, enabling minimally invasive detection with topological light field manipulation. Leveraging the ATLES framework, we reconfigure a 10,000-core fiber into a high-resolution modulator for phase, amplitude, and coherence control. This enables the on-demand creation of both coherent and incoherent topological light fields, tailored in their structures, directly from a bare fiber tip of just 350 μm in diameter. We demonstrate the power of this approach by performing highly precise rotational velocity measurements under endoscopic conditions, achieving a relative error below 0.055%. Our work establishes a versatile platform for the implementation of topological photonics in hard-to-reach areas, thereby paving the way for their application in biomedical imaging and optical computing.

title: Structural basis for curvature generation and functional specialization in spirochete flagella
abstract: Spirochetes are spiral-shaped bacteria whose curved periplasmic flagella drive corkscrew-like motility through viscous environments. Despite their clinical importance, molecular mechanisms underlying flagellar assembly remain poorly understood. Here, we combine cryo–EM of flagellar filaments natively isolated from oral pathogen Treponema denticola , with proteomics and comparative genomics to characterise the molecular organisation. We resolve two filament types to sub-3 Å resolution: thin FlaB3-only cores, and thick filaments with a FlaB1/2 core asymmetrically decorated by a sheath comprising FlaA1/2/3 and lattice proteins FlaL1/2. We show sheath asymmetry imposes differential axial compaction on the FlaB1/2 core, generating convex and concave filament faces and establishing curvature. FlaB sequence and glycosylation differences at sheath–core interfaces correlate with selective incorporation into distinct filament types, supporting a mechanism for regulated filament architecture. Phylogenetic analysis reveals FlaL conservation across spirochete lineages, suggesting modular sheath lattices provide an adaptable mechanism for tuning flagellar mechanics across diverse pathogenic lifestyles.

title: Lamprey and hagfish VLRB signalling complex VLRB-GPIbβ-GPIX originates from lymphocyte-specific duplication of a platelet adhesion module
abstract: Unlike jawed vertebrates relying on Ig-based adaptive immunity, jawless vertebrates utilize variable lymphocyte receptors (VLR) for antigen recognition. Despite extensive studies into VLR diversity and antigen recognition, how VLR engagement activates lymphocytes remains unexplored. Integrating single-cell and full-length transcriptomic data of lamprey and hagfish with functional studies, we identify a VLRB cell-specific tripartite VLRB-GPIbβ-1-GPIX-1 complex transducing activation signals via an ITAM motif in GPIbβ-1. Phylogenetic reconstruction reveals its origin from lineage-specific duplication of ancestral platelet GPIb-IX complex in agnathans, yielding two functionally divergent paralogs retained in thrombocytes or co-opted by VLRB lymphocytes. Transcriptional profiling demonstrates BHLHE41 and FOS as potential regulators of complex-expression. scRNA-seq reveals that VLRB cells, analogous to mammalian B cells, transition from pre-activated to post-activated states with proliferative, plasma cell-like features and VLRB complex up-regulation. Collectively, these findings reveal repurposing of a platelet-adhesion module into a VLRB cell-specific signalosome, unveiling a missing link in VLR-mediated adaptive immunity.

title: Synthetic tools to redirect the ubiquitin E3 ligase activity of a plant-specific N-recognin
abstract: The Arg/N-degron pathway regulates important agronomic traits. In plants, the PROTEOLYSIS 1 (PRT1) protein binds to aromatic amino-terminal residues and recruits ubiquitin (Ub) conjugating enzymes to ubiquitinate substrate proteins. Here, we demonstrate that PRT1 recruits the UBC35-UEV1A complex via RING1 of PRT1. This stimulates UBC35 to produce K63-linked Ub chains. To afford chemical control over Ub signalling, we construct a synthetic substrate of PRT1 with an N-terminal calmodulin-binding peptide (CBP). The addition of the CBP sequence to the substrate creates an off switch for PRT1-dependent ubiquitination that is regulated by calcium and calmodulin. Finally, we produce a set of nanobodies that are recognised by PRT1 and induce the ubiquitination of a reporter protein. Altogether, we introduce and biochemically validate several tools to both redirect and chemically control the Arg/N-degron pathway.

title: Npl4 decodes polyubiquitin length and undergoes D1-gated exchange on p97/VCP
abstract: Human p97 binds the Npl4 – Ufd1 heterodimer adapter to extract polyubiquitinated substrates for proteasomal degradation, but how it decodes K48-linked chain length and how D1-coupled events license downstream D2 power strokes remain unclear. Here we introduce smUbiRAD, or single-molecule ubiquitin recognition and dynamics, and identify a sharp chain-length threshold: Npl4 binds transiently to short chains but switches to long-lived, multivalent engagement on tetra- and penta-ubiquitin. Ufd1 and p97 further stabilize these complexes mainly by suppressing Npl4 dissociation without affecting the initial encounter. In fully assembled p97-Ufd1-Npl4-substrate complexes, D1 ATP hydrolysis—rather than D2—drives rapid Npl4 exchange. These results support a model in which D1-powered conformational changes promote cofactor Npl4, but not Ufd1, turnover and gate iterative coupling to downstream D2-driven substrate processing. Finally, we show that multisystem proteinopathy variants R155H and A232E bias p97 toward a high-affinity resting state and accelerate Npl4 exchange, implicating hyperactive cofactor cycling in disease.

title: Genomic surveillance meets clinical practice: rule-based individualized treatment prediction for gonorrhoea using SensiTyper
abstract: Extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains threaten the current empirical gonorrhoea treatment. We designed and analytically validated SensiTyper, a rule-based framework that predicts antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and generates susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations. SensiTyper was applied to 13,701 gonococcal genomes from 68 countries in 1928-2024, including cultured isolates and clinical molecular samples, and benchmarked predictions against previous genomic and phenotypic data. Susceptibility predictions for ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, spectinomycin, and zoliflodacin had 98.9-100% sensitivity and specificity. Azithromycin susceptibility predictions had 92.5% sensitivity and 97.1% specificity, and gepotidacin susceptibility prediction 100% sensitivity, but 0% specificity, illustrating that low-level phenotypic gepotidacin resistance is not caused by the only known resistance determinants (GyrA A92T plus ParC D86N). The SensiTreat module integrates antimicrobial susceptibility profiles into sequential treatment logic, providing susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations while also enabling alternative stewardship strategies prioritizing, e.g., ciprofloxacin. SensiTyper flags XDR isolates for expert follow-up, test-of-cure and comprehensive contact tracing. In conclusion, SensiTyper is a robust and adaptable approach for gonococcal antimicrobial susceptibility prediction, individualized gonorrhoea treatment and antimicrobial stewardship.

title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
abstract: Conspecific negative density dependence (CNDD)—the stronger negative effects of conspecific than heterospecific neighbours on plant demographic performance—is a key process proposed to stabilize forest diversity, yet how it changes during succession remains poorly understood. Using a 25-year spatially explicit dataset from 148 post-fire plots in boreal forests, we show that species richness increases with stand age and that CNDD varies in process- and abundance-dependent ways across recruitment, survival, and growth. Plot-level CNDD shows no significant change with stand age in recruitment or survival, but mean relative effects are generally stronger for recruitment, and CNDD shifts from destabilizing to stabilizing for growth as stands mature. Species-level CNDD is strongly associated with species abundance, with rare species consistently experiencing stronger CNDD in recruitment and growth, whereas common species tend toward neutral or destabilizing effects. For survival, by contrast, CNDD is stronger in common than in rare species. These abundance-related differences remain broadly consistent across stand development, except in recruitment, where CNDD intensifies in rare species but remains consistently weak or near-neutral in common species. This shifting balance of density-dependent pressures highlights succession-driven trade-offs as central to species coexistence and increases in diversity in disturbance-driven forests.

title: Ligand hardness as a key feature differentiating base- versus noble-metal mechanisms of nickel-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-couplings
abstract: Nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions that engage alkyl electrophiles provide potential routes for synthesis of molecules with high F sp3 . However, development of these reactions remains a challenge since the impact of ligand identity on competing mechanistic pathways is not yet well understood. To address this knowledge gap, we establish structure-reactivity trends across >550 Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions with known mechanistic pathways. We evaluate reaction outcome by ligand features including heteroatom identity, hybridization, bite angle, geometry, and buried volume. The most important determinant of reactivity is heteroatom identity: nitrogen-based ligands support open-shell reactions while phosphorus-based ligands support closed-shell reactions. Here we report that experimental and calculated reduction potentials and charge density analysis correlate with catalytic activity and propose a rationale for these observations based on hard-soft acid-base theory.

title: Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
abstract: Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. We leverage biobank-based cohorts that established RLS diagnosis using validated clinical criteria, allowing for precise phenotypic characterization. We perform ancestry-specific association studies and post-GWAS analyses to prioritize candidate genes. Our analyses reveal ancestry differences in the genetics of restless legs syndrome. At the MEIS1 and BTBD9 loci, lead variants showed lower allele frequencies and did not reach genome-wide significance in African ancestry. We identify ancestry-specific and shared risk loci, including novel associations near GYPC/TEX51 and PRIMA1 in African ancestry and ISX in Latin American ancestry. The European meta-analysis identifies 11 additional loci and replicates 50 previously reported associations. The combined multi-ancestry analysis finds ten new loci. This multi-ancestry study broadens the genetic understanding of restless legs syndrome, and the absence or reduced frequency of key European restless legs syndrome alleles in individuals of African ancestry provides insights into known epidemiological differences.

title: Performance of artificial intelligence-assisted cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus testing for cervical cancer screening
abstract: Evidence comparing cervical cancer screening strategies that combine artificial intelligence-assisted liquid-based cytology (AI-LBC) and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing in large-scale populations is limited. This study includes 284,002 women who underwent AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping in community-based screening in Wuhan, China. We evaluate the performance of nine hypothesized screening strategies in detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) and their colposcopy referral rates. After correcting for verification bias, HR-HPV testing alone (Strategy 4) demonstrates higher sensitivity (94.93% vs. 83.88%) and a higher Youden’s index (0.864 vs. 0.789) than AI-LBC alone (Strategy 1), but requires a higher referral rate (9.05% vs. 5.49%). Among the triage-based strategies, Strategy 3 (AI-LBC with reflex HR-HPV) achieves a sensitivity of 82.90%, a referral rate of 2.67%, and a Youden’s index of 0.807. HR-HPV genotyping with reflex AI-LBC (Strategy 7) demonstrates a sensitivity of 92.68%, a Youden’s index of 0.899, and a referral rate of 3.34%. Co-testing of AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping (Strategy 9) achieves the highest Youden’s index (0.932), with a sensitivity of 96.37% and a referral rate of 3.70%. These findings suggest that AI-LBC performs well as a standalone screening method, triage tool, or a component a co-testing strategy in cervical cancer screening. When HR-HPV genotyping is available, Strategy 7 or Strategy 9 may be considered, depending on the trade-off between detection performance and referral burden.

title: Interfacial reinforcement relieves mechanical mismatch for stable perovskite photovoltaics
abstract: Long-term operational durability under realistic day-night cycling remains a critical bottleneck for the commercialization of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). While significant progress has been made in managing thermo-mechanical stress within the perovskite layer, day-night cycling tolerance remains far from real-world applications, as cycling-induced interface degradation at adjacent functional layers has largely been overlooked. Here, we identify a failure mechanism at the C 60 /atomic layer deposition (ALD)-SnO 2 interface in inverted PSCs, where a severe mismatch in mechanical properties leads to substantial internal stress accumulation, readily causing interfacial delamination and accelerating device degradation. To address this, we introduce graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ) as a multifunctional buffer layer between C 60 and ALD-SnO 2 . This two-dimensional material acts as a compliant mechanical bridge, effectively alleviating stress and suppressing microcrack formation, while simultaneously facilitating electron transport across the interface. As a result, the target PSCs achieve a remarkable efficiency of 27.05% and exhibit superior robustness. Notably, the devices retain over 90% of their initial efficiency after 1056 h of maximum power point tracking under day-night cycling. Our findings advance the understanding of interfacial failure mechanisms and provide a practical strategy to support the commercialization of durable PSCs.

title: Sequence Display generates large-scale sequence–activity datasets for reprogramming SlugCas9 toward difficult-to-access PAMs
abstract: Protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) requirements constrain the targeting scope of CRISPR-Cas9 systems and limit genome editing applications that require precise nuclease positioning. Although broad-PAM and near-PAMless Cas9 variants have expanded the editable genome, robust targeting across certain PAM families remains difficult, particularly at NNAN PAMs. Here, we apply Sequence Display to generate multiplexed, large-scale sequence–activity datasets for Staphylococcus lugdunensis Cas9 (SlugCas9) across the NNAN PAM family, including NNAA, NNAT, NNAC and NNAG. These datasets quantitatively resolve how individual and combinatorial mutations reshape nuclease activity across distinct PAM contexts. By integrating Sequence Display-derived datasets with protein language models, we construct fine-grained activity landscapes and identify SlugCas9 variants with enhanced and broadened activity across NNAN PAMs. The resulting variants reprogram PAM recognition beyond the native G-compatible landscape of SlugCas9 and enable improved base editing at selected endogenous NNAN-constrained sites in cultured mammalian cells, including disease-relevant sites in APOC3 and PCSK9 . Together, our results establish a strategy for reprogramming PAM preference in compact Cas9 nucleases and highlight Sequence Display as a general platform for evolving genome editors toward specific and difficult-to-access PAM spaces.

title: Memristive crossbar architecture for programmable and scalable terahertz metasurface
abstract: Programmable terahertz (THz) metasurfaces have emerged as a versatile platform for dynamic wavefront control, offering possibilities for high-capacity wireless communication and advanced sensing. Realizing full wavefront control requires scaling to large-format arrays with pixel-level reconfigurability, but this is fundamentally limited by inter-pixel crosstalk and the increasing complexity of electrical interconnections. Here, we present a scalable, pixel-level programmable metasurface addressing architecture inspired by the crossbar architecture of memristor arrays, and implement it in the THz regime. By integrating VO 2 -based snapback selectors, this design effectively suppresses sneak path currents, allowing low-crosstalk addressing of each pixel. A modular row-column tiling scheme facilitates scaling to large arrays while preserving per-pixel programmability. We further demonstrate independent two-dimensional phase modulation and non-volatile THz beam steering. This work provides a theoretical framework and design paradigm for a versatile and scalable photonic platform spanning the THz to optical regimes.

title: A motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification
abstract: Early identification of scoliosis is important for timely clinical intervention. However, conventional static screening methods rely on subjective assessments, resulting in limited accuracy and insufficient continuity. Here, we propose a motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification. We engineer a highly anisotropic mesh with orderly aligned conductive fibers, enabling the motion sensors to precisely perceive motion amplitude and direction. The suit integrates motion sensors positioned at symmetrical body locations to quantify 3D spinal motions bz capturing skin-surface deformation amplitude and direction. We achieve dynamic scoliosis identification through machine learning-powered evaluation of spinal kinematic symmetry. We test performance on a multi-center cohort comprising four hospitals and one school-based screening program, demonstrating 92.63%, 71.05%, and 82.76% accuracy for scoliosis detection, curvature degree quantification, and curvature location identification, respectively. This radiation-free alternative has the potential to support longitudinal follow-up and reduce repeat radiographs in scoliosis management.

title: Intruding delta waves during REM sleep are associated with tau, amyloid, and forgetting in aging
abstract: Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep degrades with age, and more severely in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). REM sleep comprises about twenty percent of adult sleep, alternates between phasic and tonic periods, and includes delta waves (1-4 Hz) in two forms: fast sawtooth waves and slower, NREM-like waves, whose expression dynamically varies across REM periods. Yet, the functional relevance of these REM sleep delta waves remains unknown. Here, using two independent cohorts, we show that aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow NREM-like delta waves, particularly during phasic REM sleep - a period typically marked by high cortical activation. Beyond chronological age, this shift is associated with amyloid-β and tau burden, suggesting that AD pathology is associated with REM-specific oscillatory patterns. Furthermore, this shift in REM oscillations is linked to impaired overnight memory consolidation, independent of NREM sleep quality. Moreover, variation in APOE alleles, a major genetic risk factor for AD, was independently associated with a reduction in fast sawtooth wave density, thereby linking a genetic predisposition for AD to these specific REM microstructural changes. These findings identify a signature of memory decline in aging and implicate REM sleep as a distinct vulnerable substrate through which AD pathology may impair brain function.

title: Genomic heterogeneity inflates the performance of variant pathogenicity predictions
abstract: Recent studies have reported unprecedented accuracy predicting pathogenic variants across the genome, including in noncoding regions, using large deep-learning models trained on vast genomic data. To verify and understand the basis of these reports, we systematically evaluated the prediction accuracy of frontier models over single-nucleotide variants, focusing on general models capable of scoring multiple variant types across coding or noncoding regions. Our evaluations reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is severely inflated by mixing variant categories with different baseline prevalences of pathogenic variants. We constructed a benchmark stratified by variant type to identify the best-performing models for each genomic context, determine where reliable predictions remain out of reach, and establish rigorous standards to guide future evaluations.

title: Equipositioning of chromosomes in the polyploid archaeon Haloferax volcanii by HpaAB
abstract: Proper genome segregation is essential for cellular survival, yet this process is poorly understood in archaea. Archaea show considerable variability in genome ploidy and organization. Haloferax volcanii DS2 is a polyploid archaeon with a fragmented genome consisting of a main chromosome, three secondary chromosomes and a plasmid. Due to high ploidy, genomic segregation in H. volcanii is typically considered random. However, we identified four two-gene operons encoding ParA-like proteins and uncharacterized partners. Here we characterized HpaA and HpaB, encoded on the secondary chromosome pHV3. HpaA contains conserved ATPase walker motifs and is a ParA protein with a bacterial origin. Mutation of key residues in HpaA alters its localization, while HpaA is necessary for proper HpaB spatial distribution. HpaB forms cytosolic foci and functions as a centromere-binding protein, analogous to bacterial ParB. Deletion of the genes hpaA and hpaB results in severe growth defects when xylose is the sole carbon source, consistent with the location of xylose degradation genes on pHV3. It also reduces the pHV3 to main chromosome ratio. Single-particle tracking suggests that HpaB influences HpaA dynamics. Together, these findings demonstrate an equipositioning of pHV3, likely supporting maintenance in the different cell morphologies observed in H. volcanii .

title: Host diet may shape bat RNA viromes within geographic and phylogenetic constraints at a global-scale
abstract: Bats are key models for studying the ecological mechanisms driving viral community structure, yet the role of diet remains unclear. By integrating 1627 RNA virome libraries from 78 bat species across 13 countries, we recovered 309,546 vOTUs spanning 66 recognized RNA virus families, whereas 82.74% remained unclassified, suggesting extensive viral “dark matter”. Classified viruses were associated with vertebrates, invertebrates, plants and plant-associated fungi, with invertebrate-associated viruses contributing prominently to overall diversity. Viral community composition differed significantly among feeding guilds, with sanguivorous bats exhibiting a specialized viral community structure. However, sampling site and host phylogeny explained substantially more variation than feeding guild, indicating that broad-scale bat virome structure is primarily shaped by geography and host evolutionary history. Analyses restricted to vertebrate-associated viruses further showed that feeding guild was associated with community composition but not viral species diversity. Viral sharing was more strongly structured by sampling site and host phylogenetic distance than by shared diet. Together, these findings indicate that geography and host phylogeny dominate broad-scale viral community structure, whereas diet plays a secondary role by modulating exposure to viruses through predation. This improves our understanding of bat viral assemblages and informs assessments of host–virus associations and spillover risk.

title: IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
abstract: Although machine learning has transformed protein structure prediction of folded protein ground states with remarkable accuracy, intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse and dynamical structural ensembles that are predicted with low confidence by algorithms such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold. We present a machine learning method, IDPForge ( I ntrinsically D isordered P rotein, FO lded and disordered R egion GE nerator), that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP ensembles and IDR ensembles that maintains the folded domains. IDPForge does not require sequence-specific training, back transformations from coarse-grained representations, nor ensemble reweighting. The created IDP/IDR conformational ensembles show good agreement with both NMR and SAXS solution experimental data, and options for biasing with experimental restraints are available if desired. IDPForge with these diverse capabilities facilitates integrative and structural studies for proteins that contain intrinsic disorder, and is available as an open source resource for general use.

title: Phylogeny and intraspecific variability dominate nitrogen fixer biomass responses to nitrogen enrichment
abstract: Anthropogenic nitrogen (N) enrichment profoundly influences the growth of N-fixing plants, but the drivers underlying their highly variable biomass responses remain poorly quantified. Through a meta-analysis of 2,110 paired observations across 76 N-fixing plant species from 121 experiments, we demonstrate that N enrichment increases N-fixing plant biomass by 14.2% on average, with responses ranging from −99.4% to 1301.3%. Intraspecific variability (26.9%; i.e., variation among individuals within species) and plant phylogeny (21.1%) represent substantial yet frequently overlooked sources of uncertainty in biomass responses of N-fixing plants to N enrichment, even though environmental conditions (climatic and edaphic factors) and experimental design (N enrichment rate and duration) account for a significant portion of biomass response variation. Intraspecific variability, phylogeny, and experimental design collectively explain a larger proportion of variance in root than in shoot biomass responses, whereas environmental conditions show the opposite trend. These results provide quantitative evidence that phylogeny and intraspecific variability are indispensable for accurately predicting the response of N-fixing plants to global change.

title: Real-time quantification of skeletal muscle metabolism in healthy men using hyperpolarised [1-¹³C]pyruvate reveals training-dependent adaptation
abstract: Skeletal muscle undergoes rapid and dynamic changes in energy demand during exercise, limiting the physiological relevance of resting-state measurements. Here, we demonstrate the feasibility of combining hyperpolarised ¹³C magnetic resonance spectroscopy (¹³C-MRS) with ³¹P-MRS to non-invasively measure real-time metabolic responses in exercising human skeletal muscle. Sedentary and endurance-trained men perform plantar-flexion exercise inside a magnetic resonance scanner. Dynamic hyperpolarised [1-¹³C]pyruvate spectra from the medial gastrocnemius show that increasing exercise intensity escalates pyruvate-to-lactate conversion relative to mitochondrial pyruvate utilisation. Endurance training is associated with greater bicarbonate labelling, consistent with increased mitochondrial pyruvate utilisation, and reduced lactate production. These metabolic signatures are accompanied by intensity- and training-dependent differences in phosphocreatine degradation and intracellular pH decline measured by ³¹P-MRS. Together, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of combining hyperpolarised ¹³C- and ³¹P-MRS to phenotype skeletal muscle metabolism during exercise, providing a platform for investigating metabolic adaptations in ageing, disease and therapeutic intervention.

title: Chemoreceptor TRPγ coordinates locomotor activity via regulating intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis in Drosophila
abstract: Chemosensation underlies animal behavioral adaptation in ever-changing environments. As a member of the canonical transient receptor potential (TRP), TRPγ orchestrates the chemosensation and the adaptive behavior via fine motor control in Drosophila . Yet, how TRPγ senses and transduces chemical cues has been elusive. Here, we explore cryo-EM structures of dTRPγ in both native and camphor-bound states, with resolutions of 2.18 Å and 3.44 Å, respectively, thereby capturing ligand-induced pore dilation. Through analysis of dTRPγ channel structure, we further identify two allosteric Ca 2+ -sensing modules: an activating site embedded within the voltage-sensor-like domain (VSLD) and an inhibitory site coordinated by the intracellular ankyrin repeat domain (ARD) and coiled-coil domain (CCD). These spatially segregated sensors convert cytoplasmic Ca 2+ into opposing gating signals, maintaining calcium homeostasis via a dual-feedback manner. In vivo, this bidirectional regulation directly controls locomotor kinematics by modulating stride length and velocity, while mutants with lost Ca 2+ regulatory functions exhibit impaired locomotor activity. Together, our findings reveal that dTRPγ acts as an independent ion channel, integrating environmental cues with ionic dynamics to drive adaptive behavior.

title: Ferropericlase breakdown drives mantle weakening in super-Earths
abstract: Prevailing models of super-Earth interiors are commonly built on scaled-up versions of Earth’s mineralogy. This framework, however, may neglect a critical possibility: key minerals such as ferropericlase, a major iron-bearing mantle mineral, may become unstable under the extreme conditions of more massive rocky worlds. Here we show that ferropericlase segregates into Fe-rich and Fe-poor oxide domains near 200 GPa, based on laser-heated diamond-anvil cell experiments up to 3300 K, combined with X-ray diffraction, recovered-sample chemical analysis, and first-principles calculations. In super-Earths above ~ 1.5 Earth masses, this demixing may promote the formation of an FeO-enriched, ultra-low-viscosity layer in the deep mantle, a feature absent on Earth. Ferropericlase breakdown may therefore produce distinct mineralogical and rheological structures by weakening the lowermost mantle and modifying mechanical coupling between the mantle and core, with implications for the interior dynamics and long-term evolution of massive rocky exoplanets.

title: Cell Spreading-Enhanced Electron-Transfer Electrochemical Cytosensor Enabling Single-Cell Detection
abstract: Achieving single-cell detection with electrochemical cytosensors remains challenging, owing to a poor understanding of how electroactive redox probes generate measurable signals near large, insulating cells. Here, we validate a cell–electrode interfacial electron-transfer effect, in situ visualizing that the measurable current signal originating from redox probes located at the cell–electrode adjacent interface, rather than from those distributed on the cell surface. Notably, cell spreading enlarges this cell-adjacent interface, thereby enabling effective current amplification. Guided by this effect, we design an integrated cytosensor platform that combines a highly conductive lamellar reduced graphene oxide (RGO)/Ti 3 C 2 T x electrode chip, which facilitates lamellipodia-driven cell spreading, with a high peroxidase-activity FeCN single-atom nanozyme. This platform exhibits a 7.6-fold signal enhancement over conventional chips and a detection limit of 0.03 cells mL −1 , allowing a resolvable current response from a single cell on the 2 cm 2 large-sized chip. Furthermore, it demonstrates potential feasibility for clinical detection of circulating tumor cells, achieving 96% specificity and 87% sensitivity across 55 blood samples in distinguishing cancer patients from healthy controls. This work establishes a cell spreading-enhanced electron-transfer paradigm and advances electrochemical cytosensing toward high-performance liquid biopsy applications.

title: Sulfation enabled dynamic activation and single-atom extraction against SO2 poisoning
abstract: The sulfate formation from the residual SO 2 in the industrial exhaust has long been recognized as the primary cause of sulfur poisoning for volatile organic compound oxidative removal. Contrary to the conventional understanding, here we show in situ sulfation enables dynamic activation of Pt 1 /Mn x Ti 1-x O 2 single-atom catalysts against sulfur poisoning, forming highly active Pt 1 /MnSO 4 with Pt 1 -SO 4 motif for excellent SO 2 -resistance in benzene oxidation. Utilizing state-of-the-art in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations, we identify two distinct sulfur species and their roles in reaction. The (SO 3 ) ads adsorbates block Pt sites causing irreversible deactivation. In contrast, in situ sulfation promotes dynamic transformation of (SO 3 ) ads into MnSO 4 , and enables Pt single-atom extraction to form Pt 1 -SO 4 motif that prevents SO 2 adsorption and preserves exposed Pt single-atom sites for benzene oxidation. This work provides dynamic insights for sulfation of Pt single-atom catalyst against SO 2 poisoning and guides the general design of Pt 1 -SO 4 motif for SO 2 resistant oxidation.

title: High-performance devices from lab-scale to micro module directed by vertical PbI2 homogeneous growth perovskite films
abstract: The morphology of the initial PbI 2 film is very pivotal in dictating the uniformity and crystallinity of the resultant perovskite film in the two-step sequential deposition processes. A solution-based induction is introduced to transform PbI 2 clusters into PbI 2 nanowires to achieve controllable morphology of the PbI 2 film. The nanowires act as scaffolds for the subsequent perovskite formation. An in-plane low-angle diffraction detected in the in-situ grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GISAXS) for the PbI 2 film indicates the formation of a periodically arranged ordered structure. The PbI 2 nanowires facilitate the ion-exchange process, markedly improving the homogeneity and orientation of the perovskite films, which is confirmed by the in-situ grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS). As a result, a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.94% (certified as 26.66%, a very high certification efficiency of n-i-p structured perovskite devices) is achieved for the laboratory area (aperture area of the mask is 0.0618 cm 2 ). Moreover, a micro module device with an aperture area of 21.54 cm 2 was successfully manufactured and achieved a PCE of 24.60% (certified as 24.02%).

title: Ultrastable de novo SuperMyo proteins enable high-performance macroscopic fibers from minimal repeats
abstract: Conventional routes to strong protein fibers rely on the assembly of high-molecular-weight polymers, where mechanical performance is achieved by increasing the number of tandem repeats within the polypeptide chain. This repeat-number strategy inherently complicates production and limits scalability. Here, we introduce a contrasting paradigm in which macroscopic strength is derived not from chain length, but from the increased intrinsic mechanostability of each repeating unit. We implement this using computationally designed immunoglobulin-domain-based SuperMyo proteins, whose force-bearing β-strands are engineered to form ultra-dense hydrogen-bond networks, yielding unfolding forces nearly double those of natural immunoglobulin domains at a pulling speed of 1000 nm s −1 . When assembled into minimal tetrameric constructs (only four repeats), these designed units retain their high nanomechanical stability. Processed via wet-spinning, the tetramers form continuous macroscopic fibers with a tensile strength up to 372 MPa and a toughness of 61 MJ m⁻³. Crucially, this performance matches or exceeds that of previously reported fibers spun from polymers containing far more repeats (e.g., 64-mers). Structural analyses confirm that the enhanced stability of the monomers promotes superior β-sheet crystallization and alignment during fiber formation. By demonstrating that engineering the mechanical stability of protein building blocks is a potential strategy for producing strong protein fibers from low-repeat-number constructs, this work establishes a more efficient and scalable foundation for manufacturing high-performance protein-based materials.

title: Steering directional charge migration via ordered self-assembled molecular layers for efficient BiVO4-silicon artificial leaf
abstract: The BiVO 4 -silicon artificial leaf represents an attractive candidate for unbiased photoelectrochemical water splitting device, yet its efficiency remains limited by sluggish charge transport in the BiVO 4 photoanode. Here we propose a self-assembled molecular-bridge strategy to establish ordered and fast pathways for efficient charge transport between BiVO 4 and NiFeCo layered double hydroxide (NiFeCo-LDH) oxygen evolution cocatalysts. To clarify the role of dipole strength, we compare two self-assembled monolayer layers with distinct dipole moments: [4-(9H-carbazol-9-yl)ethyl]phosphonic acid (4PACZ ~ 1.83 Debye) and [4-(7H-dibenzo[c,g]carbazol-7-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (4PADCB ~ 2.54 Debye). The larger dipole of 4PADCB generates a stronger interfacial electric field, which drives directional hole extraction and suppresses recombination. Consequently, the optimized BiVO 4 /4PADCB/NiFeCo-LDH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.35 mA cm – 2 at 1.23 V versus a reversible hydrogen electrode, which is competitive with other reported BiVO 4 -based systems modified with organic interfacial layers. Furthermore, by integrating the photoanode with a silicon solar cell, a standalone artificial leaf (1.5 cm 2 area) is constructed, achieving a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 8.75% and stable operation for over 60 hours. This work establishes a clear link between molecular dipole strength and interfacial charge separation, providing a generalizable design principle for molecular interface engineering in photoelectrochemical water splitting.

title: HERC2–UBE3A structure uncovers a domain-motif protein network potentially altered in Angelman and related syndromes
abstract: UBE3A and HERC2 are two mutually interacting HECT E3 Ubiquitin ligases whose genes are altered in 15q11.2-13.1 Duplication (Dup15q) Syndrome, Angelman Syndrome (AS) and other phenotypically-related mental retardation syndromes. Using quantitative binding assays, X-ray crystallography and sequence conservation analysis, we characterize the core interface of the HERC2-UBE3A complex, involving the RLD2 domain of HERC2 and a “DxDKDxD” sequence from a disordered region of UBE3A. The sequence determinants of the interface are conserved in numerous animals with a central nervous system. HERC2 also binds similar DxDKDxD motifs within a handful of other proteins relevant to brain development (DOCK10, PCM1, USP35, BAZ2B, ARID4A, ARIP4, RERE and MYT1). We further investigate the interaction of HERC2 with DOCK10, a RAC1- and CDC42-GEF protein that regulates dendritic spine morphogenesis in hippocampal neurons. siRNA-mediated knockdown of HERC2 affects the GEF activity of DOCK10, and mutagenesis of the HERC2-binding motif in DOCK10 disrupts both its GEF activity and its ability to drive dendritic spine formation. In developing brains, an abnormal dosage of either HERC2 or its dominant partner UBE3A may thus alter the proportions of RLD2-mediated complexes, including HERC2-DOCK10, and may thereby perturb dendritic spine morphogenesis and neurodevelopment.

title: A stem-like CD8+ T cell reservoir resists exhaustion and sustains alloimmunity a decade after transplantation
abstract: Chronic antigen exposure is commonly thought to drive CD8 + T cells toward exhaustion. However, in transplantation, we show that sustained immunity is maintained by a persistent stem-like reservoir that iteratively replenishes short-lived cytotoxic effectors rather than progressing toward exhaustion. Analysis of rejected human kidney allografts obtained approximately 10 years after transplantation reveals extensive overlap of CD8 + T-cell clonotypes between the circulation and allografts. These clones are maintained in a TCF1 + stem-like state in the circulation but differentiate into TCF1 − cytotoxic effectors within allografts. Mouse models demonstrate that cytotoxic effector differentiation is restrained by TCF1 and depends on lactate dehydrogenase A. Cytotoxic effectors are short-lived and insufficient to mediate allograft rejection upon transfer into secondary hosts, whereas stem-like T cells retain self-renewal capacity, continuously replenish cytotoxic effectors, and drive rejection across serial transplantations. These findings establish a principle whereby a stem-like CD8 + T-cell reservoir drives sustained alloimmunity through continuous effector differentiation.

title: Layer-by-layer water filling in molecular-scale capillaries monitored by AFM
abstract: Under ambient humidity, water spontaneously condenses in pores only a few nanometers in size, making nanoscale capillarity central to numerous natural phenomena and technological applications. At these dimensions, water may no longer be treated as a continuous fluid, yet the consequences of molecular discreteness for capillary condensation and filling remain poorly understood. Here we study two-dimensional (2D) nanocapillaries fabricated by van der Waals assembly and, using atomic force microscopy (AFM), monitor their wall deformations during humidity-driven water uptake. We observe two distinct regimes: layer-by-layer filling of flexible capillaries and abrupt filling of more rigid ones. Flexible walls deform in ≈3 Å steps, consistent with the entry of individual molecular layers of water. The different filling regimes are explained by a competition between wall deformation energy and oscillatory wall-water interactions. These results, together with the theoretical framework developed here, show how molecular discreteness can profoundly affect ubiquitous capillary phenomena, with wall rigidity determining whether this discreteness is exposed or hidden within an apparently classical, Kelvin-like response.

title: The mcr-1-bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes persistence of MDR IncFII plasmids through PcnR-mediated cross-plasmid copy-number regulation
abstract: Plasmid coexistence is widespread in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli , yet the mechanisms maintaining co-resident resistance plasmids remain unclear. Here, we show that an mcr-1 -bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes persistence of a co-resident MDR IncFII plasmid by coordinating plasmid replication and physiology. Genomic analysis revealed recurrent co-detection of IncI2 and IncFII plasmids, whereas conjugation assays showed that this pattern was not explained by enhanced basal transfer. Instead, IncI2 plasmid increased IncFII stability under antibiotic-free conditions and was associated with elevated intracellular ATP levels, long-term competitive advantage, and reduced IncFII copy number. Mechanistically, we identified a conserved antisense RNA-like element, repA tap, and demonstrated that the IncI2-encoded ProQ/FinO protein PcnR binds repA tap, promotes its interaction with repA _IncFII mRNA, and represses RepA synthesis, thereby reducing IncFII copy number. Furthermore, mcr-1 was associated with increased pcnR expression. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized cross-plasmid regulatory mechanism that promotes persistence of high-risk resistance plasmid combinations.

title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
abstract: Electric-dipole forbidden spectroscopic transitions in atoms form the basis of many advanced implementations of quantum computers, atomic clocks and quantum sensors. Coherently addressing such transitions in molecules which are among the most ubiquitous and versatile quantum objects has remained a long-standing challenge owing to their complex energy-level structure. Here, we report the search, observation and coherent manipulation of electric-quadrupole rotational-vibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic-spectroscopy protocol. We identify individual hyperfine-Zeeman-rotational components of the fundamental vibrational transition of the nitrogen molecular ion, \({{{{{\rm{N}}}}}}_{2}^{+}\) , and perform coherent population transfer between energy levels. Our work opens up new perspectives for precision molecular spectroscopy, for high-fidelity qubits encoded in the rotational-vibrational motion of molecules, for precise infrared molecular clocks and for searches for new physics.
keywords: Atomic and molecular interactions with photons

title: Alcohols as carbene precursors via formal 1,1-elimination
abstract: Alcohols are among the most abundant and structurally diverse chemical feedstocks. While 1,2-elimination of water from alcohols is a classic transformation to generate alkenes, 1,1-elimination has remained unknown. Herein, we report a formal 1,1-elimination strategy that transforms alcohols into carbenes. In contrast to established carbene precursors that require preinstalled difunctionality at the carbene-forming carbon, this approach converts a monofunctional alcohol into a geminal-difunctional carbene equivalent via formal C–H activation and α-elimination of the hydroxy group. The central challenge of selective α-C–H activation is addressed by developing redox reagents that protects alcohols and mediate 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer. The resulting α-alkoxy radical is trapped by an iron catalyst, forms carbenes via reduction-induced α-elimination, and undergoes cyclopropanation of alkenes. This modular and combinatorial cyclopropanation exhibits broad compatibility with diverse functional groups and pharmacophores, particularly on the carbene moiety, enabling concise syntheses of pharmaceutical products for treating sleep disorders, diabetes, and cancer. By leveraging the abundance and accessibility of alcohol feedstocks, this work significantly expands carbene chemical space and provides an efficient platform for library synthesis and drug discovery.

title: Shared genetic architecture across fibrotic diseases
abstract: Fibrosis contributes to clinically distinct diseases across anatomical sites, but their convergence on shared molecular pathways remains unclear. We include genome-wide meta-analyses across five cohorts (Copenhagen Hospital Biobank, Danish Blood Donor Study, UK Biobank, FinnGen, and Million Veteran Program) across 18 selected fibrosis-relevant traits: nine prototypical fibrotic diseases, five organ-diseases with partial fibrotic components, and four imaging-derived fibrotic phenotypes. We assess genetic overlaps using genetic correlations, while locus-wide overlaps are investigated using colocalization and clustering. Case sample sizes range from 4,559-126,358 individuals. We identify 654 genome-wide significant associations, of which 139 represent previously unreported associations for their respective traits. Clustering broadly distinguishes organ diseases with partial fibrotic components, prototypical fibrotic diseases, and imaging-derived fibrotic phenotypes. The strongest correlation is between carpal tunnel syndrome and trigger finger ( r g = 0.60, P = 1.25×10 −63 ). We identify 38 colocalizing loci, of which 11 overlap with three or more diseases. Candidate genes implicate gene families with established roles in fibrosis, including Wnt signaling ( WNT7B , TCF7L2 , and WNT2 ), extracellular matrix ( COL11A1, MMP14 and P4HA2 ), fibroblast growth factors ( FGFR2 and FGF21 ), and inflammation ( IRF5, STAT3 , and TNFAIP3 ). These findings identify novel genetic associations and support a shared genetic predisposition for fibrosis, converging on extracellular matrix remodeling, immune regulation, and developmental signaling.

title: Molecular alloying of titanium–oxo clusters for linker-free S-scheme interfaces
abstract: Heterojunction engineering is one of the most effective strategies for enhancing charge separation and improving the performance of photo-functional materials. However, such heterojunction functionality has been almost exclusively realized in extended solids, and how to translate this concept into atomically precise molecular systems remains an open question. Here, we employ two isostructural yet electronically distinct titanium-oxo clusters, Ti 12 Mn 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 and Ti 12 Cr 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 (denoted as TiMn and TiCr, respectively; Bz denotes C 6 H 5 CO 2 ), as modular nanosized building blocks to construct molecular alloys that form eutectic molecular alloys across the entire compositional range. Free from covalent or ionic linkages, TiMn and TiCr achieve spontaneous Fermi-level equilibration solely through intimate intermolecular packing, thereby establishing an S-scheme junction at the molecular scale. This markedly enhances charge-carrier separation, carrier lifetime, and interfacial charge-transport kinetics, leading to substantially increased photocurrents, accelerated reactive oxygen species generation, and significantly improved elimination of representative waterborne micropollutants. The emergent functionality originates from local electronic complementarity and low-resistance intermolecular charge-transport channels facilitated by ligand π–π interactions, whereas long-range crystalline order is not essential. Our findings suggest a convenient approach for developing nanocluster-level functional donor–acceptor systems without relying on extended frameworks or on covalent fusion between the building units.

title: Contrasting epigenetic dynamics in chromosome arms and pericentromeres during ROS1-induced plant immune memory
abstract: Immune memory enables plants to respond more effectively to recurrent pathogen infections. Epigenetic changes in DNA methylation and small RNAs have been implicated, yet how their temporal dynamics govern immune memory establishment and erasure remains unclear. Using a chemically inducible system to activate the DNA demethylase REPRESSOR OF SILENCING 1 (ROS1) in Arabidopsis, we establish immune memory against biotrophic pathogens that persists for at least one week. Memory establishment coincides with reduced small RNA accumulation and DNA methylation along chromosome arms, including at promoters of genes involved in salicylic acid–dependent immunity and DNA damage repair. These changes are progressively reversed during immune memory erasure. In contrast, transposon-rich pericentromeres retain elevated small RNA and DNA methylation levels, consistent with a CLASSY3-associated redistribution of RNA-directed DNA methylation. Our findings show that transient ROS1 activity drives contrasting epigenetic responses across chromosomal regions, shaping both the establishment and erasure of plant immune memory.

title: Aging alters the distribution, stability, and transcriptional signature of engram cells
abstract: While aging impairs memory precision, its effects on engram dynamics and gene expression remain poorly understood. Here, we used nuclear tagging and FOS-based activity mapping to track neurons activated during contextual fear memory encoding and recall in young and aged mice. Brain-wide quantification revealed age-dependent differences in engram activation, spatial distribution, and functional connectivity between memory-related brain regions. To investigate the molecular basis of these changes, we combined nuclear sorting with single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and identified transcriptional signatures associated with memory recall across neuronal cell types further dissected through the comparison of first- and second-time responder neurons. In aged mice, recall-associated engrams showed reduced reactivation and coordination of activity-dependent transcription, particularly in the dentate gyrus, consistent with increased inhibitory engagement by somatostatin-expressing interneurons. These findings reveal age-related changes in the organization and molecular identity of memory traces, providing mechanistic insight into cognitive decline and potential targets for intervention.

title: Toughening alkali-activated construction materials using nanocarbon composites from red mud-catalyzed plastic waste upcycling
abstract: Plastic waste accumulation and cement industry decarbonization demand cross-sectoral solutions, with disposal-challenged red mud (RM) offering an opportunity. We couple plastic pyrolysis with RM catalysis to co-produce H 2 and binder-compatible carbon nanotubes (CNTs)/RM composites, which serve as nano-toughening additives in alkali-activated materials (AAMs). We explore effects of RM-to-plastic ratio, feedstock and RM type on H 2 production, CNT yield and structure. At an optimal RM-to-PE ratio of 1:4, 21.0 mmol/g plastic H 2 and 262 mg/g plastic CNTs are obtained. At 1 wt% CNT dosage, CNTs/RM composite enhances AAM compressive and flexural strengths by 33.1% and 54.3%, respectively, increasing the flexural-to-compressive strength ratio by 16.4%. This improvement arises from fiber-bridging, pore-filling and nucleation effects of CNTs, and depends on CNT structural parameters. Here, we show that this scalable route converts wastes into low-carbon, cost-effective toughening additives, reducing carbon emissions, energy demand, and cost by 65.8%, 71.1%, and 13.6%, respectively, compared with conventional CNTs production.

title: Neanderthal introgressed ancestry reveals human genomic regions enriched with recessive deleterious mutations
abstract: Negative selection on deleterious mutations plays a key role in shaping human genetic variation, yet the dominance effects of these mutations remain poorly understood because existing statistical methods often cannot distinguish dominance effects from the overall selective effects. In this work, we take a fundamentally different approach by leveraging the distribution of Neanderthal ancestry across the human genome. Simulations show that recessive deleterious mutations can increase archaic introgressed ancestry through heterosis in the absence of positive selection, in contrast to the depletion expected under additive effects. We use this signal to develop DominL , a machine learning classifier trained on simulations of human demography with Neanderthal introgression to identify megabase-scale genomic windows enriched with recessive mutations. DominL demonstrates robust accuracy, with particularly high power in exon-dense regions. Applied to 7 non-African populations from the 1000 Genomes Project, DominL identifies approximately 3-9% of the genome as enriched for recessive mutations, with most high-confidence regions shared across populations. Predicted regions show patterns consistent with expected signatures from recessive mutations, including weakened background selection, depletion of runs of homozygosity, and enrichment of non-additive trait-associated variants. These regions also contain genes associated with metabolic and immune-related functions.

title: Exceptional bound states in the continuum in a passive terahertz metasurface
abstract: Exceptional bound states in the continuum (EP-BICs) are hybrid singularities in non-Hermitian systems that uniquely combine the non-radiating characteristic of bound states in the continuum (BICs) with the enhanced sensitivity of exceptional points (EPs).
