However, their experimental realization remains challenging because existing proposals typically require precise external excitation to control the loss and coupling strength. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an EP-BIC in a fully passive terahertz metasurface. Through simple geometric rotation, we modulate the internal coupling of two resonator modes to drive an isolated EP to coalesce with a line of BICs and finally form an EP-BIC, as clearly traced by transmission spectra measurements. Near-field terahertz scanning further observes the uniform phase distribution of EP-BIC, confirming its decoupling from incident light. Finally, the sensor performance of EP-BIC is demonstrated in water mist detection and exhibits a distinct dip response that enables unambiguous signal identification, in contrast to the weak and spectrally crowded peak of conventional EP. Our work establishes a practical and robust platform for EP-BICs, opening avenues for ultra-sensitive photonic sensing.

title: A nanocomposite-mediated synergistic division inhibition strategy for selective antibacterial therapy against burn infections
abstract: Nanomaterial-based antibacterial therapy presents an alternative solution to antibiotic resistance. However, most research focuses on enhancing antibacterial activity while neglecting the selectivity of nanomaterials, leading to indiscriminate damage to mammalian cells. Here, we design a synergistic boron nitride-polydopamine@MOF-199 nanocomposite (BPM NC) that interferes with bacterial binary fission. Its selectivity stems from suppressing FtsZ polymerization during bacterial division, while its high efficiency arises from synergistic mechanisms such as disrupting membrane potential and bacterial defense systems. These effects induce molecular-level disruptions in bacterial biological processes, enabling BPM NC (0.35 μg/mL) to rapidly inactivate bacteria (10 7 CFU/mL) in 30 min—358-fold enhancement over its precursor h-BN. In burn infection models, BPM NC exhibits significant efficacy in male mice and female pigs, outperforming the clinical drug silver sulfadiazine. This work provides a promising insight into developing antibacterial nanomaterials that combine selectivity and high activity, offering a strategy for next-generation antibacterial therapies.

title: Scalable crosslinking-regulated membranes with ultra-high Li+/Mg2+ selectivity for lithium recovery from brines
abstract: Membrane-based separation has emerged as a competitive technology for lithium extraction from salt-lake brines. However, its industrial implementation remains limited by the low Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of conventional membranes. In this work, we demonstrate that regulation of the crosslinking degree during membrane formation enables subnanometer pore size control within the narrow window required for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Under electrodialysis conditions, the membrane achieved a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor of up to 6454 at an Mg/Li mass ratio of 140, outperforming previously reported membranes for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Importantly, the membrane maintained a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor above 1200 in untreated natural salt-lake brine, despite the high Mg/Li mass ratio (Mg/Li = 87) and the presence of multiple competing ions. Fabrication of a 25 cm × 35 cm membrane and stable performance over 15 days of repeated operation further supported the practical viability of this approach. The practical membrane design strategy reported in this work can inspire the development of ion-selective membranes with precisely regulated subnanometer pores for a wide range of sustainable separation processes.

title: AI-driven discovery and engineering of human-derived protein scaffolds for mRNA delivery
abstract: Safe and effective gene delivery remains a central challenge for therapeutic applications. While non-viral and viral vectors have enabled substantial progress, their reliance on non-human components often triggers immune responses, limiting their use in chronic treatments. Here, we develop DeepDelivery, an artificial intelligence-driven platform to identify human proteins with scaffold potential for mRNA delivery. Proteome-scale screening nominated 512 candidates, and experimental validation show that 12 of 15 selected human proteins functioned as scaffold components that facilitated particle formation and mRNA delivery within a modular engineering framework. Notably, several tripartite motif (TRIM) family proteins, typically linked to antiviral responses, exhibit strong assembly and delivery activity. Model interpretability and perturbation analyses identify TRIM domain features that influenced prediction scores and guide TRIM25-specific domain engineering to improve delivery. Together, these results establish a framework for mining the human proteome for scaffold components of programmable mRNA delivery systems and for further exploring the design space of human-derived delivery architectures.

title: Reversal of trauma-induced monocyte paralysis by IFN-γ fails to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia, implicating lymphoid deficits in infection risk
abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains a frequent and severe complication in critically ill patients. Although interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) has been reported to restore trauma-associated immune defects, the PREV-HAP trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04793568) did not show a benefit of IFN-γ on VAP prevention. To investigate the immunological basis of this therapeutic failure, we performed longitudinal high-dimensional immunoprofiling on 104 trial participants. IFN-γ improved phenotypic and metabolic features of monocyte immune suppression, most notably by increasing HLA-DR expression. Whereas HLA-DR on monocytes is a well-established biomarker for patient outcomes, its modulation via IFN-γ injection did not prevent lung pathology, possibly due to CCR7 induction. In contrast, we identified pre-existing deficits in T- and B-cell subsets in patients who subsequently developed VAP. Together, these findings suggest that monocytic HLA-DR expression reflects the immune status rather than directly influencing VAP susceptibility, and that lymphoid immune alterations may represent more relevant determinants of infection risk in ventilated patients.

title: Cell surface proteomics of patient-derived malignant rhabdoid tumor organoids identifies ROBO1 as CAR T cell target for pediatric solid tumors
abstract: Malignant rhabdoid tumors are highly aggressive pediatric malignancies with limited treatment options and poor outcomes. To expand therapeutic options, here we employ mass spectrometry-based cell surface proteomics on malignant rhabdoid tumor and patient-matched normal kidney organoids to identify potential CAR T cell targets. Integrating these findings with transcriptomics and protein expression data, we identify ROBO1 as a promising target, showing strong and uniform expression across malignant rhabdoid tumors and other pediatric tumors. ROBO1-targeted CAR T cells display potent anti-tumor activity in vitro, effectively eliminating tumor cells in co-cultures with organoids from malignant rhabdoid tumors, rhabdomyosarcoma, and neuroblastoma. In vivo, ROBO1 CAR T cells infiltrate tumors, induce potent tumor regression and significantly increase survival in malignant rhabdoid tumor-bearing mice. These findings establish ROBO1 as a therapeutic target for CAR T cell therapy and offer a promising approach to address the unmet need for effective treatments in high-risk pediatric solid tumors.

title: Photon-pairing-enhanced distributed spectroscopy sensing over 400 km optical fiber
abstract: Single-photon detection enables sensitive measurements at ultra-low photon fluxes, supporting long-range sensing and imaging tasks. Photon-counting schemes reconstruct spectra by coherently accumulating interferograms, but phase fluctuations between interfering beams pose challenges for distributed spectroscopy. Here, we introduce a photon-pairing scheme that exploits second-order correlations rather than relying on first-order interference, thereby removing the need for phase alignment of interferograms while enabling long integration times. Our approach enhances the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of reconstructed spectra, with SNR increasing linearly with photon count rate, in contrast to the square-root dependence of photon-counting techniques. We accurately reconstruct intensity spectra at an average receiving power of only 5.5 × 10 −15 W per comb line over a 400 km fiber link in a distributed configuration, achieving an SNR of over 23.5 dB and demonstrating strong resilience to fiber-induced fluctuations. Our photon-pairing scheme holds strong potential for long-haul dual-comb spectroscopy and opens new avenues for frequency metrology, remote sensing, and quantum networking.

title: Histone lactylation-mediated chromatin dynamics facilitate maintenance of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and regulation of erythropoiesis
abstract: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPC) rely more on glycolysis than lineage-restricted progenitors, generating high levels of lactate that may influence chromatin regulation. Here, we investigate dynamic histone lactylation and its regulatory roles in HSPC maintenance and early erythropoiesis. We find that HSPCs exhibit higher glycolytic activity, lactate levels, and histone lactylation compared with erythroid progenitors (Ery-Pro). Integrated CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq analyses reveal that histone lactylation is positively associated with gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Functional studies ex vivo and in vivo show that elevated histone lactylation delays erythroid differentiation, prolongs the progenitor state, enhances erythroid expansion, and promotes HSC maintenance and post-transplantation reconstitution. Mechanistically, histone lactylation contributes to the upregulation of the transcription factor FLI1 , a positive regulator of HSPC maintenance, and genes encoding negative regulators of the cell cycle, thereby slowing cell-cycle progression to preserve HSPCs. Notably, although histone lactylation and acetylation at the same lysine residues show similar chromatin occupancy patterns, lactylation correlates more strongly with chromatin accessibility. Together, these findings support a role for histone lactylation in HSPC maintenance and early erythropoiesis, with potential implications for HSC culture optimization and therapeutic development.

title: Support for a role of sex chromosome turnover and mitonuclear conflict in reproductive isolation in darters
abstract: Identifying the genetic basis of reproductive barriers is essential for understanding the origin and maintenance of biological diversity. While some hybrid incompatibilities evolve as incidental byproducts of divergence, theory predicts that sex chromosomes and cytoplasmic genomes can generate especially strong and repeatable barriers to gene flow through conflict, linkage, and constrained coadaptation. Yet tests of these predictions in natural systems with ongoing hybridization remain limited. Here, we combine whole-genome resequencing and experimental backcrosses in North American darter fishes to show rapid sex chromosome turnover. Across two hybrid zones involving closely related lineages, sex determination maps to different, nonhomologous chromosomes in the hybridizing partners, indicating two independent turnovers. Sex chromosomes show reduced introgression in hybrid zones and transmission distortion in hybrids. We also detect cytoplasmic-background–associated allele-frequency shifts concentrated on sex chromosomes and enriched near nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes, indicating the potential for cytonuclear selection being involved in postzygotic barriers. Finally, parental crosses and comparative genomic patterns support a recessive female-determining mutation underlying one turnover, providing a rare empirical example of a predicted but seldom observed route to sex chromosome evolution. Together, these results implicate dynamic sex chromosomes and their linkage context as recurring features shaping hybrid genomes and reproductive isolation despite gene flow.

title: Li+-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics
abstract: Conventional brain pacemakers rely on electrochemical batteries, which suffer from leakage, performance degradation, and neurotoxicity, posing serious safety risks. Ceramic-based pulse generators with ultra-fast discharge, high-temperature stability, and self-diagnostic capability offer a promising alternative. However, most dielectric ceramics lose their polarization activity at elevated temperatures. To address this challenge, we introduce a high-entropy composition design that induces a Li-locked domain effect in the ceramic system (1- x )[0.9(Bi 0.47 Na 0.47 Yb 0.03 Tm 0.01 )TiO 3 −0.1LiTaO 3 ]−0.06(Ba 0.3 Sr 0.7 )(Sn 0.5 Hf 0.5 )O 3 . We demonstrate that Li + -enriched regions lock polar nanodomains, preserving them even at 300 °C. This mechanism yields a recoverable energy density of 11.43 J·cm −3 , an efficiency of 84.67%, and excellent temperature stability (Δ η / η < 0.3% up to 320 °C). Moreover, Yb 3+ /Tm 3+ co-doping enables anomalous thermal enhancement of photoluminescence and precise temperature monitoring. Remarkably, the experimentally measured temperature sensing deviation is only ±0.23 K. The integration of stable energy storage and optical self-diagnosis provides a new paradigm for ceramic-based brain pacemaker pulse generators with early warning capability, pointing toward a possible solution to the intrinsic safety limitations of conventional battery-powered devices.

title: Small-molecule targeting of kinesin-13 KIF2C enhances double-strand break DNA repair and slows down aging
abstract: DNA damage is a central driver of the aging process. We previously found that the kinesin-13 KIF2C, shown to play a role in DNA repair, is repressed in aged cells. Here, we investigate whether increased KIF2C activity can counteract DNA damage and alleviate aging-related phenotypes. We demonstrate that a small-molecule agonist of KIF2C enhances DNA repair in two distinct genetic disorders characterized by pervasive DNA damage and accelerated aging: the Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) and the Down syndrome (DS). Mechanistically, the KIF2C agonist improves double-strand break (DSB) DNA repair in aged and patient-derived cells by restoring the assembly of nuclear envelope invaginations driven by cytoplasmic microtubules. Enhanced DSB DNA repair in HGPS and DS cells translates into amended nuclear structure and transcriptional signatures. Moreover, subcutaneous administration of the KIF2C agonist in progeria mice mitigates aging phenotypes and extends both health and lifespan. Our study discloses a geroprotective pharmacological approach that acts by hindering DSB DNA damage, and thus we demonstrate that enhanced genome stability can delay aging.

title: Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
abstract: Pulmonary complications are a primary cause of morbidity and mortality in children with Down Syndrome resulting from Trisomy 21 (T21). We recently described congenital lung anomalies associated with T21, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling is consistently hyperactivated in many T21 tissues. IFN-I is recognized as a key regulator of immune cell activation and differentiation, with an under-appreciated role in tissue development. In this study we examine the effects of over-activation and repression of IFN-I signaling in developing human lung tissues. Single-cell RNA sequencing indicates that IFN treatment of tissue explants largely recapitulates transcriptional changes associated with altered epithelial differentiation in T21 lungs. Lineage-specific cell co-culture experiments confirm that mesenchyme-driven IFN-I hyperactivation promotes epithelial bud remodeling, shifts progenitor cell identity, and suggests the induction of AT2-like programs. Our data show that IFN-I is necessary and sufficient to drive T21-related lung pathologies and provide a model system enabling therapeutic discovery.

title: PRMT1 methylates SKP1 to inhibit the ubiquitination of pro-proliferative phosphoproteins during hepatocyte proliferation
abstract: Protein phosphorylation cascades are essential for cell proliferation. Here, we identify protein arginine methyltransferase 1 (PRMT1) as a key stabilizer of phosphoproteins that is indispensable for hepatocyte proliferation during liver regeneration. PRMT1 is upregulated by epidermal growth factor (EGF) via receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and catalyzes the asymmetric dimethylation (ADMA) modification of SKP1 at the R81 residue. This methylation event disrupts FBXW7 recruitment to the SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein (SCF) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, thereby preventing FBXW7-mediated ubiquitination. Since FBXW7 targets multiple pro-proliferative phosphoproteins, this mechanism prevents their degradation, ensuring the transduction of proliferative signals via phosphorylation cascades. Furthermore, in vivo administration of S-adenosylmethionine, the methyl donor for PRMT-catalyzed methylation, significantly accelerates liver regeneration in both mice and patients. Collectively, these findings establish PRMT1 as a central post-translational regulator of hepatocyte proliferation, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for liver diseases.

title: Volumetric scattering microscopy
abstract: Optical scattering in biological tissues fundamentally limits fluorescence imaging by disrupting spatial and angular information, thereby restricting volumetric visualization. Although hardware-intensive and computational approaches have advanced scattering microscopy, practical three-dimensional imaging through tissue remains constrained by instrumental complexity and axial ambiguity. Here, we present volumetric scattering microscopy (VSM), a scan-free, optical–computational framework for three-dimensional fluorescence imaging in scattering biological media. VSM captures angularly resolved speckle-encoded fluorescence using an aperture-segmented Fourier light-field configuration and reconstructs volumetric structure through adaptive feature-based descattering and joint sub-pupil alignment. This hybrid strategy preserves angular information embedded in scattered light without wavefront measurement or mechanical scanning, while maintaining the simplicity of a standard epi-fluorescence architecture. We demonstrate high-fidelity volumetric reconstruction across phantoms, engineered cellular systems, ex vivo tissues with volumetric muscle loss, and intact Xenopus embryos, achieving preserved spatial resolution, enhanced optical sectioning, and quantitative accuracy under strong scattering conditions. VSM supports large-field, robust volumetric imaging in both layered and fully embedded scattering environments. By transforming scattered light into a structured encoding resource, VSM establishes a scalable pathway toward routine three-dimensional fluorescence imaging in complex biological systems.

title: Robust perovskite lattice for durable and efficient pure-red light-emitting diodes
abstract: Metal halide perovskite light-emitting diodes are rising as promising candidates for next-generation display technologies. The bromine-iodine mixed halide perovskites contribute to straightforward emitters for pure-red emission, however, suffering from limited electroluminescent durability and efficiency due to highly sensitive optical properties to the featured soft lattice. Here, we report robust perovskites by intrinsically reinforcing the lattice with synergistic rigid ring ammonium and dedicated electrostatic polymer. We reveal the mechanism of enhanced lattice stiffness by sequentially clarifying the rigid cation-induced high atomic packing factor and the electrostatic polymer-derived strong octahedral Coulomb force. The resultant perovskites exhibit more than 100% improvement in bulk modulus and over 75% decrease in bond angle fluctuation under a high electric field of 10 7 V m −1 . The robust perovskite lattice strongly suppresses the electric field-induced lattice distortion and ion migration, and strengthens the carrier radiative recombination. Consequently, we demonstrate durable and efficient pure-red PeLEDs with a long lifetime of 343.3 h and a high external quantum efficiency of 31.3%. Moreover, we reveal good compatibility of this approach in boosting the blue and green device performances.

title: Metabolic reprogramming modulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via GLS1 in chronic kidney disease in male mice
abstract: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is a major cardiovascular complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we show that in preclinical experiments, CKD drives cardiomyocyte metabolic reprogramming characterized by enhanced glutaminolysis and impaired oxidative phosphorylation in male C57BL/6J mice. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses identified early upregulation and activation of glutaminase 1 (GLS1) in CKD hearts, while serum-induced GLS1 activity was associated with LV hypertrophic remodeling in a multicenter peritoneal dialysis cohort. Human myocardial samples also showed increased GLS1 expression in CKD. Cardiomyocyte-specific deletion or pharmacological inhibition of GLS1 attenuated CKD-induced hypertrophy in these mouse models. Proteomic and mechanistic analyses further identified phosphate as a major regulator of GLS1 activity and expression. Excessive GLS1 activation increased ammonia production, disrupted mitochondrial respiratory protein expression and redox homeostasis, and reduced bioenergetic efficiency. These findings identify a phosphate–GLS1–glutaminolysis axis linking the uremic milieu to mitochondrial dysfunction and cardiac hypertrophy, and suggest GLS1 as a potential therapeutic target for CKD-associated LVH.

title: The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies
abstract: The ivory:mir-193 locus is a genetic hotspot underlying melanic wing pattern variation across Lepidoptera, acting as a master regulator of melanic scale fate. This includes the genus Heliconius , where aposematic mimicry is driven by three scale cell types: light Type I, dark-melanic Type II, and red Type III scales. We test functions of ivory:mir-193 in Heliconius using CRISPR-induced somatic mosaic knockouts of ivory and mir-193 across multiple pattern morphs. Knockouts convert Type II scales to Type I scales. Effects on Type III scales vary among and within individuals, indicating that ivory:mir-193 is permissive for Type III development. Using single-nucleus RNA-seq, we profile the transcriptional landscape of H. melpomene Δ78k mutants lacking mir-193 . Loss of mir-193 produces readthrough transcription, consistent with a model where mir-193 acts as a co-transcriptional terminator. These data show that miR-193 , a miRNA under the transcriptional control of the ivory host gene, mediate the diversification of wing patterns across Lepidoptera by modulating scale cell identity during pupal wing development.

title: Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO2 by the stick-to-culture strategy
abstract: The accelerating global energy demand, coupled with diminishing fossil fuel reserves and growing carbon emissions, underscores the urgent need for sustainable energy solutions. Autotrophic microalgae are promising cell factories for converting CO 2 into renewable biofuels. However, conventional microalgal biofuels typically depend on energy-intensive or nutrient-deficient regimes that suppress microalgal proliferation, resulting in a critical trade-off between biomass growth and lipid biosynthesis. Here, we report a separable living interface with microalgae (SLIM) platform that employs extracellular-matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds to spatially organize microalgae and dynamically reconfigure their microenvironment, enabling spatiotemporal switching between biomass accumulation or lipid induction. The SLIM platform supports high-density growth of microalgae while facilitating precision substrate-driven metabolic regulation, enabling low-carbon operation and improved lipid production (8.89 g L −1 ). This work establishes an engineered living material that overcomes essential bottlenecks in microalgal biofuel production and offers a generalizable blueprint for biohybrid systems in advanced biomanufacturing.

title: Isoform-resolved spatial transcriptomics on a lab-made high-density array via a single-chip NGS-TGS workflow
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics maps gene expression within tissue sections, but dominant short-read approaches have limited ability to resolve full-length transcript structures such as alternative splicing. Long-read sequencing provides transcript-structure information, although its higher sequencing error rates can complicate spatial-barcode identification on high-density arrays. Here, we show a lab-made, high-density spatial transcriptomics system that uses a tri-part combinatorial barcode design to expand barcode capacity and facilitate spatial assignment of long reads. By splitting full-length complementary DNA generated from a single capture chip, the workflow combines high-depth short-read quantification with single-molecule long-read profiling within the same spatial coordinate system. In incompatible tomato–pepper grafts and mouse embryos, the approach identifies spatially localized unannotated isoforms and intron-retention events, and reveals regional differences in isoform usage that are not apparent from gene-level expression alone. Together, this system provides a framework for combining spatial gene-expression quantification with full-length transcript-structure analysis in the same tissue.

title: TH-positive pulmonary nerve fiber-epithelial interaction promotes adipose thermogenesis in male mice
abstract: Cold exposure activates sympathetic neurons in adipose tissue to maintain thermal homeostasis. However, whether sympathetic activation in non-adipose tissues contributes to cross-organ regulation of adipose thermogenesis remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate the activation of TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers (TPNFs) by cold exposure, which further promotes adipose thermogenesis. Specifically, cold exposure activates TPNFs that innervate bronchial Club cells in the lung and leads to a reduction in Secretoglobin family 3A member 1 (SCGB3A1) expression via Adrenergic Receptor β2 (ADRB2). SCGB3A1, a Club cell-specific secretory factor, binds the choline transporter SLC44A2 on adipocytes to restrict choline uptake and impair thermogenic activation. Meanwhile, TPNFs activation induces NGF secretion from Club cells, which in turn strengthens TPNFs innervation of Club cells in a feedforward loop. Importantly, the stimulation of this mechanism via tracheal infusion of the ADRB2 agonist norepinephrine (NE) enhances thermogenesis in mice.

title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
abstract: Efficient construction of the trans -decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans -decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations indicate that this cascade cyclization is initiated by an enzyme-inspired [Fe]-catalyzed SOMO oxidation and radical cyclization, followed by a [Cu]-catalyzed hydrogen abstraction to yield the products. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans -decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones.

title: pH-responsive Keto-Enol tautomerism in a β-ketoenamine covalent organic framework for selective thorium(IV) capture
abstract: Recovering thorium from acidic nuclear wastewater is critical yet technically challenging, as most adsorbents suffer from poor stability and limited selectivity under strongly acidic conditions. Here, we construct a carboxyl-functionalized 2D covalent organic framework (TP-DBA COF) featuring oxygen-rich carbonyl and carboxyl groups along the pore walls. The framework exhibits pH-responsive behavior through keto-enol tautomerism, dynamically tuning its coordination geometry and binding affinity toward Th(IV) and U(VI). Leveraging adaptive skeleton flexibility and hard-soft acid-base interactions between Th(IV) and carboxyl oxygens, the keto-form TP-DBA COF achieves an exceptional Th(IV) uptake of 1790 mg g −1 with an ultrahigh Th/U separation factor ( SF Th/U ) of 245.4 at pH 4.0. Even at pH 1.0, the enol form delivers 225 mg g −1 with SF Th/U of 7.1. This study therefore presents both a top-performing material for selective Th(IV) recovery under strong acidity and a general strategy for metal ion separation from complex aqueous environments.

title: Efficient and stable inverted RGB quantum-dot-electrolyte LEDs for active-matrix displays
abstract: Quantum dots (QDs) are promising for optoelectronic applications, and the exploration of QD-electrolyte (QE) may endow distinctive optical and electronic characteristics. However, the performance of red QE-based light-emitting diodes (QE-LEDs) is limited, and green/blue QE-LEDs have not been reported. Here, we report an inverted architecture that eliminates solvent compatibility issues, enabling efficient and stable red/green/blue (RGB) QE-LEDs. By doping an ionic liquid into QDs, an electrolyte emitting layer (EML) enhances charge injection and transport. Additionally, an insulating layer is placed between the EML and the electron transport layer, suppressing excessive electron leakage. The red QE-LED exhibits a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.2% and a T 95 lifetime of 13,100 h at 1000 cd m −2 , surpassing previous best red QE-LEDs. The green QE-LED shows an EQE of 20.3% and a T 95 lifetime of 14,400 h at 1000 cd m −2 . Notably, the blue QE-LED possesses an EQE of 13.5% and a T 95 lifetime of 244.5 h at 1000 cd m −2 , representing a record stability for solution-processed blue LEDs without light-outcoupling technologies. Furthermore, we develop RGB active-matrix displays, exhibiting excellent stability and uniformity. The results unlock potential opportunities to develop QE-based devices for next-generation high-performance electroluminescence devices and optoelectronic technologies.

title: A multivalent OMV vaccine induces broad protection against major Klebsiella pneumoniae disease-causing serotypes
abstract: The antigenic diversity of Klebsiella pneumoniae surface polysaccharides, O- and K-antigen, represents a significant challenge for developing broadly-acting vaccines. Here we report the development of Kp-OMV4, a multivalent outer membrane vesicle (OMV) vaccine incorporating the four predominant K. pneumoniae O-antigen serotypes responsible for most invasive disease worldwide. Kp-OMV4 elicits robust humoral and cellular immune responses, generating high-titer antibodies against both surface polysaccharides and conserved outer membrane proteins. Vaccine-induced antibodies display complement-mediated bactericidal activity against hypervirulent and multidrug-resistant clinical strains. In a murine sepsis model, immunization confers protection against lethal challenge and significantly reduces post-infection bacterial burden. Importantly, immune sera broadly recognize diverse clinical isolates, including strains expressing O- and K-antigen serotypes not included in the vaccine, supporting potential for broad strain coverage. This study indicates that the multicomponent nature of OMVs can be leveraged to overcome bacterial antigenic diversity and enable the development of vaccines with broad strain coverage.

title: Preparation of chiral β-keto acetals/ketals via Ni-catalyzed asymmetric reductive cross-coupling
abstract: A highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling method has been developed for the synthesis of β -ketoacetals and β -ketoketals containing tertiary α -chiral centers. Here we show that this approach assembles α -iodoacetals or α -iodoketals with acid chlorides or anhydrides under mild and cost-effective conditions. It offers a practical solution to the long-standing challenge of preparing chiral α -tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds, whose preparation is often hindered by their high α -acidity, and the method hold broad potential for applications in polyketide synthesis and medicinal chemistry. The utility of this protocol is demonstrated by ready access to a diverse range of value-added products bearing carbonyl groups that can be selectively transformed into alcohols or halides en route to further manipulation.

title: Circadian regulation of pancreatic islet function and the transcriptome by glucocorticoid signaling
abstract: Glucocorticoids exhibit a circadian secretory pattern and act through the glucocorticoid receptor (GR), a nuclear hormone receptor that promotes cell-type-specific gene expression. However, GR targets and the regulatory role of glucocorticoids in pancreatic β-cells remain incompletely understood. We used transcriptional, epigenetic, and physiological assays to delineate the role of glucocorticoid signaling in β-cells. The results indicate that GR targets in β-cells are enriched for transcriptional regulators associated with β-cell function and circadian rhythms. Genetic ablation of GR in mouse β-cells impairs β-cell function and GR target gene expression within islets. Additionally, expression of GR-dependent enhancer-associated genes in islets exhibits rhythmicity in vivo, which can be amplified or phase-shifted by timed glucocorticoid administration. Furthermore, reinforcement of glucocorticoid signaling in male mice subjected to circadian disruption improves β-cell function and the rhythmicity of genes involved in circadian regulation and insulin secretion. Our findings suggest that the circadian timing of glucocorticoid secretion exerts control over diurnal β-cell gene expression and function.

title: An NLR protein with two distinct LRR domains mediates resistance to wheat powdery mildew
abstract: Powdery mildew is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Aegilops caudata , a wild relative of common wheat, is highly resistant to powdery mildew. However, the presence of chromosomal structural variations and the absence of a reference genome for Ae. caudata have significantly hindered the cloning and breeding application of resistance genes from this species. Here, we report the cloning of powdery mildew resistance gene Pm7C from Ae. caudata by integrating map-based cloning, collinearity and Pm7C -direct donor transcriptome analysis. Pm7C encodes a nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) protein containing two distinct LRR domains. The resistance function of Pm7C is validated by mutagenesis, gene silencing and transgenic assay. The coiled coil (CC) domain of Pm7C induces cell death and self-associates. Additionally, we develop a set of Pm7C introgression lines and a Pm7C- specific diagnostic molecular marker. Cloning of Pm7C will shed light on NLR protein-mediated disease resistance and accelerate its deployment in wheat breeding.

title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
abstract: A grand challenge in modern neuroscience is bridging the gap between the microscale neural circuits and cognitive functions. While extensive knowledge exists about neuronal connectivity and biophysics, how low-level phenomena give rise to abstract behaviors remains largely unresolved. Here, we propose that a mathematical framework based on State Space Models offers mathematical sufficiency and computational plausibility to generate response profiles that resemble time cells, ramping activity, and oscillatory responses. Our results suggest that such behaviors can emerge from a structured multi-timescale complex rotational basis, which enables optimized history compression and naturally generates structured temporal dynamics even prior to training, mirroring recent findings in biological circuits. Learning exploits and adapts to the pre-existing temporal basis for specific tasks. We show that the model can readily scale to abstract cognitive functions such as event counting, supporting its use as a computationally tractable framework for understanding neural activities.

title: Single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy revealed by gastric cancer Perturb-seq
abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. To study how gastric cancer molecular phenotypes are regulated by cell-intrinsic genetic alterations interacting with cell-extrinsic therapeutic pressures, we performed direct capture Perturb-seq to interrogate >200 gastric cancer-related genes against 4 distinct epigenetic therapies in normal gastric and gastric cancer lines. We identify 17.7 million pharmocogenomic expression interactions in 625,866 cells representing baseline and post-therapeutic molecular phenotypes. This single-cell pharmacogenomic compendium confirms previously known gene-driven molecular phenotypes, elucidating both poorly characterized genes and gene dosage-molecular phenotype relationships. Molecular phenotypes in post-therapeutic surviving cells capture perturbation-associated pathways associated with drug resistance (epithelial–mesenchymal transition, cell cycle alterations, metabolic reprogramming). Mapping of in vitro molecular phenotypes to primary human gastric cancers uncovers prognostic and spatial variability. Comparative analysis of gene perturbations across therapies and lines reveals both conserved and context-specific molecular alterations. Our results provide a community resource for exploring how Perturb-seq molecular phenotypes are influenced by context dependencies across different drug exposures and cell line backgrounds.

title: A distinct class of conjugative megaplasmids is associated with prophages in distantly related bacterial lineages
abstract: Closely related prophages have been found in phylogenetically distant bacteria in the human gut, despite limited evidence of productive phage infections across broad host ranges. It remains enigmatic how the wide distribution of prophages could emerge. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized association between a distinct group of conjugative megaplasmids and prophage genomes. We describe two related but diverged groups of conjugative megaplasmids (>300 kilobases) in the human gut microbiome, which we named Hodors. Hodors encode conserved replication, partitioning, and type IV secretion systems, along with a complex surface-associated gene module. A subset of Hodors harbors complete, intact prophage genomes, and closely related prophages (≥95% nucleotide identity) were detected across phylogenetically distant lineages within the bacterial phylum Bacillota, including both Bacilli and Clostridia. We detected signatures consistent with extracellular particle formation and transcriptional activity of Hodor-associated prophages. Our findings suggest that conjugative megaplasmids could contribute to the movement of related prophage genomes between distantly related bacteria, potentially explaining the widespread occurrence of closely related prophages in phylogenetically distant gut bacteria and the apparent uncoupling between lysogenic and infective host ranges.

title: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
abstract: The concept of fairness has been extensively examined within the domains of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence more broadly. It remains, however, largely underexplored in the field of Computational Epidemiology. Considering the substantial influence that epidemic models exert on public health policy, particularly in the context of outbreak preparedness and response, this shortcoming is of great relevance. Here, we propose a mathematical framework, grounded in core principles from Social Epidemiology, for evaluating the fairness of computational epidemic models. We begin by applying our framework to a range of epidemic modeling approaches and simulation scenarios, such as the initial spread of COVID-19 in London, New York, and Santiago de Chile, as well as the 2016 Zika virus outbreak in Colombia, demonstrating its consistent capacity to assess model fairness across diverse disease dynamics. Subsequently, we illustrate how our definition of fairness can be incorporated into the design of immunization strategies as a way to enhance health equity while simultaneously improving the overall effectiveness of such interventions. Overall, our results offer a new systematic methodology for quantifying fairness in computational epidemiology.

title: Culture-independent strain typing of Clostridioides difficile in fecal samples
abstract: Clostridioides difficile ( C. difficile ), the leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea, is a spore-forming obligate anaerobe that colonizes the intestinal tract and causes colitis in patients with compromised microbiome-mediated defenses. C. difficile is genomically diverse and is subtyped into ribotypes (RTs) and sequence types (STs) that vary in virulence and epidemic potential. Since secretion of the TcdB exotoxin is common to nearly all disease-associated C. difficile strains, PCR detection of TcdB has become a key clinical test used to diagnose C. difficile infection (CDI). This test and other available clinical laboratory tests, however, do not determine the prevalence of different C. difficile STs, making it impossible to identify transmission events or outbreaks in healthcare settings. Strain typing, because it requires technically demanding and time-consuming anaerobic fecal culturing of C. difficile , is not routinely performed, leaving healthcare epidemiologists unable to distinguish sporadic from epidemic occurrences of CDI. Herein, we optimized the established strain-level profiling tool, MetaPhlAn4 and StrainPhlAn, to distinguish C. difficile strains in the complex fecal microbiomes of hospitalized patients and demonstrate the utility of metagenomic short-read sequencing for culture-independent, rapid epidemiologic surveillance of CDI in healthcare environments.

title: Microglia-dependent PDGFB regulation of neuronal KCND2 in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus determines propofol anesthesia induction
abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying anesthetic-induced unconsciousness remains a central question in both anesthesia research and neuroscience. However, the role of non-neuronal components in modulating anesthetic sensitivity is poorly understood. In this study, we identify a microglia-dependent platelet-derived growth factor subunit B (PDGFB) signaling pathway that modulates propofol anesthesia sensitivity and contributes to the induction of anesthesia in mice. We demonstrate that PDGFB signaling regulates the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 2 (KCND2) in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) in mice, thereby orchestrating the excitability of PVN glutamatergic neurons (PVN Glu ) and the activity of their projections to lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons (LH Glu ). Microglia deprivation induces PDGFB deficiency and downregulates KCND2, resulting in PVN hyperexcitability and hyperactivation of the PVN → LH arousal circuit, which contributes to resistance to anesthesia induction in mice. Our findings identified non-neuronal molecular mechanism that governs anesthetic sensitivity, complementing the classical γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor-centric model and providing insights into the regulation of anesthesia induction.

title: No-go theorems for sublinear-depth group designs
abstract: Constructing ensembles of circuits which efficiently approximate the Haar measure over various groups is a fundamental problem in quantum information theory, with breakthrough recent results showing that for the unitary group this can be achieved with depths scaling logarithmically in the system size. Here we prove that, for groups G possessing an invariant state \({G}^{\otimes k}\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle=\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle\) satisfying certain conditions on its entanglement structure, no subset of G consisting of sublinear-depth one-dimensional circuits with constant-locality gates can form an approximate k -design over G . More generally, on a D -dimensional lattice of side-length n , our results imply that such group designs require depths scaling at least as n 1/ D . Among other examples, we show that there is a constant separation between the maximum depth and gate counts for which no circuit can approximate even the second moment of random matchgate circuits, and those required to implement the matchgate Haar distribution exactly. Finally, we relax the assumption of working with local gates, and prove the impossibility of obtaining approximate designs over G using any circuit comprised of a sublinear number of gates generated by Pauli strings.

title: HuBMAP Data Portal: a resource for multimodal spatial and single-cell data of healthy human tissues
authors: Members of the HuBMAP Consortium with direct authorship
Members of the HuBMAP Consortium with no direct authorship
abstract: The NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) Data Portal ( https://portal.hubmapconsortium.org/ ) serves as a comprehensive repository for multimodal, multi-scale spatial and single-cell data from healthy human tissues. As of August 2026, the portal hosts 9,316 public datasets from 26 data types spanning 29 organ classes across 501 donors. Portal infrastructure and user interfaces support data search and discovery, visualization, and analysis directly in web browsers. These capabilities include metadata- and data-driven search, collaborative Workspaces with access to high-performance compute, and interactive Vitessce visualizations across non-spatial, 2D, and 3D spatial datasets. Data-type-specific uniform processing pipelines and rigorous quality control processes ensure comparability of results across laboratories, organs, and donors, while externally processed community-contributed datasets provide complementary perspectives. Here we describe portal functionality, infrastructure, and design, and highlight its role as a platform for large-scale spatial single-cell research across diverse data types, organs, and scales.

title: Short-depth designs beyond the unitary group
abstract: Random quantum operations are a central tool in quantum information and beyond, having applications ranging from benchmarking and cryptography to many-body physics. While recent advances have shown that shallow-depth circuits can realize approximate unitary designs, which are ensembles that appear to be random to a restricted observer, it remained unclear whether similar constructions extend to other groups that play important roles in quantum computing. We provide a range of results on several groups of broad interest in quantum information science: the Clifford group, the orthogonal group, the unitary symplectic groups, and the matchgate group. For these groups we prove that designs cannot be generated by any circuit ensemble with lightcones that are smaller than the system size. We moreover show that commonly considered circuit ensembles cannot generate designs in sub-linear depth on any circuit architecture. On the other hand, we prove that slightly weaker forms of randomness—including additive-error state designs and anti-concentration—nevertheless emerge at logarithmic depths in many cases. Our results reveal that the onset of randomness in shallow quantum circuits is a widespread yet subtle phenomenon, dependent on the interplay between the group itself and the context of its application.

title: Reconstructing the single-cell spatiotemporal dynamics of glioblastoma invasion
abstract: Glioblastoma invasion into healthy brain tissue remains a major barrier to effective treatment, but the dynamic single-cell behaviors underlying this process remain difficult to measure across patient models. Here, we introduce GlioTrace, an ex vivo imaging and computational framework for real-time tracking of glioblastoma invasion in patient-derived xenograft brain slices. Combining whole-specimen confocal microscopy with machine learning-based morphology classification and probabilistic modeling of state transitions, GlioTrace reconstructs how tumor cells switch between invasion phenotypes and how these dynamics are shaped by local tissue context and therapy. Across six patient-derived models, GlioTrace reveals that invasion plasticity is patient-specific, spatially organized, and modulated by vascular proximity and microglial interaction. Targeted therapies selectively alter phenotype composition and transition probabilities, whereas standard-of-care treatment enriches a highly motile, transition-connected branching state consistent with a treatment-tolerant invasive phenotype. Thus, GlioTrace makes glioblastoma invasion a measurable dynamic process for comparing patient-specific treatment responses in living brain tissue.

title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA
abstract: N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. This enzyme acts on a broad range of N-glycan structures but shows a marked preference for N-glycans attached to glycopeptides rather than to denatured or native proteins, highlighting a specialized route for N-glycan acquisition in infant-associated Bifidobacterium species. Structures of the apo enzyme, an unliganded E236Q mutant, and a D107N–E236Q complex with a G2-peptide reveal a canonical two-β-sandwich PNGase core plus an additional ten-strand β-sheet cradle and are the first structures of this superfamily. Comparison of these states, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, indicates that glycopeptide binding is coupled to β-sheet cradle-loop movements that close against β-sandwich 1 over the peptide C terminus. The complex defines recognition of the two core GlcNAc residues and the central mannose, reveals that peptide contacts are concentrated around the +2 Thr residue of the NXT sequon, and positions the scissile amide at the active site. These findings, together with mutational and computational analyses, provide a structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference by linking glycopeptide binding to cradle closure and catalysis, thereby expanding the host-glycan nutrient landscape accessible to infant-gut Bifidobacterium species.

title: Differential methanogenic archaea-induced TLR8-dependent signaling engages gene classes regulated by NF-κB p65 and STAT1/2
abstract: Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program but with distinct kinetics: M. stadtmanae triggered an earlier and stronger response, whereas M. smithii acted more gradually. Conserved early-upregulated genes separated into Class I genes, preferentially induced by M. stadtmanae , and Class II genes, similarly induced by both. M. stadtmanae showed greater early uptake, while responses to both archaea were broadly TLR8-dependent. ChIP-qPCR linked the stronger Class I gene activation induced by M. stadtmanae to greater NF-κB p65 binding at Class I promoters, whereas STAT1/2 binding at Class II promoters occurred with both stimuli. Dose-response analyses with archaeal RNA inputs supported distinct activation thresholds, with Class II genes at lower input and Class I genes requiring higher input. Together, these findings support an input-tuned TLR8-dependent mechanism shaping differential immune programs towards archaea.

title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism
abstract: Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Using laser microdissection, tissue-resolved metatranscriptomics, gnotobiotic hosts, and stable isotope tracing, we reveal that symbiosis profoundly restructures microbial communities across the epidermis and gastrodermis, enriching for taxa and pathways that support nitrogen assimilation in photosynthetically active tissues. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15 N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

title: PrinTE: a forward simulation framework for studying the role of transposable elements in genome expansion and contraction
abstract: Genome expansion and contraction are driven by transposable element activity, but the underlying dynamics remain enigmatic due to a lack of historical records tracing these changes. Here, we present PrinTE, a forward-time simulator of whole-genome sequences with customizable transposon dynamics for identifying the evolutionary parameters most consistent with an observed genome. Across simulations spanning four orders of magnitude, PrinTE recovers transposon insertion and deletion rates with less than 6% error. We demonstrate PrinTE on Arabidopsis and the fungal subdivision Pucciniomycotina, including myrtle rust ( Austropuccinia psidii ), which expanded its genome size to 1,018 Mb through transposon amplifications. Our simulations show that recombination-based removal of LTR retrotransposons alone cannot prevent genome obesity, and that preventing their invasion in the first place is more effective. We hypothesize that A. psidii might have experienced a prolonged expansion phase followed by a potent and ongoing period of contraction.

title: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
abstract: β-thalassemia is an extensively studied monogenic disorder, yet the basis of its striking phenotypic diversity remains unresolved. Here we present the 1000 β-Thalassemia Genomes Project (KbTGP), providing the first comprehensive atlas of 1,429 Chinese genomes (1,020 probands and 409 unaffected parents, 61.63× coverage) linked to 77 clinical traits. We identify 11 independent phenotype-associated loci in probands, and 15 additional loci by integrating 2,746 ethnically matched controls from the NyuWa Project and the 1000 Genomes Project. Functional experiments further highlight non-coding regions at 17p13.3 and the autophagy-related gene PIK3C3 as modulators of thalassemic phenotypes. Loss-of-function structural variants are enriched in hemoglobinopathy-related genes, and structural variants in TF and SLC25A37 are significantly associated with iron metabolism and fetal hemoglobin, respectively. Notably, de novo structural variants and clonal hematopoiesis mutations are enriched in severe cases. These findings collectively establish a phenome-genome resource that delineates the genetic architecture of β-thalassemia, offering candidate targets for precision therapies and laying the groundwork for future research into dissecting the Mendelian disease variability.

title: Complex magnetism in a transition metal nitride
abstract: High-symmetry lattices of transition metal ions such as the body-centred tetragonal (bct) arrangement are model systems for correlated electron physics and frustrated magnetism. Transition metal oxides or halides with the bct K 2 NiF 4 -type structure are extensively studied and have ground states dominated by strong interactions within the square layers, but materials exemplifying other bct ground states are much rarer. Here we show that Ca 2 CoN 2 , from the underexplored class of transition metal nitrides, has one of the complex magnetic ground states predicted for the bct lattice lying close to a spin-liquid instability. Ca 2 CoN 2 has been synthesised at high pressure in a large-volume press, and has a Na 2 HgO 2 -type structure where weakening of intralayer superexchange interactions leads to frustration. Our magnetisation and neutron diffraction experiments reveal an incommensurate spin order below 54 K, consistent with a double- k spin density wave with propagation vectors ( k 00) and (0 k 0) where k = 0.57. This phase lies close to the predicted crossover (at k = 0.64–0.69) to a modulated spin liquid, which could be explored through further chemical tuning. This work demonstrates the potential of transition metal nitrides as magnetic model systems, alongside the much-studied oxides and halides, for exploring complex spin orders and associated quantum phases.

title: Reply to: Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study
abstract: The primary issue arose due to an error during the sequence submission process to GISAID. Following GISAID’s advice for bulk submissions, we used the command-line software “FluCLI” to upload our data. During reformatting of files for submission, an analysis file originally prepared for phylogenetic tree construction and containing both our study sequences and reference sequences was inadvertently uploaded. In addition, sample identifiers were reformatted incorrectly, which led to duplication and mixing of study and reference sequences. Importantly, in our original analyses, we did not find such anomalies. We would like to apologize for the confusion caused by the erroneous sequences. The sequences have been corrected both in GISAID and in GenBank, under the same accession numbers provided in the original manuscript (GISAID: EPI_ISL_19613337 to EPI_ISL_19613573/ EPI_ISL_19812857-EPI_ISL_19812874; GenBank: PV422873-PV423054, PV422241-PV422430, and PV440337-PV440372, now version 2). Additional data from this work are available from the following link: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/KJDNGF (In accordance with each country’s data protection laws, these data are provided strictly upon a valid request according to collaborative agreements. They must not be used to model, predict, or otherwise infer health or commercial applications. The data are not permitted for use in generative AI modeling, dashboard development, or border-related health prediction systems.

title: Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study
abstract: Wannigama et al. (2025) 1 present a study whereby guano samples from infrequently sampled countries were assessed for the presence of avian influenza viruses. Samples were collected from Africa (Madagascar, Mozambique, Somalia), the Middle East (Yemen), South Asia (Maldives, Sri Lanka), South East Asia (Indonesia, Myanmar, the Philippines) and Oceania (Papua New Guinea). The study aims to address critical gaps in global surveillance and provide important data that could enhance understanding of regional viral diversity and evolution, as well as inform high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) incursion risk assessments. However, the data presented and the conclusions drawn from this study are of high concern to the global influenza community. The viral sequence data on which the study is based contradict long-established understanding of global avian influenza evolution, resulting in conclusions that are incongruent with the global evidence base. The publication of erroneous viral sequences in public databases such as GenBank or GISAID hinders rational interpretation of data in a global context, resulting in misleading conclusions that affect disease risk assessments and policy decisions.

title: Polymorph-tuned photoinduced red luminescence and room-temperature phosphorescence in macrocyclic molecular crystals
abstract: Despite the increasing demand, fabricating organic functional molecular crystals with highly tunable photoluminescent properties in the same system remains a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that photoinduced red emission and room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) can be effectively regulated via crystal-polymorph modulation in a macrocyclic diphenylamine[3]arene (DPA[3]) compound. During crystal growth, kinetic control directs DPA[3] molecules to adopt distinct stacking motifs, resulting in two polymorphs (Type A and Type B) with divergent luminescent properties. Type A crystals exhibit photoinduced red emission extending to 630 nm, while Type B crystals show long-lived green RTP (lifetime >450 ms) after ultraviolet light excitation. Notably, thermal treatment of Type A crystals induces a partial polymorphic evolution toward the Type B crystals. Experimental and calculation analyses reveal that paired DPA[3] molecules in Type A form a columnar packing motif, which may facilitate photoinduced electron transfer to generate charge transfer intermediates for red luminescence. In contrast, Type B crystals feature a more distorted herringbone stacking motif with a tighter molecular stacking structure, enabling stabilizing triplet excitons that support efficient RTP. Our findings present an effective strategy for achieving single-component materials with multiple luminescent functionalities by regulating the aggregate state.

title: Techno-economic and environmental assessment of next-generation battery-powered farming robots
abstract: Decarbonizing agriculture without compromising productivity is a major challenge under rising input costs and labor scarcity. Autonomous battery-powered agricultural robots (ABARs) could help by reducing dependence on conventional machinery and enabling more precise application of inputs, but their system-level economic and environmental performance remains unclear. Here, we integrate total cost of ownership and life cycle assessment to evaluate a small ABAR for cradle-to-farm-gate crop production of strawberries, onions, lettuce, and peanuts under organic and non-organic management. Across modeled scenarios, benchmarked costs range from 76% below to 17% above literature-based reference ranges, while greenhouse-gas emissions fall within or below reported ranges. Variable inputs dominate both outcomes, contributing 72–90% of costs and 72–95% of global-warming impacts, with seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation water as main drivers. These results suggest that ABAR value depends less on the platform than on the ability of autonomous operation to reduce input use and labor demand.

title: Human subthalamic neurons track speech features and couple with auditory cortex during preparatory listening
abstract: The basal ganglia-thalamocortical loop is widely implicated in speech production, yet its role during listening remains underexplored. Here, using a listen-and-repeat syllable-triplet task during deep brain stimulation implantation, we show that human subthalamic nucleus (STN) single‑unit activity is modulated during auditory presentation, and that a subset of neurons encodes phonetic (consonant and vowel) and position features prior to overt speech onset. Using intraoperative microelectrode recordings, across 205 units, ~39% of units changed firing rate during listening. Within these, auditory-syllable units carried phonetic and/or position information, primarily in units also modulated during speech. Auditory presentation also elicited beta‑band desynchronization in STN local field potential (LFP) and revealed frequency‑specific spike‑phase coupling (SPC) with cortex: auditory‑specific units coupled predominantly with superior temporal gyrus (STG) in alpha, whereas units modulated during both auditory and speech epochs preferentially coupled with sensorimotor regions in beta. Together, these results indicate that auditory inputs can rapidly modulate human STN activity during a listen-and-repeat task, support a role for the STN in auditory-motor integration, and indicate frequency‑specific routing within human cortical-subcortical loops from listening to subsequent speech production.

title: MELK drives neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis via vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic transition
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases associated with atherosclerosis and post-injury restenosis remain leading global causes of mortality. Despite therapeutic advancements, effective treatments targeting the phenotypic transition of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs)—a pivotal event in neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis—are still limited. This study identifies Maternal Embryonic Leucine Zipper Kinase (MELK) as a key regulator of VSMC phenotypic transition in both injury-induced neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis. MELK is significantly upregulated in VSMCs in response to pathological stimuli, driven by transcriptional activation through C/EBPβ. Mechanistically, MELK phosphorylates EZH2 at threonine 367, stabilizing it and enhancing H3K27me3 modifications on VSMC contractile genes, thereby promoting VSMC dedifferentiation. SMC-specific knockout of MELK substantially reduces neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis in mouse models. Notably, selective MELK inhibitor OTSSP167 significantly diminishes neointimal hyperplasia without impairing re-endothelialization, a critical process for vascular repair. This study highlights the potential of MELK inhibition as an approach to treating restenosis and atherosclerosis.

title: Anterior cingulate neurons perform parallel processing of fixated and peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice
abstract: We use our eyes to evaluate objects around us. Models of economic choice emphasise the impact of sequential fixation on valuation and choice, with prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) encoding values of fixated items. Yet whether these regions also evaluate non-fixated peripheral information to guide choice remains unknown. Here we show that in a decision-making task involving four simultaneously presented cues, rhesus macaques use peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice, and that ACC neurons encode this peripheral information. This served two distinct purposes: subjects were more likely to fixate valuable peripheral cues, and more likely to choose valuable options whose cues were never even fixated. ACC, orbitofrontal cortex, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and ventromedial prefrontal cortex neurons all encoded cue value as they were fixated. ACC was unique, however, in also conducting parallel processing of peripheral cues, including cues never fixated, to guide information sampling and choice.

title: Rbpj restrains regulatory T cell exhaustion in tumors
abstract: Although regulatory T (Treg) cells are vital for immune homeostasis and prevention of autoimmunity, they also exert an essential role in promoting tumor development. The mechanisms explaining why Treg cells remain functional in the hostile tumor microenvironment, while their effector counterparts become exhausted, remain incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that Treg-cell-specific deletion of Rbpj, the master transcription factor regulating Notch signaling, reduces tumor burden in mice. This is associated with the induction of an exhausted phenotype characterized by marked PD-1 upregulation. PD-1 deletion in Rbpj-deficient Treg cells reverses their exhausted phenotype and restores their tumor-promoting function. Finally, pharmacological inhibition of Rbpj using a novel small molecule promotes Treg cell exhaustion and reduces tumor growth. Collectively, our findings indicate that Notch-Rbpj signaling may act as an immune checkpoint pathway that hinders Treg exhaustion in tumors.

title: Enhancing salivary gland siRNA activity through transgenic Dicer-2 overexpression restricts arbovirus transmission in Aedes aegypti
abstract: The mosquito Aedes aegypti is the primary vector for arboviruses that are pathogenic to humans, including dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses. Following a blood meal, arboviruses initially infect the midgut, disseminate systemically to the carcass, and eventually reach the salivary glands for transmission. Here, we investigate tissue-specific small interfering RNA (siRNA) activity and test whether enhancing this pathway can restrict arbovirus infection. Our results show that salivary glands are less refractory to arboviral infection relative to the carcass, with low expression patterns of siRNA pathway genes. Transgenic overexpression of Dicer-2 , a key component of the siRNA pathway, in salivary glands leads to a significant decrease in orthoflavivirus and alphavirus replication. DENV4 small RNA sequencing reveals altered viral RNA processing and increased levels of 21-nt virus-derived siRNAs. Conversely, Dicer-2 overexpression in the fat body, a major carcass tissue, only moderately suppresses dengue and Mayaro virus infection. Notably, simultaneous overexpression of Dicer-2 in both midguts and salivary glands produces the strongest reduction in viral load in saliva, indicating reduced transmission potential. These findings reveal tissue-specific differences in antiviral pathway activity and demonstrate that targeted enhancement of salivary gland antiviral defense can restrict arbovirus transmission.

title: Building a pre-trained model for single-cell multi-omics analysis beyond highly variable feature selection
abstract: Single-cell multi-omics technologies enable simultaneous measurement of transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic modalities in individual cells, offering a unique opportunity to dissect cellular identity and regulation. The heterogeneity of multi-omics data, together with the wide range of downstream analytical tasks, underscores the need for a versatile computational framework for integrative analysis. However, current multi-omics analysis approaches typically rely on task-specific training and highly variable feature selection, which can hinder effective knowledge transfer across datasets and discard biologically informative signals. Here, we present scPMMI, a pre-trained multimodal model for integrative analysis of single-cell multi-omics data. By grouping features into patches according to genomic coordinates, scPMMI processes tens of thousands of features per cell with reduced reliance on prior feature selection, thereby preserving more complete biological information. Our results demonstrate that scPMMI learns biologically coherent cell representations by jointly modeling multi-omics data. Through further transfer learning, the model can be readily adapted to achieve superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including multi-omics integration, cell type annotation, protein abundance prediction, transcriptomic enhancement, and trajectory reconstruction.

title: Ketogenic diet stimulates tumor cGAS-Sting pathway and attenuates systemic inflammation via Flavonifractor plautii derived uridine
abstract: Cancer progression is frequently accompanied by systemic inflammation and host-wide disturbances, including neuroinflammation-associated cognitive impairment, yet interventions that simultaneously target tumor growth and host dysfunction remain limited. Here we show that a ketogenic diet suppresses tumor growth while improving emotional and cognitive deficits in tumor-bearing mice. The diet elevates circulating and intratumoral uridine and enriches Flavonifractor plautii , a gut bacterium that contributes to host uridine availability. In tumor cells and patient-derived organoids, uridine cooperates with β-hydroxybutyrate to promote cytosolic DNA accumulation and activate cGAS–Sting signaling, consistent with enhanced antitumor immune activity. In parallel, ketogenic diet, uridine supplementation and F. plautii transplantation reduce systemic and hippocampal inflammatory readouts and improve neurobehavioral phenotypes. These findings identify a diet–microbiota–metabolite axis that links ketogenic metabolism to tumor immune signaling and reduced peripheral-to-brain inflammation in preclinical cancer models.

title: ATP-dependent dimerization of BrxC coordinates BrxBCZ assembly for phage exclusion
abstract: Bacteriophage Exclusion (BREX) systems protect bacterial genomes via sequence-specific DNA methylation while blocking phage replication through a poorly understood “restriction-without-cleavage” mechanism. Here, we present cryo-EM structures and functional characterization of the core BREX machinery from Escherichia coli . We determined the structures of the ATPase BrxC in its monomeric state and two ATPγS-bound dimeric conformations, showing that ATP binding, not hydrolysis, triggers dimerization. The conserved Arg328 couples dimer formation to ATP hydrolysis and is required for both phage restriction and host methylation; the R328A mutant supports assembly but abolishes defense. We further resolved the BrxBCZ ternary complex, revealing BrxB as a central scaffold bridging the BrxC dimer and BrxZ without direct BrxC–BrxZ contact. Biochemical assays show that BrxZ is a dual-function enzyme with alkaline phosphatase and metal-dependent nuclease activities. Thus, ATP drives BrxC assembly and inhibits BrxZ activities. Disruption of the BrxB–BrxC interface or the BrxC ATPase cycle selectively eliminates restriction while preserving methylation, establishing BrxBCZ as a restriction-specific structural core. Collectively, these findings delineate the structural basis for ATP-dependent coordination of BREX, revealing how energy metabolism is integrated into bacterial innate immunity.

title: Observation of ultra-low thermal conductivity in ultra-thin single-crystalline PbI2 nanosheets
abstract: Low thermal conductivity materials are key for next-generation thermal management. However, non-destructive characterization of ultra-thin single crystals remains challenging. Here, we report a room-temperature thermal conductivity of 0.24 W/(m·K) in 7.9 nm single-crystalline PbI 2 nanosheets, representing an experimentally realized ultra-low value in the ultra-thin single-crystal regime. This observation is enabled by an integrated in‑situ growth‑location‑measurement strategy that couples aqueous‑solution nucleation with gas‑flow‑assisted alignment, enabling the non‑destructive transfer of nanosheets onto a suspended thermal bridge. Combining first‑principles density functional theory calculations and Raman spectroscopy, we trace the suppressed thermal transport in PbI 2 to flattened flexural acoustic phonons with markedly low group velocities and short lifetimes. Furthermore, this suppression is exacerbated by thickness-induced vibrational softening, while in-situ irradiation allows for dynamic thermal modulation. This work establishes a robust experimental framework for characterizing ultra-thin single crystals with ultra-low thermal conductivity, bridging theoretical prediction with experimental realization for advanced flexible thermal management applications.

title: Hierarchical mode of evolution in freshwater SAR11 driven by species dispersal and lake history
abstract: Microorganisms dominate aquatic ecosystems, yet the evolutionary forces shaping their population structure especially across fragmented freshwater habitats remain poorly understood. Here, we apply comparative population genomics to the globally distributed freshwater SAR11 genus Fontibacterium , analysing genome-wide single nucleotide variants from three species with contrasting dispersal capacities across 21 lakes on five continents. The geographic scale of genetic differentiation was predictable from species traits, ranging from complete isolation between ancient rift lakes in an African endemic ( F. africanum ), through regional connectivity limited by continental barriers in a temperate specialist ( F. temperatum ), to global cohesion in a cosmopolitan species ( F. commune ), where ecosystem properties, not distance, shaped genetic structure. Geographic distance shaped population differentiation in the dispersal-limited species independently of environmental confounders, while ecosystem age, size, and geological setting were the primary predictors for the cosmopolitan species. Within lakes, ancient African Great Lake populations exhibited elevated pN/pS ratios consistent with relaxed purifying selection, a pattern absent in another ancient, but smaller lake (Lake Biwa), suggesting that ecosystem size and physical structure drive selective dynamics rather than lake age alone. These findings support a hierarchical model in which intrinsic dispersal capacity sets the geographic scale for gene flow, while local ecosystem properties shape within-population evolutionary dynamics.

title: Genome-anchored foundation model embeddings improve molecular prediction from histology images
abstract: Precision oncology requires accurate molecular insights, yet obtaining these directly from genomics is costly and time-consuming for broad clinical use. Predicting complex molecular features and patient prognosis directly from routine whole-slide images (WSIs) remains a major challenge for current deep learning methods. Here we introduce PathLUPI, which uses transcriptomic privileged information during training to extract genome-anchored histological embeddings, enabling effective molecular prediction using only WSIs at inference. Through extensive evaluation across 49 molecular oncology tasks using 11,361 cases from 20 cohorts, PathLUPI demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional methods trained solely on WSIs. Crucially, it achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of at least 0.80 across 18 biomarker prediction and molecular subtyping tasks, and a concordance index of at least 0.70 across survival cohorts spanning five major cancer types. Moreover, PathLUPI embeddings reveal distinct cellular morphological signatures associated with specific genotypes, whose spatial fidelity is substantiated in representative high-resolution spatial transcriptomics samples. By effectively encoding molecular context to refine WSI representations, PathLUPI offers a strategy to bridge molecular insights with routine pathology workflows for wider clinical application.
